title: Transradial Intracranial Aneurysm Embolization Using a 7F Sheath-Compatible 0.087-Inch Guide Catheter: A Single-Center Retrospective Study.
abstract: Transradial intracranial aneurysm embolization is well established, but experience with large-bore 7F sheath-based guide platforms remains comparatively limited. We evaluated the technical feasibility and periprocedural outcomes of a 7F sheath-compatible 0.087inch guide catheter for transradial intracranial aneurysm embolization.In this single-arm, noncomparative retrospective study, we reviewed consecutive patients who underwent attempted transradial intracranial aneurysm embolization using the NeuGlide as the primary guide catheter at a single center between January 2025 and May 2026. Preaccess radial ultrasonography was performed in all patients, and radial diameter ≥1.7 mm was required for 7F access. The primary outcome was completion of the intended treatment through radial access without femoral conversion.Target-vessel catheterization was achieved in 71/74 procedures (95.9%), and radial procedural completion in 69/74 (93.2%; 95% confidence interval, 85.1-97.1%). Three procedures required femoral conversion, and 2 were terminated without aneurysm treatment; overall treatment completion was 72/74 (97.3%). Guide instability occurred in 2 procedures: 1 repositioning-only event and 1 event resulting in femoral conversion; no guide exchanges occurred. Seven patients had 9 access-site component events, all managed conservatively; all 6 hematomas were low-grade (EASY I-II). Radial artery occlusion was identified in 1/15 patients formally assessed.In this radial-first cohort, the 7F sheath-compatible 0.087-inch NeuGlide guide catheter achieved a 93.2% radial procedural completion rate across multiple intracranial aneurysm treatment strategies. These findings support the NeuGlide as a technically feasible and versatile large-bore transradial platform in appropriately selected patients.

title: Does Route of Administration Affect the Outcome of Retinal Gene Therapy Clinical Trials?
abstract: Luxturna® (voretigene neparvovec-rzyl) for RPE65-associated retinal dystrophy was the first FDA-approved in vivo gene therapy and, 9 years later, remains the only approved retinal gene therapy. A search of clinicaltrials.gov identified 80 interventional phase 1-3 U.S. studies using AAV vectors, 45 using subretinal injection (SRI), and 33 using intravitreal injection (IVT). SRI efficiently transduces photoreceptors and RPE but transduces only the detached retinal area and carries procedure-related risks. IVT provides broader exposure and avoids retinal detachment but has shown limited efficacy for retinal targets and may produce dose-dependent inflammation. Overall, 11.6% of eyes in peer-reviewed publications receiving gene therapy via SRI experienced serious adverse events (SAEs); and in some studies, 100% experienced treatment-related adverse events (TRAEs). The gap between an active clinical pipeline and regulatory success raises the question: how does route of administration interact with therapeutic biology and clinical trial design? X-linked retinitis pigmentosa (XLRP) due to RPGR variants illustrates this challenge. Nine of 10 trials treating RPGR-related XLRP used SRI, with microperimetry and low light visual acuity as efficacy endpoints; 2 completed phase 2/3 studies failed to meet their primary endpoints. The XOLARIS XLRP natural history study suggests that other measures (e.g., visual field loss, central ellipsoid zone width) may better capture progression. Thus, retinal gene therapy clinical trial design must match the route of administration to the cellular target, therapeutic mechanism, and disease distribution. Emerging vectors and delivery strategies that expand retinal coverage while reducing procedural injury are critical to improve the likelihood of successful retinal gene therapy trials.

Researchers examined 80 interventional phase 1-3 U. title: State Medical Board Disciplinary Actions Related to Medical Knowledge Deficits.
abstract: The proportion of state medical board disciplinary actions taken due to medical knowledge deficits is not known. We measured the percentage of disciplinary actions with medical knowledge deficits and the association between disciplinary actions and board certification exam performance, among American Board of Internal Medicine (ABIM) physicians in California.We investigated all physicians in California with an ABIM identification number who were disciplined from January 1, 2011 to December 31, 2022. We reviewed disciplinary documentation on California's medical board website for each physician and determined through a systematic process whether actions had to do with a medical knowledge deficit. We also examined the association between these disciplinary actions and whether a physician failed on their first certification exam attempt using a chi-squared analysis.Among the 558 California disciplinary actions from 2011 to 2022, 52.3% were related to a medical knowledge deficit. In addition, 43.7% were not related to medical knowledge, and 3.9% had an 'Ambiguous' classification. Physicians who had a disciplinary action associated with a medical knowledge deficit were less likely to have passed the initial certification exam on the first attempt (chi-square=3.90, P = .048).About half of the disciplinary actions received by physicians in California with an ABIM identification number were related to medical knowledge deficits and these types of disciplinary actions were more likely among physicians who failed to pass the ABIM certification exam on the first attempt compared with those who passed. Since medical knowledge can potentially be improved, this finding allows for the possibility of a reduction in future disciplinary actions.Copyright © 2026 The Alliance for Continuing Education in the Health Professions, the Association for Hospital Medical Education, and the Society for Academic Continuing Medical Education.

title: Effect of Activin Type II Receptor Signaling in Patients With HFpEF and Pulmonary Hypertension: A Critical Analysis of Biological Mechanisms and Clinical Trials.
abstract: The totality of evidence indicates that the mechanisms underlying the increase in pulmonary vascular resistance in patients with combined postcapillary and precapillary pulmonary hypertension (CpcPH) associated with heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF) differ meaningfully from those responsible for the increase in pulmonary vascular resistance in patients with pulmonary arterial hypertension. CpcPH-HFpEF is a complex disorder involving the pulmonary veins, left atrium, and pulmonary arterioles, but recent evidence has highlighted a potentially central role for pulmonary venous and left atrial (LA) dysfunction. Epicardial adipose tissue occupies anatomical proximity to both structures, allowing derivative secretory products to influence their structure and function. The most well-characterized proinflammatory adipokine released from an expanded epicardial fat mass is activin A, which causes fibrosis and cardiomyocyte stiffness and senescence in underlying tissues by signaling through activin type II receptor signal transduction. Such signaling regulates pulmonary venular responses to mechanical stretch, and circulating activin A is elevated in patients with HFpEF who have enlarged LA chambers, pulmonary venous hypertension and increased pulmonary vascular resistance. The adipokine hypothesis of HFpEF identified activin A and activin type II receptor signaling as key adipokine mediators in the pathogenesis of HFpEF. Experimentally, activin A signaling promotes the development of both atrial myopathy and HFpEF, and activin type II receptor ligand traps alleviate HFpEF and ameliorate both the pulmonary vascular and left heart abnormalities in experimental models in which CpcPH-HFpEF is induced by obesity. These collective observations led to the prospective hypothesis that adipokine modulation by sotatercept would mediate benefits on the left heart in patients with CpcPH-HFpEF. These expectations were validated when the CADENCE trial showed that sotatercept decreased both pulmonary artery wedge pressures and left atrial volume index in patients with CpcPH-HFpEF, which are effects that could not explained by a decrease in pulmonary vascular resistance. Activin A released from an expanded epicardial adipose tissue promotes both pulmonary venous and left atrial remodeling and fibrosis in vivo, which (in turn) are effects that can be attenuated by an activin A decoy. The efficacy of sotatercept to slow the progression of CpcPH-HFpEF is now being tested in a phase III outcomes trial.

title: Self-reported geriatric impairments and treatment toxicity in older patients with multiple myeloma.
abstract: Frailty influences treatment outcomes in older patients with multiple myeloma (MM), yet existing frailty tools capture limited geriatric domains and are incompletely studied in the context of contemporary therapies. We prospectively evaluated patient-reported comprehensive geriatric assessment (CGA) domains and their associations with treatment toxicity and patient-reported outcomes (PRO) in older adults with MM. Patients aged ≥60 years with newly diagnosed or relapsed/refractory MM initiating a new therapy completed electronic CGA and PRO questionnaires at baseline and 4 months. Outcomes included clinician- and patient-reported treatment toxicity, treatment adaptations, health care use, and health-related quality of life (HRQOL). A cumulative deficit frailty index (FI) was derived from CGA and HRQOL domains. Among 90 patients (mean age, 72 years), geriatric impairments were common, particularly physical function domains. High-grade nonhematologic toxicities were significantly associated with older age, comorbidities, patient-reported functional limitations, and anxiety. Toxicity rates on the PRO version of the Common Terminology Criteria for Adverse Events (CTCAE) were higher than on CTCAE, highlighting a discordance between physician- and patient-reported treatment toxicity. Frailty was present in 22% and associated with worse baseline HRQOL and increased high-grade nonhematologic toxicity but not treatment adaptations or health care use. Average CGA and HRQOL scores remained stable over 4 months, although individual trajectories varied. Patient-reported geriatric impairments are prevalent in older adults with MM and strongly associated with nonhematologic toxicities even in the contemporary treatment era. Physician-reported CTCAE may not fully reflect patients' symptom burden. Heterogeneity in individual geriatric trajectories during treatment emphasize the need for longitudinal assessment. title: Optimizing cefiderocol use in clinical practice.
abstract: Cefiderocol is the first clinically available antibiotic to exploit bacterial iron transport systems to enter gram-negative pathogens. As its availability expands, questions remain regarding: its role relative to other agents for infections caused by NDM-producing Enterobacterales, difficult-to-treat resistant (DTR) Pseudomonas aeruginosa , carbapenem-resistant Acinetobacter baumannii complex (CRAB), Stenotrophomonas maltophilia , and rarer nonfermenters; performance and interpretation of antimicrobial susceptibility testing; dosing in special populations; and emergence of resistance. This review addresses these uncertainties, emphasizing practical guidance for clinicians.Emerging preclinical and clinical data have better defined cefiderocol's role in antimicrobial resistant (AMR) infections, supporting its preferential use for NDM-producing Enterobacterales and S. maltophilia , while reserving it for DTR P. aeruginosa and CRAB when preferred alternatives are unavailable or unsuitable. Susceptibility testing remains complex: breakpoints differ across standards organizations, broth microdilution requires specialized iron-depleted media, and disk diffusion is practical but may overcall resistance. Cefiderocol resistance is typically driven by a convergence of mechanisms, including impaired siderophore uptake, increased β-lactamase production or modification, reduced permeability, or PBP3 alterations.With its unique structure and broad activity against resistant gram-negative pathogens, cefiderocol represents an important and evolving addition to the AMR therapeutic landscape.Copyright © 2026 The Author(s). This review examined how doctors should best use cefiderocol for various resistant bacterial infections, finding it works particularly well against certain gram-negative bacteria like those producing NDM enzymes and Stenotrophomonas maltophilia. title: Identification and characterization of a novel distinct Pineal Neoplasm with Neuroendocrine and Epithelial Differentiation (PINNED).
abstract: Pineal region tumors are rare neoplasms that occur in all ages and account for less than 1% of all central nervous system (CNS) tumors in adults but are more frequent in children. Here, we describe a previously unrecognized tumor type of pineal origin characterized by a unique and consistent DNA methylation profile that does not match any known CNS tumor class and is distinct from all currently recognized pineal tumor entities. The presented cohort (n = 27) displayed a balanced sex distribution with a mean patient age of 35 years (range 7-75 years). The histopathological analyses demonstrated a highly cellular tumor showing various degrees of necrosis, mitotic activity, papillary structures, rosettes, epithelioid cytology, or signet-ring cells. The tumors consistently expressed cytokeratin 18, synaptophysin, chromogranin A, and OTX2, whereas CRX expression was absent. Four out of 16 tumors (25%) showed ATRX mutations and/or loss of protein expression as revealed by immunohistochemistry. Single-nucleus RNA sequencing confirmed molecular distinctiveness from other pineal neoplasms but revealed the closest similarities to papillary tumors of the pineal region (PTPR). Projection of the transcriptome data onto the cellular trajectory of the developing murine pineal gland suggests that pinealocyte progenitors are the cellular origins. Taken together, our findings define a novel type of pineal region tumor that we provisionally named 'Pineal Neoplasm with Neuroendocrine and Epithelial Differentiation' (PINNED). Recognition of this tumor type appears to be important for the accurate diagnosis of pineal region tumors and may have implications for future tumor classification and treatment strategies.© 2026. llm_summary: Researchers identified and characterized a previously unknown type of brain tumor that originates in the pineal gland, a small organ deep in the brain, by studying 27 patients with an average age of 35 years. The tumors showed a distinctive genetic signature and cellular features that set them apart from all other known pineal tumors, with origins likely traced to immature pineal cells. This discovery of the new tumor type, called PINNED, may improve how doctors diagnose pineal region tumors and could influence future treatment approaches.
llm_summary_expert: Researchers characterized a novel pineal region tumor type in 27 patients (mean age 35 years) using histopathological analysis, immunohistochemistry, and single-nucleus RNA sequencing. The tumors displayed consistent DNA methylation profiles distinct from known CNS tumor classes and expressed cytokeratin 18, synaptophysin, chromogranin A, and OTX2, while ATRX mutations occurred in 25% of cases. Transcriptomic analysis revealed closest molecular similarity to papillary tumors of the pineal region but suggested pinealocyte progenitors as the cellular origin.

title: The Surgical Anatomy of the Lymphatic System of the Stomach.
abstract: The gastric lymphatic system is essential for immune function and the metastasis of gastric cancer. However, variations in lymphatic anatomy, drainage patterns, and staging frameworks complicate surgical planning and oncologic decision-making. This study aims to review the anatomy of the gastric lymphatic system, the history and variation of JCGC and UICC/AJCC TNM gastric lymphatic staging classifications, while also exploring the differences between lymphadenectomy strategies. A PRISMA-guided search across PubMed, PMC, ScienceDirect, Elsevier Science, Wiley, and SpringerLink retrieved eligible studies meeting pre-determined inclusion criteria. Of the 79 entries returned, 40 eligible studies were identified after application of our inclusion and exclusion criteria. The JCGC and UICC/AJCC TNM systems differ in their staging methods. While the JCGC categorizes lymph nodes by their location relative to the tumor, the UICC/AJCC categorizes the N stage by the number of positive lymph nodes detected. Though the UICC/AJCC staging system is dominant in multiple countries, efforts have been made in recent years to align the protocols in both staging systems. As a result, D2 lymphadenectomy is widely practiced in JCGC adhering countries, whereas UICC/AJCC protocols favor selective dissection combined with neoadjuvant chemotherapy. The complexity of gastric lymphatic anatomy and the absence of a globally standardized staging classification can lead to heterogeneous lymphadenectomy strategies and inconsistent oncologic outcomes. This review emphasizes the need for a unified classification system that incorporates anatomical, oncologic, and imaging perspectives to improve staging and optimize surgical decision-making.© 2026 American Association of Clinical Anatomists and British Association of Clinical Anatomists.

title: Microsporidiosis After Solid Organ Transplantation: A Multi-Species Case Series.
abstract: Microsporidiosis is an uncommon opportunistic infection in solid organ transplant (SOT) recipients. Case-level data on multi-species disease and management remain limited.We retrospectively reviewed SOT recipients with microsporidiosis at Mayo Clinic from January 2000 through February 2026. Cases were identified by text search and institutional polymerase chain reaction (PCR) records. Clinical, microbiologic, treatment, immunosuppression, and outcome data were abstracted.Ten recipients were identified: six kidney, two kidney-pancreas, and two heart recipients. Eight had enteritis and two had disseminated disease. Enterocytozoon bieneusi caused seven infections; the remaining cases were Encephalitozoon sp. enteritis, disseminated E. cuniculi, and disseminated Anncaliia algerae. All enteritis cases experienced diarrhea; seven experienced weight loss, five developed acute kidney injury, and five required hospitalization. The most common treatment administered was nitazoxanide (n = 6). Among these three achieved clinical remission, one improved without documented remission, and two had transient or partial improvement followed by recurrent diarrhea. Among four patients whose antimetabolite was held, reduced, or replaced at or before treatment, all improved clinically. In the two initially treated without antimetabolite modification, responses were transient or incomplete. Both Encephalitozoon infections achieved clinical remission with albendazole. Disseminated A. algerae was fatal.Microsporidiosis after SOT demonstrated a species-associated clinical spectrum: E. bieneusi was confined to enteritis, whereas non-E. bieneusi species caused both enteric and disseminated disease. In E. bieneusi enteritis, nitazoxanide improved symptoms, but responses were incomplete when antimetabolite therapy was continued. Encephalitozoon infections responded to albendazole, whereas disseminated A. algerae was refractory and fatal.© 2026 Wiley Periodicals LLC.

title: Is There a Cervical Alignment Threshold Warranting Cervical Inclusion in the Construct?
abstract: Postoperative thoracolumbar (TL) realignment in patients with adult spinal deformity (ASD) may induce cervical spine (CS) decompensation. This study identifies predictors of CS decompensation after TL surgery and defines a baseline CS-alignment threshold based on C2-pelvic angle (C2-PA) for CS inclusion in the TL construct.Patients with ASD undergoing TL fusion to the sacrum with an upper instrumented vertebrae at T2 or below and available baseline radiographs and patient-reported outcome measures (PROMs) were included. CS decompensation was defined as CS surgery or >2 SD above the mean in C2-PA, cervical sagittal vertical axis (cSVA), or T1-slope cervical lordosis (TS-CL) at the studied postoperative time point.One thousand one hundred ninety patients were included; 166 (13.9%) had CS decompensation after TL surgery, including 24 (2.0%) requiring CS extension. CS decompensation was identified in 81 patients (6.8%) at 6 weeks (4 (0.3%) extensions), 13 (1.2%) at 6 months (2 (0.2%)), 43 (3.9%) at 1 year (7 (0.6%)), and 29 (2.8%) at 2 years (11 (0.9%)). Patients with CS decompensation at 6 months showed worse global and CS alignment at 6 weeks (lumbar lordosis: 53.6 vs 46.3; cSVA: 30.5 vs 38.5; P < .05). CS decompensation at 1 year was associated with worse PROMs (physical component score: 39.0 vs 35.4; Scoliosis research society score: 3.6 vs 3.3; P < .05). CS decompensation at 2 years was associated with worse CS alignment at 1 year (TS-CL: 20.8 vs 28.6; cSVA: 31.1 vs 37.8) and worse PROMs at 2 years. Higher baseline C2-PA was associated with shorter time to CS decompensation. Cox modeling identified baseline C2-PA (hazard ratio [HR] 1.05, 95% CI, 1.03-1.06), TS-CL (HR 1.05, 95% CI, 1.03-1.06), surgical invasiveness (HR 0.99, 95% CI, 0.98-0.99), and upper thoracic instrumentation (HR 2.9, 95% CI, 1.8-4.7) as predictors of CS decompensation, with a C2-PA threshold of 26.2°.Two years after TL ASD surgery, 13.9% had CS decompensation, with 14% requiring CS extension. Baseline CS alignment independently predicted CS decompensation. Patients with preoperative C2-PA >26.2° may benefit from CS inclusion in the TL construct after external validation of this threshold by future research.Copyright © Congress of Neurological Surgeons 2026. About 14% of patients showed upper neck spine problems within two years after lower spine surgery, and those with a specific baseline measurement above 26.2 degrees appeared at higher risk. The findings suggest that patients meeting this threshold might benefit from including their neck spine in the initial surgery, though further research is needed to confirm this recommendation.

title: Diastolic Function From Artificial Intelligence-Derived Electrocardiography in Mitral Annulus Calcification.
abstract: To evaluate whether a validated artificial intelligence-enabled electrocardiography (AI-ECG) model for left ventricular diastolic function (LVDF) can provide prognostic risk stratification in patients with significant mitral annulus calcification (MAC).We included patients who underwent transthoracic echocardiography and electrocardiography within 1 week between September 1, 2001, and April 30, 2023, and were not included in the AI-ECG LVDF training data set. Significant MAC was defined by consensus echocardiography criteria. Patients were assigned to 3 myocardial disease (MD) categories by the AI-ECG LVDF algorithm grading: normal/grade 1 LVDF (MD-1), grade 2 LVDF (MD-2), and grade 3 LVDF (MD-3). The analysis focused on prognostic stratification in this clinically distinct population. The primary end point was all-cause mortality.Of 2506 patients with significant MAC (mean age, 77 years; 64.1% female), 709 (28.3%) were classified as MD-1, 1510 (60.3%) as MD-2, and 287 (11.5%) as MD-3. Advanced MD grade correlated with older age, male sex, lower left ventricular ejection fraction, higher rates of comorbidities, and worse LVDF echocardiographic parameters. During a median follow-up of 2.8 years, 1059 (42.3%) patients died. Multivariable survival analysis found MD-2 (adjusted hazard ratio, 1.40; 95% CI, 1.19 to 1.64) and MD-3 (adjusted hazard ratio, 1.52; 95% CI, 1.21 to 1.92) to be independently associated with higher mortality risk, also after adjustment for mitral inflow diastolic pressure gradients.Myocardial disease grading derived from AI-ECG LVDF is independently associated with increased mortality risk in patients with significant MAC, underscoring its potential value in identifying high-risk patients in this challenging clinical population.Copyright © 2026 Mayo Foundation for Medical Education and Research. title: HER2 protein expression patterns in gallbladder adenocarcinoma and extrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma.
abstract: Gallbladder adenocarcinoma (GBCa) and extrahepatic bile duct cholangiocarcinoma (ECCa) are aggressive malignancies. For unresectable, locally advanced, or metastatic disease, systemic therapy is the only treatment option. Survival rates remain dismal, thus a better understanding of their molecular biology and study of potential targeted therapies are important unmet needs. The tissue agnostic approval of HER2-targeted therapy for medications such as trastuzumab-deruxtecan (T-DXd) for tumors with strong (3+) HER2 expression by immunohistochemistry has motivated interest in HER2 expression among these tumor types. We sought to study the frequency and clinicopathologic features of HER2 expression in GBCa and ECCa. A 14-year retrospective analysis was performed on GBCa and ECCa, including metastatic cases. HER2 immunohistochemistry (Ventana, clone 4B5) was performed on eligible cases and interpreted using the CAP/ASCO gastroesophageal adenocarcinoma scoring guidelines. Clinicopathologic features were assessed with respect to HER2 immunoreactivity, and HER2 scoring agreement was calculated using weighted kappa statistics. There were 59 total cases (GBCa n = 43, ECCa n = 16), with five cases demonstrating strong (3+) HER2 reactivity (8.5%), 22 cases showing 1 + or 2 + immunoreactivity (37.3%), and 32 with a score of 0 (54.2%). HER2 score was higher in metastases compared to corresponding primaries in 7/18 events (38.9%). Among factors considered, histologic grade differed most significantly by HER2 score, with negative cases more likely to be poorly differentiated (p = 0.006). HER2 status was not significantly associated with clinical outcomes (3-year PFS, all-cause mortality). The study describes the frequency and clinicopathologic correlates of HER2 expression in gallbladder adenocarcinoma and extrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma.© 2026. They found that only about 8.5 percent of the 59 cases showed high levels of HER2 that could qualify for targeted therapy, while more than half showed no HER2 at all. title: Efzofitimod versus placebo in patients with pulmonary sarcoidosis (EFZO-FIT): a multicentre, randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled, phase 3 trial.
abstract: Oral corticosteroids are currently standard-of-care therapy for pulmonary sarcoidosis, but they are associated with substantial toxicity and reduced health-related quality of life (HRQoL). The EFZO-FIT trial aimed to assess the efficacy and safety of efzofitimod, a novel immunomodulatory fusion protein targeting the neuropilin 2 receptor, as a steroid-sparing agent in pulmonary sarcoidosis.In this multicentre, randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled, phase 3 trial, adults aged 18-75 years with pulmonary sarcoidosis requiring treatment were enrolled at 85 study centres across nine countries (Brazil, France, Germany, Italy, Japan, Netherlands, Spain, UK, and USA). Participants were randomly assigned 1:1:1 using stratified block randomisation to receive monthly intravenous infusions of efzofitimod 3 mg/kg, efzofitimod 5 mg/kg, or placebo over a 48-week treatment period, including a 12-week oral corticosteroid taper targeting 0 mg per day (starting on day 15). Oral corticosteroid dose could be adjusted upwards in the event of worsening sarcoidosis. The primary endpoint was change from baseline in mean daily oral corticosteroid dose at week 48. Outcome and safety analyses were done in participants who received at least one dose of the study drug and had at least one post-baseline efficacy assessment. This study was registered with ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT05415137) and is complete.Between Sept 22, 2022, and Aug 14, 2025, 331 patients were screened for inclusion. 63 were excluded and 268 participants were randomly assigned to receive placebo (n=91), efzofitimod 3 mg/kg (n=89), or efzofitimod 5 mg/kg (n=88). Four patients were excluded after random assignment (one in the placebo group and three in the efzofitimod 3 mg/kg group). 264 patients who received at least one dose of study treatment and had at least one post-baseline assessment were included in the outcome analysis and safety population (90 in the placebo group, 86 in the efzofitimod 3 mg/kg group, and 88 in the efzofitimod 5 mg/kg group). Among the 264 participants, the mean age was 53·8 years (SD 10·6); 114 (43%) of 264 patients were female and 150 (57%) were male. 168 (64%) identified as White. Mean steroid dose was 10·7 mg per day (SD 4·4) at baseline and 2·9 mg per day (4·5) at week 48. No difference was seen in the magnitude of oral corticosteroid taper between the active and placebo dose groups; the placebo-adjusted change from baseline was 0·02 mg per day in the efzofitimod 3 mg/kg group (95% CI -1·49 to 1·52, p=0·98) and -0·73 mg per day in the efzofitimod 5 mg/kg group (-2·21 to 0·75, p=0·33). The percentage of participants with serious treatment-emergent adverse events was similar between groups. Malaise was more common in the placebo group (five [6%] of 90 patients vs zero in both efzofitimod groups). TEAEs that were more common in the efzofitimod groups included headache (17 [19%] of 88 patients in the efzofitimod 5 mg/kg group, 11 [13%] of 86 patients in the efzofitimod 3 mg/kg group, and four [4%] of 90 patients in the placebo group), sinusitis (nine [10%], six [7%], and two [2%] patients, respectively), wheezing (seven [8%], two [2%], and zero patients, respectively), and aspartate aminotransferase (AST) increased (five [6%], one [1%], and zero patients, respectively). Most adverse events were grade 1 or 2. Two participants died, both in the efzofitimod 3 mg/kg group (one respiratory failure and one incarceration of a pre-existing inguinal hernia). Neither event was considered to be causally related to the treatment.Efzofitimod was well tolerated but did not result in lower steroid doses at week 48 compared with placebo. title: Strategies for Managing Obesity and Cardiometabolic Risk in Young Children: Current Evidence and Future Directions.
abstract: Early-onset obesity is associated with adverse cardiometabolic risk factors and early vascular changes linked to atherosclerosis, yet evidence-based treatment options for young children remain limited. The purpose of the review is to examine current evidence for lifestyle, pharmacologic, and surgical interventions for obesity management in preadolescent children, with emphasis on cardiometabolic and atherosclerotic risk.Lifestyle and familybased behavioral interventions remain first line therapy but often produce modest and variable weight reduction. Pharmacologic options for children younger than 12 years are limited, emerging data suggest selected agents, including topiramate, lisdexamfetamine, glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists and metformin can improve weight status and cardiometabolic risk factors in carefully selected patients. Bariatric surgery provides durable weight loss and cardiometabolic benefit and adolescents with severe obesity, though data and younger children are sparse. Available interventions may improve cardiometabolic risk profiles when appropriately applied early in life, but high-quality long-term data and preadolescent children are needed.© 2026. title: Impactful Research in Microtia and Auricular Reconstruction: A Bibliometric Analysis.
abstract: Microtia is a complex congenital auricular deformity, with research spanning operative technique, epidemiology/genetics, biomaterials, and complications. Despite this breadth, there is limited work characterizing which studies have been most influential in shaping the field. This study aimed to identify and analyze the top 100 most-cited articles on microtia using a bibliometric approach.A comprehensive search using the Web of Science (WoS) was conducted to identify studies on microtia, and the top 100 articles were selected by citation count. Bibliometric data, study type (clinical, review, and basic science), clinical focus category, materials discussed, and sample sizes for clinical studies were extracted. Spearman correlation tests and Kruskal-Wallis tests were used to analyze citation patterns.The top 100 microtia studies, published between 1957 and 2022, accumulated 12,692 total citations, with a mean of 127±84 citations per article, and were published across 49 journals. Clinical studies predominated (n=58), followed by reviews (n=28) and basic science studies (n=14). Publication year significantly differed by article type (P=0.02), with basic science studies tending to be more recent. Newer publication year was associated with higher citations per year (P<0.001) but fewer total citations overall (P=0.002). Among clinical studies, technique-focused papers were most common (n=27) and were largely centered on autologous costal cartilage reconstruction (n=25). Clinical studies examining alternative materials were less represented but tended to be more recent publications.These findings suggest that the most-cited microtia literature has primarily included landmark clinical technique papers, but newer, rapidly cited work increasingly reflects emerging biomaterials and tissue engineering.Copyright © 2026 Wolters Kluwer Health, LLC. title: Bone Marrow Cell Depletion in Myelofibrosis Is Associated With High-Risk Features and Shortened Survival: A Bone Marrow Pathology Group Study.
abstract: Fibrosis is a key histologic finding in the bone marrow (BM) of patients with advanced BCR::ABL1-negative myeloproliferative neoplasms (MPN). Fibrotic MPN can be associated with variable BM cellularity ranging from hypercellular to severe cell depletion. The significance of BM cellularity in the assessment of patients with advanced stage myelofibrosis (MF) is largely unknown. The current study compares cell-depleted MF patients with cellular MF controls in terms of morphologic, genetic, laboratory, and clinical features, including patient outcome. BMs that fulfilled the diagnostic criteria for advanced fibrotic phase MF (with MF-3 or osteosclerosis) including cases of primary myelofibrosis, post-polycythemia myelofibrosis and post-essential thrombocythemia myelofibrosis were collected from eleven participating institutions. BM hematopoietic cellularity was defined as depleted if cellularity was <30% in patients <70 and <20% for those >70 years old, and cellular if normocellular or hypercellular for age. Only cases with an adequate BM core biopsy and available clinical information including long-term follow-up were included. Data from 141 patients with cell-depleted MF and 100 patients with cellular MF were available. Thirty-three (26%) patients had depleted MF at diagnosis. Cell-depleted MF group had significantly lower hemoglobin and platelet counts, and higher peripheral blasts and basophils compared to cellular MF, although it was not independently prognostic. Patients had an increased prevalence of osteosclerosis (p<0.001). Depleted MF cases were enriched in ASXL1 (p=0.007), U2AF1 (p=0.01), EZH2 (p=0.026) and MPL (p=0.029) mutations. Finally, patients with depleted MF had significantly shorter overall survival (p=0.001). Cell-depletion in MF-3 patients is strongly associated with high-risk hematological and molecular features. These patients exhibit a distinct molecular signature compared to the cellular MF group, suggesting both underlying biological differences and features of more advanced disease. Thus, morphologic evaluation of bone marrow cellularity, fibrosis and osteosclerosis in MF patients may lead to a more accurate assessment of the disease status and guide clinical management.Copyright © 2026. title: Advances in the management of renal cell carcinoma.
abstract: Renal cell carcinoma (RCC) is the most common form of kidney cancer, with 435 000 patients newly diagnosed worldwide each year. In addition to morphology and histology, molecular subtyping has advanced the diagnostic classification of RCC. Contemporary diagnosis relies on cross sectional imaging in the form of computed tomography or magnetic resonance imaging and selective biopsy. For localised disease, nephrectomy remains the standard of care, with partial nephrectomy being an option for smaller tumours. Ablation or stereotactic radiation is appropriate for selected patients. Adjuvant pembrolizumab provides improved disease-free and overall survival in high risk clear cell RCC. In metastatic disease, the introduction of immune checkpoint inhibitor based combinations has extended overall survival, providing a durable response in some patients. Despite these advances, primary and secondary resistance, along with the lack of predictive and prognostic biomarkers, remain a challenge.Published by the BMJ Publishing Group Limited. title: Management of Patients with High-risk Localised, Locally Advanced, and Biochemically Recurrent Prostate Cancer: Report from the 2026 Advanced Prostate Cancer Consensus Conference.
abstract: Innovations have improved outcomes in high-risk localised, locally advanced, and biochemically recurrent prostate cancer (PC), yet high-level evidence remains limited for many management decisions. The 2026 Advanced Prostate Cancer Consensus Conference (APCCC) surveyed an international panel on key clinical questions to complement evidence-based guidelines.Here we present the voting results for the questions on high-risk localised, locally advanced, and biochemically recurrent PC from APCCC 2026.Before the conference, a multidisciplinary panel of 144 international PC experts used a modified Delphi process to develop 313 multiple-choice consensus questions, of which 134 covered high-risk localised and locally advanced PC, including prostate-specific antigen (PSA) persistence and PSA recurrence, and side effects of treatment. These questions were administered to the 133 voting panel members "panellists" via a web-based survey prior to the conference.Consensus was defined a priori as ≥75% agreement, with strong consensus defined as ≥90% agreement. Overall, consensus was reached for 44 of the 134 questions (32.8%), with seven questions reaching a strong consensus. Results and limitations The voting results show varying degrees of consensus, as discussed in this article and as detailed in the Supplementary Material. An interactive heat map for the questions can be found at https://apccc.org/APCCC2026-votings-localised-and-locally-advanced-prostate-cancer/. These findings do not include a formal literature review or meta-analysis.The voting results can help physicians and patients navigate controversial areas of clinical management for which evidence is scant or conflicting. The findings can also help funders and policymakers in prioritising areas for future research. Importantly, APCCC 2026 once again identified important gaps (areas of no consensus) that merit evaluation in specifically designed trials.Copyright © 2026 The Author(s). Published by Elsevier B.V. llm_summary: An international panel of 144 prostate cancer experts voted on 134 clinical questions about treating high-risk and advanced prostate cancer, reaching agreement on only 44 questions, which highlights significant gaps in medical evidence for managing this disease. The voting results show that many important treatment decisions lack strong scientific consensus, meaning doctors and patients often face controversial choices with limited guidance. These findings can help identify which areas need more research to improve how doctors treat prostate cancer patients.
llm_summary_expert: The 2026 Advanced Prostate Cancer Consensus Conference surveyed 133 international experts using a modified Delphi process to develop 313 consensus questions addressing management of high-risk localised, locally advanced, and biochemically recurrent prostate cancer. Of 134 questions covering these disease states, consensus (≥75% agreement) was achieved for 44 questions (32.8%), with seven reaching strong consensus (≥90% agreement). The voting results identified substantial areas of clinical disagreement where evidence remains limited or conflicting.

title: Assessing Resident Perceptions and Needs: Global Orthopaedic Opportunities in North American Residency Programs.
abstract: Global orthopaedics includes collaborative efforts to improve clinical care, education, research, and capacity across international settings, with an emphasis on equitable, bidirectional, and sustainable partnerships. Interest in global orthopaedics among North American residents continues to grow, yet structured opportunities for clinical, educational, and research engagement in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs) remain limited. This study evaluated the availability of global orthopaedic opportunities within residency programs and assessed resident experiences, perceptions, and interest in expanding these initiatives.A cross-sectional survey was distributed to orthopaedic surgery residents in the United States and Canada through the Consortium of Orthopaedic Academic Traumatologists (COACT)-affiliated faculty and resident leads. Residents from postgraduate years 1 to 5 were eligible. Survey domains included prior global health experience, opportunities available at home institutions, resident satisfaction with existing resources, and interest in future global orthopaedic engagement. Descriptive statistics were performed.Thirty of 35 residency programs (85.7%) participated, with 299 of 300 residents completing the survey (99.7%). Forty-six respondents (15.4%) reported prior or current participation in global orthopaedic activities, most commonly through organized teaching or clinical experiences (50.0%), research collaborations (41.3%), and elective international clinical rotations (37.0%). Nearly one third of residents (30.1%) reported that their residency program offered no global orthopaedic opportunities. Residents expressed dissatisfaction with the availability of mentorship, elective international rotations, and global outreach opportunities at their home institutions. Despite limited access, interest in expanding opportunities in LMICs was notable, particularly for mentorship and guidance (73.2%), elective international rotations (72.9%), and collaborative research (54.8%).North American orthopaedic residents demonstrate substantial interest in global orthopaedic engagement that exceeds the opportunities currently available. These findings support expanding structured mentorship, international partnerships, and centralized networks such as COACT to facilitate sustainable global clinical, educational, and research opportunities during residency.Copyright © 2026 The Authors. title: Reassessing alcohol consumption and cardiovascular disease by addressing bias in observational data: results from the multi-ethnic study of atherosclerosis.
abstract: Alcohol and its relationship with cardiovascular disease (CVD) remain contentious. Several observational studies have found cardioprotective associations, while Mendelian randomization studies have found null or harmful effects of moderate drinking. Biases, including abstainer misclassification and sick-quitter effects, may obscure true associations. It is widely understood that former drinkers are often sick quitters. However, removal of former drinkers from analyses addresses bias in the abstainer group but fails to account for induced survivorship among current drinkers. This study sought to determine whether adjusting for biases altered the association between alcohol and CVD by comparing conventional models with those using (i) occasional drinkers as the reference group instead of lifetime abstainers and (ii) 'intention-to-treat' reallocation of former drinkers based on past drinking patterns.The Multi-Ethnic Study of Atherosclerosis is a prospective cohort study of 6814 participants aged 45-84 years between 2000 and 2002 without baseline CVD. A total of 6755 participants were included after excluding those with missing data. Alcohol consumption was self-reported and classified as lifetime abstainer, former, or current drinker [occasional (≤1 drink/week), light (2-7 drinks/week), moderate (8-14 drinks/week), heavy (>14 drinks/week)]. Outcomes included coronary artery calcium (CAC; 0, 1-100, 101-300, and >300) and clinical events [myocardial infarction (MI), stroke, cardiovascular mortality, composite major adverse cardiovascular events (MACEs), and heart failure]. Of 6755 participants, 20.6% were lifetime abstainers, 24.1% former drinkers, and 55.3% current drinkers. Adjusting for biases altered the observed relationship between alcohol and CVD, showing increased harm with light drinking, decreased protection with moderate drinking, and a dose-response relationship between alcohol and CAC, particularly CAC >300 in adjusted models. Protective associations between moderate drinking and MI [hazard ratio (HR): 0.64, 95% confidence interval (CI): 0.38-1.06] and cardiovascular mortality (HR: 0.81, 95% CI: 0.53-1.25) were attenuated and became non-significant. Light drinking shifted from null to increased risk for MI (HR: 1.46, 95% CI: 1.11-1.92), stroke (HR: 1.54, 95% CI: 1.17-2.03), MACE (HR: 1.33, 95% CI: 1.12-1.57), and heart failure (HR: 1.42, 95% CI: 1.10-1.84).Associations between alcohol and CVD in observational studies are sensitive to methodologic variation. Results from models correcting for abstainer/sick-quitter biases may help explain discrepant results from previous studies.© The Author(s) 2026. title: Revascularization in Asymptomatic Carotid Artery Stenosis With Hemodynamic Impairment and Cognitive Outcomes: The CREST-H Substudy of the CREST-2 Randomized Clinical Trial.
abstract: Cerebral hemodynamic impairment in patients with asymptomatic internal carotid artery (ICA) stenosis is associated with reduced cognition. It is uncertain whether revascularization might be an effective treatment for cognitive impairment in these patients.To test whether any cognitive benefit from revascularization of high-grade, asymptomatic ICA stenosis varies based on the degree of baseline cerebral hemodynamic impairment.This substudy was conducted within a multicenter phase 3 randomized clinical trial. Adults (aged 35-86 years) without dementia with eighth-grade education or higher and unilateral asymptomatic ICA stenosis greater than or equal to 70% were enrolled from January 2018 to July 2024 at 61 sites in North America (last follow-up in July 2025). Of 607 participants screened from 2485 in CREST-2, 392 were enrolled. Magnetic resonance or computed tomographic perfusion imaging tested for baseline hemodynamic impairment defined by delayed time-to-peak (TTP) arrival of intravenous contrast in the hemisphere ipsilateral minus contralateral to the stenotic artery.Carotid revascularization (endarterectomy or stenting) plus intensive medical management (IMM) vs IMM alone.The primary outcome was the difference in composite cognitive z score over 1 year based on 5 cognitive tests. The primary analysis tested for an interaction between treatment group (revascularization vs IMM alone) and degree of baseline hemodynamic impairment among those with reduced baseline cognition (cognitive z score ≤-1.0 SD).Of 392 participants enrolled (mean age, 71 years; 125 [32%] females), 61 were excluded for missing baseline imaging and 40 for missing cognitive examinations or other covariates, leaving 291 with complete data. Fifty-one had reduced cognition at baseline (25 in the revascularization group and 26 in the IMM alone group). TTP ranged from no interhemispheric TTP delay to a more-than-2-second delay. Mean (SD) cognitive z scores were -1.36 (0.51) at baseline and -1.17 (0.47) at 1 year in the revascularization group and -1.34 (0.83) at baseline and -1.01 (0.97) at 1 year in the IMM alone group. The primary analysis showed no difference in cognition by treatment group over 1 year, adjusting for treatment group × hemodynamic status interaction and other covariates (adjusted difference in cognitive z score, -0.15 SD [95% CI, -0.54 to 0.24]). The interaction was not significant (β estimate = 0.018 [95% CI, -0.025 to 0.061]; P = .40).In this substudy of a randomized clinical trial, there was no differential effect of revascularization vs IMM alone on cognition over 1 year by cerebral hemodynamic status among those with baseline reduced cognition, suggesting that revascularization does not improve cognitive dysfunction by restoring flow to the brain in chronic asymptomatic carotid stenosis.ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT03121209.

title: Investigational drug services operations: Defining core and supplemental workload metrics.
abstract: Investigational drug services (IDS) support highly complex and regulated aspects of clinical research, yet the absence of defined workload metrics limits clear and consistent understanding of IDS workload across pharmacy, research, and executive leadership. Staffing and resource requests, as well as being responsible for acceptance of new studies, require defensible, numerical workload data to secure leadership approval for additional resources. We developed a structured approach to IDS workload measurement that includes broadly applicable core metrics and site-specific supplemental metrics to support staffing justification, resource allocation, and operational planning.A modified Delphi process informed by literature-identified metrics was used to achieve expert consensus on IDS workload definitions and metrics. Subject matter experts in IDS pharmacy practice and clinical research operations participated in iterative rounds of review. Metrics were categorized into core workload elements and supplemental metrics. Core metrics broadly describe site characteristics and day-to-day operations. Supplemental metrics capture study-specific, expanded services or site-derived time-based measures.Organizing IDS workload into core and supplemental components provides a structured method to account for both routine operations and expanded study- or site- driven demands using consistent and meaningful terminology, creating a foundation for capturing and describing IDS workload data.© The Author(s) 2026. llm_summary: Researchers developed a structured system to measure the workload of investigational drug services, which support complex clinical research operations in pharmacies. Using expert input through multiple rounds of review, they created core metrics that describe routine operations and supplemental metrics for study-specific demands, providing a consistent framework for tracking workload. This organized approach enables pharmacy leaders to justify staffing needs and allocate resources more effectively based on defensible numerical data.
llm_summary_expert: Investigational drug services (IDS) operations lack standardized workload metrics, which impedes clear communication of workload demands across pharmacy, research, and executive leadership and complicates justification for staffing and resource allocation decisions. Researchers used a modified Delphi process informed by literature review to achieve expert consensus among subject matter experts in IDS pharmacy practice and clinical research operations regarding workload definitions and metrics through iterative review rounds. The resulting framework organizes IDS workload into core metrics that broadly describe site characteristics and routine day-to-day operations and supplemental metrics that capture study-specific expanded services or site-derived time-based measures. title: Uveal melanoma: innovations in therapy, prognosis, and imaging.
abstract: Uveal melanoma (UM) is the most common adult primary intraocular malignancy with local tumor control exceeding 95%, while ~50% of patients still develop metastasis. Advances in diagnostic tools, therapeutics, and prognostication guide individualized care and support a shift toward precision medicine.This narrative review covers advances in imaging, therapy, and prognosis. Literature was identified through searches of PubMed, Embase, Google Scholar, and ClinicalTrials.gov through August 2026, supplemented by reference lists and clinical practice guidelines. Topics include imaging advances in optical coherence tomography (OCT), ultrasonography, and lesion classification using artificial intelligence (AI); globe-preserving local therapies, systemic T-cell-based therapies, targeted therapies, checkpoint inhibitors, and liver-directed approaches; and prognostic tools based on gene expression profiling, preferentially expressed antigen in melanoma (PRAME), cytogenetics, and circulating tumor DNA.The clinical approach to UM is evolving rapidly, with more clinical trials than ever. Advances aim to improve early detection and preserve vision while controlling the primary tumor, and the first US Food and Drug Administration-approved therapies offer incremental improvements in survival for patients with metastatic disease. Imaging-based AI may support earlier detection, while collaboration between clinicians and laboratory scientists remains essential to improving survival.

title: Multicenter evaluation of the multiplex polymerase chain reaction QIAstat-Dx Meningitis/Encephalitis Panel for the detection of central nervous system pathogens directly in the cerebrospinal fluid.
abstract: Rapid and accurate detection of pathogens causing meningitis/encephalitis (MEN/EN) is critical to improving clinical outcomes. Multiplex polymerase chain reaction (PCR) enables simultaneous detection of multiple pathogens from the cerebrospinal fluid (CSF), offering advantages over traditional methods. This multicenter study evaluated the performance of the QIAstat-Dx Meningitis/Encephalitis (ME) Panel versus conventional methods, including the BioFire FilmArray ME (BFME) Panel. The CSF samples from patients with suspected MEN/EN along with contrived samples were tested across 13 sites in Europe/USA. Positive percent agreement (PPA) and negative percent agreement (NPA) between the QIAstat-Dx ME Panel and comparator methods were determined. A total of 1,667 clinical samples (1,527 prospective, 140 archived) were tested. Pathogens were detected by the QIAstat-Dx ME Panel in 115 (7.5%) prospective samples, including Streptococcus pneumoniae (1.1%), Haemophilus influenzae (0.5%), Listeria monocytogenes (0.3%), S. agalactiae (0.2%), Escherichia coli K1 (0.1%), Neisseria meningitidis (0.1%), S. pyogenes (0.1%), enterovirus (1.5%), human herpesvirus-6 (1.0%), herpes simplex virus-2 (0.9%) and -1 (0.3%), varicella zoster virus (0.7%), cytomegalovirus (0.3%), human parechovirus (0.3%), and Cryptococcus gattii/neoformans (0.4%). Overall PPA versus BFME (n = 1,664) was 85.4%, increasing to 95.3% after discordance resolution. PPA was 100% for N. meningitidis, S. pneumoniae, and S. agalactiae. Overall NPA was 99.9%. Among 1,154 contrived positive samples, only 27 (2.3%) incorrect results were observed. The QIAstat-Dx ME Panel demonstrated high concordance with BFME, supporting its use as a reliable, fully automated multiplex PCR platform for rapid diagnosis of community-acquired MEN/EN.IMPORTANCEThis multicenter study demonstrated that the QIAstat-Dx ME Panel delivers clinical performance comparable to that of the BioFire FilmArray ME (BFME) Panel, supporting its validity as a reliable syndromic molecular diagnostic tool for MEN/EN. With its broad pathogen coverage, rapid turnaround time (TAT), and the ability to provide amplification curves and Ct values, the QIAstat-Dx ME Panel offers a valuable option for broad and timely detection of bacterial, viral, and fungal CNS pathogens. When used alongside the SoC diagnostic methods, this panel has the potential to improve early diagnosis, guide targeted therapy, and support effective clinical management of patients with suspected MEN/EN.

title: Sex-Based Outcomes After Carotid Artery Revascularization in Symptomatic Patients: A Multi-Center Cohort Study.
abstract: Sex-based differences in outcomes after carotid revascularization remain poorly defined in symptomatic patients. We aimed to compare short and long-term outcomes between men and women with symptomatic carotid artery disease who underwent carotid revascularization across a ten-year period in three stroke centers.A retrospective study was conducted on a consecutive series of cases between 2016 and 2026. Cases included patients presenting with stroke, transient ischemic attack (TIA), or amaurosis fugax attributable to ipsilateral carotid artery stenosis within six months prior carotid endarterectomy (CEA), transcarotid artery revascularization (TCAR), or transfemoral carotid artery stenting (TFCAS). Patients with prior neck radiation were excluded. Primary outcomes were stroke, TIA, myocardial infarction (MI), and death within 30 days. Secondary outcomes included long-term stroke, TIA, MI, death, restenosis, and reintervention. Both primary and secondary outcomes were analyzed individually and as a composite endpoint. To account for sex-based differences and vulnerable plaque feature burden, a 1:1 propensity score-matched (PSM) analysis was performed among patients with available magnetic resonance angiography with vessel wall imaging (MRA-VWI).A total of 822 procedures were performed (men: 571, 69.5%; women: 251, 30.5%) with a mean age of 73.2 ± 9.2 years. Procedure distribution was similar between groups (CEA: 69.4% vs 70.9%; TCAR: 6.1% vs 5.6%; TFCAS: 24.5% vs 23.5%, p=0.89). Demographics and comorbidities were otherwise comparable between groups. Women had higher total cholesterol (185.9 ± 50.1 vs 158.1 ± 43.4 mg/dL, p<0.01), HDL (56.8 ± 18.1 vs 45.9 ± 15.2 mg/dL, p<0.01), and LDL (101.5 ± 45.4 vs 86.3 ± 38.0 mg/dL, p<0.01); however, the LDL/HDL ratio was not significant. Medication regimens were similar between groups, except estrogen use, which was exclusive to women (4.0%, p<0.01). Symptom presentation was comparable for stroke (49.0% vs 48.6%, p=0.91), TIA (32.0% vs 33.5%, p=0.69), and amaurosis fugax (22.1% vs 20.7%, p=0.67). At 30 days, the composite of stroke, TIA, MI, and death was similar (4.2% vs 4.0%, p=0.88), with no statistically significant differences in ipsilateral stroke (2.5% vs 1.6%, p=0.61), TIA (0.7% vs 1.6%, p=0.23), MI (0.5% vs 0.0%, p=0.25), or mortality (0.5% vs 1.2%, p=0.30). On long-term follow-up at 3.3 ± 2.6 years, the composite outcomes remained comparable (24.2% vs 24.3%, p=0.97), as were ipsilateral stroke (3.7% vs 5.2%, p=0.32), TIA (5.1% vs 4.0%, p=0.50), MI (2.6% vs 3.6%, p=0.45), mortality (17.5% vs 19.1%, p=0.58), restenosis (4.9% vs 7.2%, p=0.19), and reintervention rates (2.5% vs 4.8%, p=0.08). In the PSM cohort (men: 91, women: 91, N=182), the 30-day (3.3% vs 2.2%, p=1.00) and long-term (34.1% vs 31.9%, p=0.88) composite outcome of stroke, TIA, MI and death were similar. Restenosis (4.4% vs 7.7%, p=0.54), and reintervention (1.1% vs 6.6%, p=0.12) were also not statistically significantly different between groups.No statistically significant sex-based differences were identified in 30-day or long-term outcomes after CEA, TCAR, or TFCAS across a ten-year period at three high-volume stroke centers. abstract: To assess the perspectives of patients after radical cystectomy (RC) to identify potential targets for future improvement. title: Global, regional, and national burden of unintentional poisoning, 1990-2023: results from the Global Burden of Disease Study 2023.
abstract: Unintentional poisoning is a preventable cause of injury-related morbidity and mortality, yet global patterns, trends, and inequalities remain incompletely characterised. Within the Global Burden of Disease (GBD) framework, unintentional poisoning includes poisoning by carbon monoxide and poisoning by other means, a category largely informed by pesticide poisoning codes plus some indirect capture of other poisoning as part of the GBD re-distribution process. Poisonings by pharmaceuticals and illicit substances are not captured in the GBD definition of poisoning. We aimed to quantify this GBD-defined burden and assess regional variation, sociodemographic gradients, and case fatality between 1990 and 2023.We analysed GBD 2023 estimates for 204 countries and territories, modelling deaths, incidence, and disability-adjusted life-years (DALYs) using standard GBD cause-of-death and non-fatal estimation methods with 95% uncertainty intervals. We stratified results by age, sex, region, and Socio-demographic Index (SDI), and derived case fatality from modelled deaths and incidence.In 2023, unintentional poisoning from carbon monoxide and other means caused 2·54 million incident poisonings, 69 805 deaths, and 3·68 million DALYs globally, with age-standardised DALY rates declining by 47·5% since 1990. Carbon monoxide accounted for 641 932 poisonings, 30 890 deaths and 1·34 million DALYs, with the highest burdens in central and eastern Europe and central Asia. Most regions showed substantial long-term declines, and the global age-standardised DALY rate for carbon monoxide poisoning declined by 58·2% since 1990. Poisoning by other means caused 1·90 million incident cases, 38 914 deaths, and 2·34 million DALYs, with the greatest burden in sub-Saharan Africa. Most regions showed declining age-standardised DALY rates for poisoning by other means; however, there was no clear change (with the 95% uncertainty interval including zero) in the global estimate, driven by wide uncertainty intervals in several regions (including sub-Saharan Africa). Mortality and DALYs were inversely associated with SDI, and derived case fatality was highest in low-SDI regions.Global reductions in GBD-defined unintentional poisoning by carbon monoxide and other means are consistent with decades of regulatory and environmental interventions. These include bans of highly toxic pesticides, improved heating and ventilation systems, emissions controls, and adoption of carbon monoxide alarms. llm_summary: Researchers examined the global burden of unintentional poisoning from carbon monoxide and pesticides between 1990 and 2023, finding that these poisonings caused nearly 70,000 deaths and 3.68 million years of lost health globally in 2023. The burden has declined substantially since 1990, likely reflecting safety regulations and environmental improvements like pesticide bans and carbon monoxide alarms. In 2023, unintentional poisoning caused 2.54 million incident cases, 69,805 deaths, and 3.68 million DALYs globally, with carbon monoxide accounting for 641,932 poisonings and 30,890 deaths predominantly in central and eastern Europe and central Asia, while poisoning by other means caused 1.90 million incident cases and 38,914 deaths with greatest burden in sub-Saharan Africa. Age-standardized DALY rates declined 47.5% globally since 1990, with carbon monoxide poisoning showing a 58.2% decline, though poisoning by other means showed no clear global change due to wide uncertainty intervals in several regions. title: Pazopanib alternating with bevacizumab in patients with metastatic clear-cell renal cell carcinoma naive to treatment: a multicentre, single-arm, phase 1/2 trial.
abstract: VEGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitors (TKIs) are considered the backbone for the treatment of metastatic clear-cell renal cell carcinoma. We hypothesise that the administration of bevacizumab during scheduled breaks in pazopanib (TKI) treatment can improve tolerability and prolong progression-free survival compared with historical controls.In this single-arm, phase 1/2 trial in five US academic cancer centres, patients (aged ≥18 years) with histologically confirmed metastatic clear-cell renal cell carcinoma, Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group performance status of 1 or less, and adequate organ functions were included. The phase 1 portion included patients with up to one previous therapy with high-dose IL-2 or an anti-PD-1 compound alone or in combination with a CTLA-4 inhibitor. The phase 2 portion enrolled only patients with treatment-naive metastatic clear-cell renal cell carcinoma. The primary endpoint of phase 1 was to find the recommended phase 2 dose (RP2D). We tested a novel regimen using four dose levels: oral pazopanib (600 or 800 mg daily on days 1-28, followed by a 7 day break) alternating with intravenous bevacizumab (5, 7·5, or 10 mg/kg, one on day 36 and one on day 50) on a 10-week cycle in patients with metastatic clear-cell renal cell carcinoma naive to TKI treatment. The primary endpoint of phase 2 was median progression-free survival, assessed by a masked central statistician review. Dose selection (in patients who had completed 15 weeks) and activity (in patients who had completed one full 10-week cycle of the novel regimen) were analysed in the per-protocol population. Safety analyses included all patients who received any treatment. This trial was registered with ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT01684397) and is ongoing but closed to new participants.Between Nov 21, 2012, and June 11, 2018, phase 1 enrolled 25 patients, with 18 patients evaluable for dose-limiting toxicity during the extended 15-week safety assessment period. The RP2D was established as pazopanib 800 mg daily (days 1-28) and bevacizumab 10 mg/kg on days 36 and 50 of a 10-week cycle. Between Jan 23, 2019, and Oct 19, 2023, phase 2 enrolled 53 patients, of whom 51 (including six from phase 1) were evaluable for activity and 59 were evaluable for safety. 36 (71%) patients were male and 15 (29%) were female, and 48 (94%) patients were White. 33 (65%) patients in phase 2 had favourable risk per the International Metastatic Renal Cell Carcinoma Database Consortium categories. After a median follow-up of 63·7 months (IQR 16·2-73·5), median progression-free survival was 24·8 months (95% CI 17·2-34·3). The most common grade 3-4 treatment-related adverse events were hypertension (20 [34%] of 59) and elevated aspartate aminotransferase (seven [12%]) and alanine aminotransferase (ten [17%]). Five (8%) patients discontinued the study for drug-related serious adverse events. No treatment-related deaths occurred.The phase 1 portion identified the safe RP2D. The phase 2 portion showed that this novel regimen has promising antitumour activity in patients with metastatic clear-cell renal cell carcinoma in the predominantly favourable risk group who are naive to treatment. title: Characterising the genomic landscape of two clinical risk groups in CD30+ T-cell lymphoproliferative disorders with cutaneous involvement: a multi-institutional retrospective study.
abstract: CD30+ T cell lymphoproliferative disorders (CD30+ T LPD) with cutaneous involvement comprise a diverse group of neoplasms with variable clinical outcomes. The molecular mechanisms underlying the prognostic differences in these diseases are poorly understood.In this multi-institutional retrospective study, 79 patients with CD30+ T LPD were evaluated. DNA and RNA sequencing were performed on skin biopsy samples to characterise molecular features. Patients were assigned to low- and high-risk groups based on treatment recommendations in clinical records. Pathogenic pathways, immune microenvironments, transcriptomic profiles, driver mutations, and mutation signatures were compared between the risk groups.Across risk groups, there was high mutational recurrence in genes involved in epigenetic regulation and intracellular signalling pathways. Mutational signature analysis revealed a shared prevalence of 5-methylcytosine deamination, UV exposure, defective mismatch repair, and POLE-associated proofreading deficiency. In contrast, gene set enrichment analysis showed that the high-risk group was enriched in pathways governing cell cycle progression, DNA damage response, and immune activation compared to the low-risk group. Furthermore, immune microenvironment deconvolution showed a higher abundance of resting dendritic cells in the low-risk group. Finally, high-risk patients exhibited significant overexpression of clinically relevant proteins, highlighting potential alternative treatment approaches for this population.Mutation analyses suggest diverse pathogenesis in these diseases. The high-risk and low-risk groups diverge in gene expression profiles and immune microenvironment, suggesting that these biological differences hold prognostic significance. Molecularly informed therapeutic strategies should be investigated prospectively through clinical trials.This work was supported by developmental funds of the Duke Cancer Institute as part of the P30 Cancer Center Support Grant. title: Optimizing inferior petrosal sinus sampling: results of a multicenter study.
abstract: Inferior petrosal sinus sampling (IPSS) confirms a central source of adrenocorticotropic hormone (ACTH) secretion in Cushing's disease (CD). We explored IPSS protocols to optimize diagnostic sensitivity and reduce laboratory testing burden. Patients from the multicenter Registry of Adenomas of the Pituitary and Related Disorders (RAPID) who underwent IPSS for management of CD, and in whom central:peripheral (C:P) ACTH levels were evaluated, were included. A total of 93 patients (mean age 44 ± 13 years, 17% male; 78% MRI-negative, 84% long-term remission) were analyzed. At baseline, 77% of patients showed a C:P ACTH ratio ≥2X, and all of these patients reached ≥3X C:P ACTH after stimulation. Among patients with a baseline ratio <2X, 57% (n = 12/21) crossed the ≥3X threshold after stimulation, prolactin normalization confirmed one additional patient, with two further patients remaining indeterminate. Stimulation produced 3.1-, 2.8-, and 1.9-fold increases in C:P ACTH at 2, 5, and 10 min post-stimulation, respectively, with the best response at 2-5 min. Cumulatively, 77%, 79%, 88%, 90%, and 91% of patients met criteria for CD by 0, 2, 5, 10, and 15 min, respectively. In this confirmed-CD cohort these proportions represent test sensitivity, rising from 77.4% (95% CI 67.6-85.4%) at baseline to 91.4% (95% CI 83.8-96.2%) by 15 min. Because all patients had surgically confirmed CD, these values reflect test sensitivity rather than overall diagnostic accuracy. Diagnostic yield plateaued by 15 min with negligible gain thereafter, and baseline together with a limited number of early post-stimulation samples captured most cases. These retrospective, hypothesis-generating findings suggest that a streamlined protocol may reduce laboratory and interpretive burden while preserving sensitivity, pending prospective validation.Copyright © 2026 The Author(s). title: Domain Adaptation of a Large Language Model for Radiology Impression Generation - Multi-Reader Evaluation.
abstract: To evaluate the clinical and practical trade-offs between domain adaptation and fine-tuning of large language models (LLMs) for radiology impression generation, with outcomes assessed through blinded expert radiologist review. In this retrospective institutional review board (IRB)-approved study 3,123,836 CT and MR reports were split into domain adaptation (80%), fine-tuning (16%), validation (2%), and test (2%) sets. Five LLM models were compared to ground truth: a base Llama-3-8B model (Meta) domain-adapted with mixed general, medical, and radiology text then fine-tuned using small (n = 1,280) and large (n = 499,814) number of report-impression pairs (DA + FTs, DA + FTl), an OpenBio-8B model with identical fine-tuning (Bio + FTs, Bio + FTl) and Gemini-1.5-Flash-002 used out-of-the-box. Four radiologists independently rated generated radiology impressions for abdominal CT and MR reports using six 5-point Likert items. Automated NLP metrics were also assessed. Domain adaptation improved performance in low-data regimes (mean score of DA + FTs 24.3 ± 2.8 vs. Bio + FTs 22.8 ± 3.5, P = 0.0004), but offered diminishing returns with large-scale fine-tuning (DA + FTl 24.9 ± 4.0 vs. Bio + FTl 25.0 ± 3.8, P = 0.89). Large-scale fine-tuned open-source models surpassed the commercial model in expert-rated quality and harmful output rates. Agreement among radiologists was low (ICC 0.22-0.49). Automated metrics showed weak correlation with human evaluation (ρ < 0.32). Domain adaptation improves LLM performance when labeled clinical data are scarce, but its incremental benefit diminishes as the fine-tuning dataset grows. Standard NLP metrics poorly reflect clinical relevance, underscoring the need for expert-informed evaluation. The findings help define the data-efficiency threshold for LLMs cost-effective deployment in clinical practice.© 2026. title: A Digital Mental Health Literacy Program Reduces Adolescent Depression and Anxiety Symptoms in a District-Wide Trial.
abstract: Adolescent mental health problems have risen sharply, creating an urgent need for scalable solutions. Although several mental health literacy (MHL) programs show promise, none with broad implementation feasibility have demonstrated reductions in adolescents' anxiety or depression. This study examined the mental health outcomes of a brief, digital MHL program.We conducted a preregistered cluster-randomized trial using an intent-to-treat approach with all ninth graders in a U.S. school district (N = 1,080), comparing an 80-minute digital MHL program to a time- and format-matched active control also framed as supporting mental health. Ten weeks later, students completed self-report measures of depression, anxiety, and MHL-related knowledge, attitudes, and help-seeking motivation.Students in the MHL condition reported significantly lower depression and anxiety symptoms. Increased willingness to seek help partially mediated the effect on depressive symptoms, but not anxiety.Findings indicate that brief digital MHL instruction can improve adolescent mental health under routine school conditions, offering a practical, scalable strategy for promoting mental health in school systems.Copyright © 2026 The Society for Adolescent Health and Medicine. title: The Exposome and Its Impact on Health and Disease.
abstract: The exposome, a term introduced by Christopher Wild, refers to all environmental exposures affecting an individual from conception onward. It was later conceptually divided into 3 partially overlapping domains, according to the nature and origin of exposures. Since its initial definition, the exposome has attracted increasing scientific interest, and mounting evidence has correlated it to a wide range of diseases, establishing that disease development consists of an intricate interplay between the endogenous-genomic background and the environment. In this review, we introduce the concept as well as elements and importance of the exposome, examine the methodologic approaches that are being employed in exposomics research, discuss challenges related to its study, and report several global exposome-related initiatives and their goals. It is increasingly clear that exposures significantly influence disease, highlighting the need for exposome research to match the scope and rigor of the Human Genome Project. This approach could help us better understand how the environment affects health, fully realize the exposome's potential in medical science, and advance the development of sophisticated, personalized medicine.Copyright © 2026 Mayo Foundation for Medical Education and Research. llm_summary: The exposome refers to all environmental exposures a person experiences from birth throughout life, and researchers reviewed evidence showing that these environmental factors significantly influence disease development alongside genetic factors. The review examined different types of environmental exposures, research methods used to study them, and global initiatives aimed at understanding how the environment affects health. This research suggests that studying environmental exposures with the same intensity as genetic studies could help develop personalized medicine and better explain how surroundings influence human health.
llm_summary_expert: The exposome, defined as all environmental exposures affecting an individual from conception onward, has been conceptually organized into three partially overlapping domains based on the nature and origin of exposures. This review examines the concept of the exposome, its constituent elements, methodologic approaches employed in exposomics research, and associated challenges in studying environmental influences on health. Mounting evidence has established correlations between the exposome and a wide range of diseases, demonstrating that disease development results from an intricate interplay between endogenous-genomic background and environmental factors. The authors discuss several global exposome-related initiatives and their objectives, emphasizing that exposome research requires scope and rigor comparable to the Human Genome Project to fully understand environmental influences on health. Advancing exposome research could enhance understanding of how environmental exposures affect health outcomes and facilitate development of sophisticated, personalized medicine approaches.

title: A pivotal Phase 2 study of derazantinib for previously-treated, locally advanced or metastatic cholangiocarcinoma with FGFR2 aberrations: FIDES-01.
abstract: To evaluate safety and efficacy of FGFR1-3 kinase inhibitor derazantinib, in advanced intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma (iCCA) harboring FGFR2 fusions or rearrangements (FGFR2F), mutations (FGFR2M), or amplifications (FGFR2A), previously treated with chemotherapy.Open-label, non-controlled Phase 2 trial. Patients with advanced iCCA, ≥1 prior chemotherapy, and FGFR2F (Substudy 1) or FGFR2M/FGFRA (Substudy 2), received once-daily oral derazantinib 300 mg until disease progression, unacceptable toxicity, consent withdrawal or investigator decision to stop. Efficacy was assessed by central radiology review using RECIST v1.1. Primary endpoints were objective response rate (ORR; Substudy 1) and 3-month progression-free survival (PFS3; Substudy 2). Other endpoints were PFS, ORR (Substudy 2), disease control rate (DCR), duration of response (DOR), and overall survival (OS). In Substudy 1, ORR and DCR were 22.3% (23/103 partial responses) and 75.7%, respectively; median (95% CI) PFS was 8.1 (5.5,8.3) months, DOR was 6.5 (4.6,9.2) months, and OS was 17.2 (12.5,22.4) months. In Substudy 2, PFS3 was 63% (27/43), ORR was 9.3% (3 partial, 1 complete response), DCR was 69.8%, and OS was 11.9 (8.4,15.9) months. There were no Grade 4 or 5 drug-related events. FGFR inhibitor class-specific toxicities included drug-related hyperphosphataemia (38%, Grade 3: 3%) and dry eye (36%). Nail disorders (10%, any grade or causality), stomatitis (5%), retinal events (5%), and palmar-plantar erythrodysesthesia (1%) were infrequent.In previously chemotherapy treated, FGFR-inhibitor-naïve patients with iCCA harboring FGFR2 fusions, mutations, or amplifications, derazantinib showed clinically meaningful efficacy with durable objective responses, and a manageable safety profile.Copyright © 2026 The Author(s).
