llm_summary: Researchers tested a drug called derazantinib in patients with advanced bile duct cancer that had specific genetic changes and had not responded to previous chemotherapy. The drug produced tumor shrinkage in about one-fifth of patients with certain genetic mutations, with effects lasting several months, though results were more modest in patients with other genetic variations. The treatment was generally well-tolerated with manageable side effects, suggesting it may offer a useful option for this difficult-to-treat cancer type.
llm_summary_expert: FIDES-01 was an open-label, non-controlled Phase 2 trial evaluating the FGFR1-3 kinase inhibitor derazantinib in previously chemotherapy-treated patients with advanced intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma harboring FGFR2 fusions, mutations, or amplifications. In Substudy 1 (FGFR2 fusions), derazantinib achieved an objective response rate of 22.3% with a median progression-free survival of 8.1 months and median overall survival of 17.2 months. In Substudy 2 (FGFR2 mutations or amplifications), the 3-month progression-free survival rate was 63% with an objective response rate of 9.3% and median overall survival of 11.9 months. The drug demonstrated a manageable safety profile with no Grade 4 or 5 drug-related adverse events, though class-specific toxicities included hyperphosphataemia in 38% of patients and dry eye in 36%. title: Comparative plaque- and liquid-based phage susceptibility testing of Pseudomonas aeruginosa isolates in a cystic fibrosis randomized clinical trial.
abstract: The optimal phage susceptibility testing (PST) method is unclear. Here, two PST methods were compared using Pseudomonas aeruginosa isolates recovered from patients with cystic fibrosis enrolled in a placebo-controlled clinical trial of a single intravenous dose of a four-phage cocktail (WRAIR-PAM-CF1). In total, 508 P. aeruginosa sputum isolates were evaluated, including isolates collected before or after phage or placebo treatment, isolates from the same trial participants over time, and isolates of different colony morphologies from the same participants at the same time point. Susceptibility to phages PaWRA01Φ11, PaWRA01Φ39, PaWRA02Φ83, and PaWRA02Φ87 and a cocktail of all four phages was assessed using a plaque assay (PA) and a Biolog Omnilog-based liquid assay (LA) with the same bacterial inoculum. A total of 170/508 isolates (33%) and 195/508 isolates (38%) were identified as susceptible to the cocktail by PA and LA, respectively. Among the susceptible isolates, 169/170 (99%; PA) and 187/195 (96%; LA) also tested susceptible to at least one of the four phages in the cocktail. Susceptible percent agreement between the PA and LA ranged from 76% to 100% and non-susceptible percent agreement ranged from 89% to 100% for all phages studied and the cocktail. Phage PaWRA02Φ83 demonstrated the greatest individual activity, with 164/508 (32%) and 188/508 (37%) isolates testing susceptible by PA and LA, respectively. The four-phage cocktail provided numerically broader coverage of P. aeruginosa (i.e., had the highest susceptibility rate) than did any single phage. There was high concordance between PST results by PA and LA.IMPORTANCEStandardization of phage susceptibility testing (PST) methods is essential to support phage therapy trials and any future clinical implementation. There are no standardized PST methods or interpretive criteria for PST. In this study, PST was performed by a plaque assay and a Biolog Omnilog-based liquid assay on Pseudomonas aeruginosa isolates recovered from cystic fibrosis patients enrolled in a clinical trial. Susceptibility of 508 isolates to four phages and a cocktail of all four was evaluated. There was high concordance between susceptibility assessed by plaque and liquid assays and numerically broader coverage of P. aeruginosa by the cocktail compared to any single phage. This manuscript should be of interest to those performing PST.

llm_summary: Researchers compared two laboratory methods for testing whether bacteria from cystic fibrosis patients were susceptible to four therapeutic viruses (phages) used to fight infections. Both the plaque assay and liquid-based methods showed similar results, with about one-third to one-third of the 508 bacterial isolates tested being susceptible to the four-phage combination. The high agreement between the two testing methods suggests either approach could be used to standardize how phage susceptibility is measured in future clinical trials.

title: Minimally invasive versus open liver resection for hepatocellular carcinoma in older adults: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
abstract: As the population ages, an increasing number of older adults are diagnosed with resectable hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). Although minimally invasive liver resection (MILR) has shown perioperative advantages, its safety and efficacy in older patients are not fully established. This meta-analysis evaluated the outcomes of MILR compared to open liver resection (OLR) in older adults (≥ 65 years) with HCC.A search was conducted in Medline, Embase, CINAHL, and The Cochrane Library from their inception until November 20, 2025. The review adhered to PRISMA guidelines and was prospectively registered on PROSPERO (CRD420251239665).Fourteen retrospective studies comprising 3,092 older adults were included (1,367 MILR, 1,725 OLR). title: Population Genetic Screening of Hemoglobinopathy Carrier Prevalence Compared to Medical Records.
abstract: To better understand the gap between hemoglobinopathy (HBP) prevalence and that which is documented in electronic medical records (EMRs) to quantify genetic HBP carrier prevalence compared to case counts documented in the EMR.We used genetic data from the Tapestry study to quantify the prevalence of HBPs and carrier traits, targeting sickle cell disease and β-thalassemia. Genetic findings were compared with International Classification of Diseases, 10th Revision (ICD-10) codes for hemoglobinopathies (D56 for β-thalassemia and D57 for SCD).A total of 50,008 participants were included in the genetic analysis. Twelve participants with diagnosis codes for α-thalassemia and sickle cell disease were previously confirmed with genetic results leaving 49,996 individuals. Of those, 116 participants' (0.23%) genetic testing demonstrated heterozygosity for sickle cell trait, and a majority self-reported Black ancestry (75%). Most (n=97 of 116) did not carry a sickle cell ICD-10 diagnosis code. There were 98 (0.20%) participant carriers for β-thalassemia with White ancestry most common (80.6%), followed by Asian ancestry (15.3%). Only 47 (48.0%) had a β-thalassemia ICD-10 diagnosis code.Our findings demonstrate that sickle cell and β-thalassemia carrier traits are prevalent at clinically significant levels and are substantially under-represented in EMRs. This gap raises important public health concerns, as under-identification may lead to missed opportunities for early diagnosis, reproductive counseling, and preventive care. These results highlight the need for enhanced public health efforts and primary care engagement to improve detection and equitable management of hemoglobinopathies.Copyright © 2026 Mayo Foundation for Medical Education and Research. title: Vaccines, Bias, and the Perils of Non-peer-reviewed Studies: Fueling Misinformation and Vaccine Hesitancy.
abstract: Unvetted scientific claims about vaccines can spread rapidly and undermine decades of progress in immunization and public trust. A recent non-peer-reviewed analysis, promoted at political hearings, in the documentary "An Inconvenient Study," and on social media, has been used to suggest that vaccinated children experience higher rates of chronic illness than unvaccinated peers. Despite standard regression models, critical flaws - uncontrolled confounding, exposure misclassification, unequal follow-up, and outcome multiplicity, invalidate causal inference. An independent group of international experts critically appraises this analysis and contrast its claims with the consistent evidence confirming vaccine safety and effectiveness. We also show how poorly designed studies can distort public discourse, amplify misinformation, and fuel vaccine hesitancy. We outline actions to strengthen research integrity, such as transparent data sharing, labeling of non-peer-reviewed content, and evidence-based communication. Safeguarding public health demands that vaccine evidence be methodologically sound, reviewed, and interpreted by qualified experts.© The Author(s) 2026. title: The fallibility of the T6 neurological level of injury for determining autonomic dysreflexia risk.
abstract: The T6 neurological level of spinal cord injury (SCI) is classically taught as differentiating who is and is not at risk for autonomic dysreflexia (AD); yet the reliability of this metric has rarely been tested.To determine how often individuals with SCI above and below the T6 neurological level of injury (NLI) experience symptomatic AD, quantify AD in the autonomic physiology laboratory, and describe underlying mechanisms that clinically manifest.Cross-sectional.Academic medical center.138 individuals with/without SCI.Not applicable.Symptoms of AD were quantified using the validated Autonomic Dysfunction Following SCI-AD survey. Deep autonomic physiology characterization was further completed (n = 34 uninjured controls, n = 28 individuals with SCI) to identify underlying AD mechanisms. Continuous blood pressure, heart rate, regional vascular resistance in the arm/leg, and pre/posttest catecholamines were recorded. Vascular responsiveness and baroreflex sensitivity were assessed with intravenous phenylephrine boluses. Foot cold pressor and bladder pressor tests served as below level mild noxious stimuli to elicit controlled AD.AD symptoms were, as expected, significantly higher after SCI compared to uninjured controls (p < .001). Symptomatic AD was identified in 77% of individuals with SCI at/above T6, compared to 38% with injuries below T6. McNemar's statistic indicated the T6 neurological level poorly differentiated who developed symptomatic AD (p = .039). During laboratory testing, 57% of those with SCI at/above T6 experienced AD, as did 57% of those with injuries below T6 (p = .33). Physiologically, AD in individuals with SCI below T6 can be due to heightened vascular responsiveness and poor baroreflex sensitivity, leading to minimal compensatory bradycardia.Symptomatic and objective AD occurs in those with SCI above and below the T6 NLI threshold. As such, targeted autonomic testing must translate to the bedside to accurately quantify AD risk. In the interim, though the T6 threshold has become cannon in many patient and resident education materials regarding AD risk, evidence suggests clinical care should avoid using this strict cutoff.© 2026 American Academy of Physical Medicine and Rehabilitation.

llm_summary: Researchers examined whether the T6 spinal level—a traditional cutoff used to predict who develops autonomic dysreflexia, a dangerous sudden blood pressure spike after spinal cord injury—actually reliably identifies at-risk patients. They found that autonomic dysreflexia occurred in similar rates among people with injuries above and below T6, suggesting this threshold poorly predicts who will experience the condition. The findings indicate that doctors should use more targeted testing rather than relying on this single anatomical marker to assess individual risk.
llm_summary_expert: Researchers examined 138 individuals with and without spinal cord injury (SCI) in a cross-sectional study to evaluate whether the T6 neurological level of injury reliably predicts autonomic dysreflexia (AD) risk, using validated symptom surveys and deep autonomic physiology characterization including continuous blood pressure monitoring, vascular resistance measurement, catecholamine quantification, and controlled noxious stimuli testing. The findings indicate that symptomatic and objective AD occurs across the T6 neurological level threshold, suggesting that clinical care should.

title: Prediction of All-Cause Mortality, Cardiovascular Mortality, and Angiographic Coronary Disease From LVEF Reserve: Findings From the Multicenter REFINE PET Registry.
abstract: Left ventricular ejection fraction reserve (LVEF-R), defined as stress EF minus rest EF, is a marker for high-risk coronary artery disease in patients undergoing positron emission tomography myocardial perfusion imaging, but its prognostic and diagnostic significance in large real-world populations remains incompletely defined. We aimed to analyze the association of LVEF-R with mortality and high-risk obstructive coronary artery disease in a large multicenter cohort.We analyzed 34 976 patients from 13 sites who underwent gated rest and vasodilator stress positron emission tomography myocardial perfusion imaging from the Registry of Flow and Perfusion Imaging for Artificial Intelligence with PET. Associations between LVEF-R and all-cause mortality and cardiovascular death were assessed using multivariable Cox regression models. In a subset with invasive coronary angiography (n=6843), the relationship between LVEF-R and angiographic disease was evaluated.A total of 9392 (26.9%) patients had an LVEF-R<0%. Over a median follow-up of 4.1 years, lower LVEF-R demonstrated a graded association with higher mortality. Compared with LVEF-R>5%, adjusted hazard ratios for all-cause mortality were 1.20 for LVEF-R 0% to 5% ([95% CI, 1.13-1.28]; P<0.001), 1.32 for -5% to 0% ([95% CI, 1.23-1.42]; P<0.001), and 1.38 for ≤-5% ([95% CI, 1.24-1.52]; P<0.001). A negative LVEF-R was also associated with high-risk coronary artery disease, including left main and 3-vessel disease.LVEF-R is an independent predictor of mortality, with a graded association between impaired reserve and adverse outcomes. A negative LVEF-R identifies patients with a higher likelihood of multivessel or left-main coronary artery disease, supporting its role as a clinically relevant marker of high-risk disease.

title: Surgeon Ergonomics of Lateral Lumbar Interbody Fusion Across Four Patient Positions: A Proof-of-Concept Simulation Study Using Motion Capture and Electromyography.
abstract: Study DesignProof-of-concept simulation-based biomechanical pilot study.ObjectivesTo compare surgeon posture and muscle activity across four lateral lumbar interbody fusion (LLIF) positions and rank them by overall ergonomic burden.MethodsFive right-handed spine surgeons (case volumes 15 to 500 or more) each simulated a single-level LLIF on a synthetic model in four positions, three using direct vision (lateral decubitus, prone seated, prone lateral) and one using a camera and monitor (prone camera). Whole-body motion capture and surface EMG were recorded simultaneously, analyzed by surgical phase, and summarized per surgeon.ResultsNeck-flexion intensity was greatest in lateral decubitus and lower in every prone position, with the same ranking in all five surgeons (exact Friedman p=3.0e-06, Kendall W=1.00). Arm elevation was highest in prone seated. Across four summaries of posture and muscle activity, prone camera was the most favorable position in every surgeon, while the others reordered by measure. All positions scored medium-to-high risk. No two-position comparison reached adjusted significance, as expected at this sample size.ConclusionsPatient position in LLIF does not appear to change patient outcome, but it changes what the operation costs the surgeon. Lateral decubitus loaded the neck in every surgeon regardless of case volume or preference, prone seated loaded the shoulder, and prone camera was most favorable overall. Surgeons can reduce their exposure through position and setup, and ergonomics offers an objective way to compare setups when patient outcomes cannot separate them. These are proof-of-concept findings in five surgeons and require confirmation in a larger sample.

title: Optimizing Clinical Education: A Level-of-Learner Placement Model for Academic-Practice Partnerships.
abstract: Clinical education helps prelicensure undergraduate nursing students link theory to practice, develop clinical judgment, and build professional identity. Increasing enrollment, workforce demands, and limited placement capacity require clinical education models that intentionally match learner readiness with unit readiness.Standard placement processes may fail to align learner readiness, course expectations, and unit readiness, resulting in uneven learning experiences and increased burden for faculty, clinical nurse teachers, preceptors, and unit staff.This article describes the Level of Learner Clinical Placement Model for prelicensure nursing students across early, intermediate, and advanced points in the curriculum. The model may be applied in a Dedicated Education Unit, preceptorship, hybrid, observation, and faculty-led placements; it is not limited to Dedicated Education Unit settings.The model provides the overall conceptual structure for academic-practice partners, clarifies expectations for unit staff through related tools, and supports intentional progression toward practice readiness.Copyright © 2026 Wolters Kluwer Health, LLC. The proposed model clarifies expectations for unit staff through related tools and supports intentional progression toward practice readiness while addressing constraints from increasing enrollment, workforce demands, and limited placement capacity. The abstract does not report quantitative outcome data, comparative effectiveness results, or empirical validation of the model's impact on student learning or clinical outcomes.

title: AI-Assisted Lung Segmentation for Lung Transplant Volumetry: Effect of Radiation Dose Reduction.
abstract: Accurate lung volumetry is essential for donor-recipient size matching in lung transplantation. This study evaluated the impact of radiation dose reduction on the robustness of AI-based whole-lung segmentation, 5-lobe segmentation, and automated tissue classification.Fifty cases from the Cancer Image Archive (TCIA) Low-dose CT Image and Projection Data set were analyzed. A reduced-dose data set at 10% of the routine dose for each case was generated using validated projection-domain noise insertion. Whole-lung and 5-lobe segmentation were performed using the Lung CT Segmenter module with the lungmask deep learning model in 3D Slicer. Segmentation accuracy was quantified using the Dice similarity coefficient (DSC), 95th percentile Hausdorff distance (HD95), and maximum Hausdorff distance (HDmax). Automated tissue classification and volumetry were performed using the Lung CT Analyzer module.Whole-lung segmentation demonstrated excellent consistency between full-dose and 10% dose images (mean DSC 0.997±0.002, HD95 0.73±0.26 mm). In contrast, 5-lobe segmentation showed substantially lower accuracy and greater variability, even at routine dose. Automated tissue classification revealed a mean decrease in functional (inflated) lung volume of 17.12%±5.69% in the right lung and 17.15%±5.56% in the left lung, accompanied by marked increases in emphysema, infiltrated, and collapsed volumes.AI-based whole-lung segmentation remains highly accurate at 10% of the routine dose, supporting its potential for lung transplant volumetry. However, tissue classification and 5-lobe segmentation exhibited notable degradation, highlighting limitations of existing tools at ultra-low dose levels.Copyright © 2026 Wolters Kluwer Health, LLC. title: Left Atrial Appendage Occlusion Versus Oral Anticoagulation in Atrial Fibrillation: A Comprehensive Evidence Synthesis.
abstract: Oral anticoagulation (OAC) remains the cornerstone of stroke prevention in atrial fibrillation (AF) but is limited by bleeding risk. Left atrial appendage occlusion (LAAO) devices offer an alternative; however, recent randomized trials have reported inconsistent efficacy compared with OAC.We conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials (RCTs) comparing LAAO with OAC through April 1, 2026, using MEDLINE, EMBASE, and Cochrane CENTRAL. Eligible studies enrolled adults (≥18 years) with AF randomized to LAAO or OAC. Primary and secondary outcomes were pooled as risk ratios (RR) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Individual patient-level data (IPD) were reconstructed from published Kaplan-Meier curves for time-to-event sensitivity analyses.Six RCTs (n = 7,004; mean age 72 years; CHA2DS2‑VASc 3.9; HAS‑BLED 1.7; mean follow-up 38 months) were included. LAAO showed no significant difference in ischemic stroke (RR 1.20, 95% CI 0.82-1.76), major bleeding (RR 0.77, 95% CI 0.50-1.17), or all-cause mortality (RR 0.96, 95% CI 0.82-1.13) compared with OAC. Hemorrhagic stroke risk was significantly lower with LAAO (RR 0.53, 95% CI 0.30-0.93). Reconstructed IPD demonstrated similar stroke and bleeding risks (HR 1.24 and 0.84, respectively) but lower all-cause mortality with LAAO (HR 0.70, 95% CI 0.52-0.95).LAAO provides comparable ischemic stroke prevention and major bleeding outcomes to OAC and reduces hemorrhagic stroke risk. Reconstructed IPD analyses suggest a possible mortality benefit that warrants further investigation. Future studies using contemporary devices and post-ablation populations are needed to refine patient selection and further characterize the comparative clinical outcomes of LAAO and OAC in AF patients.© 2026 Wiley Periodicals LLC.

title: Snare-Assisted Retrieval of a Mechanically Locked-Open TEER Device: A Novel Bailout Technique.
abstract: Transcatheter edge-to-edge repair (TEER) is an established intervention for patients having severe mitral regurgitation (MR) with prohibitive surgical risk. Complications during deployment related to device malfunction are uncommon but necessitate prompt decision-making and management. A 54-year-old gentleman with dilated cardiomyopathy, severe left ventricular dysfunction, and severe MR underwent TEER using the MyClip system (Meril Life Sciences Pvt. Ltd., Vapi, Gujarat, India). Initial deployment across the A2-P2 scallops of mitral leaflets achieved partial MR reduction. Significant residual MR required a second clip for optimal leaflet coaptation. While deploying the second clip, it failed to close because of a mechanical locking failure. So, we everted the clip, pulled back to LA, and it stayed in open position and failed to close. We report a novel bailout snare technique that enabled safe retrieval without the need for a second transseptal puncture. The ability to close the clip arms prior to withdrawal minimized the risk of tearing the atrial septum and facilitated the successful completion of the TEER procedure. Another clip was deployed successfully, resulting in significant MR reduction. This case demonstrates a rare complication during deployment, a malfunction of the device, and a novel strategy for safely bailing out a challenging intra-procedural complication.© 2026 Wiley Periodicals LLC.

The medical team developed a novel rescue technique using a snare device to safely retrieve the malfunctioning clip without requiring additional punctures, allowing them to successfully place another clip and complete the procedure. This case demonstrates both a rare complication during valve repair and an effective bailout strategy for managing device malfunctions.

During deployment of a second clip intended to optimize leaflet coaptation, mechanical locking failure occurred, leaving the device locked in an open position within the left atrium. The authors developed a novel snare-assisted bailout technique that enabled safe retrieval of the malfunctioning clip without requiring a second transseptal puncture. The ability to close the clip arms prior to withdrawal using the snare minimized the risk of atrial septal tearing and allowed successful completion of the procedure with deployment of an alternative clip. This case report demonstrates a rare device malfunction complication during TEER and presents a novel retrieval strategy for managing this challenging intra-procedural scenario.

title: Global Burden of Anorexia Nervosa and Bulimia Nervosa, 1990 to 2023, With Forecasts to 2050: A Global Burden of Disease Study 2023 Analysis.
abstract: Eating disorders are a major cause of nonfatal mental health burden, yet global evidence on their long-term trends, geographic distribution, and future trajectories remains limited.To estimate the global, regional, and national prevalence and disability burden of anorexia nervosa and bulimia nervosa-and mortality attributable to anorexia nervosa-from 1990 to 2023, and to forecast prevalence to 2050.Using Global Burden of Disease (GBD) 2023 methods, data were synthesized from systematic literature reviews, population surveys, and vital registration systems. Estimates were produced for 204 countries and territories from 1990 to 2023, with forecasts through 2050. These data were analyzed from October 2025 to August 2026.Anorexia nervosa or bulimia nervosa diagnosis.Counts and age-standardized rates with 95% uncertainty intervals (UIs) for anorexia nervosa and bulimia nervosa prevalence, years lived with disability (YLDs), and disability-adjusted life-years (DALYs), and anorexia nervosa mortality, reported by age, sex, and location.In 2023, an estimated 18.1 million people (95% UI, 13.9-24.0) globally were living with anorexia nervosa or bulimia nervosa, of whom 12.6 million (69.4%) were female, 5.5 million were male (30.6%), and 41.2% were aged 10 to 24 years. These cases accounted for 3.83 million DALYs (95% UI, 2.23-5.69). Since 1990, the global number of prevalent cases increased by 71.0%, while age-standardized prevalence and DALY rates rose by about 21%. Females experienced substantially higher prevalence and DALY rates than males. The highest age-standardized prevalence rates were observed in high-income regions, particularly Australasia and Western Europe, whereas the largest relative increases in age-standardized prevalence occurred in East Asia, South Asia, and Southeast Asia. Forecasts indicate continued increases in prevalent cases through 2050.This GBD 2023 analysis found that anorexia nervosa and bulimia nervosa contribute substantially to global nonfatal health loss. These findings support the integration of eating disorders into mental health surveillance, prevention, and service planning worldwide.

llm_summary: Researchers examined global trends in anorexia nervosa and bulimia nervosa from 1990 to 2023, finding that approximately 18 million people worldwide were living with these eating disorders in 2023, with cases increasing by 71 percent since 1990. Women accounted for nearly 70 percent of cases, and young people aged 10 to 24 represented 41 percent of those affected, with the highest rates occurring in wealthy regions like Western Europe and Australia. The study projects that the number of people with these eating disorders will continue to rise through 2050, highlighting the need for improved mental health services and prevention efforts globally.
llm_summary_expert: Researchers used Global Burden of Disease 2023 methods to synthesize data from systematic literature reviews, population surveys, and vital registration systems across 204 countries and territories to estimate the prevalence, disability burden, and mortality of anorexia nervosa and bulimia nervosa from 1990 to 2023, with forecasts through 2050. In 2023, an estimated 18.1 million people globally were living with anorexia nervosa or bulimia nervosa (69.4% female), accounting for 3.83 million disability-adjusted life-years, with 41.2% of cases occurring in individuals aged 10 to 24 years. Since 1990, the global number of prevalent cases increased by 71.0%, while age-standardized prevalence and disability-adjusted life-year rates rose by approximately 21%, with substantially higher rates observed in females compared to males. The highest age-standardized prevalence rates were observed in high-income regions including Australasia and Western Europe, whereas the largest relative increases in age-standardized prevalence occurred in East Asia, South Asia, and Southeast Asia.

title: Reimagining U.S. medicine's professionalism movement: institutional professionalism and medicine's collective identity crisis.
abstract: U.S. medicine's modern-day professionalism movement is approaching its third decade. Within this movement and across a broad array of initiatives, medicine has recast issues of professionalism from a more macro-level and sociological focus on the profession to a more micro-level and individual-oriented focus on professionals. In this commentary, the authors adopt a historical lens and briefly outline the movement to date before recommending a shift from professionalism's current focus on the individual to a more macro- and institutional-level framing. In doing so, the authors seek to redirect the focus of prevailing professionalism discussions from professionals to the profession as they argue for a more sociological emphasis on the issue of medical work and its control as opposed to an emphasis on the values, motives, behaviors, and competencies of individual physicians and trainees. To better respond to contemporary professionalism challenges, the authors introduce a new concept-institutional professionalism-and identify 3 foci in arguing for placing a greater emphasis on the profession rather than the individual: (1) semantics, (2) theory (including the deployment of sociological constructs such as organizational fields and institutional logics), and (3) a more layered micro- (individual), meso- (organizational), and macro-level (institutional) understanding of medical work. The authors argue that professionalism, as the countervailing logic to those of managerialism and commercialism, will cease to functionally exist unless medicine responds in a more collective and institutional-level fashion to current encroachments on its work. A failure to do so will leave behind a conceptually isolated and hollowed-out profession that retains the language of professionalism while losing the institutional conditions needed to support it.© The Author(s) 2026. llm_summary_expert: The authors examine U. S. medicine's professionalism movement over nearly three decades, noting that current initiatives have shifted focus from macro-level sociological concerns about the profession itself to micro-level individual-oriented approaches emphasizing physician values and behaviors. They propose a conceptual reframing toward "institutional professionalism" that redirects attention from individual professionals to the profession as a collective entity by emphasizing three key areas: semantic precision, sociological theory including organizational fields and institutional logics, and multilevel analysis spanning individual, organizational, and institutional dimensions. The authors argue that professionalism functions as a countervailing logic against managerialism and commercialism, and this function will deteriorate unless medicine responds through collective and institutional-level action rather than individual-focused interventions.

title: State-of-the-Art Review: Native Joint Septic Arthritis Epidemiology, Pathogenesis, Microbiology, Diagnosis, Management, and Outcomes.
abstract: Native joint septic arthritis (NJSA) is a time-sensitive orthopedic and infectious diseases emergency associated with substantial morbidity, mortality, and long-term functional impairment. This State-of-the-Art Review synthesizes current evidence on NJSA epidemiology with a primary focus on bacterial etiologies, risk factors, pathogenesis, microbiology, clinical presentation, and diagnostic challenges, including the absence of validated diagnostic criteria and limitations of culture-based evaluation. We summarize current diagnostic approaches with a focus on synovial fluid interpretation and the expanding role of molecular diagnostics. Management principles emphasize timely surgical source control, appropriate antimicrobial therapy, and coordinated multidisciplinary care. Outcomes are reviewed through the lens of relapse, reinfection, and functional recovery, highlighting the influence of host factors, joint involvement, and timeliness of intervention. Finally, we identify persistent gaps in evidence including optimal surgical timing, treatment duration, oral transition, clinical utility of emerging diagnostics, and outline research priorities to improve NJSA care and outcomes.© The Author(s) 2026. llm_summary: This review examined native joint septic arthritis, a serious infection inside joints that requires emergency treatment, by analyzing current evidence on how it develops, what causes it, how doctors diagnose it, and how to treat it. The authors found that current diagnostic methods have significant limitations because there are no agreed-upon diagnostic criteria and culture tests often miss infections. The review identifies important gaps in knowledge about the best timing for surgery, how long to treat patients, and when to switch from intravenous to oral antibiotics.
llm_summary_expert: This state-of-the-art review synthesizes current evidence on native joint septic arthritis (NJSA), a time-sensitive orthopedic and infectious disease emergency, with primary emphasis on bacterial etiologies, epidemiology, pathogenesis, and risk factors. The review addresses critical diagnostic challenges including the absence of validated diagnostic criteria and limitations of culture-based evaluation, while summarizing current diagnostic approaches with focus on synovial fluid interpretation and the expanding role of molecular diagnostics. Management principles emphasized in the review include timely surgical source control, appropriate antimicrobial therapy, and coordinated multidisciplinary care as essential components of NJSA treatment. Outcomes are evaluated through the lens of relapse, reinfection, and functional recovery, with consideration of how host factors, joint involvement, and timeliness of intervention influence patient prognosis. The review identifies persistent evidence gaps including optimal surgical timing, treatment duration, oral transition protocols, and clinical utility of emerging diagnostics, establishing research priorities to improve NJSA care and outcomes.

title: Diagnostic approach and management strategy for patients with exertional rhabdomyolysis - Results from an international survey of healthcare professionals.
abstract: BackgroundRhabdomyolysis is a complex and potentially life-threatening syndrome characterized by the rapid breakdown of damaged skeletal muscle. Despite its clinical significance, universally accepted diagnostic criteria and standardized management guidelines are lacking.MethodsA cross-sectional online survey about the current diagnostic approach, assessment of risk factors and severity, and management of follow-up of rhabdomyolysis was conducted among clinicians across Europe, Australia, and the USA.ResultsFifty-four respondents from 16 countries completed the survey. Results revealed considerable variability in hospital admission practices, and patient follow-up. Some agreement was found in the frequent use of genetic and neurophysiological testing in as diagnostic tools. The survey revealed no consensus on which CK-level would be considered cut-off levels for rhabdomyolysis.ConclusionsThe survey found little to no coherent approach to diagnosing, assessment of severity, nor follow-up of rhabdomyolysis among respondents who were primarily neurologists and pediatric neurologists. It highlights the need for international guidelines in the diagnostic process, treatment and follow-up of rhabdomyolysis as well as a universally agreed definition of rhabdomyolysis.

The survey found major differences in how doctors decide when to admit patients to the hospital, what blood test results they use to confirm the diagnosis, and how they follow up with patients afterward. The results suggest that doctors need to agree on common standards for diagnosing this condition and managing patient care.

title: Nationwide Trends in Neoadjuvant Chemotherapy Utilization for Pancreatic Adenocarcinoma From 2012 to 2021.
abstract: Neoadjuvant chemotherapy (NAC) is increasingly recommended in recent years to treat pancreatic adenocarcinoma (PDAC), even those tumors that are upfront resectable. Utilization across different hospital systems based on patient factors, tumor location, and tumor stage is not clear. We aimed to evaluate changes in NAC use for PDAC over the past decade using a nationwide cancer database.The National Cancer Database was queried for patients with stage I-III PDAC treated with surgery between 2012 and 2021. Patients were only included if they were documented to have chemotherapy at any point before or after surgery. Multivariable logistic regression controlling for patient clinical and demographic characteristics evaluated associations with NAC use.During the study period, 28,458 patients were treated with NAC and surgery or surgery and adjuvant chemotherapy. The percentage of all patients receiving NAC significantly increased year after year from 28% in 2012 to 65% in 2021 (P < 0.001). A significant increase in NAC was seen for patients when stratified by type of surgical resection (pancreatoduodenectomy, total pancreatectomy, or distal pancreatectomy; P < 0.001, all). A significant increase in NAC for stage I and II PDAC was noted during the study period (P < 0.01) but not for stage III (P > 0.05). This increase in NAC for stage I and II PDAC patients was similarly noted when stratified by surgery type (P < 0.001, all). Patients receiving care at an academic research facility had a higher proportion of patients undergoing NAC compared to those seen at a comprehensive community facility (51% versus 37%, P < 0.001). A multivariable logistic regression model demonstrated that younger age, Charlson-Deyo Score three or higher, non-Spanish Hispanic ethnicity, receipt of care at academic research facility, patients in a rural or urban location (versus metro), positive lymph nodes, and higher tumor T stage were independent predictors of NAC use (P < 0.05, all). Patients without insurance, poor grade, and tumors in the tail of the pancreas were likewise significantly less likely to receive NAC (P < 0.05, all).NAC use has significantly increased in the past 10 y, especially for stage I and II tumors. NAC has increased for all types of pancreas resection for PDAC. Key patient, tumor, and location differences determine whether or not a patient is treated with NAC.Copyright © 2026 Elsevier Inc. title: The characteristics of perivascular proinflammation in 4-repeat tauopathies.
abstract: Progressive supranuclear palsy (PSP) and corticobasal degeneration (CBD) are both neurodegenerative diseases characterized by aggregates composed of 4-repeat (4R) tau protein. They have distinct neuropathological features and classic clinical symptoms; however, the signs and symptoms overlap across the two syndromes. Accumulating evidence suggests that dysregulated immune response is a major contributing factor to neurodegeneration but its role in 4R-tauopathies remains undetermined. The aim is to explore the involvement of neuroinflammation from a vascular perspective in 4R-tauopathies. Autopsies from four controls, three PSP, and three CBD cases were assessed. Samples were obtained from the superior/middle frontal gyrus (S/M-FG) and basal ganglia (BG). Immunofluorescence staining included neuroinflammatory markers: glial fibrillary acidic protein (GFAP), ionized calcium-binding adapter molecule 1 (Iba1), cluster of differentiation 68 (CD68); vascular markers: collagen type IV (ColIV), monocarboxylate transporter-1 (MCT1), and α-smooth muscle actin (αSMA). Maximally projected confocal z-stack images of vasculature were used as a mask to quantify total perivascular GFAP+/Iba1+/CD68+ labeling. GFAP immunoreactivity ratio between MCT1 and αSMA double labeled arteries and veins was quantified to further differentiate venular and arteriolar involvement into proinflammatory activation. Both PSP and CBD had widespread perivascular proinflammatory changes, although greater in CBD. The activated GFAP+ astrocytes and microglia/macrophages in CBD were distributed extensively in S/M-FG and BG, with S/M-FG WM more affected. In PSP, abundant neuroinflammation was found in BG. The involvement of vasculature type was distinct among the two 4R-tauopathies, while CBD showed comparable proinflammatory changes in arterioles and venules, PSP exhibited predominant proinflammation in venules. The regional pattern of perivascular proinflammation differed between PSP and CBD, corresponding to the characteristic affected brain regions. CBD had more severe perivascular proinflammation that involved both arterioles and venules, while venules were more affected in PSP. Perivascular proinflammation may be a critical pathophysiological process in 4R-tauopathies.© 2026 The Author(s). title: Comparing SGLT2 Inhibitors on Incident Major Adverse Kidney Events in Type 2 Diabetes: A Target Trial Emulation.
abstract: To determine whether canagliflozin, dapagliflozin, and empagliflozin differ in rates of major adverse kidney events (MAKE) in adults with T2D at moderate cardiovascular risk and without stage 3+ chronic kidney disease (CKD) at baseline.Using target trial emulation and U.S. claims data from commercial, Medicare Advantage, and traditional Medicare plans, we compared canagliflozin, dapagliflozin, and empagliflozin among adults ≥ 21years with T2D at moderate cardiovascular risk (1-5% annualized MACE or death risk), without insulin use or stage 3+ chronic kidney disease (CKD) at baseline, initiating treatment from January 1, 2014, and December 31, 2021. Propensity scores estimated via super learner ensemble were incorporated as inverse probability weights into Cox models examining major adverse kidney events (MAKE: stage 3+ CKD, kidney failure, kidney replacement therapy initiation) and all-cause death under intention-to-treat analysis through December 31, 2022.The weighted cohort included 41,248, 17,548, and 72,638 adults initiating canagliflozin, dapagliflozin, and empagliflozin, respectively. One-year post-initiation, rates of MAKE were 3.2% in the dapagliflozin and empagliflozin arms and 3.5% in the canagliflozin arm; by three years, 8.4%, 8.5%, and 9.1%. Compared to canagliflozin, MAKE risk was lower with dapagliflozin (HR 0.91; 95%CI 0.85-0.97) and empagliflozin (HR 0.93; 95%CI 0.88-0.97), with no difference between dapagliflozin and empagliflozin.Empagliflozin and dapagliflozin were associated with modestly lower adverse kidney event rates compared to canagliflozin. These findings provide clinically actionable evidence to support selection of SGLT2i to reduce CKD risk in a highly prevalent subset of people with T2D.Copyright © 2026. Published by Elsevier Inc.

title: Melanoma risk in astronauts: Clinical screening, surveillance, and the microgravity paradox.
abstract: Astronauts show significantly elevated melanoma incidence and mortality relative to the general population, a finding with direct relevance to an expanding civilian spaceflight population. We conducted a systematic review to characterize this risk and translate it into practical guidance for dermatologists. Of 11 studies meeting eligibility criteria, only one was a human clinical or epidemiological study; the remainder were experimental, and consistently showed that simulated microgravity suppresses melanoma proliferation, adhesion, migration, and invasion while promoting apoptosis through collapse of FAK-RhoA-mTORC1-ERK1/2 mechanotransduction, a laboratory finding in direct tension with the clinical risk observed in astronauts. The majority of astronauts studied were career pilots, an occupational group with an independently established approximately two-fold melanoma incidence and elevated mortality specifically among pilots from cockpit UVA exposure accrued before spaceflight, which we identify as the most clinically substantial explanation for this paradox. We recommend risk-stratified pre-flight total-body skin examination with dermoscopy, deferral of dermatologic management to the ground rather than in-flight, post-flight surveillance after long-duration missions, and individualized counseling that distinguishes career astronauts from the demographically distinct civilian spaceflight population now emerging through missions such as Inspiration4 and Polaris Dawn.Copyright © 2026. Published by Elsevier Inc.

The researchers recommend skin screening before spaceflight and ongoing monitoring afterward, with different guidance for professional astronauts versus civilian space travelers.

abstract: MR elastography of the brain provides quantitative biomarkers of mechanical properties of brain tissue. Prior studies have shown that an advanced 3D MRE can differentiate idiopathic normal-pressure hydrocephalus from other neurodegenerative disorders. In this pilot study, we assessed whether a simplified 2D MR elastography protocol, which is more widely available, could detect stiffness differences between patients with idiopathic normal-pressure hydrocephalus and patients with cognitive impairment due to causes other than idiopathic normal-pressure hydrocephalus, thus providing preliminary diagnostic discrimination while using a previously developed 3D MR elastography classifier as a secondary exploratory comparator.In this prospective study, 10 patients with clinically diagnosed idiopathic normal-pressure hydrocephalus and 10 patients with cognitive impairment due to non-idiopathic normal-pressure hydrocephalus causes underwent 2D brain MR elastography between September 2024 and April 2025. Median stiffness was extracted from a standardized, manually defined region of interest at the brain vertex. A previously validated 3D MR elastography pattern-analysis support vector machine classifier was applied to this prospective cohort as a secondary exploratory comparator. Group differences were assessed using Wilcoxon rank sum tests. Diagnostic performance was evaluated using receiver operating characteristic analysis as an exploratory assessment of discrimination.Median stiffness was higher in the group with idiopathic normal-pressure hydrocephalus than the group with non-idiopathic normal-pressure hydrocephalus cognitive impairment (1.62 vs 0.98 kPa; P < .001). Stiffness demonstrated excellent discriminatory ability, yielding an apparent area under the curve of 1.00 with an optimal threshold of 1.43 kPa. The 3D support vector machine decision metric also yielded an apparent area under the curve of 1.00. The pretrained support vector machine model classified 18 of 20 subjects correctly (accuracy: 90.0% [95% CI, 68.3%-98.8%]). Although promising, these performance estimates should be interpreted cautiously given the limited sample size.This study provides preliminary evidence that a 2D MR elastography protocol may help discriminate idiopathic normal-pressure hydrocephalus from other disorders causing cognitive impairment, providing a foundation for larger, multicenter validation studies for assessing reproducibility, generalizability, and potential clinical utility.© 2027 by American Journal of Neuroradiology.

title: Direct Injection of Meningeal Diverticula for Localization of CSF-Venous Fistulas: Technique and Clinical Applications.
abstract: The recognition of CSF-venous fistulas as a cause of spontaneous intracranial hypotension has increased dramatically in recent years, in large part due to the more pervasive use of lateral decubitus myelography. Lateral decubitus positioning is critical for identification of CSF-venous fistulas, because most of these fistulas arise from meningeal diverticula along the nerve root sleeves. These diverticula must be filled with dense contrast to allow for confident visualization of contrast in veins draining CSF-venous fistulas. Even with an excellent technique, decubitus CT or fluoroscopic myelography can fail to detect some CSF-venous fistulas. In this technical report, we describe the use of direct contrast injection into the meningeal diverticula for the identification or further characterization of CSF-venous fistulas. This is a potentially useful problem-solving technique that can increase diagnostic confidence for this sometimes elusive pathology. We have found it useful to both detect CSF-venous fistulas and exquisitely determine their site of origin within meningeal diverticula.© 2027 by American Journal of Neuroradiology.

title: Cardiac mechanical efficiency in patients with cardiogenic shock.
abstract: Cardiogenic shock (CS) is characterized by impaired left ventricular (LV) mechanical performance and adverse remodelling. We evaluated whether transthoracic echocardiography (TTE)-derived modified cardiac efficiency (mCE), integrating stroke work and residual LV volume, is associated with short- and long-term mortality in CS and whether its prognostic value differs by shock aetiology.In this retrospective cohort study, consecutive adults admitted with CS to the cardiac intensive care unit at Mayo Clinic (2007-2018) were included if TTE was performed within 24 h. mCE was calculated as (stroke volume × estimated LV end-systolic pressure) divided by LV end-systolic volume and categorized into quartiles. Primary outcome was in-hospital mortality; secondary outcome was 1-year mortality. Multivariable logistic and Cox models adjusted for illness severity, comorbidity burden, shock aetiology, cardiac arrest, vasoactive therapy, and mechanical circulatory support. Among 667 patients, median mCE was 48 mmHg (IQR 32-74). In-hospital mortality was 28% and increased stepwise across decreasing mCE quartiles. The lowest quartile had a 2.5-fold higher adjusted odds of in-hospital death (OR 2.53; 95%CI: 1.49-4.37; P < 0.001). One-year mortality was 41%; the lowest quartile had a two-fold higher adjusted hazard of death (HR 2.05; 95%CI: 1.45-2.89; P < 0.001). Associations were stronger in acute coronary syndrome-related CS (interaction P = 0.035 for in-hospital; P = 0.015 for 1-year). Within the lowest quartile, reduced systolic pressure further amplified mortality risk.Early TTE-derived mCE was independently associated with short- and long-term mortality in CS, particularly in acute coronary syndrome-related CS, and captured the interaction between ventricular remodelling and mechanical performance underlying high-risk phenotypes.© The Author(s) 2026. title: Inflammation in coronary syndromes in clinical practice: a clinical consensus statement of the Association for Acute Cardiovascular Care of the European Society of Cardiology, the European Society of Cardiology Working Group on Myocardial and Pericardial Diseases, the European Society of Cardiology Council on Basic Cardiovascular Science, and the European Society of Cardiology Council for Cardiology Practice.
abstract: Inflammation is a key driver of coronary syndromes across the continuum from chronic coronary syndromes to acute coronary syndromes. It contributes to atherogenesis, plaque destabilization, and ischaemic events and influences myocardial injury, repair, and remodelling. Inflammatory activity is further amplified by metabolic and autoimmune comorbidities such as diabetes, obesity, and connective tissue diseases, with obesity representing a major driver of chronic low-grade inflammation through adipose tissue dysfunction and cytokine activation, while psychosocial stress and environmental exposures including air pollution serve as additional triggers. Genetic variations, including human leucocyte antigen genotypes, modulate individual susceptibility to vascular inflammation and myocardial injury. This expert consensus from the European Society of Cardiology's Association for Acute CardioVascular Care summarizes the current understanding of inflammation across the full spectrum of coronary syndromes, including underlying mechanisms, relevant biomarkers, and imaging approaches that characterize vascular inflammation, and integrates insights from experimental and clinical studies. Importantly, this document provides explicit consensus-based guidance on when, how, and in whom inflammation should be assessed and treated in routine clinical practice. While the causal association between inflammation and atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease is well established, pharmacological modification of inflammation has produced conflicting evidence. Some agents, such as low-dose colchicine, have demonstrated modest reductions in cardiovascular events, although results across trials have been inconsistent. Other anti-inflammatory therapies have not shown clinical benefit, whereas selective cytokine inhibition with canakinumab has reduced cardiovascular risk at the cost of increased infection rates. The present manuscript also focuses on the evaluation of inflammatory activity in cardiovascular patients in routine clinical practice. It further discusses criteria for patient selection and clinical decision-making regarding the introduction of anti-inflammatory therapy in individuals with established atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease.© The Author(s) 2026. title: Brain perivascular macrophages regulate endothelial cell function via a cMAF-dependent transcriptional program in mouse and human.
abstract: Brain perivascular macrophages maintain brain physiology, yet their transcriptional regulators and functions in health and disease remain unclear. Using single-cell multi-omics and functional experiments, we identify cellular musculoaponeurotic fibrosarcoma oncogene (cMAF) as a key transcription factor for brain perivascular macrophages, and conditional deletion of cMAF disrupts their phenotype in vivo. Functionally, cMAF drives insulin-like growth factor-1 (IGF1) expression in perivascular macrophages, enabling communication with endothelial cells. Consistently, cMAF deletion in perivascular macrophages causes transcriptional alterations in cerebral arteries, affecting vascular functions. Notably, cMAF emerges as the main transcription factor for human perivascular macrophages, suggesting conservation of this transcriptional module. During Alzheimer's disease (AD), human perivascular macrophages upregulate cMAF and IGF1 to enhance communication with vascular cells, and this response is abrogated in APOE4 carriers. Lastly, we explore an uncharacterized polymorphism in cMAF, providing evidence that the cMAF program is protective against AD. Targeting cMAF in perivascular macrophages may offer new therapeutic strategies for neurodegenerative and cerebrovascular diseases.Copyright © 2026 The Authors. Published by Elsevier Inc. When they removed cMAF from these immune cells in mice, the cells lost their normal characteristics and blood vessel function was disrupted. In humans with Alzheimer's disease, these immune cells increased cMAF production to protect blood vessels, but this protective response was weakened in people carrying a specific genetic variant called APOE4.

title: Involuntary Treatment in First-Episode Psychosis and Mania: A Retrospective Population-Based Cohort Study.
abstract: The study aimed to examine how involuntary status at first presentation affects 5-year trajectories of first-episode psychosis or first-episode mania (FEP/FEM).The authors conducted a population-based cohort study on FEP/FEM. Legal status at first episode was classified as involuntary or voluntary. Participants were followed up to 5 years to examine relapse, emergency department use, vocational status, and Social and Occupational Functioning Assessment Scale (SOFAS) scores. Relapse was compared by using log-rank tests; repeated-measures outcomes used mixed-effects models that adjusted for age and sex, with linear, logistic, or negative binomial regression as appropriate.The cohort included 200 individuals (voluntary, N=139; involuntary, N=61). The involuntary group was older than the voluntary group (p<0.001) and had greater illness severity (Clinical Global Impressions-Severity mean=5.5 vs. 5.1, p=0.002) at FEP/FEM. Time to relapse did not differ, nor did emergency department visits or psychiatric hospitalizations. Functioning improved at a similar rate in both groups; however, the involuntary group remained lower in functioning (SOFAS mean difference=-5.9, p=0.007) and had higher odds of being vocationally disengaged throughout follow-up (odds ratio=3.82, p=0.009).The authors found that involuntary treatment at FEP/FEM is common and is characterized by greater baseline illness severity. Involuntary status can serve as an entry point into care without excess long-term service utilization, and both groups showed similar rates of functional improvement. Persistently lower functioning and higher odds of vocational disengagement in the involuntary group support the need for targeted vocational interventions.

However, the involuntary group maintained persistently lower functioning (SOFAS mean difference −5.9) and had higher odds of vocational disengagement (odds ratio 3.82) throughout the study period. These findings suggest that involuntary treatment at first episode serves as an effective entry point into care without generating excess long-term service utilization, though targeted vocational interventions may.

title: Organ Donation-Reaching the Next Generation: To and Through High School.
abstract: Current transplant rates meet only 10% of the global demand, and the quintessential reason is the lack of donors. The same holds for blood donations, with the number of younger donors increasingly declining.This project tested the hypothesis that awareness, knowledge, and comfort levels of blood, organ, and bone marrow (BM) donation are low among high school students but can be raised through education.A pre-/post-comparative cohort study was conducted using a 59-item electronic questionnaire administered to students in grades 9, 10, and 11 in a single high school between November 2025 and January 2026 before and after a 10-minute presentation in high school classrooms.A total of 112 students participated (59% females, age 14-17). Awareness level (5-point scale from 1 (very aware) to 5 (not aware)) was moderate-high for organ and blood donation and moderate for BM (median (IQR) 2 (1-3), 2 (1-2) and 3 (2-4), respectively). Notable increases in knowledge pertained to the number of patients on the transplant list (from 55% pre to 83% post, P < .01), the number of organs that can be donated (from 14% to 22%, P < .01), and the volume of blood per blood donation (from 17% to 24%, P < .01). Comfort level (from 1 (very) to 5 (not at all)) was higher for deceased organ donation than for living organ donation and blood donation (median (IQR) 2 (1-3) vs. 3 (2-4) and 3 (3-4), P < .05) and increased for deceased organ and blood donation after the presentation (median (IQR) 1 (1-3) and 2 (1-3), respectively, P < .001 vs. pre).Dedicated peer-to-peer initiatives can raise awareness, knowledge, and comfort levels for blood, organ, and BM donation among high schoolers.Copyright © 2026 Elsevier Inc. They found that the transformed cancer cells showed immune evasion features similar to Hodgkin lymphoma that develops on its own, though an immune-suppressing protein called PD-L1 was less common in the earlier transformation subtype. These findings suggest that despite originating from different starting points, both types of transformation develop similar strategies to escape immune detection.

title: A Novel Arthroscopic Curette Microphone for Cartilage Defect Preparation in Joint Preservation Surgery: Proof-of-Concept and Tissue-Specific Debridement Audio Features.
abstract: ObjectiveDuring open chondral defect preparation, audible debridement sound changes mark the transition from deep cartilage to the calcified cartilage layer. We developed a novel curette microphone to characterize these audio feature differences during arthroscopic defect preparation.DesignA piezoelectric curette microphone was used to transmit and record debridement sound from 12 defect preparations (6 deep cartilage, 6 CCL) using human osteochondral allograft remnants. Live audio from the device was used to stop each debridement at the intended level, which was verified histologically. Spectrograms and power-spectral density plots were used to describe the audible transition from deep cartilage to CCL. We compared 22 audio features describing loudness, frequency, and complexity between the two tissue levels.ResultsCurette strokes against the deep cartilage were louder, higher frequency, and more acoustically complex than strokes against the CCL (p < 0.001). Cartilage debridement generated acoustically complex frequency bands above 2.5 kHz that diminished upon reaching the CCL. Debridement of the CCL produced a simpler audio profile that was predominant below 350 Hz.ConclusionThe novel curette microphone presented here transmits high-fidelity debridement audio that can be used to accurately distinguish tissue depth based on the distinct audio profiles of the deep cartilage and CCL.

title: Diagnostic challenges in light chain (AL) amyloidosis for high-risk patients.
abstract: Immunoglobulin light-chain (AL) amyloidosis is associated with high early mortality, particularly when the diagnosis occurs after advanced cardiac or multiorgan dysfunction has developed. Existing reviews have addressed diagnosis and management, but the evolving concept of high-risk disease in the modern therapeutic era has received less attention.This review explores how the definition of high-risk AL amyloidosis has evolved, with attention to organ involvement, cardiac biomarkers, clonal characteristics, tissue diagnosis, amyloid typing, multimodality imaging, artificial intelligence (AI)-supported diagnostic tools, multidimensional prognostic models, and novel B-cell maturation antigen (BCMA)-targeted immunotherapies. A focused Mayo Clinic literature search, supplemented by targeted PubMed searches by the authors, prioritized recent studies together with relevant consensus documents and landmark publications.Improving outcomes in AL amyloidosis will depend not only on the development of more potent therapies but also on the ability to deliver them before irreversible organ damage dictates the course of the illness. If advances in artificial intelligence, multimodal diagnostic tools, and highly active immunotherapies can be incorporated into everyday practice, the field may gradually move away from reacting to established high-risk disease and toward preventing patients from reaching that stage.

title: Psychometric validation of the Ru-SATED 4.0 multidimensional sleep health scale in a representative U.S. sample.
abstract: To develop and psychometrically validate a self-report questionnaire assessing multidimensional sleep health among U.S. adults using item response theory (IRT) and classic test theory analyses.The Ru-SATED 4.0 scale evaluates 6 sleep health dimensions (Regularity, Satisfaction, Alertness, Timing, Efficiency, Duration). We assessed the scale's comprehensibility with cognitive interviews (n=23) and Lexile analysis. We administered Ru-SATED and other self-reported measures to an adult sample (N=2,000; 18-89y) from the YouGov.com Internet panel, representative of the U.S. population in terms of age, sex, race/ethnicity, and education. We used factor analysis to identify the best combination of 6 items (1 per dimension); calibrated these using IRT Graded Response Models; and examined associations with validated measures to establish construct validity.Cognitive interviews confirmed comprehensibility of the items and response options. The final 6 items had excellent model fit in factor analysis (RMSEA=0.08, SRMR=0.03, CFI=0.97, TLI=0.95). IRT calibration showed individual items varied in their degree of severity assessed (location parameters) and amount of information contributed (discrimination parameters) to overall test scores (θ values). Ru-SATED scores demonstrated moderate internal consistency (r=0.7), convergent validity with other sleep scales (|r|=0.3-0.6), and test-retest reliability (r=0.6) one month later. Ru-SATED scores had smaller correlations with depression/anxiety measures (|r|=0.3-0.4), indicating discriminant validity, and differed significantly among individuals with and without self-reported sleep disorders (Cohen's d=0.93, 95% CI=-1.04-0.81).To our knowledge, this is the first study of Ru-SATED scores using IRT and classic test theory analyses. title: Global, Regional, and National Burden of Bone Cancers, 1990 to 2023, With Forecasts to 2050: A Systematic Analysis for the Global Burden of Disease Study 2023.
abstract: Primary bone cancers include multiple histologic types, with survival differing by age and location. Results from the Global Burden of Diseases, Injuries, and Risk Factors Study (GBD) 2023 were analyzed to support policies and initiatives worldwide.To estimate the global burden of bone cancer from 1990 to 2023 and forecast future trends to 2050.This systematic analysis estimated bone cancer incidence, mortality, and disability-adjusted life-years (DALYs) in 204 countries and territories grouped by GBD super-regions and World Bank income groups from 1990 to 2023, with forecasts through 2050. Individuals of all ages with bone cancers included in the GBD 2023 study were included in analyses. Data were analyzed from June 2023 to July 2025.The GBD 2023 study used standardized estimation methods to describe bone cancer incidence, mortality, and DALYs in 2023, as well as trends over the past 3 decades and forecasts through 2050. All estimates are presented with 95% uncertainty intervals (UIs), and age-standardized rates (ASRs) were calculated using GBD-specific age weights.In 2023, there were 111 000 (95% UI, 81 300-164 000) malignant bone cancer cases, 76 600 (95% UI, 60 700-96 300) deaths, and 3.02 million (95% UI, 2.29 million-3.96 million) DALYs globally. A bimodal age distribution was noted in both incidence (peaking at ages 10 to 14 years and 65 to 69 years) and mortality (peaking at ages 15 to 19 years and 65 to 69 years). The highest ASRs for incidence were in Southeast Asia, East Asia, and Oceania (1.6 per 100 000; 95% UI, 1.1-2.4), while Sub-Saharan Africa had the highest ASRs for DALYs (51.0 per 100 000; 95% UI, 27.7-79.7). By World Bank income group, upper-middle-income countries had the highest ASRs for incidence, whereas low-income countries exhibited the highest ASRs for both mortality and DALYs. Globally, incident cases, deaths, and DALYs increased from 1990 to 2023, while global mortality and DALY ASRs were relatively stable; high-income countries experienced a decline in mortality and DALY ASRs. Forecasts suggest a potential increase in global cases and deaths by 2050.In this systematic analysis, the burden of bone cancer varied by age, geography, and time, underscoring global disparities. These findings provide valuable insights to inform health system planning and resource allocation tailored to different settings.

llm_summary: Researchers analyzed global data from 1990 to 2023 to understand the burden of bone cancer worldwide, finding approximately 111,000 new cases and 76,600 deaths in 2023, with cases occurring most frequently in children and elderly people. The disease burden varied significantly by region and income level, with low-income countries experiencing the highest death rates despite having fewer total cases. Projections suggest the number of bone cancer cases and deaths may increase by 2050, highlighting the need for better health planning and resource allocation in different parts of the world.
llm_summary_expert: Researchers analyzed data from the Global Burden of Diseases, Injuries, and Risk Factors Study 2023 to estimate bone cancer incidence, mortality, and disability-adjusted life-years (DALYs) across 204 countries and territories from 1990 to 2023, with forecasts through 2050. In 2023, there were approximately 111,000 malignant bone cancer cases, 76,600 deaths, and 3.02 million DALYs globally, with a bimodal age distribution peaking in adolescence and older age groups. Age-standardized incidence rates were highest in Southeast Asia, East Asia, and Oceania, while Sub-Saharan Africa had the highest age-standardized DALY rates, and low-income countries exhibited the highest mortality and DALY rates despite upper-middle-income countries having the highest incidence rates. From 1990 to 2023, absolute numbers of incident cases, deaths, and DALYs increased globally, though age-standardized mortality and DALY rates remained relatively stable, with high-income countries experiencing declines in these rates.

title: Diagnostic insights from twenty years of bilateral inferior petrosal sinus sampling for cushing disease at mayo clinic.
abstract: Bilateral inferior petrosal sinus sampling (BIPSS) is used to distinguish pituitary from ectopic sources of ACTH-dependent Cushing syndrome (CS). We reviewed two decades of BIPSS experience at a single referral center to assess diagnostic performance, safety, and patient outcomes.Retrospective cohort study of patients who underwent BIPSS between 1998 and 2018.Of 156 adults undergoing BIPSS for ACTH-dependent CS, 143 had technically successful sampling and adequate follow-up and formed the evaluable cohort. A pituitary source was identified by a baseline central-to-peripheral ACTH ratio ≥2.0 or a post-stimulation (ovine corticotropin-releasing hormone [oCRH] or desmopressin) ratio ≥3.0.Diagnostic sensitivity, specificity, and lateralization accuracy of BIPSS. A confirmed pituitary source was defined by post-operative hypocortisolism after the index transsphenoidal operation; ACTH-positive corticotroph histology was supportive.Of the 143 patients, 109 had a definitive final diagnosis and formed the basis of the diagnostic analysis. BIPSS separated pituitary from ectopic ACTH sources with a sensitivity of 98.9% (95% CI 94.3-99.8) and a specificity of 85.7% (95% CI 60.1-96.0). The inter-petrosal gradient predicted the side of the adenoma in 59% of cases at baseline and 60% after stimulation (n = 100). Technical success was achieved in 94.2% of procedures, with no recorded major morbidity. Among the 94 patients in remission, 14 (15%) recurred over a mean of 3 years.Among patients in whom a definitive diagnosis was ultimately established, BIPSS distinguished pituitary from ectopic ACTH-dependent CS with high sensitivity and more modest specificity. Its value for adenoma lateralization is limited relative to current imaging. The cohort provides an oCRH-era reference point as practice moves to desmopressin.© 2026. llm_summary: Researchers reviewed twenty years of data on a diagnostic test called bilateral inferior petrosal sinus sampling, which helps doctors determine whether abnormal cortisol levels come from a pituitary gland tumor or elsewhere in the body. The test successfully distinguished between these two sources in nearly 99 out of 100 cases, though it was less reliable at pinpointing which side of the pituitary gland the tumor was located on. The procedure was safe with a 94% technical success rate and no major complications reported.
llm_summary_expert: Researchers examined bilateral inferior petrosal sinus sampling (BIPSS) outcomes in 143 adults with technically successful procedures and adequate follow-up who underwent testing between 1998 and 2018 to distinguish pituitary from ectopic sources of ACTH-dependent Cushing syndrome. BIPSS diagnostic performance was assessed using baseline central-to-peripheral ACTH ratios ≥2.0 or post-stimulation ratios ≥3.0 (with ovine corticotropin-releasing hormone or desmopressin), with pituitary source confirmation based on post-operative hypocortisolism or ACTH-positive corticotroph histology. title: Diagnostic Accuracy of Paracentral Acute Middle Maculopathy for Arteritic Anterior Ischemic Optic Neuropathy.
abstract: The purpose of this study was to evaluate the diagnostic accuracy of paracentral acute middle maculopathy (PAMM) detected on optical coherence tomography (OCT) macula for differentiating arteritic anterior ischemic neuropathy (AAION) from nonarteritic anterior ischemic optic neuropathy (NAION) in a multicenter United States cohort.Retrospective, multicenter diagnostic accuracy analysis.This study included patients diagnosed with AAION or NAION at the University of Minnesota, Mayo Clinic, and Johns Hopkins Wilmer Eye Institute between January 2020 and January 2025. Inclusion criteria consisted of patients older than 50 years who had obtained OCT macula within 14 days of symptom onset. AAION diagnoses were confirmed by temporal artery biopsy or positron emission tomography/computed tomography.Two masked fellowship-trained neuro-ophthalmologists independently evaluated OCT images for the presence of acute PAMM.Sensitivity, specificity, positive predictive value (PPV), and negative predictive value (NPV) of PAMM for AAION were calculated.A total of 119 patients were included, consisting of 27 patients with AAION and 92 patients with NAION. PAMM was identified in 18.5% of patients with AAION and 5.4% of patients with NAION (p = 0.032). The sensitivity, specificity, PPV, and NPV of PAMM for AAION was 19% [95% CI: 0.08-0.37], 94.6% [95% CI: 0.88-0.98], 50% [95% CI: 0.24-0.76], and79.8% [95% CI: 0.71-0.86] respectively. Three of five NAION patients with PAMM had provoked NAION associated with severe systemic hypoperfusion.PAMM is a highly specific but insensitive OCT marker for AAION. Although its presence should increase clinical suspicion for AAION, PAMM may rarely occur in patients with NAION particularly in the setting of systemic hypoperfusion and should be interpreted within the overall clinical context.Copyright © 2026. title: Respiratory and Gastrointestinal Mycobiome Profiles Identify Distinct Patient Clusters Associated with Asthma Control.
abstract: The human microbiome contributes to asthma pathogenesis, yet most studies have focused on bacterial communities. This pilot study aimed to characterize fungal communities across multiple body sites in adults with asthma and evaluate whether integrated multisite mycobiome profiles are associated with asthma control.We enrolled 24 adults with asthma evaluated at Mayo Clinic between 2020 and 2022. Oral wash, nasal swab, sputum, and stool samples were collected, and fungal communities were characterized using ITS2 sequencing. Multisite mycobiome data were integrated using an unsupervised clustering approach , with a two-cluster solution selected for exploratory clinical comparisons. Clusters were compared with respect to fungal composition, site-specific diversity metrics, and asthma control.Two patient clusters with distinct multisite mycobiome profiles were identified. Cluster 1 demonstrated poorer asthma control, with lower Asthma Control Test scores than Cluster 2 (median [IQR], 15.0 [13.0-17.5] vs. 18.0 [17.0-19.0]; p = 0.040). Compared with Cluster 2, Cluster 1 exhibited a higher relative abundance of Cladosporium in nasal and sputum samples, and greater sputum fungal diversity (p = 0.016). In contrast, Cluster 2 exhibited a higher relative abundance of Candida in stool and sputum samples. No significant differences in fungal diversity were observed in oral, nasal, or stool samples.Integrated multisite mycobiome profiling identified distinct fungal community patterns associated with asthma control, highlighting the need for larger, longitudinal studies to define their clinical relevance.Copyright © 2026. title: Sex-related differences in outcome of tricuspid valve surgery in severe isolated secondary tricuspid regurgitation.
abstract: Significant secondary tricuspid regurgitation (STR) is associated with worse morbidity and mortality. To-date, evidence on isolated tricuspid valve surgery in STR remains controversial, with uncertainty regarding management strategies. We aimed to investigate sex differences in the association of isolated tricuspid valve surgical repair/replacement (TVR) with outcomes of mortality and heart failure (HF) hospitalizations in STR.Patients with severe STR without significant aortic valve or organic mitral valve disease, congenital heart disease, pacemakers, previous valve intervention, malignancy, or end-stage kidney/liver disease were identified. Isolated TVR was studied as a time-dependent covariate in association with mortality and HF hospitalizations. Among 2857 patients (median age 76 years; 62% women), 143 underwent isolated TVR (58% repair; 42% replacement; 64% with low TRI-SCORE risk category) at a median of 56 days. Over a median of 1.6 (IQR 0.2-5.2) years, 1771 patients died and 1259 had HF hospitalization. When adjusting to age, comorbidities, left/right ventricular function, pulmonary hypertension, haemoglobin level, and dyspnoea, isolated TVR was associated with lower mortality in females (HR 0.54 95% CI 0.35-0.83) but not males (HR 1.29 95% CI 0.90-1.83), P-interaction<0.01; this remained the case when restricting to groups with normal left/right ventricular function. Isolated TVR was associated with HF hospitalization without interaction with sex (HR 0.68, 95% CI 0.46-0.998), P-interaction=0.51.Isolated TVR for STR was associated with decreased HF hospitalizations in both females and males but improved survival only in females.
