title: Technology Assistance and Fixed-Bearing Design Were Associated with Higher Revision-Free Survival at 15 Years After UKA: A Cohort Study of 2,234 Consecutive Knees.
abstract: Unicompartmental knee arthroplasty (UKA) is an alternative to total knee arthroplasty for isolated compartment osteoarthritis; however, concerns persist regarding its long-term durability. The purpose of this study was to evaluate revision-free survivorship, risk factors for revision, and clinical outcomes in a large consecutive series of contemporary UKAs.We retrospectively reviewed consecutive primary UKAs performed from 2000 to 2021 at a single tertiary academic center. Revision-free survivorship was estimated using a Kaplan-Meier analysis, and risk factors for revision were assessed using Cox proportional hazards modeling. Clinical outcomes were assessed using the Knee Society Score (KSS).A total of 2,234 UKAs were included. Fixed-bearing implants were used in 78% of UKAs. Technology assistance was used in 59% of UKAs (fluoroscopy, 43%; robotic assistance, 15%; computer navigation, 1%). The mean patient age was 65 years, the mean body mass index was 31 kg/m2, and 49% of UKAs were performed in female patients. Patient race was White in 97% of UKAs, and patient ethnicity was not Hispanic or Latino in 94%. Revision-free survivorship was 92% at 10 years and 85% at 15 years. Overall, 118 UKAs were revised, most commonly through conversion to total knee arthroplasty (97%). The most frequent indications for revision were progression of osteoarthritis in an adjacent compartment (41%), aseptic loosening (23%), unexplained pain (9%), and hardware failure (9%). Factors associated with a lower risk of revision in the univariable analysis included technology assistance (hazard ratio [HR], 0.4; p < 0.01) and high surgeon volume (HR, 0.5; p < 0.01). Mobile-bearing design (HR, 1.9; p < 0.01) was associated with an increased risk of revision in the univariable analysis. The mean KSS improved from 47 preoperatively to 75 at 5 years postoperatively (p < 0.001).In this large consecutive series, UKA demonstrated excellent long-term survivorship, with an approximately 1% annual risk of revision through 15 years. Technology assistance, a fixed-bearing implant design, and high surgeon volume were each associated with a lower risk of revision, underscoring the importance of operative technique and implant selection in achieving durable outcomes.Therapeutic Level III. title: Renal Decline Before Heart Transplantation in Left Ventricular Assist Device-Supported Recipients: United Network for Organ Sharing Analysis.
abstract: Although baseline renal impairment and post-heart transplantation (HT) dialysis are established clinical predictors, the prognostic impact of pre-HT renal decline in patients bridged with left ventricular assist devices (LVADs) remains unclear. We retrospectively analyzed patients from the United Network for Organ Sharing registry who underwent HT following LVAD support between 2009 and 2024. Renal decline was defined as a greater than or equal to 40% reduction in estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) from listing to HT. Among 10,454 patients, 624 (6.0%) experienced pre-HT renal decline. Patients with renal decline had longer waitlist durations (median 297 vs. 197 days; p < 0.001), lower eGFR at HT (42.0 vs. 70.6 ml/min/1.73 m2; p < 0.001), and higher rates of post-HT dialysis (23.7 vs. 12.8%; p < 0.001). Independent predictors of renal decline included longer waitlist time and perioperative blood transfusions, whereas HeartMate 3 LVAD use was protective. Renal decline was independently associated with an increased risk of post-HT dialysis (adjusted odds ratio [aOR]: 2.64) and all-cause mortality (adjusted hazard ratio [aHR]: 1.16), with post-HT dialysis strongly predicting mortality (aHR: 3.48). Renal deterioration is a significant predictor of post-HT dialysis and mortality in LVAD-bridged patients. Incorporating renal trajectory into risk stratification may enhance candidate selection and promote perioperative renal protection strategies.Copyright © ASAIO 2026.

title: A phase I trial of intravenous vesicular stomatitis virus expressing thyroidal sodium iodide symporter (NIS) and human interferon beta (hIFNβ) in metastatic or recurrent endometrial cancer.
abstract: We report the results of a Phase I trial of intravenous (IV) vesicular stomatitis virus (VSV) engineered to express human interferon beta (hIFNβ) and thyroidal sodium iodide symporter (NIS) in patients with stage IV or recurrent endometrial cancer (EC).Eligible patients with stage IV or recurrent EC with largest tumor diameter ≤ 5 cm were enrolled and received a single IV infusion of VSV-hIFNβ-NIS in a standard '3 + 3' dose escalation. Five dose-levels were planned. Primary endpoint was determination of the maximum tolerated dose (MTD). Secondary endpoints included pharmacokinetics, pharmacodynamics, tumor response, and immune correlates. An exploratory post-hoc analysis evaluated clinical responses to subsequent immune checkpoint inhibitor (ICI)-based therapies.From 9/15/2017-1/10/23, 21 eligible patients were treated. One patient at DL2 experienced grade 3 dehydration associated with cytokine release syndrome (CRS) and one experienced transient grade 4 asymptomatic lymphopenia, prompting protocol modification of the DLT definition. One of six patients at DL4 experienced grade 3 delirium meeting DLT criteria. Dose escalation to DL5 was not feasible because of investigational agent production limitations; MTD was not reached. The most common treatment related AEs were transient hematologic toxicities, liver enzyme elevations, and CRS. At day 29, 8 patients had progressive disease (PD); 1 entered hospice due to PD before day 29. Two patients had stable disease for at least 6 months following VSV-hIFNβ-NIS. Of the 15 patients who received subsequent ICI-based therapy following VSV-hIFNβ-NIS, 4 had durable SD with a median follow up of 40.4 (95% CI 30.4-not reached) months.IV VSV-hIFNβ-NIS had an acceptable safety profile in patients with advanced or recurrent EC. Further investigation of VSV-hIFNβ-NIS, particularly in combination with immune checkpoint blockade, is warranted.Copyright © 2026 Elsevier Inc. All rights reserved.

title: Femoral Neck Morphology: A Computed-Tomography-Based Anatomic Framework Informs Medial Collar Design for Contemporary Collared Cementless Femoral Stems.
abstract: The level of femoral neck resection in total hip arthroplasty (THA) affects implant position, restoration of limb length, and degree of cortical support available for collared cementless stems. With increasing use of computed tomography (CT)-based planning and collared stems, understanding femoral neck and calcar morphology at the osteotomy plane is valuable. The aims of this study were to (1) quantify femoral neck cortical thickness at the achieved osteotomy plane reconstructed from postoperative imaging and adjacent levels, (2) assess the effect of osteotomy height on regional cortical support, and (3) determine the medial collar length that best matches cortical thickness at the osteotomy plane.We reviewed preoperative CT scans from 100 consecutive primary THAs performed by a single surgeon using a single cementless femoral stem design. Using multiplanar reconstruction, calcar cortical thickness was measured on axial images at the osteotomy plane (zero mm) and at standardized levels 5.30 mm proximal and 5.30 mm distal to that plane. At each level, thickness was recorded at five locations (anterior, posterior, medial, antero-medial, and postero-medial). The medial cortical thickness at the osteotomy plane was used to determine the collar length, minimizing absolute overhang/underhang, which corresponds to its median.Cortical thickness increased from proximal to distal levels, most prominently in the medial (P < 0.001) and postero-medial (P < 0.001) regions. Antero-medial thickness increased from the proximal level to the osteotomy plane (P = 0.004), but did not increase further distally (P = 0.641). For this cohort and osteotomy technique, the collar length minimizing mean absolute overhang or underhang was 5.3 mm, the median medial cortical thickness at the osteotomy plane.At and around the planned femoral neck osteotomy plane, medial and postero-medial cortices were thickest and increased in thickness distally, whereas antero-medial thickness plateaued. These data provide an anatomic reference that may inform cementless femoral stem collar geometry and future implant design.Copyright © 2026 Elsevier Inc. All rights reserved.

title: Artificial Intelligence as a Bridge to Gaps in Delirium Prediction, Detection, and Management.
abstract: Delirium affects up to one-third of hospitalized older adults and is associated with adverse outcomes. Despite its clinical importance and the availability of validated screening tools, current care gaps extend beyond under-recognition to inconsistent risk stratification, workforce constraints, documentation burden, fragmented intervention delivery, and practical challenges with monitoring of response. We review how artificial intelligence (AI) could bridge these gaps and distinguish model development and validation, real-world clinical implementation, and emerging concepts in delirium care.Prediction models leveraging multimodal health record data, including structured variables and unstructured clinical notes, report good discrimination for delirium risk stratification, but only a few models have been integrated into clinical practice. A live multimodal machine learning model increased targeted delirium detection, yet a pre-post comparative study found a longer length of stay; improved recognition alone therefore does not equate with improved outcomes. Natural language processing, large language models, computer vision, ambient sensing, and wearable technologies enable more continuous, objective, and less labor-intensive assessment compared with traditional screening methods, but evidence remains limited with concerns about false positives and generalizability. AI-supported delirium management through reinforcement learning and digital twins is currently largely conceptual. Responsible AI adoption requires a clearly defined intended use, external validation, action pathways, equitable performance, privacy and security, consent and transparency, clinician oversight, patient preferences, and post-deployment monitoring.AI is most defensible as an adjunct that connects evidence-based delirium care to reliable execution rather than as a replacement for clinical assessment. Prospective comparative studies should evaluate patient outcomes, resource use, and balancing measures.© 2026 The American Geriatrics Society.

title: Overlooked Writings of Sir William Gowers on Neurology in General Practice, Shorthand, and Education.
abstract: Sir William Richard Gowers (1845-1915), long hailed as the "Father of Clinical Neurology," has been the subject of 2 biographies and many essays relating to his contributions to the study of nervous disorders. Yet, despite extensive bibliographies, several of his publications have hitherto escaped notice. We reviewed archival sources and digital repositories to identify overlooked works. This led to the discovery of his contributions to George Alexander Gibson's 1901 Text-Book of Medicine, which distilled neurology for the general practitioner, as well as lectures and articles on shorthand and education, reflecting his interest in communication, educational practice, and the process of learning. Gowers advocated cultivating ambidexterity in youth, reasoning that it may confer resilience against neurologic injury later in life. Recovered only through primary source research, these writings broaden our understanding of Gowers' intellectual range, showing him not only as a pioneering specialist in the study of nervous disorders but also as a physician engaged with general medicine and educational reform.

title: A Comparison of Two Strategies for Converting to Adalimumab Biosimilarsa.
abstract: We retrospectively compared 2 strategies for adalimumab biosimilar conversion at an academic medical center to better understand the effects of each strategy.The formulary for our institution is managed by physician- and pharmacist-led task forces, in collaboration with our specialty pharmacy and pharmacy benefit manager. We implemented 2 phased strategies to increase adalimumab biosimilar utilization. First, we added preferred biosimilars to the formulary at parity to reference product and relied on prescribers to promote conversion. Second, we added an interchangeable biosimilar and removed reference product from the formulary while leveraging specialty pharmacy workflows for prescription conversions, streamlined facility inventory, and minimized dependence on prescriber workflows. For both strategies, we evaluated prescribing trends, dispensing data, and pharmaceutical spend for all medical center patients, specialty pharmacy patients, and patients with the top 3 specialty pharmacy payers.During phase 1 (quarter [Q] 2 of 2023 [2Q23] to 1Q24), reference product dispensing remained largely unchanged (<5% reduction). Phase 2 (2Q24 to 2Q25) resulted in a significant reduction in specialty pharmacy dispenses of reference product, from 95.7% to 19.0%. This phase also resulted in a 76.0% reduction in medical center adalimumab/biosimilar spend. At the end of phase 2, biosimilar accounted for 42.6% of all medical center patient prescriptions. title: Recommendations for the Examination, Processing, and Reporting of Non-neoplastic Pericardial Diseases: A Consensus Statement on Pericardial Disease from the Society for Cardiovascular Pathology and the Association for European Cardiovascular Pathology.
abstract: Recent advances in the evaluation and management of pericardial diseases highlight the importance of accurate pathologic assessment. Despite these current developments, the handling, processing, and reporting of pericardial specimens have not been formally addressed in recent years. This consensus document is intended to enable the pathologist to evaluate the pericardium as a surgical specimen as well as at postmortem examination, with particular emphasis on standardized gross and microscopic assessment of the pericardium.An international expert panel comprising volunteer members of the Society for Cardiovascular Pathology and the Association for European Cardiovascular Pathology was convened to develop consensus recommendations. Strong agreement on best practices was achieved through a series of in-person and hybrid virtual meetings. The document outlines recommendations for the handling and processing of surgical pericardial specimens, including appropriate histochemical and immunohistochemical stains and ancillary diagnostic studies. Guidance for the systematic examination of the pericardium at autopsy is also provided. In addition, a nomenclature for common and well-defined pathologic processes is proposed, together with relevant differential diagnoses. The recommended terminology encompasses the predominant inflammatory cell infiltrates and the spectrum of organization from fibrinous pericarditis to established pericardial fibrosis.This consensus document provides a standardized framework for the pathologic evaluation of the pericardium with the goal of improving diagnostic consistency, facilitating communication among clinicians and pathologists, and promoting uniformity in clinical practice and research.Copyright © 2026. title: Artificial intelligence-derived splenic response in cardiac positron emission tomography is associated with major adverse cardiovascular events: a multi-site study.
abstract: Inadequate pharmacologic stress may limit the diagnostic and prognostic accuracy of myocardial perfusion imaging (MPI). The splenic ratio (SR), a measure of stress adequacy, has emerged as a potential imaging biomarker. We developed an artificial intelligence (AI) method to derive SR and evaluated the prognostic value in a large multicentre 82Rb-PET cohort undergoing regadenoson stress testing.We retrospectively analysed 16 650 patients from six sites in the REFINE PET registry with clinically indicated MPI and linked clinical outcomes. SR was calculated using fully automated algorithms as the ratio of splenic uptake at stress vs. rest. Patients were stratified by SR into decile groups. The primary outcome was major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE). Survival analysis was conducted using Kaplan-Meier and Cox proportional hazards models adjusted for clinical and imaging covariates, including myocardial flow reserve (MFR ≥2 vs. <2) and presence of ischaemia. The cohort had a median age of 69 years, with 59% male patients. Common risk factors included hypertension (81%), dyslipidaemia (77%), diabetes (35%), and prior coronary artery disease (31%). Median follow-up was 3.4 years. Patients with high SR in the testing cohort (n = 950) had an increased risk of MACE [hazard ratio (HR) 1.19, 95% confidence interval (CI) 1.06-1.34, P = 0.005]. Among testing patients with preserved MFR (≥2; n = 8067), high SR remained independently associated with MACE (HR 1.43, 95% CI 1.20-1.70, P < 0.001). Even among patients with preserved MFR and no ischaemia in the testing cohort(MFR≥2, SDS<2; n = 6508), high SR remained independently associated with MACE (HR 1.54 95% CI 1.26-1.88, P < 0.001).Elevated AI-derived SR was independently associated with adverse cardiovascular outcomes, including among patients with preserved MFR. These findings support SR as a novel, automated imaging biomarker for risk stratification in 82Rb PET MPI.© The Author(s) 2026. title: CT and MRI in periprocedural transcatheter mitral valve replacement: expert recommendations by the European Society of Cardiovascular Radiology (ESCR) and the North American Society for Cardiovascular Imaging (NASCI).
abstract: Transcatheter mitral valve replacement (TMVR) is a minimally invasive treatment option for symptomatic patients with severe mitral valve disease who are at high surgical risk or ineligible for open-heart surgery. The procedure has been associated with improved quality of life and functional status in selected patients and is increasingly recognized as a valuable therapeutic option in the management of complex mitral valve disorders. A multidisciplinary Heart Team is essential to ensure the clinical success of TMVR, and imaging specialists play a central role in the preprocedural assessment for patient and device selection, during the procedure, to guide and monitor the implantation, and after the procedure, for follow-up and for the correct diagnosis of short- or long-term complications. Echocardiography is required for initial diagnosis, for assessment of valve hemodynamics, intraprocedural guidance and monitoring. However, a multimodality approach including CT and/or MRI is frequently needed to correctly manage the phase of preprocedural planning and the diagnosis of complications. This consensus document, developed by a working group of experts from the European Society of Cardiovascular Radiology (ESCR) and the North American Society for Cardiovascular Imaging (NASCI), provides evidence-based recommendations for CT and cardiac MRI acquisition and post-processing in procedural planning and postprocedural evaluation in patients undergoing TMVR. Emphasis is placed on the technical requirements and standardization of imaging protocols, which must account for the heterogeneity of imaging equipment used in clinical settings. The document also outlines recommendations for all necessary preprocedural measures to ensure consistency, accuracy, and effective communication among specialists. KEY POINTS: Question How can CT and MRI acquisition, measurement, and reporting for TMVR be standardized to support accurate procedural planning, device selection, and follow-up? Findings This expert consensus provides recommendations for standardized CT and MRI protocols, key measurements, and structured reporting throughout TMVR planning and follow-up. Clinical relevance CT and MRI assessment may improve patient selection, procedural planning, multidisciplinary communication, and detection of postprocedural complications, supporting safer and more consistent TMVR practice across centers.© 2026. title: Agentic AI-Generated vs. Clinician-Authored Hospital Course Narratives for Cardiology Hospitalizations: A Blinded Physician Evaluation.
abstract: Background: Discharge summaries are essential for safe transitions of care, but writing the hospital course narrative is time intensive. Large language models can generate plausible clinical narratives, yet prior approaches often rely on static inputs and remain vulnerable to omissions and factual inconsistencies. Methods: We developed an electronic health record (EHR)-integrated agentic artificial intelligence (AI) system that uses Gemini 2.5 Pro and Model Context Protocol tools to retrieve clinical notes, diagnostic reports, diagnoses, medications, and appointments on demand. In this retrospective, blinded, paired study, 50 inpatient cardiology encounters were randomly selected from admissions July 13 to 27, 2024, at Mayo Clinic, Rochester, Minnesota. Five physicians rated AI-generated and clinician-authored hospital course narratives for each encounter (250 ratings) on 0-to-10 scales for overall quality, clarity, completeness, accuracy, and readability and indicated a preference. The primary outcome was the paired difference in overall quality (linear mixed-effects model with crossed random intercepts for encounter and reviewer). Secondary domains were analyzed similarly with Bonferroni adjustment, and preference with a crossed random-effects logistic model. Results: Clinician-authored narratives were preferred in 132 ratings (52.8%) and AI-generated narratives in 118 (47.2%) (odds ratio for clinician-authored preference, 1.12; 95% CI, 0.71 to 1.78). Overall quality did not differ significantly (mean, 7.27 AI-generated versus 7.42 clinician-authored; difference, -0.15; 95% CI, -0.86 to 0.56; p=0.627). AI-generated narratives were rated higher for clarity (0.36; 95% CI, 0.07 to 0.65) and readability (0.72; 95% CI, 0.20 to 1.24) but lower for completeness (-0.84; 95% CI, -1.36 to -0.32) and accuracy (-0.35; 95% CI, -0.66 to -0.05). After Bonferroni correction, only lower completeness remained significant (adjusted p=0.012). Conclusions: Hospital course narratives generated by the EHR-integrated agentic AI system did not differ significantly from clinician-authored narratives in physician-rated overall quality or preference. Lower completeness supports continued clinician review before use in the medical record.

title: Propionate, a short-chain fatty acid, is associated with disease activity in pediatric-onset multiple sclerosis.
abstract: Short-chain fatty acids (SCFAs), metabolites found in fermented foods and produced by colonic bacterial fermentation of dietary fibers, may mediate gut-brain axis crosstalk influencing the course of multiple sclerosis (MS). In this study, SCFAs are measured in plasma and paired stool samples by targeted mass spectrometry in a large cohort of deeply phenotyped individuals shortly after MS onset. Propionate is consistently associated with a protective effect on three clinical and imaging activity-related outcomes. Findings are reproduced in an equally large external cohort for plasma and stool measurements. Despite the correlation between plasma SCFAs and SCFA-producing gut microbial taxa, propionate levels are not correlated with dietary fiber, suggesting that intake may not be sufficient to modulate its levels and ensuing inflammation. In conclusion, propionate is consistently associated with lower disease activity, and exogenous administration may be more likely than fiber supplementation to confer protective effects on MS activity in proof-of-concept clinical trials.Copyright © 2026 The Authors. title: MONKEY Challenge: Machine-learning for Optimal detection of iNflammatory cells in KidnEY transplant biopsies.
abstract: Accurate quantification of inflammatory cells in Periodic Acid-Schiff (PAS)-stained kidney transplant biopsies is essential for Banff classification but remains subjective and labor-intensive. To address this, the MONKEY challenge benchmarked deep learning (DL) methods for automated detection of mononuclear leukocytes and their subtypes.A multicenter dataset of 118 biopsies with co-registered PAS and immunohistochemically restained slides, comprising over 131,000 annotated cells, was used. The algorithms were evaluated on hold-out validation and test set using Free-response Receiver Operating Characteristic (FROC) analysis, alongside precision, recall, and F1-scores.Across diverse architectures, performance converged, with the top models achieving F1-scores up to 0.75 for overall detection. Lymphocyte detection performed well (F1 up to 0.78), whereas monocyte detection remained more challenging (F1 up to 0.47). To explore the potential clinical applicability of automated inflammatory cell detection, the winning model was integrated with renal tissue segmentation models, enabling compartment-specific evaluation and quantitative assessment of Banff-related lesions. In an independent multicenter cohort of 180 kidney transplant biopsies, DL-derived quantitative measurements demonstrated strong correlations with consensus pathologist scoring for several inflammation-related Banff lesions, particularly total inflammation and interstitial inflammation.This study establishes the first multicenter, PAS-based, IHC-validated benchmark for inflammatory cell detection and provides a clinically grounded resource to support the development of robust, generalizable AI systems for transplant pathology. Beyond benchmark performance, our extended tissue-specific analyses demonstrate that inflammatory cell detection on routine PAS slides can be anatomically contextualized and translated into quantitative measurements that align with conventional Banff lesion assessment, providing a foundation for future AI-assisted evaluation of kidney transplant biopsies.Copyright © 2026. When integrated with tissue analysis tools, the AI system's measurements correlated well with expert pathologist assessments, suggesting potential for assisting doctors in evaluating transplant health.

Performance was evaluated using Free-response Receiver Operating Characteristic analysis with precision, recall, and F1-scores as primary endpoints, with top models achieving F1-scores of 0.75 for overall inflammatory cell detection, 0.78 for lymphocytes, and 0.47 for monocytes. title: Pathology of the Parietal Pericardium: A Consensus Statement on Pericardial Disease from the Society for Cardiovascular Pathology and the Association for European Cardiovascular Pathology.
abstract: Pericardial diseases encompass a broad spectrum of infectious, inflammatory, metabolic, traumatic, iatrogenic, and neoplastic disorders occurring in the setting of both localized and systemic conditions. Advances in understanding of the pathogenesis and diagnosis of pericardial disease have been substantial. Despite extensive literature on the clinical aspects of pericardial disease, relatively few studies have focused on its pathologic features.An international panel from volunteer members of the Society for Cardiovascular Pathology and the Association for European Cardiovascular Pathology conducted a comprehensive review of the literature to develop a consensus document on the recommendations for pathologic evaluation of the parietal pericardium. This first document summarizes our state-of-the-art understanding of the etiological and morphological aspects of pericardial diseases, including pericardial effusions, cardiac tamponade, infectious and non-infectious pericarditis, and constrictive pericarditis, and incorporates updated clinical definitions and diagnostic criteria.This consensus review highlights the role of pathology in the diagnosis of pericardial disease. Future efforts should explore establishing contemporary reference ranges for normal pericardial fluid volume, refining the pathologic characterization of pericarditis, correlating histopathologic findings with advanced cardiac imaging, and elucidating the molecular mechanisms driving the progression of pericardial fibrosis to constrictive disease.Copyright © 2026. title: Learning through Caregiving: A Qualitative Study of Reflections From a Medical Student Elective for New Parents.
abstract: Many new parents in medicine, particularly medical students, do not feel supported by their institutions. One structural support present in most pediatric residencies is a new parent elective; however this is rarely available for students. This study seeks to better understand the lived experience of medical students during a new parent/caregiving elective at the University of Minnesota to learn how we can better support student parents.We conducted a retrospective qualitative study of students' written reflections during a caregiving elective, using reflexive thematic analysis through an inductive approach to identify common patterns and ideas within the dataset.We analyzed 54 reflections from 16 students (39% of invited participants (n=41)). We found three themes: 1) Students' experiences of the common challenges of early parenthood prompts or leads to personal transformation; 2) Students rely on relationships from inside and outside of medicine to find support and community; and 3) The intersections of parenthood, patienthood, and medical training influence how students interact with the medical system and contribute to their identities as future physicians. As students experienced parenting, they often related these experiences to their medical training in ways that likely affect their growing identities as future physicians.Student parents who participated in this caregiving elective described common experiences of becoming a parent and utilized these experiences to develop skills that will help them become better doctors. They also appreciated support from this elective. Additional institutional support may better facilitate their emerging parent and physician identities.Copyright © 2026. Published by Elsevier Inc.

title: Mitochondrial-derived peptide humanin alleviates AKI-to-CKD transition by inhibiting TRIM28-mediated ubiquitination of Suclg1.
abstract: Acute kidney injury (AKI) resulting from ischemia-reperfusion injury (IRI) may subsequently progress to chronic kidney disease (CKD) and eventually end-stage renal disease (ESRD). Humanin, a mitochondria-derived peptide, has been implicated in various physiological and pathological processes and exhibits cytoprotective effects against inflammation, apoptosis, and oxidative stress. Nevertheless, its role in the AKI-to-CKD transition remains poorly understood. This study showed that renal humanin expression was downregulated in a murine IRI model and this reduction was significantly correlated with renal function decline and kidney fibrosis progression. Exogenous supplementation of S14G-humanin (HN) was found to protect against kidney fibrosis induced by IRI. Mechanistically, HN attenuated kidney fibrosis by stabilizing succinate-CoA ligase subunit alpha (Suclg1) by inhibiting tripartite motif-containing protein 28 (TRIM28)-mediated ubiquitination of Suclg1. Inhibition of Suclg1 abolished the renoprotective effects of HN, underscoring the critical role of Suclg1 in the AKI-to-CKD transition. Moreover, HN-mediated upregulation of Suclg1 reduced superoxide dismutase 2 (SOD2) succinylation, linking metabolic reprogramming to mitochondrial dysfunction and fibrotic progression. Collectively, these findings reveal a critical role of humanin in mitigating kidney fibrosis and identify Suclg1 as a promising therapeutic target in the AKI-to-CKD transition.Copyright © 2026. abstract: To explore rural-and nonrural differences in healthcare utilization in primary and endocrinology care among adults with diabetes who experienced hypoglycemia or hyperglycemic crises requiring emergency department (ED) or hospital care.This is a retrospective cohort study from a large integrated healthcare system between January 1, 2020, and October 1, 2024. We identified adults (≥18 years) with diabetes who had an ED encounter or hospitalization with a primary diagnosis of hypoglycemic or hyperglycemic (diabetic ketoacidosis or hyperosmolar hyperglycemic state) crisis, subset to those in rural areas (population <20,000) or nonrural areas, and quantified differences in rates of subsequent healthcare utilization with primary care and endocrinology at 30, 60 and 90 days post-discharge.We identified 1258 individuals experiencing an index hypoglycemic (N = 677: 26.4% rural, 73.6% urban) or hyperglycemic (N = 581: 19.3% rural, 80.1% urban) crisis. Within 30 days of discharge, rural residents had fewer primary care clinician encounters (39.5% vs 49.3%, P = 0.003) and endocrinologist encounters (8.6% vs 16.3%, P = 0.001) than urban residents. title: Development and Internal Validation of the RMC-COMPASS Clinical Prognostic Model for SMARCB1-deficient Renal Medullary Carcinoma.
abstract: SMARCB1-deficient renal medullary carcinoma (RMC) is a rare, highly aggressive malignancy affecting predominantly young individuals with sickle hemoglobinopathies. However, no disease-specific prognostic tools exist. We aimed to develop and internally validate a prognostic model for overall survival using routinely available variables measured at diagnosis.This single-institution retrospective cohort study included 180 patients with SMARCB1-deficient RMC (2003-2025). In total, 16 prespecified candidate predictors were evaluated. For internal validation, the complete variable and distribution selection process was repeated within 1000 bootstrap resamples across 50 multiply imputed datasets. Coefficients of the final log-normal accelerated failure time model were uniformly shrunk by the resulting optimism-corrected calibration slope, and clinical utility was assessed by 24-mo decision curve analysis (DCA).Renal Medullary Carcinoma Clinical and Outcomes Model for Prognostic Assessment and Survival Stratification (RMC-COMPASS) retained Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group performance status, number of involved anatomic disease sites beyond the primary tumor, neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio, and corrected calcium. The optimism-corrected C-index was 0.64 (95% confidence interval [CI] 0.61-0.71) and the calibration slope was 0.895 (95% CI 0.589-1.20). RMC-COMPASS showed higher discrimination than the International Metastatic Renal Cell Carcinoma Database Consortium score (C-index 0.58) and DCA demonstrated positive net benefit across clinically relevant thresholds. Limitations include the single-institution design and lack of external validation.RMC-COMPASS is the first internally validated prognostic model for SMARCB1-deficient RMC. It provides individualized survival estimates through a freely available web-based calculator (https://trialdesign.org/one-page-shell.html#RMC-COMPASS) to support prognostic counseling, while prespecified risk groups are intended for stratification in future prospective studies. The model is not validated for treatment selection and requires external validation before routine clinical use.Copyright © 2026 European Association of Urology. Published by Elsevier B.V. title: Unusual Morphologic Variants of Solitary Fibrous Tumor: A Case Series of 17 Cases Featuring 10 Distinct Histomorphologies.
abstract: Solitary fibrous tumors (SFTs) are mesenchymal neoplasms characterized by spindled-to-ovoid cells, fibrous stroma, prominent staghorn vasculature and harbor characteristic NAB2::STAT6 fusion. Although most SFTs are readily recognized histologically, some display unusual morphologic features that mimic other mesenchymal neoplasms and obscure the diagnosis.Following institutional review board approval, we identified 17 SFTs with unusual morphologic features from our institutional archives. Clinicopathologic features, immunohistochemistry, molecular findings, and Demicco risk stratification were reviewed. Molecular confirmation was available by RNA-based next-generation sequencing fusion panel.The cohort included 17 tumors (9 males, 8 females). Sites included deep soft tissue of pelvis (n=3), thigh (2), abdominal wall (1), dermis of temple (1), sinonasal tract (2) and visceral sites including liver (n=3), lung (n=2), brain (1), thyroid (1), and stomach (1). Median tumor size was 6 cm (range 3.5-15 cm). Histologic patterns included angiosarcoma-like (n=2), pleomorphic liposarcoma-like (n=2), osteosarcoma-like (n=2) with one showing true heterologous osteosarcomatous differentiation, GLI1-altered neoplasm-like (n=3), conventional small round cell morphology (n=4) including one with Ewing-sarcoma-like immunophenotype, pseudoglandular (n=1), low-grade fibromyxoid sarcoma-like (n=1), soft tissue angiofibroma-like (n=1), and sinonasal glomangiopericytoma-like (n=1). Five tumors were considered morphologically consistent with dedifferentiated SFT. All tumors retained at least focal conventional SFT morphology. STAT6 IHC was positive in 16/17 tumors; NAB2::STAT6 fusion was confirmed in all 11 cases tested.SFTs may display a wide range of histologic patterns mimicking other benign and malignant mesenchymal neoplasms. Awareness of these variants and integration of IHC and molecular studies are critical to avoid misdiagnosis.Copyright © 2026. Published by Elsevier Inc.

title: Initial Diabetes Therapy After Coronary Artery Bypass Grafting and Long-Term Outcomes.
abstract: Type 2 diabetes (T2D) is common among patients undergoing coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG), but optimal post-CABG glucose-lowering therapy remains uncertain.We conducted a retrospective cohort study using the OptumLabs Data Warehouse of adults with T2D undergoing isolated CABG from 2012-2024. Follow-up began 30 days after discharge. Glucose-lowering therapy was modeled as a time-varying exposure with patients contributing no-observed-therapy person-time until the first qualifying post-discharge fill. Pairwise comparisons used stabilized inverse probability of treatment weighting. The primary outcome was all-cause mortality; secondary outcomes were heart failure hospitalization, stroke, and repeat coronary revascularization.Among 19,237 patients, 24.9% had no observed post-discharge therapy, 42.8% received metformin, 22.9% received insulin, and 9.4% received GLP-1RA/SGLT2i therapy. All active therapies were associated with lower mortality compared with no observed therapy, including GLP-1RA/SGLT2i (HR 0.71, 95% CI 0.58-0.87), metformin (HR 0.60, 95% CI 0.55-0.66), and insulin (HR 0.75, 95% CI 0.67-0.84). Among active therapies, metformin was associated with lower mortality than insulin (HR, 0.61 [0.54-0.70]); GLP-1RA/SGLT2i comparisons with metformin and insulin were less precise. Metformin was also associated with lower cumulative incidence of heart failure hospitalization than no observed therapy and insulin, and lower stroke incidence than insulin.Observed glucose-lowering therapy initiation after CABG was associated with lower mortality compared with no observed therapy across all active treatment groups. These findings highlight a potential care gap and suggest that proper initiation of diabetes therapy after CABG represents an important opportunity to improve long-term outcomes following surgical revascularization.

title: Virtual liver biopsy for detecting steatohepatitis in chemotherapy-treated patients: comparison with whole-liver radiomics and external validation.
abstract: Chemotherapy-associated steatohepatitis (CASH) increases the risk of postoperative liver failure and mortality in patients undergoing liver surgery. However, non-invasive diagnosis remains an unmet need. Radiomics has potential for characterizing liver parenchyma. This study evaluated the performance of a virtual liver biopsy for CASH prediction, comparing it with whole-liver radiomic analysis.Two retrospective series of patients undergoing hepatectomy for colorectal liver metastases were analyzed: the public "Colorectal-Liver-Metastases" dataset (training and internal validation) and a monocenter series from Humanitas Research Hospital (external validation). Inclusion criteria were preoperative chemotherapy (≥ 2 months) and post-chemotherapy CT (thickness ≤ 5 mm). IBSI-compliant radiomic features were extracted from whole-liver parenchyma and from a virtual biopsy (manually segmented 2-mL cylinder of non-tumoral liver parenchyma). Estimated liver volume (eLV) was computed using three orthogonal diameters. Four XGBoost models were developed (70/30 split, 5-fold cross-validation): clinical; clinical + VB-radiomics (ViB); clinical + VB-radiomics + eLV (ViBE+); clinical + whole-liver radiomics (WholeLiver).One hundred eighty patients were included: 105 internal (63 males, mean age 58.9 years, 38% CASH+) and 75 external (44 males, mean age 62.4 years, 19% CASH+). WholeLiver and ViBE+ models achieved excellent and comparable performance in internal validation (WholeLiver: AUC = 0.857 (95% BS-CI: 0.676-0.954), accuracy = 0.774 (95% BS-CI: 0.613-0.903); ViBE + : AUC = 0.831 (95% BS-CI: 0.549-0.956), accuracy = 0.839 (95% BS-CI: 0.710-0.935); p = 0.814), outperforming ViB model (AUC = 0.724 (95% BS-CI: 0.483-0.896), accuracy = 0.774 (95% BS-CI: 0.613-0.903)). SHAP analysis confirmed liver volume metrics as key predictors. In external validation, the ViBE+ model achieved AUC = 0.745 (95% BS-CI: 0.604-0.886) and accuracy = 0.680 (95% BS-CI: 0.562-0.783).Virtual biopsy provides a reproducible, non-invasive radiomic sampling strategy for CASH prediction. Combined with liver volume metrics, it achieves performance comparable to whole-liver analysis, supporting its potential clinical application.Question Despite its association with postoperative morbidity, the non-invasive preoperative assessment of CASH remains challenging in patients undergoing liver surgery. Findings Radiomic analysis based on a virtual liver biopsy, combined with volumetric measurements, showed excellent performance in predicting CASH, comparable to whole-liver analysis, with liver volume emerging as a key predictor. Critical Relevance Statement A standardized virtual biopsy-based radiomic analysis represents a promising non-invasive approach for evaluating liver parenchymal injury, as demonstrated in preoperative assessment of CASH and identification of high-risk surgical patients.© 2026. title: GLP-1 receptor agonist use in patients with minor stroke is associated with lower risk of post-stroke dementia.
abstract: Minor ischemic stroke is associated with increased risks of post-stroke dementia independent of stroke recurrence, yet there are no guideline-recommended therapies targeted at cognitive outcomes. Glucagon-like peptide - 1 receptor agonists (GLP-1RAs) have been shown to be associated with lower risk of dementia among diabetes patients; however, their effect on cognitive outcomes among minor stroke patients is largely unknown.This retrospective cohort study used de-identified electronic health record data from the TriNetX US Collaborative Network (2016-2025). Adult patients with minor ischemic stroke (NIHSS ≤ 5 and non-disabling) were included. Patients with prior intracranial hemorrhage, mood disorders, anxiety disorders, cognitive impairment, or dementia were excluded. GLP-1RA use was defined as a prescription prior to or within 3 months of stroke diagnosis. After 1:1 propensity score matching on 75 baseline characteristics, outcomes were assessed over a 5 year follow-up using Kaplan-Meier analysis and Cox proportional hazards models.After propensity score matching, 1,425 patients per group were analyzed. Mean age was 60.7 years, with diabetes present in 92.7% and mean HbA1c of 8.7%. GLP-1RA use was associated with a 48% lower hazard of post-stroke dementia (3.4% vs. 7.0%, HR 0.52 [95% CI 0.37-0.74]) and a 31% lower hazard of other neurocognitive complaints (17.2% vs 25.6%, HR 0.69 [95% CI 0.59-0.81]) over 5 years. GLP-1RA use was also associated with reduced mortality (4.4% vs. 8.8%; HR 0.57 [95% CI 0.42-0.77]) and major ischemic stroke (1.5% vs. 2.7%; HR 0.59 [95% CI 0.35-1.01]). No significant difference in intracranial hemorrhage rates was observed.Among this cohort of minor ischemic stroke patients mostly with concomitant diabetes, GLP-1RA use was associated with significantly reduced risks of post-stroke dementia and other neurocognitive complaints. These findings support prioritizing GLP-1RA use for diabetic patients who suffered minor ischemic stroke. title: Comparative validation of standard screening tools and an exploratory model for detecting obstructive sleep apnea in hypertrophic cardiomyopathy.
abstract: Despite representing a highly prevalent comorbidity, standard screening tools for obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) lack validation in the hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM) population. We sought to prospectively evaluate the diagnostic accuracy of three widely used screening tools against gold-standard polysomnography in an HCM cohort and to explore the potential for a tailored predictive model.In this prospective cohort study, patients with HCM completed the Epworth Sleepiness Scale (ESS), Berlin (BQ) and STOP-Bang questionnaires before undergoing inpatient overnight polysomnography.Of 159 participants (median age 60; 64% male), 90 (57%) had OSA (46% mild, 26% moderate, 28% severe). Standard tools yielded modest performance: STOP-Bang [AUC 0.59 (0.50-0.68), sensitivity 77% (68-86), specificity 40% (28-52)]; ESS [AUC 0.58 (0.49-0.67), sensitivity 24% (15-33), specificity 92% (86-98)]; and Berlin [AUC 0.62 (0.53-0.71), sensitivity 65% (55-75), specificity 57% (45-69)]. In contrast, an exploratory model incorporating age, BMI, and waist-hip ratio showed promising preliminary results [AUC 0.82 (0.74-0.88), sensitivity 60% (48-72), specificity 84% (75-91)].This study underscores the high prevalence of OSA in patients with HCM and demonstrates that standard screening tools developed for the general population perform poorly in this cohort, complicating clinical triage when polysomnography is delayed. While the derived exploratory model may represent an improvement in risk stratification, these findings require extensive external validation. Targeted screening strategies tailored to the unique pathophysiology of HCM remain necessary to improve OSA identification and management in this high-risk population.© 2026. The Author(s).

title: Trichrome-based deep learning for quantitative assessment of steatosis, hepatocellular ballooning, and fibrosis in metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis.
abstract: This study aimed to develop and evaluate Tri-MASH, a trichrome-based deep learning model for quantitative assessment of steatosis, classic hepatocellular ballooning, and fibrosis, and to explore their spatial relationships. Inflammatory-cell density was evaluated as an exploratory measure.Tri-MASH was trained using 161 training specimens and internally evaluated on 30 randomly selected, nonoverlapping specimens. External evaluation comprised 39 biopsies independently scored by four pathologists and 524 baseline and week-72 biopsies from 262 clinical-trial participants. Internal-validation F1 scores ranged from 78.9% for inflammatory-cell detection to 99.2% for sinusoidal fibrosis. In cohort 1, associations with median pathologist assessments were very strong for steatosis (Rs = 0.85) and fibrosis (Rs = 0.87-0.88) and moderate for ballooning (Rs = 0.55). In cohort 2, exploratory pooled analyses showed moderate associations for steatosis (Rs = 0.52), ballooning (Rs = 0.54), and total and portal-septal fibrosis (Rs = 0.50); confidence intervals and p values were unadjusted for repeated observations within participants. Inflammatory-cell density correlated poorly with lobular inflammation grade (Rs=-0.01 to 0.14). Continuous measurements characterized within-arm longitudinal variation, including variation despite unchanged fibrosis stage. In a selected 50-biopsy subset enriched for NAS ballooning grade 2, case-specific median distances to sinusoidal fibrosis were shorter for ballooned hepatocytes than for lipid droplets (p < 0.0001).Tri-MASH enables integrated quantitative and spatial analysis of steatosis, classic hepatocellular ballooning, and fibrosis on a single trichrome section. The current data support its use as an adjunctive quantitative research platform rather than a replacement for conventional H&E-based assessment or standalone clinical grading; inflammatory-cell output did not reproduce conventional lobular inflammation grading.© 2026. title: Effects of semaglutide on cardiac structure and function in heart failure with preserved ejection fraction and obesity: a pre-specified cardiac magnetic resonance substudy of the CAMEO-SEMA trial.
abstract: Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists improve symptoms in patients with obesity and heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF). We recently demonstrated that semaglutide reduces exertional pulmonary artery wedge pressure (PAWP) in obesity-related HFpEF, but potential effects of semaglutide on cardiac structure and function that may underlie these hemodynamic improvements remain unclear. In this prespecified cardiovascular magnetic resonance (CMR) substudy of the randomized CAMEO-SEMA trial, 49 participants (33 semaglutide, 16 placebo, 28 female) underwent CMR at baseline and 52 weeks, within 1 day of invasive exercise hemodynamic assessment. The prespecified primary CMR endpoint was change in left atrial (LA) reservoir strain; other prespecified CMR endpoints included LV filling dynamics, which were assessed by early filling rate indexed to end-diastolic volume (eFR/EDV). Compared with placebo, semaglutide improved LA reservoir strain (+5.7% [95% CI, +0.3 to +9.7]; P=0.037) and eFR/EDV (+0.64 s-1 [95% CI, +0.42 to +1.00]; P<0.0001). Improvements in LA reservoir strain and LV filling dynamics were associated with reductions in exercise PAWP (r=-0.46, P<0.001 and r=-0.65, P<0.0001, respectively). With respect to other prespecified CMR endpoints, semaglutide reduced LV mass, restored more physiologic LV geometry, and improved right ventricular function and biventricular myocardial mechanics. The results of this CMR substudy indicate that in patients with obesity-related HFpEF, semaglutide improves LA function and LV diastolic filling dynamics, identifying improvements in myocardial function that may contribute to semaglutide's improvement of hemodynamics. title: Artificial Urinary Sphincter Revision with Pump Preservation: A Prospective Feasibility Study.
abstract: To evaluate the feasibility and safety of preserving a normally functioning pump during AUS revision surgery.Following institutional review board approval, we prospectively evaluated consecutive patients undergoing AUS revision for mechanical or non-mechanical failure at a single tertiary referral center between 2023 and the present. Demographic, operative, and postoperative outcomes were collected.Sixty AUS revisions were analyzed. Median time from primary implantation to revision was 8.6 years (IQR 3.9-13.1). Most revision procedures were performed for cuff-related mechanical failure (65%). A normally functioning pump was preserved in all patients. Median operative time was 43 minutes (IQR 33-51), and all procedures were performed on an outpatient basis. Devices were reactivated after a median of 2 weeks compared with our standard 6-week activation following pump replacement. No pump-related complications, including hematoma, pain, or malposition, were observed. No patient required reoperation for pump malfunction, and no pump-specific mechanical failures occurred.Pump-specific mechanical failure is uncommon. Among 1,327 AUS revision procedures in our institutional database (3,144 total AUS procedures), only 11 (0.82%) were attributable to pump malfunction. In appropriately selected patients with a normally functioning pump, preservation of the existing pump appears feasible and safe while avoiding unnecessary scrotal dissection, permitting earlier device activation, and potentially reducing postoperative morbidity. Longer-term follow-up is needed to confirm the durability of this selective revision strategy.Copyright © 2026 Elsevier Inc. All rights reserved.

title: Amyloid nomenclature 2026: update, novel proteins, and discussion of intracellular aggregates and toxicity. Recommendations by the International Society of Amyloidosis Nomenclature Committee.
abstract: Protein misfolding followed by aggregation into amyloid fibrils is a more common process than previously believed, and knowledge of the underlying mechanisms and their associations with disease is rapidly expanding. The International Society of Amyloidosis (ISA) has long maintained a Nomenclature Committee to meet the need for uniform terminology, amyloid protein names and abbreviations, and to harmonize these with other nomenclature systems. For this update, virtual meetings and electronic correspondence preceded the 2026 ISA meeting in Montevideo, Uruguay, resulting in the present revised document. Amyloid is defined by the beta-sheet structure of its principal fibril protein, although amyloid deposits formed in vivo contain additional components. The principles underlying the recommended amyloid nomenclature remain unchanged but have been further clarified. The number of known human amyloid fibril proteins associated with systemic amyloidosis remains 19. Most are linked to genetic variants and are extremely rare. In animals, nine different fibril proteins have been identified in association with systemic amyloidoses. The rapidly growing body of knowledge concerning pathological intracellular protein aggregates and their contribution to tissue vulnerability is covered in an expanded section of this paper.

title: The Association Between Hospital Comprehensive Stroke Center Designation Status and Stroke Rate Reporting in the Society of Thoracic Surgeons/American College of Cardiology Transcatheter Valve Therapy Registry After Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement: Implications for Hospital Performance Assessment.
abstract: The Michigan Structural Heart Consortium showed that transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) stroke rates were associated with hospital Comprehensive Stroke Center (CSC) designation, suggesting that hospital structural factors affect stroke reporting. We sought to determine whether CSC designation is nationally associated with reported stroke rates and the potential impact on hospital performance and Transcatheter Valve Therapy National Data Registry (TVTR) public reporting.Consecutive TVTR cases from January 2016 through June 2023 were included, excluding sites reporting to the TVTR <1 year or performing <20 total TAVR procedures. The primary outcome was in-hospital stroke rate. Secondary outcomes were disabling stroke and 30-day stroke. Major bleeding, death, acute renal failure, and a composite end point were falsification end points to determine whether CSC status was uniquely associated with stroke. Multivariable hierarchical models were created starting with patient covariates and sequentially adding hospital variables to account for determinants of stroke. The impact of CSC status on hospital performance was estimated by correcting CSC hospital stroke rates in the validated TVTR 30-day composite model.A total of 525 919 TAVRs at 800 sites were included, and 10 963 strokes (2.1%) were reported within 30 days: 8284 (1.6%) in-hospital and 2679 (0.5%) after discharge. A total of 4733 (0.9%) were disabling strokes. Multivariate analysis showed that CSC status and participation in TAVR trials were independent predictors of in-hospital stroke rate (P=0.033 and 0.012) and disabling stroke (P=0.033 and 0.007), but not falsification end points (P=NS). Participation in TAVR trials and operator volume were independent predictors of 30-day stroke (P=0.039 and P=0.041). The impact of CSC status on the 30-day composite model showed performance improvement for 8 of 153 CSC hospitals.CSC hospital status and participation in TAVR trials are significant predictors unique for stroke. Correcting for the association of CSC status on stroke rate resulted in an estimated 8 of 153 hospitals improving their TVTR 30-day composite model performance. Further work is needed to account for potential ascertainment bias for stroke in public reporting.

title: Financial Payments From Drug Manufacturers to Oncologists and Use of Guideline-Preferred Cancer Treatments.
abstract: Payments from the drug industry influence physicians' prescribing decisions. Whether industry payments affect the likelihood that patients receive the guideline-preferred treatment for their cancer is unknown.We used fee-for-service Medicare claims to identify patients with an incident cancer diagnosis from 2014 to 2020. We used the National Comprehensive Cancer Network (NCCN) guidelines to identify cancers with variation in clinical benefit among recommended treatment options and to identify the preferred treatment as of each patient's diagnosis date. The primary exposure was drug industry payments received by the patient's medical oncologist during the year before diagnosis, categorized as no payment, payment for preferred treatment only, payment for nonpreferred treatment only, or payment for both. The primary outcome was receipt of a preferred treatment.There were 14 cancer scenarios comprising 15,607 patients; 60.2% were managed by oncologists who received no payment, 21.9% by oncologists who received payment for guideline-preferred treatment, 30.6% by oncologists who received payment for nonpreferred treatment, and 12.7% by oncologists who received both payment types. Among patients whose oncologist received no payments, 41.6% received payments for preferred treatment versus 51.5% of those whose oncologist received payments for guideline-preferred treatment only, 34.7% of those whose oncologist received payments for nonpreferred treatment only, and 42.9% of those whose oncologist received payments for both payment types. After adjustment, payment for guideline-preferred treatment was associated with a greater likelihood of receiving preferred treatment (risk ratio [RR] = 1.06 [95% CI, 1.01 to 1.13]) and payment for nonpreferred treatment was associated with a lower likelihood (RR, 0.93 [95% CI, 0.89 to 0.98]). Association magnitude increased as payment dollar value increased.Industry payments were associated with increased use of the promoted cancer treatment, regardless of whether that treatment was guideline-preferred or nonpreferred for a given patient.

title: Second-line CD19 CAR T vs platinum salvage and autologous stem cell transplant for primary mediastinal B-cell lymphoma.
abstract: Primary mediastinal B-cell lymphoma (PMBCL) is a rare form of large B-cell lymphoma (LBCL), with ∼90% of patients cured with frontline treatment. For relapsed or refractory (R/R) disease, the optimal treatment is unclear. CD19 chimeric antigen receptor T-cell (CAR T) therapy has been established as the preferred second-line (2L) treatment for primary refractory or early-relapsing LBCL based on the overall survival benefits observed in landmark phase 3 trials. However, patients with PMBCL were underrepresented in these pivotal studies. This study evaluated outcomes of 252 patients treated with 2L therapies for R/R PMBCL at 14 US institutions between 2001 and 2025. Platinum-based salvage therapy with intent to proceed to high-dose therapy and autologous stem cell transplant (HDT/ASCT; platinum cohort) and CD19 CAR T therapy (CAR T cohort) were given as 2L therapies in the real-world setting in 157 and 26 patients, respectively. Overall response rate (ORR), complete response (CR) rate, and median progression-free survival (PFS) were significantly higher in the CAR T cohort compared with the platinum cohort (ORR, 91.3% vs 44.2%; P< .001; CR, 65.2% vs 14.7%; P< .001; median PFS, not reached vs 3.5 months; hazard ratio, 0.28; 95% confidence interval, 0.15-0.54; P = .001). No significant difference was observed in overall survival. llm_summary: Researchers compared two second-line treatments for patients with relapsed or refractory primary mediastinal B-cell lymphoma, a rare blood cancer: CD19 CAR T therapy (a treatment using modified immune cells) versus platinum-based chemotherapy followed by stem cell transplant. CD19 CAR T therapy produced higher response rates and longer progression-free survival than the chemotherapy approach, though overall survival did not differ significantly between the two groups. These findings suggest CD19 CAR T may be more effective as a second-line treatment for this specific lymphoma type.

title: Duffy testing to benefit children's population health: a cost-effectiveness analysis.
abstract: The Duffy-null phenotype is reported in ∼1 in 10 individuals in the United States and results in absolute neutrophil counts (ANC) that are 40% to 50% lower than most institutional reference intervals. Misinterpretation of normal ANC values for this population leads to avoidable diagnostic testing and referrals. We aimed to evaluate the economic value of serologic Duffy testing vs no testing obtained alongside other recommended blood work at 9 to 12 months of age, using a Markov cohort design incorporating all levels of currently practiced diagnostic neutropenia workups across scenario analyses. The analysis was conducted from a US societal perspective over a lifetime horizon across all accepted willingness-to-pay thresholds. The primary outcome was the incremental net monetary benefit (iNMB) in US dollars ($) per quality-adjusted life-year. Duffy testing was favored in the base-case and all scenario analyses, with iNMB ranging from $2.18 to $92.77 per child tested for Duffy status. The cost of Duffy serological testing, the cost of the neutropenia workup, and the prevalence of low ANC were the 3 parameters with the greatest variation that affected the iNMB. Probabilistic analyses showed that universal testing was favored in 100%, 100%, 100%, 95%, and 100% of 10 000 iterations in the base-case, full workup, annual follow-up, minimal workup, and targeted testing scenarios, respectively. The Duffy-null prevalence threshold required for universal testing to be cost-effective was 7.6%, 1.6%, 1.3%, and 9.0%, respectively, and 4.9% for targeted testing. At these thresholds, universal serologic Duffy testing would align with cost-effective implementation in at least 20 states in the United States today.© 2026 American Society of Hematology. llm_summary: Researchers evaluated whether testing infants for the Duffy-null trait, a genetic variation affecting white blood cell counts in about 1 in 10 Americans, would save money by preventing unnecessary diagnostic tests and doctor visits. The analysis found that universal Duffy testing would be cost-effective and provide modest economic benefits ranging from $2 to $93 per child tested. The findings suggest that adding this simple blood test to routine infant screening could reduce unnecessary medical procedures across multiple US states.

title: Health-Related Quality of Life Among Individuals With Histiocytic Neoplasms in the Modern Era of Targeted Therapies.
abstract: Histiocytic neoplasms include Langerhans cell histiocytosis (LCH), Erdheim-Chester disease (ECD), and Rosai-Dorfman disease (RDD). The discovery of MAPK pathway mutations has led to the approval of BRAF and MEK inhibitors, reducing disease-specific mortality. There is a critical need to define the health-related quality of life (HRQoL) among adults with histiocytic neoplasms in the modern era of targeted therapies.We conducted a multi-institutional study including 196 adults with histiocytic neoplasms (73 LCH, 67 ECD, and 56 RDD) who completed the Patient-Reported Outcomes Measurement Information System (PROMIS)-29 + 2 Profile v2.1, including 48 with longitudinal assessments. A total of 113 (57.7%) patients were not receiving treatment at the time of baseline survey. Primary endpoints were physical health (PH) and mental health (MH) summary scores, and the secondary outcome was the PROMIS Preference (PROPr) score, an overall health utility metric.Patients with ECD had worse PH scores than those with LCH or RDD (odds ratio [OR], 4.82; P=.006). Single-system pulmonary LCH (OR, 5.99; P=.028) and multisystem disease (OR, 2.49; P=.018) were also associated with worse PH scores than single-system disease. Multisystem disease was associated with worse MH scores (OR, 2.17; P=.036). An exploratory mixed-model longitudinal analysis (n=48) demonstrated improvements in PH scores among patients with ECD and in MH and PROPr scores among those with LCH over a median follow-up of 6 months.Within histiocytic neoplasms, ECD and multisystem involvement define a high-risk HRQoL phenotype characterized by multidomain impairment. Longitudinal data suggest potential improvements in select domains with targeted therapy. However, mean scores remained below population norms. These patients may benefit from proactive, bundled supportive care and closer HRQoL monitoring.

title: Association Between the Neutrophil:Lymphocyte Ratio After Hospitalization for Sepsis and Long-Term Outcomes: A Population-Based Cohort Study.
abstract: Long-term outcomes after sepsis survival remain poor. No clinical laboratory tests are in use for stratifying long-term risk after sepsis, limiting the development of secondary prevention. The peripheral blood neutrophil:lymphocyte ratio (NLR) reflects innate and adaptive immune cell balance, and may reflect an immune milieu which is associated with long-term risk after sepsis. Accordingly, we evaluated the association between the NLR in the weeks after sepsis hospitalization discharge-a time when patients are routinely seen in post-ICU clinics-and long-term outcomes.Population-based cohort study.Ontario, Canada, 2010-2020.Adults discharged alive from a sepsis hospitalization.None.The exposure was the first outpatient NLR-derived from the complete blood count-measured 15-90 days after sepsis discharge. Among 37,250 survivors with available NLR, the median (interquartile range [IQR]) time-to-measurement was 34 days (22-54 d), and the median NLR was 2.7 (1.8-4.2). Within 1 year, 17,732 patients (47.6%) were rehospitalized or died (median [IQR] time-to-event, 82 d [27-185 d]). The frequency of rehospitalization or death increased across increasing NLR quartiles: 34.2%, 41.5%, 50.3%, and 64.4% (ptrend < 0.001). Compared with the lowest quartile, adjusted hazard ratios (95% CI) were 1.24 (1.18-1.29), 1.54 (1.48-1.62), and 2.25 (2.15-2.35) across higher quartiles. For most patients, NLR after sepsis returned to its patient-specific presepsis ambient level, which was itself prognostic.Among sepsis survivors, outpatient NLR measured 15-90 days after discharge is strongly associated with 1-year risk of rehospitalization or death. As a simple, widely available biomarker, the NLR may support early postsepsis risk stratification and inform development of secondary prevention strategies.Copyright © 2026 The Author(s). llm_summary: Researchers examined whether a simple blood test measuring the ratio of two types of white blood cells could predict which sepsis survivors would face serious health problems within a year of leaving the hospital. title: Mycoplasma pneumoniae CARDS toxin hijacks annexin A2 to enhance clathrin-mediated endocytosis and induce a cytopathic effect.
abstract: Mycoplasma pneumoniae is a primary cause of bacterial community-acquired pneumonia. One of its key virulence factors, the community-acquired respiratory distress syndrome (CARDS) toxin, replicates most clinical symptoms of the infection. Although CARDS toxin exhibits multi-receptor binding affinity, the mechanisms governing its cellular entry remain poorly understood. In this study, we characterized the toxin entry pathway mediated by the host protein annexin A2 (AnxA2). Using flow cytometry and biotinylated membrane protein analysis, we demonstrate that CARDS toxin induces a rapid, transient translocation of AnxA2 to the plasma membrane, peaking at 15 min post-exposure. This recruitment occurs via a phosphorylation-independent mechanism, distinguishing it from the Src-dependent recruitment typically observed in other physiological contexts. Co-immunoprecipitation (co-IP) of the clathrin heavy chain revealed an enhanced AnxA2-clathrin association that accelerates clathrin-mediated endocytosis of toxin. Endosomal fractionation, immunofluorescence, and co-IP studies confirmed the time-dependent co-localization and physical interaction of CARDS toxin with AnxA2 within early endosomes. Furthermore, CRISPR/Cas9-mediated knockout of AnxA2 in A549 cells demonstrated that this protein is essential for the internalization of CARDS toxin; its absence not only reduces the toxin binding but also effectively impairs the rapid cellular uptake required to trigger the downstream cytopathic effects and vacuolation. These results establish that CARDS toxin modulates host surface remodeling through AnxA2 cell surface translocation to facilitate efficient cellular entry, identifying a rate-limiting step in M. pneumoniae pathogenesis.

llm_summary: Researchers investigated how a toxin produced by the bacterium that causes pneumonia enters human cells by studying a host protein called annexin A2. They found that the toxin triggers this protein to move to the cell surface within 15 minutes, which then helps pull the toxin inside the cell through a process called clathrin-mediated endocytosis. When researchers removed the annexin A2 protein entirely, cells could no longer efficiently take up the toxin, suggesting this protein is essential for the bacterium's ability to damage lung cells.

CARDS toxin induced rapid translocation of AnxA2 to the plasma membrane, peaking at 15 minutes post-exposure through a phosphorylation-independent mechanism, and enhanced the association between AnxA2 and clathrin heavy chain to accelerate clathrin-mediated endocytosis. Time-dependent co-localization and physical interaction of CARDS toxin with AnxA2 were confirmed within early endosomes, and CRISPR/Cas9-mediated knockout of AnxA2 reduced toxin binding and impaired rapid cellular uptake. AnxA2 knockout cells demonstrated substantially diminished downstream cytopathic effects and vacuolation compared to wild-type cells, establishing AnxA2 as essential for efficient CARDS.

title: Mivocabtagene Autoleucel CD19 Chimeric Antigen Receptor T-Cell Therapy in Stiff Person Syndrome: A Nonrandomized Clinical Trial.
abstract: Stiff person syndrome (SPS) is a progressive, autoimmune neurologic disease characterized by muscle stiffness and painful spasms, leading to substantial disability. Mivocabtagene autoleucel, a fully human, autologous CD19 chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) T-cell therapy with CD28 costimulation, showed durable clinical benefit on a named-patient basis in SPS.To evaluate the efficacy and safety of mivocabtagene autoleucel in adult SPS.This pivotal, single-arm, open-label, nonrandomized phase 2 study enrolled participants from September 2024 to May 2025 at 3 US sites. Individuals aged 18 to 75 years with antibody-positive SPS and inadequate response to immunomodulatory/immunosuppressive therapies as determined by investigators were included.Patients received low-dose lymphodepletion (fludarabine, 30 mg/m2/d, and cyclophosphamide, 300 mg/m2/d, for 3 days), followed by a single mivocabtagene autoleucel infusion (1 × 108 CAR T cells).Primary end points were the change from baseline to week 16 in the timed 25-ft walk (T25FW) and safety. Secondary end points were modified Rankin Scale score, Distribution of Stiffness Index score, Heightened Sensitivity Scale score, and Hauser Ambulation Index score. Exploratory end points included pharmacokinetic and pharmacodynamic assessments and biomarkers.Of 27 patients enrolled, 26 (median [range] age, 56.0 [32.0-73.0] years; 16 [61.5%] female) were treated. Median (range) follow-up was 6.5 (4.4-12.2) months. The primary efficacy end point was met, with significant week 16 improvement from baseline in T25FW of a mean of -7.69 seconds (SD, 10.03; 95% CI, -11.74 to -3.64; P < .001) and a median (IQR) of -4.8 (-11.9 to -2.5) seconds (45.6% median improvement); improvement was sustained (median, 44.4%) among 16 of 26 patients who reached the 24-week time point. All secondary efficacy end points showed significant week 16 improvements from baseline (modified Rankin Scale score: mean, -0.8 points [SD, 0.86; 95% CI, -1.1 to -0.4; P < .001], Distribution of Stiffness Index score: mean, -1.5 points [SD, 1.75; 95% CI, -2.2 to -0.8; P < .001]; Heightened Sensitivity Scale score: mean, -3.2 points [SD, 2.01; 95% CI, -4.0 to -2.3; P < .001]; Hauser Ambulation Index score: mean, -1.6 points [SD, 1.13; 95% CI, -2.1 to -1.2; P < .001]). The most common grade 3/4 treatment-related adverse event was neutropenia (5/26 patients [19.2%]). Low-grade cytokine release syndrome and immune effector cell-associated neurotoxicity syndrome occurred in 24 of 26 patients (92.3%; 10/26 [38.5%] grade 1; 14/26 [53.8%] grade 2) and 3 of 26 patients (11.5%; all grade 1), respectively; all resolved without sequelae. B-cell depletion and clear changes suggestive of immune reset were observed. At last follow-up, all patients remained free of immunomodulatory therapies for SPS.In this nonrandomized clinical trial, a single dose of mivocabtagene autoleucel resulted in immunotherapy-free remissions with a consistent, well-tolerated safety profile, demonstrating a highly effective therapy in antibody-positive SPS with the potential for durable remissions. Long-term follow-up is ongoing.ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT06588491.

llm_summary: Researchers tested a new cell therapy called mivocabtagene autoleucel in 26 patients with stiff person syndrome, a rare autoimmune disease causing muscle stiffness and pain. After receiving the treatment, patients showed significant improvement in walking speed and other measures of stiffness at 16 weeks, with benefits sustained at 24 weeks, and most patients stopped needing other immunosuppressive medications. The therapy was generally well-tolerated, though this was a small study without a comparison group, so longer follow-up is needed to confirm the durability of these results.

The most common grade 3/4 adverse event was neutropenia in 19.2% of patients, with low-grade cytokine release syndrome occurring in 92.3% of patients.

title: Effects of Nrf2 deletion on exercise training-induced adaptations of resistance arterioles from skeletal muscle.
abstract: Exercise training induces adaptation of resistance arterioles but the cellular mechanisms that are stimulated during exercise training bouts, and which underlie adaptation to repeated bouts of exercise, remain largely unknown. The nuclear erythroid-2-related factor (Nrf2) plays a critical role in maintaining cellular redox homeostasis in response to heightened metabolic stress, such as may occur during bouts of exercise. We hypothesized that Nrf2 plays a critical role in exercise training-induced adaptations of resistance arterioles from locomotory skeletal muscle. To test this hypothesis, vascular responses of resistance arterioles from the soleus muscle of wild type (WT) and Nrf2 knockout (Nrf2 KO) rats were evaluated after exercise training or cage confinement. Exercise training enhanced flow-induced vasodilation in arterioles from the soleus muscle of WT rats, but not in arterioles from Nrf2 KO rats. Exercise training also altered myogenic responses differently in arterioles from WT and Nrf2 KO rats. After exercise training, myogenic responses were greater in arterioles from WT rats as compared to Nrf2 KO rats. Exercise training enhanced vasodilation to the NO donor, DEA-NONO-ate, in arterioles from both WT and Nrf2 KO rats. Similarly, exercise training increased contractile responses to phenylephrine in arterioles from both WT and Nrf2 KO rats. Expression of calcium-activated potassium (BK) channels was reduced in arterioles from Nrf2 KO rats. Thus, although Nrf2 appears necessary for some adaptations to exercise training in skeletal muscle arterioles, compensatory pathways that are Nrf2-independent maintain contractile and vasodilatory function in skeletal muscle arterioles, and these pathways can be upregulated by exercise training.Copyright © 2026.
