llm_summary: Researchers examined whether genetic risk factors for schizophrenia and bipolar disorder together influence brain activity patterns in healthy people, and whether these patterns relate to depression symptoms in patients with schizophrenia-spectrum disorders. They found that specific combinations of genetic risk scores were associated with different levels of activity in brain regions involved in decision-making and memory, and that lower activity in one of these regions correlated with more depressive symptoms in patients. These results suggest that the overlap between genetic risks for these two disorders may help explain why some people with schizophrenia experience mood problems.
llm_summary_expert: Researchers examined the interaction between polygenic risk scores (PRS) for schizophrenia and bipolar disorder in 263 healthy participants using genome-wide association variants and Bayesian continuous shrinkage methods to predict resting-state brain activity measured by fractional amplitude of low-frequency fluctuations (fALFF). In healthy participants, lower schizophrenia PRS combined with higher bipolar disorder PRS was associated with reduced dorsolateral prefrontal cortex fALFF, while higher scores for both PRS were associated with increased angular gyrus fALFF, with convergent results confirmed using alternative statistical approaches. In an independent sample of 40 individuals with schizophrenia-spectrum disorders, dorsolateral prefrontal cortex fALFF showed a negative correlation with depressive symptoms. These findings suggest that genetic risk variants for schizophrenia and bipolar disorder jointly modulate spontaneous brain activity in regions potentially relevant to mood symptomatology in schizophrenia-spectrum disorders. The study's interpretation depends on the assumption that brain activity patterns in healthy individuals predict clinically relevant phenotypes in affected populations, which requires validation in prosp.

title: Clinical phenotypes, autoimmunity and outcomes in Rosai-Dorfman disease: An international multicentre cohort study.
abstract: Rosai-Dorfman disease (RDD) is a rare histiocytic neoplasm with diverse clinical behaviour and immune abnormalities with unknown clinical significance. We performed a retrospective cohort study of 162 patients with RDD from 2003 to 2025 at five international referral centres. Median age was 48 years and 64.8% were female. Multisystem disease occurred in 87 patients (53.7%), commonly involving skin/subcutaneous tissue (49.4%), lymph nodes (39.5%) and bones (34%). Molecular testing was available for 102 patients; 40 (39.2%) were mitogen-activated protein kinase/rat sarcoma virus oncogene homolog signaling pathway (MAPK/RAS)-altered, commonly with kirsten rat sarcoma viral oncogene homolog (KRAS) or mitogen-activated protein kinase 1 (MAP2K/MEK) alterations. MAPK/RAS alterations were associated with multisystem disease (p = 0.0034). Autoimmune disease (AID) was documented in 29 patients (17.9%), usually preceding RDD, and 45/95 patients (47.4%) with available autoantibody status had at least one positive autoantibody. Among 153 patients with response data, objective response occurred in 94 (61.4%). Response distribution differed by disease extent; single-system disease was associated with more complete responses and less progression than multisystem disease. At a median follow-up of 2.49 years, eight deaths occurred; 5-year overall survival was 93.4%. AID and autoantibody positivity were not associated with response or overall survival. These findings support disease extent and molecular status as clinically relevant dimensions of RDD assessment, while autoimmune and serological abnormalities should be interpreted in clinical context.© 2026 British Society for Haematology and John Wiley & Sons Ltd.

llm_summary: Researchers examined 162 patients with Rosai-Dorfman disease, a rare blood cancer, to understand how it develops and progresses. They found that disease spread to multiple body systems was associated with specific genetic changes and predicted worse treatment outcomes, while autoimmune conditions occurring alongside the disease did not affect survival. These results suggest that the extent of disease spread and genetic testing should guide how doctors assess and treat this condition.

title: Folate and folic acid intake in relation to molecular subtypes of colorectal cancer: pooled analyses of up to 8970 cases and 8098 control participants.
abstract: Higher intakes of the B-vitamin folate are associated with modest reductions in colorectal cancer risk. Intertumoral heterogeneity has been suggested to affect the relationship, but studies to date have been limited in number and size.This study aimed to determine whether associations between intake of the B-vitamin folate (from diet and folic acid supplements) and the risk of colorectal cancer vary by tumor molecular marker status for BRAF and KRAS mutations, microsatellite instability (MSI), and/or the CpG island methylator phenotype (CIMP).The full study population included 8970 colorectal cancer cases and 8098 control participants from observational case-control and cohort studies within the Genetics and Epidemiology of Colorectal Cancer Consortium (GECCO) and the Colon Cancer Family Registry (CCFR). Folate intake was assessed by food frequency questionnaire or diet history. Multivariable odds ratios (OR) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were estimated using multinomial logistic regression. Differences in associations between tumor subtypes were assessed using case-only logistic regression.Total folate intake and folate supplement use were inversely associated with the risk of colorectal cancer, whereas the relationship for dietary folate was weaker. These associations did not vary substantially among CRC subtypes defined by individual tumor markers. Possible heterogeneity was observed only for CIMP, with a stronger inverse association between total folate intake and CIMP-low/negative compared to CIMP-high colorectal cancer (pdifference=0.07). Associations were also inverse for total folate and subtypes defined by marker combinations, except for a null association for the less common Jass Type 2 subtype of MSS/MSI-low, CIMP-high, BRAF-mutated, KRAS-wildtype (pdifference=0.06 compared to the traditional adenoma-carcinoma pathway).Overall, the putative protective effect of folate intake in colorectal cancer development appears to be broad, not limited to specific subtypes defined by BRAF, KRAS, MSI, and CIMP status, or combinations of these markers, in the tumor.Copyright © 2026. llm_summary: Researchers examined whether the protective effect of folate, a B-vitamin found in foods and supplements, against colorectal cancer differed depending on the genetic characteristics of the tumors in a large study of nearly 9,000 cancer cases and 8,000 controls. Higher total folate intake and supplement use were associated with lower colorectal cancer risk overall, and this protective effect appeared consistent across different tumor types rather than limited to specific genetic subtypes. The findings suggest that folate's potential cancer-prevention benefit is broad-based, though this observational study cannot prove that folate directly causes the risk reduction.

title: Beyond Coronary Artery Disease: Etiologies and Outcomes of the Shark-Fin ECG Pattern: A Systematic Review.
abstract: The shark-fin sign (SFS) is a rare, high-risk electrocardiographic pattern reported in commonly linked with obstructive coronary artery disease (CAD).To characterize the electrocardiographic patterns, etiologies, and clinical outcomes associated with the SFS.We systematically reviewed PubMed, EMBASE, Scopus, and Cochrane from inception through May 20, 2026, including all studies with participant-level data.Eighty-five papers involving 104 patients were included; 66.3% had non-obstructive etiologies. The obstructive CAD patients were predominantly male (97.1%), while other etiologies were predominantly female (60.8%). Among CAD cases, the left main coronary artery (LMCA)/proximal left anterior descending artery (LAD) was the culprit in 75.0%, and SFS localization matched coronary anatomy in 91.4%. VT/VF and death each occurred in 37.1%, with adverse outcomes confined to those with LMCA/LAD lesions. Among other etiologies, Takotsubo syndrome (TTS, 31.7%), vasospasm (14.4%), myocarditis (6.7 %) and neurologic emergencies (4.8%) were the most frequently reported. VT/VF occurred in 43.4% and 27.5% died. Among patients with TTS, 63.6% experienced VT/VF or death, compared with ventricular arrhythmias in 66% of patients with vasospasm.SFS is a high-risk ECG pattern rather than a diagnosis and warrants urgent etiologic evaluation and cardiac monitoring. Most published data are derived from patients without established CAD. LMCA/LAD disease, TTS, and coronary vasospasm were associated with particularly high-risk hospitalizations. Primary non-cardiac causes should also be considered when clinically suspected.Copyright © 2026. Published by Elsevier Inc.

title: A central hub model for remote delivery of multisite clinical trial interventions.
abstract: Digital health technologies enable remote delivery of clinical interventions, creating opportunities to redesign multisite trials. Traditional trials require participating sites to deliver interventions independently, potentially increasing implementation variability and operational complexity. Centralized models instead allow local recruitment and assessments while coordinating intervention delivery through one hub. We describe the feasibility of this model in RECOVER-NEURO, an NIH-funded, five-arm phase 2 randomized trial overseen by the Duke Clinical Research Institute. The trial enrolled 328 participants across 22 US sites with cognitive symptoms associated with long COVID. Sites conducted recruitment, consent, and clinical assessments, while an NYU Langone Health hub managed study kit preparation and distribution, device programming, onboarding, remote supervision, adherence monitoring, and equipment recovery. Participants were randomized to BrainHQ cognitive training alone; BrainHQ plus cognitive rehabilitation (PASC-CoRE), delivered via telehealth by Mount Sinai and Emory University investigators; BrainHQ plus active transcranial direct current stimulation (tDCS); BrainHQ plus sham tDCS; or non-adaptive computer-based puzzles and games as an active comparator. Interventions were delivered remotely over 10 weeks using home-based study kits. Participants completed a mean of 44.0 ± 10.9 sessions over 68.8 ± 11.3 days. Of 320 participants who received intervention, 260 (81.3%) were consistently adherent. The hub initiated intervention within 13.5 ± 6.1 days of first participant contact, supported up to 168 concurrently active participants, and achieved a 96.9% equipment return rate. The intervention phase was completed in 375 days. These findings demonstrate the feasibility of centralized remote delivery of digital and device-based interventions in a large multisite trial and may inform future decentralized or hybrid clinical trials. title: The Complementary Impact of Amino Acid PET with Diffusion and Perfusion MRI for Glioblastoma Tumor Delineation.
abstract: While standard MRI imaging is known to underestimate glioblastoma tumor extent, advanced imaging techniques including 18-FDOPA PET, dynamic contrast enhanced (DCE) perfusion MRI, and diffusion weighted MRI (DWI) have been utilized on clinical trials to identify tumor within and beyond gadolinium enhancement for radiation targeting. This clinical trial analysis quantifies how DCE, DWI and 18-FDOPA PET identify tumor beyond standard imaging, and whether these techniques are complementary and feasible.Patients with newly diagnosed glioblastoma enrolled on a phase II clinical trial underwent pre-radiation 18-FDOPA PET/CT, DCE, DWI, and standard MRI sequences. Tumor volumes were separately delineated using each imaging modality and incorporated into radiation target volumes, and were compared for overlapping and non-overlapping segments.In 153 enrolled patients included in this analysis, tumor was identified beyond conventionally used radiation volume expansions of 5-, 10-, 15-, and 20 mm from standard MRI tumor volumes in 86%, 56%, 38% and 20% of patients, respectively. Advanced imaging techniques identified partially overlapping tumor volumes; PET identified tumor outside of the advanced MRI subvolumes in 88%, while DWI and DCE identified tumor outside of standard MRI and PET in 95% cases, indicating these imaging techniques are complementary.Advanced imaging techniques including DCE, DWI, and 18-FDOPA PET allow complementary delineation of glioblastoma beyond contrast-enhancing tumor from standard MRI, and may be most valuable when used in combination. These advanced imaging methods can potentially facilitate accurate tumor targeting with reduced CTV expansions to spare normal tissue and enable safe hypofractionated radiation therapy.Copyright © 2026 The Author(s). title: Glucagon-Like Peptide-1 Receptor Agonist Exposure and Long-Term Outcomes in Patients with Asymptomatic Carotid Stenosis: A Propensity Score-Matched Real-World Analysis.
abstract: Asymptomatic carotid stenosis is a prevalent manifestation of atherosclerotic disease and, despite contemporary guideline-directed medical therapy, remains associated with downstream cerebrovascular events and mortality. Given the vascular and cardiometabolic benefits of glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1As), we evaluated whether GLP-1A exposure is associated with lower long-term event rates in patients with asymptomatic carotid stenosis.This retrospective study used the TriNetX US Collaborative Network. Adults (≥18 years) with carotid stenosis (January 1, 2016, to September 30, 2025) were included; patients with prior/baseline cerebrovascular events and those undergoing carotid revascularization within 6 months were excluded to operationalize an asymptomatic cohort. GLP-1A exposure was defined as any GLP-1A use within 6 months after carotid stenosis diagnosis; nonexposed patients served as comparators. Cohorts were propensity score-matched 1:1, and outcomes were assessed using Kaplan-Meier and Cox proportional hazards models.After matching, 30,332 patients were included in each cohort. GLP-1A exposure was associated with lower hazards of ischemic stroke (hazard ratio [HR] 0.63, 0.71, and 0.73 at 1, 3, and 5 years; 5-year cumulative event probability 5.55% versus 6.85%), hemorrhagic stroke (HR 0.63, 0.69, and 0.74; 2.04% versus 2.35%), large vessel occlusion stroke (HR 0.70, 0.77, and 0.81; 2.04% versus 2.27%), and all-cause mortality (HR 0.42, 0.58, and 0.64; 17.11% versus 21.49%). The composite of ischemic stroke or mortality was also lower (HR 0.48, 0.61, and 0.66; 20.88% versus 25.85% at 5 years) in the GLP-1A-exposed cohort.In a large real-world cohort with asymptomatic carotid stenosis, GLP-1A exposure was associated with lower hazards of stroke subtypes, large vessel occlusion stroke, and mortality across 1-5 years. llm_summary: Researchers examined whether a diabetes medication called GLP-1 receptor agonist could reduce stroke and death risk in patients with narrowed carotid arteries in the neck that had not yet caused symptoms. In a large real-world study of over 30,000 matched patients, those taking the medication had lower rates of stroke and death over five years compared to those who did not take it. However, because this was an observational study rather than a controlled experiment, it cannot prove the medication directly caused these improvements.
llm_summary_expert: Researchers examined whether glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonist (GLP-1A) exposure was associated with reduced long-term cerebrovascular and mortality outcomes in a retrospective cohort of 30,332 propensity score-matched adults with asymptomatic carotid stenosis identified from the TriNetX US Collaborative Network between January 2016 and September 2025. GLP-1A exposure was defined as any use within 6 months after carotid stenosis diagnosis, and outcomes including ischemic stroke, hemorrhagic stroke, large vessel occlusion stroke, and all-cause mortality were assessed using Kaplan-Meier and Cox proportional hazards models over 5 years. GLP-1A-exposed patients demonstrated lower hazard ratios across multiple endpoints, with 5-year cumulative ischemic stroke probability of 5.55% versus 6.85% in unexposed patients and all-cause mortality of 17.11% versus 21.49%. The composite outcome of ischemic stroke or mortality at 5 years was also lower in the GLP-1A.

title: Lisocabtagene maraleucel combined with ibrutinib in R/R CLL or SLL: primary results from TRANSCEND CLL 004.
abstract: Patients in the lisocabtagene maraleucel (liso-cel) plus ibrutinib cohort of the phase 1/2, open-label TRANSCEND CLL 004 study had relapsed/refractory (R/R) chronic lymphocytic leukemia (CLL)/small lymphocytic lymphoma (SLL) and received liso-cel (50 × 106 [dose level 1 (DL1)] or 100 × 106 [DL2] chimeric antigen receptor-positive T cells) with concurrent ibrutinib from enrollment through 90 days after liso-cel infusion or longer per investigator discretion. Primary end point was complete response/remission (CR)/CR with incomplete marrow recovery (CRi) by investigator assessment. Among 56 patients who received ibrutinib plus liso-cel (DL1, n = 5; DL2, n = 51), median age was 64.5 years (range, 44-77), 98% had high-risk cytogenetics, and median number of prior therapies was 5 (range, 1-13). Median follow-up was 24.8 months (range, 3.1-51.8). At DL2, CR/CRi rate was 45% (95% confidence interval [CI], 31-60), and overall response rate was 86% (95% CI, 74-94). Median duration of response was not reached (NR; 95% CI, 28.7 to NR) for patients with CR/CRi. Median progression-free survival was 31.4 months (95% CI, 20.1 to NR). In DL1 plus DL2, the most common grade ≥3 treatment-emergent adverse events (TEAEs) were neutropenia (52%) and anemia (41%). Cytokine release syndrome was reported in 80% of the patients (grade 3, 4%; no grade 4/5), and neurological events were reported in 41% (grade 3/4, 11%; no grade 5). Ibrutinib-related TEAEs were reported in 68% of the patients (grade 3/4, 43%; no grade 5). Liso-cel plus ibrutinib demonstrated notable efficacy in patients with R/R CLL/SLL with predictable and manageable safety. llm_summary: Researchers tested whether combining two cancer treatments—lisocabtagene maraleucel, a type of engineered immune cell therapy, and ibrutinib, a targeted drug—could help patients with relapsed or refractory chronic lymphocytic leukemia who had exhausted other options. Among 56 patients studied, 45% achieved complete remission and 86% responded to treatment overall, with a median follow-up showing responses lasting over two years. The combination produced manageable side effects including low blood cell counts and immune reactions, suggesting this approach may offer meaningful benefit for this difficult-to-treat patient population.
llm_summary_expert: The TRANSCEND CLL 004 phase 1/2 trial evaluated lisocabtagene maraleucel (liso-cel) combined with concurrent ibrutinib in 56 patients with relapsed/refractory chronic lymphocytic leukemia or small lymphocytic lymphoma, with a median follow-up of 24.8 months and primary endpoint of complete response or complete response with incomplete marrow recovery. At the recommended dose level 2, the complete response/remission rate was 45% with an overall response rate of 86%, and median progression-free survival was 31.4 months. The most common grade 3 or higher treatment-emergent adverse events were neutropenia (52%) and anemia (41%), with cytokine release syndrome occurring in 80% of patients (4% grade 3, no grade 4/5) and neurological events in 41% (11% grade 3/4, no grade 5). Ibrutinib-related adverse events occurred in 68% of patients with 43% experiencing grade 3/4 severity and no grade 5 events.

title: Transcriptional landscape of nodular lymphocyte-predominant Hodgkin lymphoma and T-cell/histiocyte-rich large B-cell lymphoma: tumor microenvironment and checkpoint genes.
abstract: Nodular lymphocyte-predominant Hodgkin lymphoma (NLPHL) is a rare B-cell malignancy with an indolent course, yet some cases relapse or transform to Tcell/ histiocyte-rich large B-cell lymphoma (THRLBCL). Biological factors underlying poor outcomes in NLPHL are largely unknown, and the relationship between THRLBCL and untransformed NLPHL has not been systematically defined. We analyzed 178 NLPHL and 22 THRLBCL cases using whole-transcriptome RNA sequencing and clinical data. NLPHL patients were younger, had limited-stage disease, and better outcomes than THRLBCL patients. Variant immuno-architectural patterns (IAP) in NLPHL showed THRLBCL-like transcriptional profiles, especially with splenic involvement and high Lymphocyte-Predominant International Prognostic Score (LP-IPS). In-silico deconvolution of the tumor microenvironment (TME) revealed B-cell enrichment in classic NLPHL, intermediate profiles in variant NLPHL, and increased activated CD4+ and CD8+ T-cells and macrophages in THRLBCL. Higher follicular helper T-cell content was associated with shorter event-free survival in an exploratory analysis. NLPHL cases showed strong B-cell and T-helper signatures, whereas THRLBCL cases were enriched for macrophage and cytotoxic T-cell pathways and expressed higher immune checkpoint genes, suggesting an immunosuppressive TME. Signatures defined a spectrum from classic to variant NLPHL and THRLBCL. External validation in independent cohorts reproduced this gradient, supporting a continuous microenvironmental spectrum spanning NLPHL and THRLBCL.

They found that the immune cells surrounding tumors form a spectrum, with classic cases showing more B-cells and variant cases showing more immune-suppressing features similar to the aggressive form. These immune patterns may help predict which patients will have worse outcomes, though further research is needed to confirm this connection.

title: Predictors of learning the memory support system in individuals with amnestic mild cognitive impairment.
abstract: The Memory Support System (MSS) is a memory compensation tool that utilizes a calendar/notebook. Although baseline global cognition, declarative memory, and personality have been shown to predict MSS learning, the learning efficiency across amnestic mild cognitive impairment (aMCI) subtypes remains unclear. To address this gap, this study compared MSS learning in participants with single-domain aMCI (SD-aMCI) versus multi-domain aMCI (MD-aMCI).Five hundred and thirty-six participants with aMCI (SD-aMCI = 268; MD-aMCI = 268) participated in 10-day MSS training during the Healthy Action to Benefit Independence in Thinking ® (HABIT) program. Ordinal logistic regression tested for differences in MSS learning between SD-aMCI and MD-aMCI, with age, gender, education, depression, and baseline global cognition as covariates.Younger age, male gender, fewer years of education, and better baseline global cognition were associated with higher MSS learning efficiency. Participants with SD-aMCI had significantly higher odds of achieving higher MSS final learning score at training end, after controlling for age, gender, education, depression, and baseline global cognition.While age, gender, education, and global cognition are important in MSS learning, having cognitive deficits in domains beyond memory further reduces the ability to learn the MSS. Clinicians may need to tailor training sessions according to participants' cognitive profiles to facilitate learning outcomes.

llm_summary: Researchers examined whether people with mild memory problems could learn to use a memory support system—a calendar and notebook tool—and whether those with memory-only problems learned better than those with multiple cognitive difficulties. Younger age, male gender, lower education, and better overall thinking ability predicted better learning of the system, and people with memory-only problems learned significantly better than those with broader cognitive decline. Clinicians may need to adjust training approaches based on each person's specific cognitive strengths and weaknesses.

title: A Validated Artificial Intelligence Model Versus Urinary Supersaturation Alone for Predicting Kidney Stone Composition.
abstract: To develop and validate an artificial intelligence (AI) model that can identify kidney stone composition more accurately than the EQUIL2 urine supersaturation (SS) algorithm.Patients with both a 24-hour urine SS panel and a kidney stone composition analysis conducted within 90 days of each other between September 24, 2015, and March 15, 2024, were identified (n=13,000 unique patients). Kidney stones were classified as either majority calcium oxalate (CaOx), majority calcium phosphate (CaP), uric acid, or other. A model was developed to predict kidney stone classification using demographic characteristics plus urinary SS panel results. This model was subsequently validated on a held-out data set of paired measurements collected between March 16, 2024, and March 15, 2025 (n=1653). The urinary SS for CaOx, hydroxyapatite (CaP), brushite (CaP), and uric acid were calculated using EQUIL2 according to routine clinical practice and expressed using the delta Gibbs free energy scale.The AI model was significantly more accurate in the validation data set for identifying stone composition compared with SS alone (accuracy, 0.73 vs 0.33; P<.01). Additionally, the model outperformed SS alone in the validation data set for correctly identifying kidney stone composition in all analyses stratified into clinically relevant subgroups by age and sex.In all kidney stone categories and within various subgroups, the AI model outperformed the EQUIL2-calculated SS as well as previously published AI models in the correct prediction of CaOx, CaP, and uric acid kidney stones when using the 24-hour urine SS panel.Copyright © 2026 Mayo Foundation for Medical Education and Research. llm_summary: Researchers developed an artificial intelligence model to predict kidney stone composition using urine test results and compared it to a traditional mathematical method called EQUIL2. The AI model correctly identified stone type 73 percent of the time compared to only 33 percent for the traditional method when tested on new patient data. This suggests that AI analysis of urine chemistry could help doctors better understand what type of kidney stones patients form.
llm_summary_expert: Researchers developed and validated an artificial intelligence model using demographic characteristics and 24-hour urinary supersaturation panel results to predict kidney stone composition in a cohort of 13,000 patients with paired urine chemistry and stone analysis measurements collected between September 2015 and March 2024. The AI model was subsequently validated on an independent dataset of 1,653 paired measurements collected between March 2024 and March 2025, with kidney stones classified into four categories: majority calcium oxalate, majority calcium phosphate, uric acid, or other compositions. The AI model demonstrated significantly higher accuracy than the EQUIL2 urinary supersaturation algorithm alone in the validation dataset, achieving 73% accuracy compared to 33% for supersaturation alone (P<.01). The AI model outperformed supersaturation calculations and previously published AI models across all kidney stone categories and in clinically relevant subgroups stratified by age and sex. The study is limited by its reliance on 24-hour urine supersaturation panels as the primary input feature, which may restrict generalizability to clinical settings where such comprehensive urinary analysis is unavailable.

title: Early Correlates of High-Risk Lymphatic Subtype on T2-Weighted Pre-fontan Cardiac MRI and Associated Clinical Outcomes.
abstract: Lymphatic dysfunction is a severe complication of the Fontan circulation. Type 3 and 4 lymphatic subtypes identified on T2-weighted cardiac MRI (CMR) are associated with worse Fontan outcomes. Correlates of lymphatic subtype are incompletely described. Of the 171 patients with single ventricle physiology who underwent pre-Fontan CMR with T2-weighting to define lymphatic subtype between 2017 and 2021, 148 had standard-risk lymphatics (subtypes 1, 2, and 3 without pre-Fontan chylous effusions), and 23 had high-risk lymphatics (subtypes 3 with a history of pre-Fontan chylous effusions and 4). The two groups did not differ by demographic, anatomic, or pre-Fontan surgical features. High-risk subtype patients had more pre-fontan hospital days (84 vs. 44, p < 0.001), worse atrioventricular valve regurgitation (AVVR) by echocardiogram, higher aortopulmonary collateral (APC) burden (38% vs. 30%, p = 0.004) and Qp: Qs (1.2 vs. 1.05, p = 0.01) by CMR, and higher left pulmonary artery pressure (11mmHg vs. 10mmHg, p = 0.04) and higher systemic ventricular end diastolic pressure (8mmHg vs. 7mmHg, p = 0.02) by cardiac catheterization. High-risk patients were more frequently deemed to be unsuitable for Fontan palliation (22% vs. 4%, p = < 0.001) while those who did undergo palliation had longer post-Fontan length of stay (14 days vs. 9 days, p = 0.01) and more post-fontan chest tube days (10.5 vs. 7, p = 0.002). This study demonstrates a link between pre-Fontan clinical factors and lymphatic subtype. Further work is needed to understand whether modification of these risk factors might impact lymphatic anatomy.© 2026. Patients with high-risk lymphatic patterns had more complications before surgery, were more likely to be deemed unsuitable for the procedure, and experienced longer hospital stays afterward. The findings suggest that certain heart and circulatory problems may be connected to lymphatic dysfunction, though further research is needed to determine whether treating these problems could improve lymphatic health.

title: Assessment of atrioventricular interaction and response to balloon pulmonary angioplasty in chronic thromboembolic pulmonary hypertension using cardiac MRI.
abstract: This study aimed to evaluate atrioventricular interaction in patients with chronic thromboembolic pulmonary hypertension (CTEPH) and to determine the effects of balloon pulmonary angioplasty (BPA) on reversible cardiac remodeling assessed by cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR) imaging.In this prospective single-center study, 52 patients with CTEPH (mean age: 58 ± 11 years; 34 females) and 35 healthy controls underwent CMR imaging. Twenty-five patients (mean age: 60 ± 12 years; 19 females) who underwent BPA received follow-up CMR at a mean interval of 7 ± 5 months. Cardiac structure, function, myocardial deformation, and epicardial adipose tissue (EAT) were assessed based on cine images.Compared with controls, patients with CTEPH demonstrated predominant right-sided cardiac involvement, characterized by reduced right ventricular ejection fraction (p < 0.001), marked enlargement of right atrial (RA) and ventricular (RV) volumes, and severely impaired right heart strain (all p < 0.001). Left ventricular systolic function was relatively preserved, with mildly impaired global circumferential strain (p = 0.011) and a trend toward attenuated longitudinal strain (p = 0.055), whereas all left atrial (LA) strain components were markedly impaired (all p < 0.05), indicating altered atrioventricular interaction. Following BPA, the right heart structure, RV function and deformation, and LA conduit strain improved. EAT was comparable between groups and remained unchanged after BPA.CTEPH involves marked right heart systolic dysfunction and early biventricular diastolic abnormalities associated with impaired atrioventricular interaction. BPA could reverse cardiac remodeling by improving right heart structure, function, and partially recovering atrial deformation after pressure relief.Questions Atrioventricular interaction abnormalities and reversible cardiac remodeling in chronic thromboembolic pulmonary hypertension (CTEPH) after balloon pulmonary angioplasty (BPA) remain insufficiently characterized. Findings CTEPH is associated with impaired right heart strain and altered atrioventricular interaction; BPA improves right heart structure and function and partially recovers atrial deformation. llm_summary: Researchers used heart imaging to examine how chronic blood clots in the lungs affect heart function and whether a procedure called balloon pulmonary angioplasty could reverse the damage. Patients with this condition showed weakened right heart function and abnormal interactions between the heart's chambers, but the procedure improved right heart structure and function while partially restoring normal chamber activity. These findings suggest that relieving pressure on the heart through this procedure can reverse some of the cardiac damage caused by chronic lung blood clots.
llm_summary_expert: Researchers examined atrioventricular interaction and cardiac remodeling in 52 patients with chronic thromboembolic pulmonary hypertension (CTEPH) and 35 healthy controls using cardiac magnetic resonance imaging, with 25 CTEPH patients receiving follow-up imaging after balloon pulmonary angioplasty (BPA) at a mean interval of 7 ± 5 months. Compared with controls, CTEPH patients demonstrated predominant right-sided cardiac involvement including reduced right ventricular ejection fraction (p < 0.001), marked enlargement of right atrial and ventricular volumes, severely impaired right heart strain (all p < 0.001), and markedly impaired left atrial strain components (all p < 0.05), indicating altered atrioventricular interaction. Following BPA, right heart structure and function improved, right ventricular deformation recovered, and left atrial conduit strain improved, whereas epicardial adipose tissue remained comparable between groups and unchanged after intervention. The findings indicate that CTEPH involves marked right heart systolic dysfunction and early biventricular diast.

title: Maximal Aerobic Capacity and Aging in Female Masters Athletes: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis.
abstract: Maximal aerobic capacity ( V ˙  O2max) represents the highest rate at which the body can use oxygen during intense exercise and is a key determinant of endurance performance. Although age-related declines in V ˙  O2max have been well documented in male individuals, less is known about this trajectory in female Masters athletes, defined as individuals aged 40 years or older who often engage in lifelong endurance training.We performed a systematic review and meta-analysis to quantify cross-sectional age-related differences in directly measured V ˙  O2max among female Masters endurance athletes.PubMed and Web of Science were searched from database inception to 14 May, 2025 for studies reporting directly measured V ˙  O2max in female Masters endurance athletes aged 40 years or older. Eligible exercise modalities included running, cycling, swimming, and large muscle-mass ergometry, with testing conducted under standard environmental conditions. Two reviewers independently screened studies, extracted data, and assessed risk of bias using a modified Joanna Briggs Institute checklist. Pooled mean V ˙  O2max values were calculated for predefined age groups (40-49, 50-59, 60-69, and 70 years or older) using a random-effects meta-analysis. Meta-regression was used to estimate the relationship between age and V ˙  O2max.Sixty-nine studies, including 1903 female Masters athletes, met the inclusion criteria. Pooled mean relative V ˙  O2max was 45 mL·kg-1·min-1 (95% confidence interval [CI] 43.0-46.8) in athletes aged 40-49 years, 40 mL·kg-1·min-1 (95% CI 38.5-41.7) in those aged 50-59 years, 35 mL·kg-1·min-1 (95% CI 33.2-37.1) in those aged 60-69 years, and 30 mL·kg-1·min-1 (95% CI 27.2-31.8) in athletes aged 70 years or older. Meta-regression demonstrated that each additional year of age was associated with a 0.57 mL·kg-1·min-1 lower V ˙  O2max (95% CI - 0.70 to - 0.44; P < 0.0001), equivalent to about 11.7% per decade. The association was consistent across testing modalities.This systematic review and meta-analysis demonstrates a progressive age-related decrease in directly measured V ˙  O2max among female Masters endurance athletes. Maximal aerobic capacity declines at an average rate of 0.57 mL·kg-1·min-1 per year after age 40 years, corresponding to approximately 11.7% per decade. This decline is evident across endurance sport disciplines and appears consistent with physiological changes associated with aging despite sustained endurance training. These findings provide female-specific reference values and a quantitative framework for future studies on aerobic capacity trajectories in female athletes.The protocol was registered on the Open Science Framework (OSF; https://doi.org/10.17605/OSF.IO/S2RXZ ).© 2026. title: Artificial Intelligence Models to Predict Recurrence in Patients with Differentiated Thyroid Cancer: A PROBAST + AI Systematic Review of Clinical Applicability.
abstract: Differentiated thyroid cancer (DTC) generally carries an excellent prognosis, yet recurrence occurs in up to 8-9% of patients. Artificial intelligence (AI) models are increasingly proposed to predict DTC recurrence; however, their methodological quality and clinical readiness are poorly defined. We conducted a systematic review to evaluate the methodological quality, risk of bias, and applicability of these models using the PROBAST + AI framework.We searched Ovid MEDLINE, Embase, Cochrane databases, Scopus, and Web of Science from inception to July 13, 2026. Eligible studies included original research developing or validating AI models for recurrence in DTC. Model quality (for development), risk of bias (for evaluation), and applicability were assessed using the PROBAST + AI framework, with a focus on discrimination, calibration, and validation strategies (PROSPERO; registration number [CRD420251004644]).Of 673 records screened, 34 studies were included (21 unique datasets and 13 UCI-derived publications), encompassing 21,267 patients with a recurrence rate of 7.8%. Most were developed in Asian cohorts (17 of 21 datasets) and were structured clinical/tabular variables (82.4%), including demographic, clinical, laboratory, and pathological data, whereas the remaining models incorporated multimodal inputs such as imaging-derived or radiomic features. Notably, nearly one quarter of included studies (13 of 34, 38%) represented reanalysis of a single dataset. Discrimination was reported in 22 of 34 studies (64.7%) (area under the receiver operating characteristic curve [AUC] 0.67-1.00), though only 10 studies assessed calibration, none with standardized metrics. The PROBAST + AI assessment revealed high overall quality concerns in 26 of 34 (76.5%) development studies due to reliance on single-center cohorts, inadequate handling of missing data, and absence of external validation. Only 6 of 34 included studies (17.6%) were judged to have low overall quality concern, whereas 17 of 34 (50.0%) were rated as having low applicability concern.AI models for predicting DTC recurrence show promising discriminatory performance but have substantial methodological shortcomings in development, and a lack of calibration and external validation necessary for clinical use. Given the guidelines' emphasis on risk-adapted de-escalation of therapy, the development of robust, validated, and clinically calibrated AI tools is a priority. Current evidence remains insufficient to support routine clinical use.

title: Expert Strategies: Controversies in Management of Sinonasal Malignancies-Global Perspectives Through a Mixed Methods Approach.
abstract: Sinonasal malignancies (SNMs) are a rare group of diseases with limited high-level evidence to guide management. Where data are currently lacking, contemporary management principles may be guided by clinical expertise and experience.Structured qualitative thematic interviews with multidisciplinary international experts in the management of SNMs. A mixed-methods design involving qualitative and quantitative analysis of the collected data was completed.A total of 40 experts comprising 22 academic institutions across nine countries were included. Surgical factors, including anatomic limitations of resectability and criteria for consideration of orbital exenteration, are discussed. There are mixed opinions on the role of induction systemic therapy and when to employ its use. Nuances in the management of specific histopathologies, including olfactory neuroblastoma, adenoid cystic carcinoma, sinonasal mucosal melanoma, adenocarcinoma, nasopharyngeal carcinoma, sinonasal undifferentiated carcinoma, squamous cell carcinoma, and rhabdomyosarcoma, are explored. Commonalities and discrepancies between experts are summarized. The importance of histopathology-specific management and multidisciplinary management is highlighted.Management of SNMs is complex, with a wide variety of practice patterns among experts. This work serves as a modern guide for expert management paradigms where little data currently exists.© 2026 The Author(s). llm_summary: Researchers interviewed 40 international experts from 22 academic institutions about how to treat sinonasal malignancies, which are rare cancers in the nasal passages and sinuses. The study found that experts use widely varying treatment approaches depending on the specific type of cancer, with mixed opinions on when to use chemotherapy before surgery and whether to remove the eye in advanced cases. Because sinonasal malignancies lack strong scientific evidence to guide treatment, this expert consensus serves as a practical guide for doctors managing these uncommon diseases.
llm_summary_expert: Researchers conducted a mixed-methods study involving structured qualitative thematic interviews with 40 multidisciplinary experts across 22 academic institutions in nine countries to identify contemporary management principles for sinonasal malignancies where high-level evidence is limited. The study examined expert opinions on surgical factors including anatomic resectability limitations and orbital exenteration criteria, the role of induction systemic therapy, and histopathology-specific management approaches across eight tumor types including olfactory neuroblastoma, adenoid cystic carcinoma, and sinonasal mucosal melanoma. The analysis identified both commonalities and discrepancies among experts regarding optimal management strategies, with particular emphasis on the importance of histopathology-specific and multidisciplinary approaches. Management of sinonasal malignancies demonstrates substantial variation in practice patterns among international experts despite similar institutional settings and clinical experience. This work provides a contemporary guide for expert management paradigms in a disease area where randomized controlled trial evidence is currently lacking.

title: A translational platform for brain-computer interfaces and adaptive neuromodulation: Technical characterization, long-term validation, and implementation of the CorTec brain interchange-BCI2000 ecosystem.
abstract: Adaptive neuromodulation systems and implantable brain-computer interfaces (BCIs) are promising therapies for neurological and psychiatric disorders. However, their broader translation into research and clinical practice remains limited by technological complexity, restricted access to implantable research platforms, and the lack of standardized, reproducible experimental workflows. We therefore aimed to develop and validate an open, general-purpose translational ecosystem that enables rapid development, evaluation, and dissemination of novel neuromodulation and implantable BCI paradigms.Approach: The CorTec Brain Interchange (BIC) implantable neural sensing and stimulation device was integrated with the open-source BCI2000 platform to create a modular, extensible neuromodulation ecosystem. We established a standardized battery of quantitative assessments to characterize implantable neuromodulation systems to comprehensively evaluate the CorTec BIC device through benchtop characterization, long-term preclinical in vivo validation, and a human feasibility demonstration using the benchtop BIC system connected to externalized leads.Results: Comprehensive benchtop characterization of the BIC device independently validated previously reported performance while extending its evaluation through quantification of recording noise, acquisition and stimulation latencies, and validation of impedance measurements. Long-term in vivo validation in five canines, with the longest implantation exceeding three years, demonstrated stable chronic recordings while also capturing progressive deterioration of individual channels through longitudinal changes in signal quality and impedance. The ecosystem enabled active functional decoding more than two years after implantation, closed-loop stimulation using arbitrary spectral biomarkers, capturing brain stimulation evoked potentials, detection of epilepsy-associated biomarkers and observational assessment of their response to stimulation. In addition, we translated an established one-dimensional BCI cursor-control paradigm to the BIC benchtop system, demonstrating ecosystem portability and feasibility with a human participant. Finally, we share surgical protocols, imaging and analysis pipelines, datasets, and software to facilitate reproducible neuromodulation research.Significance: We present a versatile, open-source translational ecosystem that supports a wide range of neuromodulation and implantable BCI applications with minimal modification. By combining comprehensive hardware characterization with standardized software tools and experimental workflows, this work provides a practical reference for researchers adopting the BIC platform while establishing a broadly applicable framework for systematic characterization of implantable neuromodulation systems. The ecosystem lowers technical barriers to implantable neurotechnology research, promotes reproducibility, and provides a foundation for accelerating the development and clinical translation of next-generation adaptive neuromodulation and implantable BCI therapies for patients with neurological and psychiatric disorders.© 2026 IOP Publishing Ltd. Long-term testing in dogs over more than three years showed the device could maintain stable recordings and enable brain-controlled functions, while a human feasibility test demonstrated the system's potential for clinical use. title: The Triple-Tapered Uncemented Femoral Stems in Slight Varus Demonstrated Excellent Early Survivorship and Clinical Results.
abstract: Femoral stem alignment in total hip arthroplasty (THA) can influence implant stability and long-term fixation. The triple-tapered uncemented stems have gained widespread use, and the recommended surgical technique often results in slight varus positioning. The effect of this alignment pattern on implant performance remains uncertain. The purpose of this study was to evaluate how coronal alignment of triple-tapered stems affects survivorship, periprosthetic fracture incidence, clinical outcomes, and radiographic results.A retrospective review of an institutional joint registry identified 1,730 primary THAs implanted with one of three triple-tapered, uncemented femoral stems. Coronal alignment at three months postoperatively classified 1,315 stems (76.0%) as neutral (0 ± 3°), 408 (23.6%) as varus, and seven (0.4%) as valgus. Outcomes assessed included revision and reoperation rates, periprosthetic fractures, Harris Hip Scores (HHS), and radiographic findings. The mean follow-up was two years (range, 2 to 8).There were six femoral stem revisions (0.3%) that occurred, all in neutrally aligned stems, yielding a 5-year survivorship free of femoral revision of 99.5% (95% confidence interval [CI], 98.9 to 99.9) for neutral stems and 100% for varus stems (P = 0.60). Survivorship free of any revision (P = 0.82) or any reoperation (P = 0.68) did not differ between groups. Periprosthetic fractures occurred in 15 neutral stems (1.1%) and one varus stem (0.2%) (P = 0.10). Periprosthetic fracture rates were also similar between collared and collarless designs (P = 0.18).More than 20% of triple-tapered stems were implanted in slight varus. Varus alignment did not adversely affect 5-year implant survivorship or periprosthetic fracture incidence. The triple-tapered uncemented stems, with or without a collar, demonstrated excellent early performance even when inserted in slight varus. These findings support the continued use of broach-based techniques that may naturally position the femoral stem in mild varus and provide reassurance that such alignment does not compromise early fixation or stability.Copyright © 2026. Stems placed in a slightly inward angle (varus) performed just as well as those in a neutral position, with both showing excellent survival rates above 99 percent and similar rates of fractures. These findings suggest that the slight inward positioning that naturally occurs during standard surgical techniques does not harm the implant's early performance.
llm_summary_expert: Researchers examined 1,730 primary total hip arthroplasties implanted with triple-tapered uncemented femoral stems, classifying coronal alignment at three months postoperatively as neutral (76.0%), varus (23.6%), or valgus (0.4%), with mean follow-up of two years. The primary endpoints were femoral stem revision rates, periprosthetic fracture incidence, Harris Hip Scores, and radiographic findings. title: A Systematic Review of Skin Substitutes and Collagen Dressings for Primary Surgical Wound Healing: Implications for Total Joint Arthroplasty.
abstract: Skin substitutes and collagen dressings are commonly used as adjuncts to treat chronic, non-healing wounds. Recently, surgeons have begun to use these products in patients undergoing primary total joint arthroplasty (TJA). The purpose of this study was to evaluate the efficacy and cost of the prophylactic use of these dressings in primary TJA and any surgical incision with primary closure.The MEDLINE, Embase, and Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials databases were searched for studies published on skin substitutes and collagen dressings used in any surgical incision with primary wound closure, including primary TJA. All included studies underwent qualitative assessment and quantitative homogeneity testing followed by a systematic review to assess the efficacy of collagen and skin substitute dressings. After a critical appraisal of 8,776 publications, 11 studies were included for analyses.Of the 11 included studies, seven evaluated collagen dressings and four evaluated placenta-derived tissue dressings, with inconsistent results and heterogeneous outcome reporting. There were seven studies that reported lower wound complication rates with a skin substitute or collagen dressing, six of which reached statistical significance. There was one study that evaluated collagen dressing use in primary TJA and demonstrated a reduction in wound-related reoperations (one of 30 versus three of 30); however, the authors did not recommend routine use. Among the placenta-derived studies, healing time outcomes were inconsistent.There is no high-quality evidence to support the use of skin substitutes or collagen dressings after primary TJA. Non-arthroplasty studies found modest benefit in primary wound healing for surgical wounds other than primary TJA; however, wound biology in these locations fundamentally differs from the hip or knee. Extrapolating the use of these dressings to primarily closed TJA incisions is not supported by the limited currently available literature.Copyright © 2026. Published by Elsevier Inc.

title: New Large Language Models Outperform Older Models and Hallucinate Less in Operative Note Data Extraction.
abstract: Recent improvements in large language models (LLMs) may provide a scalable solution for registry data curation. However, trust in model outputs remains limited by hallucinations, wherein models invent information. Given the rapid pace of LLM development, the purpose of this study was to compare the accuracy and hallucination rates of a "newer" and an "older" and previously evaluated LLM in extracting total hip arthroplasty (THA) operative variables.Surgical approach, fixation technique, and bearing surface were manually abstracted from 1,000 primary THA operative notes from 47 different surgeons. Using 25% of the dataset, we iteratively developed prompts to query two locally hosted LLMs (one released in 2024, the older model, and the other released in 2026, the newer model) to extract those three data points. We tested the extraction pipeline for the best prompts on the remaining 75% of the dataset. We calculated performance metrics and manually assessed 100 sample output reasonings from each model for hallucinations.Overall Performance: The newer model exhibited higher accuracy than the older model across all three data extraction tasks: surgical approach (98 versus 96%), fixation technique (98 versus 96%), and bearing surface (93 versus 89%). For each task, the highest-performing prompt technique for the newer model was comparatively simpler than the highest-performing prompt technique for the older model. Hallucination Rate Analyses: Across all evaluated extraction domains, the newer model demonstrated significantly lower hallucination rates compared with the older model. Hallucination rates for surgical approach, fixation technique, and bearing surface extraction were 5, 3, and 11% for the newer model versus 49, 20, and 49% for the older model, respectively.The newer LLM extracted THA operative variables more accurately and hallucinated substantially less with simpler prompts than the 2-year-old model. These findings suggest LLMs are improving their ability to follow directions and reason without inventing information. However, lower rates of hallucinations persist, limiting trustworthiness.Copyright © 2026. Published by Elsevier Inc.

llm_summary: Researchers compared two artificial intelligence language models to see how well they could extract surgical information from hip replacement operation notes, testing whether newer models hallucinate less, or invent false information. The newer model from 2026 was significantly more accurate and made far fewer errors than the older 2024 model across all three types of information extracted, though both models still occasionally invented details. These results suggest that newer artificial intelligence systems are improving at following instructions and providing reliable information, but some risk of fabrication remains.

The study employed iterative prompt development on 25% of the dataset followed by testing on the remaining 75%, with manual assessment of 100 sample outputs from each model for hallucinations. The newer model demonstrated higher accuracy across all three extraction tasks (surgical approach 98% versus 96%, fixation technique 98% versus 96%, bearing surface 93% versus 89%) and substantially lower hallucination rates (5%, 3%, and 11% respectively versus 49%, 20%, and 49% for the older model). The newer LLM achieved superior performance using simpler prompt techniques compared to the more complex prompts required for optimal performance of the older model. Although hallucination rates were substantially reduced in the newer model, persistent hallucinations across all extraction domains limit the trustworthiness of LLM outputs.

title: MR Elastography in Disorders of CSF Dynamics: Current Evidence, Pitfalls, and the Road to Clinical Adoption.
abstract: Disorders of CSF dynamics, including idiopathic normal pressure hydrocephalus, idiopathic intracranial hypertension (IIH), and spontaneous intracranial hypotension (SIH), are frequent clinical and imaging phenotypes that overlap with other disease processes. Although conventional MRI remains central for identifying characteristic morphologic features, many imaging findings have variable sensitivity, particularly across disease stages. As a result, current diagnostic pathways and treatment selection are still often reliant on invasive, snapshot-based physiologic tests. MR elastography (MRE) provides a noninvasive, quantitative approach to probe brain viscoelastic properties reflecting tissue microstructure and mechanical strain. These properties are influenced by intracranial pressure volume states within the Monro Kellie constraints, offering a potential "systems level" biomarker of intracranial compliance and CSF venous coupling. This review summarizes the technical foundations of brain MRE relevant to radiologists, including the fundamentals and technical aspects of the technique, and the key sources of measurement variability that influence interpretability and reproducibility. It synthesizes the current clinical evidence supporting MRE for diagnosis, phenotyping, and longitudinal treatment assessment across CSF dynamics disorders, with emphasis on practical integration into contemporary imaging workflows and standardized region of interest reporting. Finally, we highlight the limitations of existing literature and priorities for future research for MRE in this patient population.© 2026 by American Journal of Neuroradiology.

title: Ventilator Modes Used to Facilitate Liberation From Mechanical Ventilation: A Scoping Review.
abstract: Liberation from invasive ventilation involves gradual decrements in respiratory support, spontaneous breathing trials, or both. Although various ventilator modes have been studied to facilitate weaning, the approaches used across trials for the highest risk patients are not well summarized. We sought to summarize the different ventilator modes and liberation strategies that have been investigated in randomized controlled trials (RCTs) of critically ill adults at risk for difficult or prolonged weaning from invasive ventilation.We searched MEDLINE, Embase, PubMed, and Cochrane Library databases from inception to January 2026.We conducted a scoping review of RCTs that enrolled critically ill adults (≥ 18 yr) who received invasive ventilation for greater than or equal to 24 hours and were considered to have either difficult or prolonged weaning (Weaning according to a New Definition [WIND] group "no wean," "difficult weaning," or "prolonged weaning") and compared two or more assisted ventilatory modes. We excluded trials that compared ventilatory modes for spontaneous breathing test (SBT) conduct, invasive vs. noninvasive ventilation, or tracheostomized patients at the time of randomization.We extracted data related to eligibility criteria, outcomes, and weaning protocols and assessed risk of bias using a modified Cochrane risk of bias tool in duplicate.Among 38 eligible trials, the most studied ventilatory modes were pressure support ventilation (71.1%, 27 trials) and synchronized intermittent or intermittent mandatory ventilation (31.6%, 12 trials). The most frequently studied automated modes were SmartCare/pressure support (15.8%, six trials) and proportional assist ventilation (15.8%, six trials). Weaning typically used a gradual reduction in support without a mode change (52.6%, 20 trials), or with intermittent SBTs (31.6%, 12 trials). Overall risk of bias was commonly high due to a probably high risk of selective reporting.Diverse modes and strategies have been evaluated to achieve liberation. Future research should focus on adequately powered, high-quality trials of the effect of commonly used and widely available modes and strategies on clinically important outcomes for liberation from mechanical ventilation of high-risk patients.Copyright © 2026 The Authors. title: Task Force 9: Clinical Considerations for the Care of Athletes with Cardiac Channelopathies.
abstract: Cardiac channelopathies, including long QT syndrome, catecholaminergic polymorphic ventricular tachycardia, Brugada syndrome, and short QT syndrome, are heterogeneous conditions, which can lead to varying risks in athletes depending on their symptoms, disease severity, genotype, and therapies initiated. Historically, athletes with these conditions were excluded from participation with blanket restrictions, despite an absence of data. More recently, a number of studies have provided more scientific evidence to guide decision making and have been incorporated into these guidelines for athletes with cardiac channelopathies. Many athletes with these conditions may be supported in their decision to return to play as part of a shared decision-making model when they have been assessed, risk stratified, and appropriately treated by a specialist with expertise in these conditions.Copyright © 2026 by the American College of Sports Medicine.

title: Task Force 4: Clinical Considerations for the Care of Athletes with Genetic Cardiomyopathies.
abstract: The updated AHA/ACC Scientific Statement on Clinical Considerations for Competitive Sports Participation for Athletes with Cardiovascular Conditions presents the clinical considerations for athletes with genetic cardiomyopathies, including hypertrophic, dilated, arrhythmogenic, and left ventricular hypertrabeculation. This ACSM Official Pronouncement complements the 2020 ACC/AHA Scientific Statement by providing athlete-specific context, practical guidance for shared decision-making, and genotype-informed risk assessment for competitive sports participation, moving away from blanket sports disqualifications. Sports participation recommendations for each condition are tailored to risk levels, symptomatology, and genotype. Regular follow-ups and close surveillance are advised. This evolving approach underscores the importance of individualized care, ongoing research, and the integration of new data to better inform shared decision-making on the risks and benefits of competitive sports in athletes with cardiomyopathies.Copyright © 2026 by the American College of Sports Medicine.

title: Explaining Cancer Clinical Trial Willingness: The Relative Roles of Information Empowerment and Interpersonal Discrimination.
abstract: Racial and ethnic disparities in cancer trial participation persist. Structural racism frameworks emphasize medical mistrust and discrimination in healthcare, whereas communication inequality frameworks emphasize gaps in awareness, knowledge, and exposure. Guided by both, we examined racial and ethnic differences in trial willingness, whether interpersonal discrimination in healthcare and information empowerment (trial knowledge, awareness, information confidence, and prior experience) account for them, and whether the two mechanisms are related or interact.Data (N = 2,812) came from a 2023 multistate cancer focused needs assessment in Arizona, Florida, and the Midwest. Race and ethnicity were categorized as non-Hispanic (NH) White, NH Black, Other NH, and Hispanic (any race). Willingness was modeled using ordinal logistic regression. Model 1 adjusted for sociodemographic characteristics and region; Model 2 added discrimination; Model 3 added information empowerment instead; Model 4 added both. Whether the two mechanisms interact was tested using a likelihood ratio test.In Model 1, Hispanic and Other NH adults were less willing to join a cancer clinical trial than NH White adults, whereas NH Black adults did not differ significantly. Discrimination (Model 2) only slightly attenuated these differences, whereas information empowerment (Model 3) moved them toward parity. In Model 4, lower willingness persisted only for Other NH adults. All four information empowerment measures and healthcare discrimination were associated with greater willingness. llm_summary: Researchers examined why racial and ethnic differences exist in willingness to participate in cancer clinical trials, studying whether lack of knowledge about trials or experiences of discrimination in healthcare explained these differences. Information empowerment—including trial knowledge, awareness, and confidence—was more strongly associated with willingness than discrimination experiences, and addressing communication gaps moved most racial and ethnic groups toward equal participation levels. The findings suggest that improving trial information and outreach may be more effective than addressing discrimination alone in reducing disparities in cancer trial participation.
llm_summary_expert: Researchers examined racial and ethnic differences in cancer clinical trial willingness among 2,812 adults from a 2023 multistate needs assessment in Arizona, Florida, and the Midwest, using ordinal logistic regression to test whether interpersonal discrimination and information empowerment (trial knowledge, awareness, information confidence, and prior experience) explained observed disparities. In the baseline model adjusted for sociodemographic characteristics, Hispanic and Other non-Hispanic (NH) adults showed lower willingness than NH White adults, while NH Black adults did not differ significantly. Information empowerment substantially attenuated disparities and moved willingness toward parity across groups, whereas discrimination alone produced only slight attenuation, with trial knowledge demonstrating a stronger association with willingness than healthcare discrimination per standard deviation. When both mechanisms were included in the model, lower willingness persisted only among Other NH adults, and the two mechanisms were associated but did not interact. The findings suggest that equity efforts should prioritize trial communication and proactive invitations while addressing disrespectful care, though the persistent disparity among Other NH adults requires further disaggregated investigation.

title: Primary Tumor Biology, Recurrence and Survival After Colorectal Liver Metastasis Resection: The BIO-CRLM Study.
abstract: To evaluate whether integrated primary tumor biology, combining primary tumor location and RAS/BRAF status, defines recurrence phenotypes and survival trajectories after liver resection for colorectal liver metastases (CRLM).Selection for resection remains largely morphology-based, although tumor biology strongly influences post-hepatectomy outcomes. Primary tumor site and RAS/BRAF status are individually prognostic, but whether their integration identifies distinct post-resection trajectories is unclear.An international multicenter cohort of patients undergoing liver resection for CRLM between 2017 and 2023 was analyzed. Integrated biology was defined a priori as left-sided-wild-type, right-sided-wild-type, rectal-wild-type, left-sided-RAS-mutant, right-sided-RAS-mutant, rectal RAS-mutant, and BRAF-mutant disease. Primary outcomes were recurrence-free survival (RFS) and overall survival (OS). Secondary outcomes included early recurrence, disseminated first recurrence, and first recurrence phenotype.Among 3162 patients from 44 centers, 2415 (76.4%) developed recurrence and 1342 (42.4%) died. Integrated biology was independently associated with both RFS and OS (global P<0.001 for both). Compared with left-WT tumors, the highest mortality risks were observed in BRAF-mutant disease [hazard ratio (HR): 2.68, 95% CI: 2.02-3.57, P<0.001] and right-RAS-mutant disease (HR: 2.32, 95% CI: 1.94-2.79, P<0.001). Integrated biology was also associated with early recurrence, disseminated first recurrence, and first recurrence phenotype. Rectal-RAS-mutant tumors had the strongest association with lung-only recurrence [relative risk ratio (RRR): 3.38, 95% CI: 2.22-5.13, P<0.001] and disseminated recurrence (RRR: 2.57, 95% CI: 1.86-3.55, P<0.001) relative to liver-only recurrence.Integrated primary tumor biology identifies clinically distinct post-hepatectomy disease trajectories after CRLM resection. title: How I Teach: Management of Acute Respiratory Distress Syndrome Using the MAPS Framework.
abstract: Teaching learners to manage acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) requires integration of complex concepts, including ARDS pathophysiology, airway management, mechanical ventilation, and evidence-based adjunctive and rescue therapies. Given this complexity, ARDS is well suited for a longitudinal educational approach that combines conceptual learning with bedside application and deliberate reinforcement. We describe a longitudinal weeklong curriculum for teaching ARDS management that integrates focused content delivery, patient-centered bedside application, spaced repetition, and simulation-based practice.© The Author(s) 2026. The curriculum integrates multiple learning methods including focused lectures, bedside application with real patients, repeated reinforcement of key concepts, and simulation-based practice to help learners master this complex medical condition. title: Defining and managing NF1-related peripheral nerve sheath tumors at risk for malignant transformation: Consensus from the Atypical Neurofibroma Symposium.
abstract: People with neurofibromatosis type 1 (NF1) are at risk for developing peripheral nerve sheath tumors (PNSTs) ranging from benign neurofibromas to high-grade sarcomas. PNSTs known as atypical neurofibromas are at increased risk for malignant transformation. In 2017 the term ANNUBP (atypical neurofibromatous neoplasm of uncertain biologic potential) was proposed for PNSTs at increased risk for malignant transformation based on histopathologic features. Subsequently it was recognized that PNSTs not meeting ANNUBP criteria could still have concerning clinical, imaging and molecular features. A State of the Science conference addressed how to define these pre-cancerous PNSTs and reached consensus regarding clinical management and priority areas of research. Key recommendations from this symposium include: (1) using a combination of histologic, molecular and imaging features to define pre-malignant "at-risk" PNST; (2) recognizing that people with NF1 may be divided into "higher-risk" and "average-risk" for MPNST based on features such as their germline NF1 variant, internal tumor burden and history of malignancy or radiotherapy and; (3) the need to validate consensus screening and surveillance strategies based on personal and tumor-related risk factors. These recommendations will advance the ability to standardize care, and potentially fuel research that enables early diagnosis, prevention of malignant transformation and improved outcomes.Published by Oxford University Press on behalf of the Society for Neuro-Oncology 2026.

title: Beyond Complete Revascularization in STEMI: Revisiting the Vulnerable Plaque Hypothesis and the Emerging Role of Preventive PCI in Non-Culprit Coronary Arteries.
abstract: Complete revascularization is the preferred treatment strategy for hemodynamically stable patients with ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) and multivessel coronary artery disease. However, substantial residual cardiovascular risk persists despite successful treatment of angiographically or physiologically significant lesions, highlighting the limitations of revascularization strategies based solely on stenosis severity or ischemia. Increasing evidence demonstrates that many subsequent acute coronary syndromes originate from biologically high-risk, non-flow-limiting non-culprit plaques rather than flow-limiting lesions. In this review, we discuss the evolution of STEMI management from the recent focus on complete revascularization toward plaque-guided strategies, including the role of invasive and non-invasive imaging for vulnerable plaque assessment, the emerging evidence supporting preventive PCI of high-risk non-culprit lesions, and ongoing clinical trials shaping this field. Collectively, these advances provide a framework for investigating precision revascularization strategies that integrate plaque morphology, coronary physiology, multimodality imaging, and patient-level cardiovascular risk. Ongoing randomized trials are essential to determine whether plaque-guided preventive intervention improves clinically meaningful outcomes beyond contemporary approaches to revascularization and optimal medical therapy.© 2026 Wiley Periodicals LLC.

title: Physician Job Choice and Support for Abortion Access in the Post Dobbs Landscape: a Survey Study of High-Risk Specialty Trainees.
abstract: Physicians have always had to balance personal ethics, professional obligations, and legal constraints when providing abortion care; however, since the United States Supreme Court ruling in Dobbs v. Jackson Women's Health Organization, the legal framework governing this care has shifted substantially, raising concerns about physician workforce stability. The primary aim in our pilot study was to assess how likely states' abortion laws will influence where physicians accept their first job after residency or fellowship. Our other objectives were to assess physician support for abortion access and well-being post Dobbs. We hypothesized that the majority of physicians would be likely to consider states' abortion laws when looking for first post training jobs, would support abortion access, and would have had their well-being affected.We surveyed anesthesiology, emergency medicine, and obstetrics-gynecology (OB-GYN) residents and fellows.We achieved only a 1.2% response rate. In this small data set, a majority (65.6%) of residents and fellows said that they are likely to consider state abortion laws when deciding where to accept their first post-training job, with OB-GYNs (90.7%) having the greatest majority. Eight out of ten physicians were supportive of medical and surgical abortion access (87.2%; 86.1%). A majority of physicians were supportive of abortion across all demographics, even Catholics, deviating only when assessed by political party affiliation. A majority of physicians (56.5%) were negatively affected by the Dobbs decision, regardless of the abortion law where they practice. Cisgender women and OB-GYN trainees were most impacted.The response rate limits any generalizability of our findings, and future research is needed. In this pilot study, the majority of physicians indicated that they will consider states' abortion laws when accepting their first job, and a minority of physicians may be willing to work in states with abortion bans. To promote physician retention and recruitment, future research should investigate how access to reproductive care impacts physicians' professional and personal well-being.

A majority of respondents indicated they would consider state abortion restrictions when deciding where to accept their first job, with obstetrician-gynecologists showing the strongest preference to avoid restrictive states. However, the study's very low response rate of 1.2% means these findings may not represent the views of all physicians in these specialties.
llm_summary_expert: Researchers surveyed anesthesiology, emergency medicine, and obstetrics-gynecology residents and fellows to assess how state abortion laws influence physician job choice, support for abortion access, and well-being following the Dobbs v. Jackson Women's Health Organization decision. The study achieved a 1.2% response rate and measured physicians' likelihood of considering state abortion laws when accepting first post-training positions, their support for medical and surgical abortion access, and self-reported impacts on well-being. Among respondents, 65.6% indicated they would likely consider state abortion laws when choosing their first job, with 90.7% of OB-GYN trainees reporting this consideration, and approximately 87% supported medical abortion access and 86% supported surgical abortion access. A majority of physicians (56.5%) reported negative effects on well-being from the Dobbs decision, with cisgender women and OB-GYN trainees experiencing the greatest impact.

title: Aligning Clinical Trial Reporting: A systematic analysis and position statement by the International Consortium for MDS.
abstract: Variability in how clinical trial elements are reported can hinder accurate interpretation and comparison of trial results. Here, we systematically analyzed published manuscripts of therapeutic clinical trials in myelodysplastic syndromes/neoplasms (MDS) focusing on how key data elements were reported and made recommendations on how to improve this reporting. We included peer-reviewed full text manuscripts that reported results of clinical trials in MDS and were published between January 1, 2015 to December 31, 2024. We analyzed the presence or absence of several pre-determined key reporting elements and then synthesized these data to evaluate for consistency across manuscripts. We identified substantial variability in descriptions of patient characteristics, as well as the definitions used for response criteria. For example, baseline ANC was reported in only 16% of lower-risk MDS studies and 23% of higher-risk MDS studies, while baseline bone marrow blast percentage was reported in only 55% of higher-risk MDS manuscripts. In addition, response endpoints lacked standardization, with six unique definitions of RBC transfusion independence identified in lower-risk MDS trials and seven different definitions of overall response rate identified in higher-risk MDS trials. Informed by the results of this analysis, we then performed a modified-Delphi process for members of the International Consortium for MDS (icMDS) to develop consensus-based recommendations for consistent and accurate reporting of MDS clinical trial results. We advocate that these recommendations serve as benchmarks and templates for clinical trial reporting in MDS to improve interpretability and comparison of results.Copyright © 2026 American Society of Hematology.

The study led to recommendations for standardized reporting to make future trial results easier to compare and understand.
