title: Serologic Discrimination of Histologic Classes in Lupus Nephritis: A Cross-Sectional Analysis with Exploratory 12-Month Outcomes.
abstract: Anti-dsDNA positivity and hypocomplementemia are markers of active lupus nephritis (LN), but their ability to discriminate between histologic phenotypes remains underexplored, particularly for mixed proliferative/membranous LN (mixed LN). We compared baseline serologic markers across proliferative LN, membranous LN, and mixed LN, and evaluated their discriminative performance for histologic class.We conducted a retrospective cross-sectional study of 132 patients with biopsy-proven LN, categorized according to the International Society of Nephrology/Renal Pathology Society (ISN/RPS) classification into proliferative LN (class III/IV), membranous LN (class V), and mixed LN (class III/IV+V). Baseline anti-dsDNA and complements C3 and C4 were compared across groups. Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis assessed the ability of individual and combined markers to discriminate between histologic classes. Kidney outcomes at 12 months were explored in a secondary cohort (n=88).Of 132 patients, 57 had proliferative LN, 32 had membranous LN, and 43 had mixed LN. Anti-dsDNA was significantly higher, and C3 and C4 significantly lower, in proliferative and mixed LN compared to membranous LN (P<0.05 for all), while proliferative and mixed LN did not differ significantly. On ROC analysis, individual markers achieved AUCs of 0.68-0.71 for distinguishing proliferative or mixed LN from membranous LN, with combined models yielding AUCs of 0.73. However, discrimination between proliferative and mixed LN was poor (combined AUC 0.62). At 12 months, kidney outcomes were comparable across groups.Mixed LN exhibits a serologic profile resembling proliferative LN, both sharing elevated anti-dsDNA and low complement levels, but distinct from membranous LN. title: Interferon-γ-Mediated Inflammation: To Kill or Not to Kill.
abstract: In the host immune system, cytotoxic T cells (CTLs) play a critical role in mounting an effective attack against tumorigenic cells. CTLs can drive this immunity through two mechanisms: direct lysis of tumor cells via cytolytic granule release and secretion of inflammatory cytokines such as interferon-γ (IFN-γ). While IFN-γ is well known for its role in upregulating major histocompatibility complex (MHC) class I presentation and differentiating naïve T cells into T helper 1 cells, its role in direct killing of tumor cells is less understood. In a recent study, we found that tumor cells lacking the signaling kinases TANK-binding kinase 1 (TBK1) and inhibitor of κB kinase ε (IKK-ε) were more easily killed by IFN-γ-producing T cells than their wild-type counterparts. In the absence of both kinases, IFN-γ upregulated the expression of both tumor necrosis factor receptor 1 (TNFR1) and the left-handed nuclei acid sensor Z-DNA-binding protein 1 (ZBP1) to trigger cell-autonomous apoptosis. Loss of TBK1 and IKK-ε also heightened nuclear factor κ-light-chain-enhancer of activated B cells (NF-κB) activation downstream of IFN-γ, along with increased production of inflammatory chemokines and cytokines. Thus, IFN-γ-induced death was paired with an inflammatory environment when the two kinases were absent. Our study illustrates that TBK1 and IKK-ε not only have a role in mediating a type I IFN response but also in regulating IFN-γ-induced death and NF-κB-dependent inflammation. Herein, we briefly highlight how the wiring of these kinases may have evolved over time to combat opportunistic pathogens and how this may shape our approach to cancer immunotherapy.

title: H3K9 demethylase KDM3A potentiates interferon signaling and macrophage-driven inflammation in atherosclerosis.
abstract: Macrophages drive atherosclerosis through inflammatory activation programs shaped by metabolic and epigenetic reprogramming. H3K9 methylation enforces heterochromatin states and represses transcription, whereas removal of this histone modification creates transcriptionally permissive chromatin. Here, we identified KDM3A-mediated H3K9 demethylation to enhance chromatin accessibility at interferon (IFN) signaling loci, thereby promoting IFN production and downstream IFN-dependent transcriptional and chemokine responses. In a mouse model of atherosclerosis, hematopoietic Kdm3a deficiency reduces lesion size, necrotic core formation, and neutrophil recruitment. Mechanistically, Kdm3a-deficient macrophages show impaired chemokine secretion and reduced neutrophil recruitment both in vitro and in vivo. In primary human macrophages, KDM3A knockdown suppressed IFN responses; consistently KDM3A-dependent gene signatures were enriched in IFN-inducible macrophages within human atherosclerotic plaques, and computational modeling predicted a shift toward more stable plaque phenotypes upon KDM3A inhibition. Together, these findings establish KDM3A as an epigenetic regulator that sustains IFN-driven macrophage activation and promotes progression of atherosclerosis, nominating KDM3A as a potential target for selectively modulating IFN-dependent inflammation.

title: Early Treatment Failure in Patients With Relapsed/Refractory Multiple Myeloma Receiving Bispecific T-Cell Engagers: Development and Validation of the CHARGE Prognostic Index.
abstract: Outcomes with bispecific T-cell engagers (TCEs) in relapsed/refractory multiple myeloma (RRMM) are heterogeneous. A practical tool to guide prognosis is needed. We developed a model integrating clinical, biological, and treatment-related variables to predict progression-free survival (PFS) in patients receiving B-cell maturation antigen (BCMA)- or G-protein-coupled receptor class 5 member D-directed TCEs.We evaluated outcomes of 577 BCMA-directed and 366 talquetamab treatments across 15 US Multiple Myeloma Immunotherapy Consortium centers. Variables significantly associated with inferior PFS in a multivariate Cox model were incorporated into a prognostic score and validated in an independent multicenter International Myeloma Foundation cohort.With a median follow-up of 8.4 months, the median PFS was 6.4 months (7.0 months for BCMA TCE; 6.1 months for talquetamab); 92% of patients were triple-class-refractory. Six variables significantly associated with inferior PFS-high-risk cytogenetic abnormalities (HRCAs) [del(17p) or ≥2 HRCAs], hyperferritinemia (≥600 ng/mL), anemia (hemoglobin <9 g/dL), early relapse (<18 months from frontline therapy), general performance status (Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group Performance Status ≥2), and exposure to prior BCMA-directed therapy-were combined to form the CHARGE index, stratifying patients into three risk groups. The median PFS was 21.8 months (95% CI, 11.7 to not reached), 7.1 months (95% CI, 6.1 to 10.1), and 1.6 months (95% CI, 1.2 to 2.5) in the low-, intermediate-, and high-risk groups, respectively; hazard ratios (HRs) were 2.0 (95% CI, 1.5 to 2.7) and 4.8 (95% CI, 3.5 to 6.7) for intermediate- and high-risk versus low-risk groups. External validation (n = 173) showed that the median PFS was not reached, 7.0 months, and 3.0 months, with corresponding HRs of 2.9 (95% CI, 1.7 to 4.9) and 4.8 (95% CI, 2.6 to 8.7).The CHARGE index provides a simplified and externally validated framework for predicting treatment outcomes in patients with RRMM receiving TCEs.

title: Beyond the Squeeze: Nanodomain Control of Smooth Muscle Mechanotransduction in the Gut.
abstract: Gastrointestinal smooth muscle cells (SMCs) generate the forces that drive digestion while continuously sensing and adapting to mechanical deformation. How SMCs detect force and convert it into localized chemical and electrical signals remains poorly understood. We propose that mechanosensory output depends on the spatial organization of the nanodomain a channel occupies, and not on the intrinsic properties of that channel alone. Within these environments, mechanosensitive channels integrate opposing depolarizing and hyperpolarizing currents, translating mechanical load into contraction, relaxation, mechanical compliance, or adaptive remodeling. This junction does not appear to be a permanent structure, because it is assembled during development, maintained under load, and eventually lost with age. Which of those elements fails may then determine the clinical phenotype that results. Two questions remain unresolved within this framework: whether stretch reorganizes the nanodomain itself and whether force is also sensed at organelle membranes rather than at the cell surface alone. Emerging tools may finally resolve these dynamics within the active syncytium, uncovering targets for treating dysmotility.

title: Exploratory biomarker analysis of ribociclib plus letrozole in recurrent low-grade serous carcinoma: A GOG-3026 correlative study.
abstract: Ribociclib plus letrozole demonstrated meaningful activity in recurrent low-grade serous ovarian carcinoma (LGSOC) in the phase II GOG-3026 trial. However, biomarkers associated with CDK4/6 inhibitor response remain undefined. We conducted an exploratory translational analysis to identify molecular and immune biomarkers associated with clinical outcomes.Archival FFPE tumors from 24 GOG-3026 patients were analyzed. Immunohistochemistry assessed ER, PR, p16, phosphorylated RB (pRB), and Ki-67. Whole-exome sequencing (n = 14) and RNA sequencing (n = 12) evaluated genomic alterations and immune transcriptional profiles. Associations between biomarkers and objective response rate (ORR), clinical benefit rate (CBR), progression-free survival (PFS) and overall survival were evaluated using 2-sided tests at a 5% significance level, without multiple testing adjustment.Among 24 patients, ORR was 37.5% and CBR was 87.5%. Lower Ki-67 expression was significantly associated with CBR (r = -0.437, p = 0.0326). Higher p16 expression showed a trend toward shorter PFS (Cox proportional hazard regression: HR 2.8, 95% CI 0.96-9.20; Monte Carlo permutation log-rank test: p = 0.0633). ER, PR, pRB expression and MAPK pathway alterations were not associated with response or survival. The most common genomic alterations involved BRAF, KRAS, NRAS and FANCD2. RNA sequencing identified three immune phenotypes: immune-hot, intermediate, and immune-cold. No partial responders had an immune-hot phenotype, while four of five partial responders clustered in the intermediate group.Lower Ki-67 expression may predict clinical benefit from ribociclib plus letrozole, while higher p16 expression may be associated with shorter PFS. title: Hofbauer Cells and Placental Villous Inflammation in Spontaneous Preterm Birth: Spatial and Functional Analyses.
abstract: Preterm birth is a major cause of neonatal morbidity/mortality strongly associated with pathological placental inflammation, but cellular mechanisms leading to this inflammation are poorly understood.Our objectives were to ascertain which immune cells are in the placental villi, understand cell-specific profiles through technologies maintaining cell localization within the tissue, and determine the role of Hofbauer cells in the dysregulated placental inflammation during preterm versus term birth with a focus on spontaneous preterm birth.We first evaluated what cells (immune) are in the placental villi and which could be contributing to placental inflammation. We included 228 patients with preterm or term deliveries, both spontaneous and non-spontaneous, and obtained placentas for histological analysis and performed imaging mass cytometry and spatial transcriptomics on a subset of tissue (n=24). Fresh placentas were also obtained to determine the inflammatory mediator profile and cell-specific protein production by enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay and flow cytometry (n=8-11).Imaging mass cytometry revealed that placental macrophages (Hofbauer cells) were the main immune cell in the placental villi. Furthermore, we observed that preterm placentas, both spontaneous and non-spontaneous, had significantly increased CD163+ and CD68+ cells compared to term. Placental villi macrophages in spontaneous preterm versus spontaneous term analyses revealed a predominance of inflammatory genes and pathways with an involvement from trophoblast cells supporting inflammation, whereas stromal cells were primarily involved in extracellular matrix remodeling. Spontaneous vs non-spontaneous comparisons supported that even though both preterm birth groups are inflammatory, key inflammatory pathways such as TNF⍺ are enriched in spontaneous PTB, while in the term comparisons the pathways were either not related to inflammation or vastly different, with IL-2 being the top signaling pathway. In an ex vivo model of inflammation using placental explants, we found increases in pro-inflammatory mediators that coincided with our bioinformatic analyses. Primary cell experiments, using isolated cytotrophoblasts and Hofbauer cells, further supported that Hofbauer cells were a key contributor to pro-inflammatory mediator production.This work showcases the cell-specific profile of placental macrophages and the inflammatory profile observed in preterm placentas and provides novel insights into the pro-inflammatory role of Hofbauer cells in the placental villi.Copyright © 2026. title: Relationship between integrated myocardial flow reserve and obstructive coronary artery disease and major adverse cardiac events: Findings from the multicenter REFINE PET Registry.
abstract: Although myocardial flow reserve (MFR) is a powerful marker of prognosis in patients undergoing positron emission tomography myocardial perfusion imaging (PET MPI), MFR cannot distinguish between epicardial and microvascular disease. Integrated MFR (iMFR) has been proposed to better detect epicardial coronary artery disease (CAD) by combining MFR with focal perfusion abnormalities.We studied 34,761 patients as part of the REFINE PET registry of patients undergoing 82Rb or 13N-ammonia PET MPI. A subset of the above population without prior CAD (N=2,869) had a diagnostic angiogram within 180 days of PET MPI. Regions with an MFR <2 and a regional perfusion defect by total perfusion deficit (TPD) were defined as 'focally impaired' on a pixel by pixel basis. Regions with an MFR <2 without a regional perfusion defect were defined as 'diffusely impaired'. We also evaluated a separate angiographic cohort imaged with a third tracer, 18F-flurpiridaz, in the Flurpiridaz-301 trial (N=231). iMFR metrics were evaluated for the prediction of obstructive CAD and major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE).Of the 34,761 registry patients, 9,782 (28%) experienced MACE over a median follow-up of 3.8 years. In the angiographic cohort, 1,597 of 2,869 patients (56%) had obstructive CAD. For the diagnosis of obstructive CAD, the extent of focally impaired myocardium had an AUC of 0.77 (95% CI 0.75-0.79), outperforming conventional minimal-segment MFR (AUC 0.73, 95% CI 0.71-0.74, P<0.001), but did not differ significantly from ischemic TPD or physician visual scoring. For the prediction of MACE, the extent of diffusely impaired myocardium provided the most prognostic information in multivariable Cox models (adjusted HR per SD 1.35, 95% CI 1.32-1.38; C-statistic 0.723), compared with global MFR (C-statistic 0.722) and focally impaired myocardium (C-statistic 0.711).The extent of focally impaired myocardium by iMFR outperformed conventional MFR for the diagnosis of obstructive CAD but performed similarly to ischemic TPD and physician visual scoring. title: Pre-Liver Transplant Immunotherapy and Post-Transplant Outcomes in HCC: Global LIFT-HCC-1 Study.
abstract: Use of immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) before liver transplantation (LT) for hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) remains controversial with limited data on post-LT overall and recurrence-free survival (OS and RFS). We aimed to investigate factors associated with long-term post-LT outcomes in ICI-treated LT patients.This global study analyzed ICI-treated HCC patients who underwent LT between 2015-2025. Determinants of allograft rejection, HCC recurrence, and OS were assessed using Cox proportional hazards and Fine-Gray competing-risk models with follow-up starting at LT, with hazard ratios (HRs) or subdistribution hazard ratios (SHRs).Of 408 patients, 23% met Milan criteria at ICI initiation, rising to 43% at LT. During a median follow-up of 21.2 (95%CI,18.9-25.4) months after LT, rejection, recurrence, and death occurred in 19%, 26%, and 21%, respectively. Non-HBV etiologies (HCV: aSHR=3.86; non-viral: aSHR=2.55) and irAEs (aSHR=1.87, 95%CI=1.11-3.14) were associated with higher rejection risk, whereas older age (aSHR per 10 years=0.74, 95%CI=0.58-0.94) and washout >90 days (aSHR=0.49, 95%CI=0.26-0.93) reduced this risk. AFP≥20 (aSHR=2.14, 95%CI=1.27-3.61) and being outside Milan at LT (aSHR=2.17, 95%CI=1.12-4.17) were associated with recurrence. Severe rejection (aHR=6.09, 95%CI=2.05-18.1) and HCC recurrence (aHR=15.9, 95%CI=7.08-35.9) were associated with shorter OS. No significant difference in outcomes was observed between patients with downstaged HCC and those always within Milan criteria, with comparable 3-year OS (80.8% vs 86.9%, p=0.92) and RFS (83.8% vs 86.5%, p=0.88).Tumor burden and AFP at LT were associated with HCC recurrence. Higher rejection risk was associated with non-HBV etiology, irAEs, younger age, and shorter ICI washout period. llm_summary: Researchers examined whether immune-boosting cancer drugs given before liver transplants affected survival outcomes in patients with liver cancer, analyzing 408 patients treated between 2015 and 2025. About one-quarter of patients experienced cancer recurrence and one-fifth died during the follow-up period, with higher cancer markers and larger tumors at transplant time associated with worse outcomes. The findings suggest that carefully timed treatment and monitoring of tumor size may help improve survival, though larger studies are needed to confirm these results.
llm_summary_expert: Researchers examined 408 hepatocellular carcinoma patients treated with immune checkpoint inhibitors before liver transplantation between 2015-2025, assessing post-transplant allograft rejection, hepatocellular carcinoma recurrence, and overall survival using Cox proportional hazards and competing-risk models. During median follow-up of 21.2 months after transplantation, rejection occurred in 19% of patients, recurrence in 26%, and death in 21%, with non-hepatitis B virus etiologies and immune-related adverse events associated with higher rejection risk while older age and washout periods exceeding 90 days reduced rejection risk. Alpha-fetoprotein levels of 20 or greater and tumor burden outside Milan criteria at transplantation were associated with increased hepatocellular carcinoma recurrence risk, whereas severe rejection and hepatocellular carcinoma recurrence were strongly associated with shorter overall survival. Patients with downstaged hepatocellular carcinoma achieved comparable three-year overall survival and recurrence-free survival to those meeting Milan criteria throughout treatment, with no statistically significant differences observed between groups. title: Using an Artificial Intelligence ECG-Derived Biological Age for Risk Stratification of Patients Undergoing Surgical Aortic Valve Replacement.
abstract: Artificial intelligence using a convolutional neural network can estimate patients' age from ECG data. We aimed to assess the prognostic value of AI ECG-derived age in predicting outcomes following surgical aortic valve replacement (SAVR).Preoperative ECGs obtained within 30 days before surgery were used to calculate AI ECG-derived age in 5,503 patients undergoing SAVR. Age gap was defined as AI ECG-derived age minus chronological age. Associations between age gap and postoperative outcomes were evaluated. A threshold of age gap >5 years was used to define advanced ECG age.Median chronological age was 73.2(65.3-79.5) years, and AI ECG-derived age was 70.4(64.6-74.8) years. Median age gap was -3.0(-8.4 to 2.5) years. In 35.7% of patients, AI ECG-derived age exceeded chronological age, and in 16.7% it was >5 years. Patients with advanced ECG age were younger but had higher rates of diabetes, renal failure, and current smoking and had higher BMI. Postoperatively, advanced ECG age was associated with increased risk of 30-day mortality (OR 1.69, p=0.043), blood transfusion (OR 1.44, p<0.001), gastrointestinal complications (OR 1.83, p=0.022), prolonged ventilation (OR 1.41, p=0.047), higher postoperative creatinine levels (B +0.09 mg/dL, p=0.014), longer ICU stay (B +13.3 hours, p=0.001), and longer hospital stay (B +0.7 days, p=0.007). Advanced ECG age was also independently associated with increased long-term mortality (HR 1.25, p=0.003).AI ECG-derived age identifies a subgroup of SAVR patients with advanced physiological aging. An elevated age gap is independently associated with worse early postoperative outcomes and reduced long-term survival following SAVR.Copyright © 2026. Published by Elsevier Inc.

llm_summary: Researchers used artificial intelligence to estimate biological age from heart electrical readings in patients undergoing aortic valve replacement surgery and found that patients whose hearts appeared older than their actual age had worse surgical outcomes, including higher death rates and longer hospital stays. About one in six patients showed this advanced heart age pattern, and this finding remained associated with increased long-term mortality risk even after accounting for other factors. The results suggest that AI-derived heart age may help identify patients at higher risk before surgery.
llm_summary_expert: Researchers examined 5,503 patients undergoing surgical aortic valve replacement to assess whether artificial intelligence-derived ECG age, calculated using a convolutional neural network applied to preoperative electrocardiograms, could predict postoperative outcomes. Advanced ECG age was defined as AI ECG-derived age exceeding chronological age by more than 5 years, which occurred in 16.7% of the cohort. Patients with advanced ECG age demonstrated significantly increased risk of 30-day mortality (odds ratio 1.69), blood transfusion (odds ratio 1.44), gastrointestinal complications (odds ratio 1.83), prolonged ventilation (odds ratio 1.41), and longer intensive care unit and hospital stays compared to those without advanced ECG age. Advanced ECG age remained independently associated with increased long-term mortality (hazard ratio 1.25) following surgical aortic valve replacement. These findings suggest that AI ECG-derived age identifies a physiologically advanced subgroup at elevated risk for both early postoperative complications and reduced long-term survival, though the observational design precludes causal inference.

title: Two-Year Clinical and Hemodynamic Outcomes After Transcatheter Mitral Valve Replacement in Severe Mitral Annular Calcification.
abstract: The SUMMIT-MAC trial is evaluating the safety and effectiveness of the Tendyne Transcatheter Mitral Valve Replacement (TMVR) system in patients with severe mitral annular calcification (MAC). Primary outcomes demonstrated significant improvements in mitral regurgitation severity, heart failure symptoms, and quality-of-life; leading to FDA approval of Tendyne. Intermediate term TMVR outcomes have not been reported.The SUMMIT-MAC cohort (NCT03433274) enrolled high surgical-risk patients with severe MAC (average volume 5,679 ± 5,670; range 741 to 37,437 mm3) and significant mitral valve dysfunction. Independent assessments of mitral disease were performed at an echocardiography core laboratory and adverse events were adjudicated by a clinical events committee. Two-year follow-up visits were achieved in 95% of available patients, with an average follow-up of 18.7 months.The cohort included 103 patients from 37 sites. Mean age was 78.0±6.5 years, 55% were women, 74% were in NYHA functional class III/IV, and mitral regurgitation was present in nearly all patients at baseline (97% grade >2+). At 2 years all-cause mortality was 32.3% (32 patients) and cardiovascular mortality was 23.6% (23 patients). 97% (56/58) of patients with available echocardiograms at 2 years had ≤1+ mitral regurgitation. Additionally, at 2 years, 84% of patients were in NYHA functional class I/II and quality-of-life improved significantly (KCCQ-OS, Δ24.2±19.6 points; p<0.0001).In a high-risk cohort of patients with mitral valve disease and severe MAC, Tendyne TMVR had acceptable sustained clinical outcomes and quality-of-life over 2 years. The reduction of mitral regurgitation severity was sustained through 2-years post TMVR.Copyright © 2026. Published by Elsevier Inc.

llm_summary: The SUMMIT-MAC trial evaluated a catheter-based mitral valve replacement procedure called Tendyne in high-risk patients with severe calcium buildup in their heart's mitral valve. After two years, the procedure successfully reduced abnormal blood leakage through the valve in nearly all patients and improved heart function and quality of life in most participants. However, the study observed a mortality rate of about one in three patients, which reflects the advanced age and serious health conditions of the enrolled population.
llm_summary_expert: The SUMMIT-MAC trial evaluated the safety and effectiveness of the Tendyne Transcatheter Mitral Valve Replacement system in 103 high surgical-risk patients with severe mitral annular calcification and significant mitral valve dysfunction, with independent core laboratory assessments of mitral disease and adjudicated adverse events. Two-year follow-up was achieved in 95% of available patients with a mean follow-up of 18.7 months, during which all-cause mortality was 32.3% and cardiovascular mortality was 23.6%. At 2 years, 97% of patients with available echocardiograms had mitral regurgitation of ≤1+, and 84% of patients were in NYHA functional class I/II compared with 74% in class III/IV at baseline. Quality-of-life improved significantly at 2 years as measured by the Kansas City Cardiomyopathy Questionnaire Overall Summary score. In this high-risk cohort with severe mitral annular calcification, Tendyne TMVR demonstrated sustained reduction of mitral regurgitation severity and improved functional status.

title: Deep Learning-Accelerated 3D T2 CUBE MRI of the Cochlea at 1.5T and 3T: Sonic DL With AIR Recon DL Versus AIR Recon DL Alone.
abstract: Three-dimensional fast spin-echo MR cisternography (CUBE) of the internal auditory canal (IAC) and cerebellopontine angle (CPA) requires longer acquisition times that can limit clinical throughput. We evaluated whether a deep learning (DL)-based highly accelerated reconstruction technique, Sonic DL`™ (SDL), combined with a commercially available DL denoising reconstruction (AIR™ Recon DL, ARDL), preserves or improves subjective image quality and cochlear anatomy visualization relative to standard CUBE-ARDL while shortening scan time.Consecutive patients underwent brain MRI for suspected IAC pathology at 1.5T and 3T with paired acquisition of standard 3D CUBE-ARDL and an accelerated 3D CUBE-SDL sequence. Both used the same voxel size at 1.5T (0.6x0.6x1.2 mm3) and 3T (0.6x0.6x0.6 mm3). Scan times for CUBE-ARDL versus CUBE-SDL were 2:33 versus 1:41 min at 1.5T and 1:55 versus 1:11 min at 3T. Two independent neuroradiologists blinded to MRI acquisition method scored randomized, de-identified images on a 5-point Likert scale across five domains (overall image quality, noise, sharpness, artifacts, cochlear anatomy visualization). Reader-averaged scores for CUBE-ARDL and CUBE-SDL were compared with paired Wilcoxon signed-rank tests, with reader-specific and cumulative link mixed model (CLMM) sensitivity analyses and false discovery rate (FDR) adjustment; intraclass correlation coefficients (ICC) quantified inter-reader reliability for each technique; Gwet's AC2 and weighted (Conger's) kappa with linear ordinal weights quantified pooled inter-reader agreement.After exclusion of 5 training cases per field strength, 49 (1.5T) and 34 (3T) patients were analyzed. CUBE-SDL scored significantly better than CUBE-ARDL for all five domains at both field strengths (all FDR-adjusted P < .001), consistently for each reader and in the CLMM. Inter-reader reliability (ICC) for CUBE-SDL was moderate-to-excellent at 3T (0.63-0.92) and moderate at 1.5T (0.65-0.74), generally exceeding CUBE-ARDL (3T: 0.35-0.61; 1.5T: 0.50-0.71). Pooled inter-reader agreement (Gwet's AC2) ranged from 0.56 to 0.89.A combined Sonic DL acceleration with ARDL-denoised reconstruction for 3D T2 CUBE produced significantly higher subjective image quality at both 1.5T and 3T, and, at 3T, higher inter-reader reliability than standard CUBE-ARDL, while shortening acquisition time by 34%-38%. These findings support further evaluation, including diagnostic accuracy studies, of CUBE-SDL as an alternative to CUBE-ARDL.© 2026 by American Journal of Neuroradiology.

abstract: Proton therapy has emerged as an important technique for locally advanced breast cancer (LABC), driven primarily by the need to reduce cardiopulmonary dose during comprehensive nodal irradiation, particularly when the internal mammary chain is targeted. Since the first clinical proton experience in patients with LABC and unfavorable cardiac anatomy in 2010, proton radiation therapy for LABC has evolved considerably: delivery technique has progressed from passive scattering and uniform scanning to pencil beam scanning and intensity modulated proton therapy, whereas breast radiation oncology overall has shifted from field-based to volumetric, contour-driven planning. RADCOMP, the first large prospective randomized trial comparing proton and photon regional nodal irradiation, completed accrual in 2024 (n = 1239); its 2025 health-related quality-of-life analysis showed similarly excellent patient-reported outcomes in both arms, whereas the trial's primary endpoints of locoregional control and major cardiac events remain pending. Beyond RADCOMP, most published experience remains single-institutional and technically heterogeneous. This critical review examines the historical development, technical evolution, and clinical application of proton therapy for LABC, with attention to contouring philosophy, robustness evaluation, and optimization of normal tissue-related side effects. Because proton plans are more sensitive to contour accuracy, setup, and range uncertainty than photon plans, and because proton entrance-dose behavior differs fundamentally from the photon skin-sparing effect, target delineation and plan robustness assessment require deliberate, disease-specific decision-making. We provide practical guidance for radiation oncologists, physicists, and dosimetrists, particularly those at centers early in their proton breast experience, and outline priorities for standardized reporting as long-term RADCOMP outcomes mature.Copyright © 2026 Elsevier Inc. title: Initiating Proton Ocular Treatments on General-Purpose Beamlines: Challenges and Trends From the Survey of US Facilities.
abstract: Historically, ocular melanomas and other eye cancers accounted for a substantial share of proton therapy patients. Although the number of proton facilities in the United States increased rapidly in the last decade, as of 2025, only roughly 1 out of 6 had active ocular proton therapy (OPT) programs. Despite the robust growth in the number of proton treatments overall, eye treatments appear to have peaked in 2016. We aimed to identify barriers to the expansion of the availability of hypofractionated proton therapy for ocular cancer patients.A questionnaire was designed and distributed to proton facilities in the United States to query the level of interest in eye treatments and the challenges to establishing and supporting ocular programs. The responses were analyzed separately for the Adopters representing active programs, and the Aspirants who were not yet offering OPT.Proton therapy facilities now operate in half of the US states. However, OPT is currently delivered in only 7 states. The use of pencil beam scanning application for ocular treatments is on the rise, as older facilities employing scattering techniques work to upgrade their beamlines. Despite a substantial interest at many facilities in developing ocular treatments on general-purpose beamlines, the lack of commercialized solutions and information on best practices has been identified as a barrier. Specific areas were identified with the most acute lack of currently available guidance.Access to OPT is lagging that of proton therapy in general. Limited local accessibility, relative to alternative treatments, likely contributed to the stagnation in proton patient numbers. As the experience on non-dedicated beamlines at Adopter facilities grows, it is timely and important for the community, comprising both practitioners and vendors, to guide and facilitate establishment of new ocular programs, while maintaining the high standard of care for which OPT is known.Copyright © 2025 Elsevier Inc. The main barriers identified were the lack of commercially available equipment designed for eye treatments and insufficient guidance on best practices for facilities wanting to start these programs. title: Comparative Analysis of Acute Skin Reactions After Postmastectomy Photon and Intensity Modulated Proton Therapy.
abstract: We sought to compare target coverage, skin dose, physician-assessed adverse events, and patient-reported skin outcomes in a large cohort of patients receiving postmastectomy intensity modulated proton therapy (IMPT) or photon radiation therapy (XRT).Women with unilateral, noninflammatory breast cancer treated with postmastectomy radiation therapy using IMPT or XRT to 50 Gy relative biological effectiveness (RBE) were included. Skin planning objectives for both modalities prioritized ≥90% of the skin volume receiving >90% of the prescription dose, which is expected to control microscopic disease, while maintaining dose homogeneity. IMPT planning objectives limited the dose to 1 cc of skin to ≤105% of the prescription dose, with an ideal constraint of ≤96%. Target and skin dosimetry were evaluated. Acute Common Toxicity Criteria for Adverse Events (CTCAE) grade ≥2 dermatitis and skin-specific patient-reported outcomes using the Patient-Reported Outcomes version of the Common Terminology Criteria for Adverse Events (PRO-CTCAE) were compared between modalities.Among 176 women (93 IMPT, 83 XRT), the median skin D0.01cc, D1cc, and D10cc were higher in XRT plans than in IMPT plans, although the differences were all less than 3%. Acute grade ≥2 dermatitis occurred in 47% (IMPT) and 48% (XRT) and was not associated with treatment modality (P = .91). Grade 3 dermatitis occurred in 3% (IMPT) and 7% (XRT) (P = .22), with no grade 4 events. At 12 months post-RT, XRT patients reported more skin color changes than IMPT patients (26% vs 6%, P = .04), the only significantly different patient-reported skin outcome.Patient and provider-reported adverse skin events were mild and comparable between IMPT and XRT. title: Best Practice and Recommendations for Pregnant Orthopedic Surgeons Part II: Early Career and Practice.
abstract: Pregnancy during orthopedic surgery practice presents unique challenges related to family planning, workplace accommodations, occupational exposures, board certification requirements, and postpartum return to work. Despite increasing numbers of women entering orthopedic surgery, there remains a lack of centralized guidance addressing pregnancy-related considerations. The purpose of this review is to summarize current evidence, to provide practical recommendations for orthopedic surgeons navigating pregnancy during their career, and to guide practice partners and organizations on how to create a culture of support and belonging during this time frame.Available literature, professional society guidance, federal workplace regulations, and occupational safety data were reviewed. Key topics included advanced maternal age and fertility considerations, American Board of Orthopaedic Surgery (ABOS) certification accommodations, workplace disclosure and legal protections, occupational exposure to methyl methacrylate (MMA) and ionizing radiation, physical demands of orthopedic practice, postpartum support, parental leave, and breastfeeding accommodations.Delayed childbearing associated with orthopedic training and career progression may contribute to increased rates of infertility and obstetric complications among female orthopedic surgeons. Federal protections, including the Pregnant Workers Fairness Act, Family and Medical Leave Act, and Equal Employment Opportunity Commission regulations, provide important frameworks for workplace accommodations. Contemporary evidence demonstrates that occupational exposure to MMA and radiation during orthopedic procedures remains below established safety thresholds when appropriate precautions are employed. Physical demands such as prolonged standing, heavy lifting, and extended work hours may warrant workplace modifications during pregnancy. Postpartum support, equitable parental leave policies, and access to lactation accommodations may improve surgeon well-being and facilitate successful return to clinical practice.Pregnancy should be recognized as a normal life event rather than a barrier to success in orthopedic surgery. Evidence-based accommodations, occupational safety measures, supportive workplace policies, and equitable parental leave practices can promote maternal and infant health while supporting professional development. Normalizing pregnancy and postpartum support within orthopedic surgery is essential to fostering a more inclusive and sustainable workforce.Copyright © 2026 by the American Academy of Orthopaedic Surgeons.

title: Dose-Linear Energy Transfer Interactions Predict Capsular Contracture After Proton Postmastectomy Radiation Therapy.
abstract: Pencil beam scanning proton therapy enables highly conformal dose distributions and is increasingly used for postmastectomy radiation therapy (PMRT) to reduce cardiopulmonary exposure. However, implant-based reconstruction (IBR) in the setting of PMRT remains susceptible to capsular contracture, and the potential contribution of elevated linear energy transfer (LET) in pencil beam scanning has not been well characterized. This study aimed to investigate the combined effects of dose-LET and dose-averaged LET on capsular contracture after proton PMRT and to derive preliminary, exploratory volume cutoff values of dose-LET volume constraints (DLVCs).We conducted a retrospective case-control study of patients with consecutive breast cancer who underwent mastectomy followed by IBR and conventionally fractionated proton PMRT (50 Gy in 25 fractions) between 2015 and 2021. Patients who developed Baker grades III to IV capsular contracture were identified and matched 1:2 with controls using nearest-neighbor matching based on clinical and pathologic variables. Dose-LET volume histograms (DLVHs) were calculated for peri-implant tissue (5-mm shell around the implant). Generalized linear mixed-effects regression was used to identify DLVH indices significantly associated with capsular contracture. Redundant indices were removed using Spearman correlation analysis. DLVCs were derived from receiver operating characteristic curve analysis and evaluated using a support vector machine-based normal tissue complication probability model with leave-one-out cross-validation.Among 145 consecutive patients, 8 developed capsular contracture and were matched to 16 controls. Three independent DLVH indices were significantly associated with capsular contracture (P < .01): V (55.8 Gy [relative biological effectiveness {RBE} value = 1.1], 2.2 keV/μm), V (50.3 Gy [RBE value = 1.1], 5.4 keV/μm), and V (32.8 Gy [RBE value = 1.1], 0.9 keV/μm). After Benjamini-Hochberg false discovery rate correction across all 4096 DLVH indices, all 3 remained significant (q_Benjamini-Hochberg = 0.052). The corresponding DLVCs were V (55.8 Gy [RBE value = 1.1], 2.2 keV/μm) < 0.0017%, V (50.3 Gy [RBE value = 1.1], 5.4 keV/μm) < 0.0033%, and V (32.8 Gy [RBE value = 1.1], 0.9 keV/μm) > 96.98%. The support vector machine-based normal tissue complication probability model achieved an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve value of 0.867, with an accuracy of 91.7%, a sensitivity of 87.5%, and a specificity of 93.8%.Capsular contracture following proton PMRT is significantly associated with the combined effects of dose-LET and dose-averaged LET in peri-implant tissue. The derived DLVCs represent exploratory candidate dosimetric constraints that warrant further investigation and prospective validation in patients with breast cancer undergoing proton PMRT with IBR.Copyright © 2026 Elsevier Inc. title: Biologic Reconstructive Techniques for Intercalary Bone Loss.
abstract: Management of segmental bone loss has been a difficult challenge with standard techniques of bone grafting. In recent times, there have been many surgical advances in this field, primarily stemming from our ability to address segmental bone loss. The aim of this article was to provide an overview of biologic techniques to manage these segmental bony defects, including their indications and outcomes. We will focus on the options of distraction osteogenesis, induced membrane technique, and vascularized bone grafting. There are scenarios that may call on one specific surgical approach over another. Distraction osteogenesis is a reliable option for traumatic injuries with adequate soft-tissue coverage, whereas the induced membrane technique may be best served for infected cases. Vascularized bone may be the best option when facing patients who require radiation or chemotherapy in the oncologic setting or have concurrent soft-tissue deficits in the trauma setting. The techniques may also be combined to take advantage of their individual attributes. Ultimately, a team approach should be used to determine the best reconstructive option for large segmental bony defects.Copyright © 2026 by the American Academy of Orthopaedic Surgeons.

llm_summary: This review examined three surgical techniques for treating large gaps in bone caused by trauma or disease: distraction osteogenesis (gradually stretching new bone), induced membrane technique (using the body's natural healing response), and vascularized bone grafting (transplanting living bone with blood vessels). Each technique has different advantages depending on the patient's situation, such as whether the bone loss resulted from infection, trauma, or cancer requiring radiation. The authors recommend using a team approach to select the best technique or combination of techniques for each patient's specific needs.

A multidisciplinary team approach is recommended to determine the most appropriate reconstructive strategy for each patient's specific clinical scenario.

title: The Evolution of Radiation Therapy in Children's Oncology Group Trials, From 1998 to 2025.
abstract: Significant advancements in external beam radiation therapy (RT) over the past 20+ years have occurred with evolution from 2-dimensional techniques based on plain film x rays to 3-dimensional conformal and intensity modulated photon techniques. Likewise, proton radiation therapy (PRT) was also introduced and has become more widely available. Each advance in radiation technique improves targeting and has the potential to mitigate late effects associated with RT. In this study, we use metadata from past and present Children's Oncology Group trials that included RT to describe the evolution of different RT modalities across time and disease sites.Imaging and Radiation Oncology Core database was queried for protocols with at least 1 patient receiving RT from 1998 to 2025. Protocol metadata, including primary disease site, study timeline, and quality assurance , was extracted, as were nonidentifiable patient-level variables including age, institution, year of enrollment, and RT modality used. Descriptive statistics were used for downstream analysis.The study population comprised 8898 patients, including 7881 from the United States and 1017 from other countries. The median age at enrollment was 9 years; California, Texas, Florida, and New York were among the top contributing states. Of the 83 included Children's Oncology Group trials, 48 included at least 1 patient receiving PRT. The number of trials allowing PRT peaked in 2010 with 17 protocols. Trials involving central nervous system tumors and rhabdomyosarcoma/soft tissue sarcomas dominated both in the number of trials and enrollment. They were also among the earliest to incorporate PRT into treatment protocols. From 1998 to 2025, 3-dimensional photon-based treatments declined from 73% to 15%, whereas intensity modulated radiation therapy/volumetric modulated arc therapy usage rose from 26% to 89% over the same interval. The use of PRT increased from 2% pre-2000 to nearly 40% in 2021, which has since stabilized. Quality assurance review demonstrated >90% protocol compliance across all RT modalities both nationally and internationally.Over 25 years of Children's Oncology Group experience, photon therapy has transitioned from 3-dimensional conformal to intensity modulated radiation therapy/volumetric modulated arc therapy, whereas PRT use has continued to expand, particularly in central nervous system and rhabdomyosarcoma/soft tissue sarcomas trials. These trends highlight how pediatric cooperative group studies continue to shape national standards and underscore the need for future work linking modality adoption with toxicity, survivorship, and access across diverse treatment settings.Copyright © 2026 Elsevier Inc. title: Clinical and procedural outcomes of IVUS-guided versus angiography-guided PCI in unprotected left main coronary disease: An updated meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials.
abstract: The clinical benefit of intravascular ultrasound (IVUS)-guided percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) in patients with unprotected left main coronary artery disease (ULMCAD) remains uncertain. We performed an updated meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials (RCTs) comparing IVUS-guided versus angiography-guided PCI in ULMCAD.We performed a meta-analysis of RCTs identified through PubMed, Cochrane CENTRAL, Scopus, and Web of Science from inception through May 2026. The primary outcome was major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) at the longest follow-up period. Dichotomous outcomes were analyzed as risk ratios (RRs) and continuous outcomes as mean differences (MDs), both with 95% confidence intervals (CIs).Four RCTs comprising 1446 patients were included. MACE showed no statistically significant difference between groups (RR 0.57, 95% CI 0.30-1.09; P = 0.09). However, following exclusion of OPTIMAL Trial in leave-one-out sensitivity analyses, IVUS-guided PCI was associated with a statistically significant reduction in the incidence of MACE. title: Clinical evaluation of a vision-language model for optimizing triage and clinical workflows in critical care.
abstract: Clinical deterioration in hospitalized patients is often preceded by subtle, dynamic physiological changes that are difficult to detect using intermittently charted electronic health record (EHR) data. Our objective was to evaluate the reliability, interpretability, and clinical relevance of a Vision‑Language Model (VLM)-based triage framework that analyzes physiological trend images, by comparing VLM-generated outputs with attending physician assessments as the expert clinical comparator.We conducted a single-center expert agreement pilot study including 100 adult patients with two hours of dynamic monitoring data across four vital signs (SpO2, RR, HR, BP). A structured prompt was developed using the Gemini 2.5 Flash model. Two independent reviewers assessed VLM outputs for clinical interpretation, artifact detection, and triage classification. We evaluated reviewer agreement using percent agreement and weighted Cohen's κ. A secondary risk-oriented analysis measured classification concordance and over-triaged cases as lower-risk classifications, while cases underestimating patient acuity were designated as higher-risk misclassifications.The VLM demonstrated moderate to substantial agreement in triage classification with the attending physician and a low rate of under-triage. The VLM assigned the same patient acuity category as attending physician in 75 % of cases and underestimated acuity in 7 % of cases, compared with 14 % underestimation by the physician in training.VLMs extend generative artificial intelligence capabilities by enabling image‑grounded clinical reasoning and offer signal‑processing capabilities for interpreting time‑stamped physiological trends.The VLM demonstrated reliable clinical interpretation and an acceptable safety profile, however its integration into clinical workflows for early recognition of physiological deterioration and patient acuity assessment requires further rigorous evaluation and comparison to currently used track-and-trigger systems and patient monitoring methods.Copyright © 2026 Elsevier B.V. title: Best Practice and Recommendations for Pregnant Orthopedic Surgeons Part I: Navigating Residency.
abstract: Family planning and maternity leave concerns contribute to reasons why the percentage of women in orthopedic surgery is disproportionally and consistently low. Without institutional policies, these stressors are often placed on the pregnant resident in training. The establishment of formal department policies allows for clear, universal expectations, which helps decrease negative peer perception and overall dissatisfaction. This practice not only supports current trainees but can also help attract more diverse applicants to create a sustainable workforce. This is the first of a two-part paper that outlines key evidence-based considerations for pregnancy during residency. Importantly, we address the balance of early disclosure with confidentiality, call schedules, medical appointments, and return-to-work considerations, including lactation policies. Creation of these formal guidelines will require an investment in the department but can lay the foundation for a new generation of surgeons who thrive both at home and in the operating room.Copyright © 2026 by the American Academy of Orthopaedic Surgeons.

title: Myositis with nemaline rods: Clinical features and treatment outcomes.
abstract: Several idiopathic inflammatory myopathies (IIM), originally classified under polymyositis, evolved into distinct entities. Herein, we describe clinical features and treatment outcomes of a potentially novel clinico-histopathological entity: myositis with nemaline rods (MNR).We performed retrospective chart review of the Mayo Clinic electronic medical records to identify patients with nemaline rods and muscle inflammation on biopsy, not fitting into any IIM subgroup, and extracted clinical and laboratory data. Additional immunohistochemical studies were performed on muscle biopsies.Eleven patients were identified, with mean age at onset 61.8 years (SD = 9.8), seven were female. MNR had a distinctive phenotype with rapidly progressive weakness, predominantly affecting swallowing, axial, and proximal limb muscles, often with prominent myalgia. No patients had monoclonal gammopathy. Creatine kinase levels were elevated in 73% of patients. Muscle histopathology revealed nemaline rods in non-atrophic and atrophic fibers. Inflammation was often endomysial, where both CD4+ and CD8+ T cells invaded nonnecrotic muscle fibers. A significant proportion of CD8+ T cells were KLRG1+. Of patients with follow-up, 6/8 responded to immunosuppressive treatment with some going into remission. Although MNR shares features with sporadic late-onset nemaline myopathy (SLONM) and inclusion body myositis (IBM), it has important distinctions. Unlike SLONM, MNR shows endomysial inflammation and no monoclonal protein; unlike IBM, MNR exhibits distinct clinical features, rapid progression, and responsiveness to immunotherapy.MNR is associated with a unique combination of clinical and histopathological features, responding well to treatment in most cases. Future studies are needed to explore underlying mechanisms and identify serological biomarkers.Copyright © 2026 The Authors. Published by Elsevier B.V. All rights reserved.

title: Micro-energy acoustic pulse therapy attenuates diabetic nephropathy by restoring renal proliferative capacity and progenitor cell homeostasis independent of glycemic control.
abstract: Diabetic nephropathy (DN) is characterized by progressive renal dysfunction and impaired intrinsic repair capacity. Micro-energy acoustic pulse (MAP) therapy is a non-invasive mechanical stimulation modality with emerging regenerative potential; however, its effects on diabetic kidney disease remain unclear. This study aimed to investigate whether MAP therapy attenuates DN and to explore its effects on renal cellular dynamics.DN was induced in rats using streptozotocin (STZ). Diabetic animals received weekly bilateral renal MAP treatment for six weeks. Renal function and histopathological changes were evaluated. Renal mitotic activity and resident cell populations were analyzed by flow cytometry using phospho-histone H3 (H3P), CD133, and CD90.STZ-induced diabetic rats developed persistent hyperglycemia, renal dysfunction, and structural injury. MAP treatment significantly improved renal functional parameters and attenuated glomerular damage without affecting blood glucose levels. Diabetic kidneys exhibited reduced mitotic activity and depletion of CD133+ and CD90+ cell populations, both of which were partially restored following MAP treatment. In addition, MAP shifted these populations toward smaller, regenerative phenotypes.MAP therapy attenuated functional and structural features of experimental diabetic nephropathy despite persistent hyperglycemia and was associated with partial restoration of renal mitotic and repair-associated cell populations. These findings support further investigation of low-energy mechanical stimulation as a kidney-directed adjunct to current metabolic therapies, while additional mechanistic, dose-response, and long-term safety studies remain necessary.Copyright © 2026 Elsevier Inc. title: International Consensus Guidelines for Radiation Target Volume Delineation for Skull Base Chordoma-A Particle Therapy Co-operative Group Initiative.
abstract: To develop consensus guidelines for radiation therapy target volume delineation in skull base chordoma.An international panel of 15 radiation oncologists with experience treating skull base chordoma received anonymized case histories and Digital Imaging and Communications in Medicine (DICOM) data of preoperative and postoperative imaging from 3 representative cases (superior, mid, and lower clival chordomas) after varied degrees of surgical resection. Panelists defined the preoperative gross tumor volume (GTV), residual GTV (if any) and an intermediate and high dose clinical target volume (CTV). A count mapping 3-dimensional histogram generated contours based on overlapping voxels included in each target to identify the approximately 40% and 75% levels of consensus in the panel. Qualitative comparison of these contours identified areas of consistent practice and clinically relevant variation. A modified Delphi consensus approach was used to formulate contouring recommendations and generate consensus contours. Similarities between individual contours and the consensus contour were assessed using Sorensen-Dice similarity coefficient and mean distance to agreement (DTA) in centimeter.Delineation of preoperative GTV was most consistent with a mean Dice coefficient of 0.85 and mean DTA of 0.13 cm. Residual GTV (present in 2 cases) was the least congruent with a mean Dice of 0.45 and mean DTA of 0.37 cm. Consensus modifications of residual GTV included identification of residual disease in the lateral clivus, cavernous sinus, atlantooccipital joint, and prevertebral soft tissues. The panel recommended CTV_Intermediate encompass the entire tumor bed with median 5 mm margin, the remainder of the clivus, and be modified to account for decompression of previously "pushing" tumor. CTV_High should encompass bone and mucosa of the entire primary tumor bed and any residual disease with median 5 mm margin.This international collaborative effort establishes contouring guidelines for skull base chordoma based on knowledge of patterns of failure, patterns of spread, surgical findings, and existing practice patterns within the particle therapy community.Copyright © 2026 The Authors. title: Global survey and analysis of inter-responder agreement on osteofibrous dysplasia, osteofibrous dysplasia-like adamantinoma, and classic adamantinoma.
abstract: Osteofibrous dysplasia (OFD), OFD-like adamantinoma, and classic adamantinoma are bone tumors arising primarily in anterior tibiae. Their distinction can be challenging and is based on the amount/configuration of keratin-positive cells. This study assessed inter-responder agreements among pathologists in their diagnosis. We designed an online survey comprising 18 multiple-choice questions, each with hand-drawn schematic illustrations of hematoxylin-and-eosin (H&E) and the corresponding keratin immunohistochemistry slides, to assess how diagnostic concordance varied with the keratin-positive epithelial clusters. We circulated this survey to all members of International Society of Bone and Soft Tissue Pathology and of Society for Pediatric Pathology, additional pathologists, and a pre-selected expert panel. A total of 1458 diagnoses from 81 participants (including 19 from expert panel) were analyzed using Fleiss and Randolph ĸ metrics. While responses to two control questions on classic adamantinoma and OFD lacking keratin-positive cells were nearly unanimous, responses to the remaining 16 questions showed an overall fair agreement among all participants (Fleiss ĸ: 0.234 [95% CI: 0.227-0.241]), including expert panel (Fleiss ĸ: 0.268 [95% CI: 0.238-0.299]) and remaining responders (Fleiss ĸ: 0.216 [95% CI: 0.207-0.226]). For each of the 14 questions illustrating epithelial cluster(s) with varying cell numbers and/or arrangements, agreement was fair-to-moderate (Randolph ĸ: 0.245 to 0.472), with no significant difference between expert panel and remaining responders. We identified a lack of agreement among experts and globally on the characteristics of keratin-positive epithelial clusters in OFD-like adamantinomas, suggested target areas for delineation to improve diagnostic reproducibility, and provided a rationale for the terminology "atypical OFD."© 2026. title: The role of biomarkers in understanding and targeting adaptive resistance in metastatic colorectal cancer.
abstract: Metastatic colorectal cancer (mCRC) is characterized by molecular heterogeneity and the development of adaptive resistance to systemic therapies. Biomarkers have become central to understanding resistance biology and guiding treatment selection, spanning established genomic alterations, circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA)-based monitoring, and emerging molecular classifications. Herein, we provide a synthesis of biomarker-driven resistance mechanisms across major therapeutic classes in mCRC, including anti-EGFR, anti-VEGF, BRAF-targeted, KRAS-targeted, HER2-directed, and immunotherapy-based approaches. PubMed/MEDLINE and Google Scholar were searched for relevant literature published through August 2026. Resistance to targeted therapies converges on reactivation of key signaling pathways, particularly MAPK, through genomic and microenvironmental factors. ctDNA represents an important tool for longitudinal assessment of tumor evolution and has demonstrated clinical validity in selected settings, including molecular selection for anti-EGFR rechallenge. Across other therapeutic classes, ctDNA dynamics and resistance profiling are primarily prognostic or investigational, and prospective evidence that ctDNA-guided treatment adaptation improves outcomes remains limited. Emerging biomarkers, including immune-related gene expression patterns, features of the tumor microenvironment, and metabolic adaptations, may improve prediction of therapeutic response. Integration of longitudinal biomarker assessment with ctDNA profiling may enable earlier detection of resistance and more individualized treatment strategies, although the clinical benefit of ctDNA-guided treatment adaptation remains to be established.

title: HLA-antibody testing female donors with a pregnancy history augments the low titer group O whole blood supply.
abstract: Low titer group O whole blood (LTOWB) use across the United States is increasing. This simulation calculated the number of female donors who would qualify for LTOWB donation if HLA-antibody screening was implemented in different strategies.Using US nativity data and information on blood donors from 2023, a model was constructed that calculated how many of these donors would be males and nulliparous females, neither of which require HLA-antibody screening before LTOWB donation. The model then calculated how many parous females would be HLA-antibody sensitized based on each woman's parity in three antibody screening scenarios: all parous women, all parous women ≥50 years old, and all parous women older than the 99th percentile of the age of final birth. These calculations were performed for RhD-negative and RhD-positive donors.The model calculated that there would be 222,239 RhD-negative male and 74,655 nulliparous RhD-negative female donors. title: Can Pediatric Emergency Medicine Clinicians Identify Solid Organ Injuries Using Contrast-Enhanced FAST in Abdominal Trauma?
abstract: Contrast-enhanced FAST (cFAST) has demonstrated superior sensitivity to B-mode FAST for detecting solid organ injury in blunt abdominal trauma, yet no prior study has evaluated cFAST image interpretation by pediatric emergency medicine (PEM) clinicians. We evaluated the sensitivity and specificity of cFAST interpretation for solid organ injuries by PEM clinicians following a web-based didactic.In this prospective, single-center study (February-May 2026), PEM clinicians credentialed in B-mode FAST without prior cFAST training completed a web-based didactic. Participants interpreted 12 simulated cases (25 cine clips), evaluating 41 organs (15 injured, 26 non-injured), all reviewed by a cFAST expert or cFAST-trained pediatric radiologist with CT confirmation. Pooled organ-level sensitivity and specificity were calculated with clustering correction using robust standard errors.Among 41 participants, 1681 organ-level decisions were analyzed. Pooled sensitivity was 87.97% (95% CI: 84.96%-91.09%), specificity was 89.12% (95% CI: 86.53%-91.78%), negative predictive value (NPV) was 92.77% (95% CI: 90.99%-94.59%), and positive predictive value was 82.34% (95% CI: 78.68%-86.17%). False-negative decisions occurred in 4.4% (n = 74/1681).After a web-based curriculum, PEM clinicians achieved high sensitivity, specificity, and NPV with few missed injuries, supporting future investigation of cFAST as an adjunctive screening tool in pediatric blunt abdominal trauma risk-stratification assessments.© 2026 Wiley Periodicals LLC.

title: Immersive Reality in Cardiothoracic Surgical Education.
abstract: Immersive reality technologies, including virtual reality, augmented reality, mixed reality, and related extended reality platforms, are reforming how surgeons learn complex anatomy, rehearse procedures, develop technical skills, and manage unexpected or rare intraoperative crises. Cardiothoracic surgery is particularly well suited to these tools because postgraduate training occurs in a high-stakes environment characterized by complex 3-dimensional anatomy, limited operative exposure, minimally invasive/robotic approaches, open communication, and the need for synchronized team performance. Immersive platforms facilitate anatomy education and procedural planning and enable deliberate practice and nontechnical skills training. Although most studies remain small, heterogeneous, and focused on surrogate outcomes rather than patient outcomes, evidence from surgical education and cardiothoracic surgery literature demonstrates that these tools impart improvement in knowledge, confidence, procedural accuracy, and simulator performance. This article defines immersive reality technologies, reviews their educational rationale and emerging applications in cardiothoracic surgery, proposes an implementation framework for training programs, and highlights limitations related to haptics, validation, privacy, equity, and regulatory oversight. The next phase should focus on validation of outcome-linked curricula that integrate immersive simulation into competency-based surgical education.

title: Transapical Beating-Heart Septal Myectomy for Symptomatic Nonobstructive Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy: Initial Clinical Experience.
abstract: Nonobstructive hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (nHCM), defined as hypertrophic cardiomyopathy without left ventricular outflow tract obstruction, remains challenging to treat because of its heterogeneous pathophysiology. This study evaluated the safety and efficacy of transapical beating-heart septal myectomy in patients with symptomatic nHCM.Patients with symptomatic, drug-refractory nHCM were prospectively enrolled to undergo transapical beating-heart septal myectomy through a left minithoracotomy. Under real-time transesophageal echocardiographic guidance, septal myectomy was tailored to relieve systolic cavity obliteration and mid-to-apical ventricular obstruction and to enlarge the left ventricular cavity. The primary end point was procedural success at 6 to 12 months postoperatively, defined as fulfillment of all prespecified criteria compared with baseline: ≥1-class improvement in New York Heart Association functional class, ≥10-point increase in Kansas City Cardiomyopathy Questionnaire score, ≥10-mL increase in stroke volume, and normal or grade I diastolic function.Between January 2023 and January 2025, 97 consecutive eligible patients with nHCM underwent transapical beating-heart septal myectomy at Tongji Hospital. At postoperative 6 to 12 months, procedural success was achieved in 87.6%. Specifically, New York Heart Association functional class I increased from 0% at baseline to 93.8% at follow-up, the median Kansas City Cardiomyopathy Questionnaire score improved from 64 (interquartile range, 56-69) to 87 (interquartile range, 82-92; P<0.001), the stroke volume increased from 53.5 mL (interquartile range, 41.0-66.6 mL) to 70.8 mL (interquartile range, 61.3-82.3 mL; P<0.001), and normal or grade I diastolic function increased from 65.6% to 97.9%. Among patients who underwent paired cardiopulmonary exercise testing (n=58), peak oxygen uptake increased by 1.1±2.9 mL/kg/min (P=0.008). In an exploratory, hypothesis-generating analysis of 12 patients with paired 13N-ammonia positron emission tomography, coronary flow reserve increased from 1.8±0.3 to 2.0±0.4 (P=0.034). Adverse events included mitral valve injury (n=1) and ventricular septal perforation (n=1), the latter resulting in 1 postoperative death.Transapical beating-heart septal myectomy was associated with favorable left ventricular geometric remodeling and meaningful improvements in symptoms, health status, and functional capacity in selected patients with symptomatic nHCM. title: A deep learning framework for oligopeptide candidate discovery across metabolism-related contexts.
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI)-based methods are increasingly critical in therapeutic peptide discovery but have been concentrated in certain applications, such as the development of antimicrobial peptides. Therapeutic peptide discovery in contexts such as metabolism, endocrinology, and tissue regeneration remains challenging due to a paucity of available indication-specific training data. Here, we propose a deep learning-based pipeline, Deepeptide, capable of identifying candidate oligopeptides for various metabolism-related contexts. Leveraging the intrinsic relationships between disease indication, biological processes, and molecular function, Deepeptide identifies oligopeptides associated with disease-related processes as lead candidates. Deepeptide was applied in five representative disease-related contexts: angiogenesis, lipid metabolism, osteogenesis, glucose metabolism, and anti-angiogenesis. Overall, 62% of the identified oligopeptide candidates demonstrated significant bioactivity, with most of them showing comparable potency to the benchmark therapeutic agents. These findings highlight the potential utility and generalizability of Deepeptide for oligopeptide lead discovery across metabolism-related contexts.Copyright © 2026 The Authors. title: First bite syndrome in neurologic practice: A narrative review of a distinct paroxysmal craniofacial pain syndrome.
abstract: This narrative review aims to provide a comprehensive overview of the etiopathogenesis, clinical features, diagnosis, and treatment of first bite syndrome.Though well described by the Otolaryngology and Maxillofacial surgical specialties, first bite syndrome is rarely discussed in Neurology literature. Headache specialists may see these patients as a referral for trigeminal neuralgia or undiagnosed paroxysmal facial pain.Relevant literature was identified through searches of major medical databases from their inception until May 29, 2026. After removing duplicates and excluded abstracts (e.g., incorrect subject matter, non-English, abstract only) and adding additional articles identified from references of reviewed articles, 163 unique articles on first bite syndrome were further analyzed for information on etiology, clinical presentation, prognosis, or treatment.First bite syndrome typically presents with unilateral paroxysmal facial pain along the parotid and mandibular region, triggered by salivation. The pain is worsened by strong sialagogues such as acidic or sour foods and tends to improve after the first few bites of a meal. It may be aching/cramping or sharp, shock-like pain along the jaw or mandible, and can be mistaken for trigeminal neuralgia or temporomandibular disease. First bite syndrome can be seen following surgery in the parotid, parapharyngeal, or neck region, as well as with salivary gland tumors or other neoplasms in the parapharyngeal space. Individuals with first bite syndrome may experience gradual improvement with time, and a smaller number may experience complete resolution of symptoms. For those who do not improve, or for those with severe pain, neuropathic medications or botulinum toxin administration may be beneficial.First bite syndrome is underrecognized in clinical practice. Clinicians should be familiar with its clinical presentation and maintain a high index of suspicion when patients present with facial pain associated with salivation. Differentiation of first bite syndrome from other causes of facial pain is important to guide evaluation and therapy, and to help avoid unnecessary medications and procedures.© 2026 American Headache Society.

title: UICC TNM 9th Edition Updates: Cancers of the Colon and Rectum.
abstract: The expanding medical knowledge of tumour behaviour and advances in imaging, pathology, and therapeutic options require that TNM to be regularly updated. The 9th edition of the Union for International Cancer Control (UICC) TNM Classification of Malignant Tumours was published in 2025 [UICC 9th Edition (2025)] to take effect on January 2026. Updates are performed in collaboration with the AJCC. Not all sites were updated in the 9th edition and were planned to be revised later. The update of cancers of the colon and rectum is reported. The main changes are: clarification on what constituted regional or metastatic nodes (obturator nodes are regional for carcinomas of the rectum), that for low rectal cancer regional lymph nodes include superficial inguinal nodes, the inclusion of tumour deposit (TD's) - discrete tumour nodules in pericolic or perirectal fat as a stage descriptor, and subdivision of M1c into M1c1 (peritoneal only) and M1c2 (peritoneal with other sites). Key changes include clarifying which lymph nodes count as regional spread, recognizing tumor deposits in surrounding fat as a staging factor, and dividing one category of distant spread into two more specific types. These revisions, taking effect in 2027, aim to improve how doctors classify and stage these cancers more accurately.

Key changes include clarification that obturator nodes are regional for rectal carcinomas, inclusion of superficial inguinal nodes as regional lymph nodes for low rectal cancer, and incorporation of tumour deposits in pericolic or perirectal fat as a stage descriptor. Stage groupings have been updated to reflect these anatomic and pathologic refinements. These revisions are scheduled to take effect in January 2026 and were developed collaboratively between the UICC and AJCC.

title: Novel wounded porcine skin ex vivo methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus and Pseudomonas aeruginosa infection models.
abstract: Chronic wounds are a growing challenge in clinical practice and can be associated with infection by antimicrobial-resistant bacteria. With increasing demand for pathophysiology research and therapeutic technology development, biologically relevant platforms like infected swine skin explants are used; however, explants are not typically studied in conjunction with normal microbiota, which recapitulates the clinical scenario. The current study generated 1- and 8-cm diameter wounded swine skin explants from shaved, sanitized swine skin harvested immediately after euthanasia. Tissue morphology was evaluated over 9 days using a custom histological grading scale and growth dynamics of skin microbiota monitored. Explant viability decreased after 3 days in association with a peak in normal microbiota of varying diversity. Stable co-colonization of wound beds with clinical Pseudomonas aeruginosa and methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus isolates alongside microbiota over 3 days was demonstrated. In summary, the presented 1- and 8-cm explant models maintain normal microbiota and are suitable for microbiome and/or wound infection treatment or prevention studies.

The skin samples remained viable for three days and successfully maintained both the normal microbiota and stable co-colonization of two dangerous bacteria, methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus and Pseudomonas aeruginosa. Tissue morphology was assessed over 9 days using a custom histological grading scale, while growth dynamics of skin microbiota and pathogen colonization were monitored throughout the study period. title: Diagnostic accuracy of the ovine CRH test in ACTH-dependent Cushing syndrome.
abstract: Determining the cause of adrenocorticotropin (ACTH)-dependent Cushing syndrome may require bilateral inferior petrosal sinus sampling (BIPSS). Ovine corticotropin-releasing hormone (oCRH) has been unavailable in the United States since 2020 and human CRH supply is constrained worldwide. We retrospectively reviewed 97 adults at one tertiary referral centre (1998-2018) who underwent oCRH stimulation as the peripheral component of BIPSS and in whom the sampling result was concordant with the final diagnosis: Cushing disease (CD; n = 87) or ectopic ACTH-dependent Cushing syndrome (EADCS; n = 10). Ten published threshold magnitudes and three exploratory in-sample thresholds were evaluated. The area under the curve was 0.854 (95% CI 0.681-0.986) for ACTH and 0.807 (0.593-0.953) for cortisol. All five published ACTH thresholds from ≥31% to ≥50% classified the primary cohort identically (sensitivity 95%, specificity 70%); an exploratory optimum of ≥73% gave 94% and 80%, with overlapping confidence intervals and the difference driven by one ectopic patient. Bootstrap resampling showed stable discrimination but marked threshold instability, with optimal cut-offs ranging from 18% to 80%. Adding two histologically confirmed ectopic patients with central BIPSS gradients reduced specificity at Δ73% to 75%. Applying published 30-minute criteria at 30 minutes modestly changed performance. Peak ACTH occurred by 30 minutes in 62% and by 60 minutes in all patients. These estimates apply to a BIPSS-referred population and do not support adoption of a new threshold.© the author(s).

title: Oral Cellular Neurothekeoma: Case Report and Brief Review of the Literature.
abstract: Cellular neurothekeoma (CNT) is a rare benign mesenchymal neoplasm of uncertain histogenesis distinct from dermal nerve sheath myxoma. Oral involvement is exceedingly uncommon.A 22-year-old woman presented with a 5-month history of a painful enlarging intraoral mass involving the left buccal and labial gingiva, associated with difficulty eating and speaking. Imaging revealed an ill-defined soft tissue mass without bone involvement. An initial excisional biopsy was interpreted as nodular fasciitis. After recurrence at 6 months, conservative resection was performed. Histopathologic evaluation demonstrated a multilobular submucosal neoplasm composed of spindle to epithelioid cells arranged in fascicular and nodular patterns within a myxoid stroma, separated by hyaline collagen, with admixed lymphoplasmacytic inflammation. Tumor cells were negative for S100, cytokeratin AE1/AE3, desmin, CD34, EMA, and ALK, with focal positivity for SMA and PGP9.5. Ki-67 showed a low proliferative index (<5%). Molecular testing was negative for USP6 gene rearrangement. These findings supported a diagnosis of CNT.We report the 10th case of oral CNT, highlighting the importance of comprehensive histologic, immunohistochemical, and molecular evaluation to avoid misdiagnosis.Copyright © 2026 Wolters Kluwer Health, LLC.
