title: Antiseizure medication use in self-limited epilepsies of childhood: A scoping review by the ILAE Pediatric Medical Therapies Task Force.
abstract: Self-limited focal epilepsies (SeLFEs) of childhood, including self-limited epilepsy with centrotemporal spikes (SeLECTS), self-limited epilepsy with autonomic seizures (SeLEAS), childhood occipital visual epilepsy (COVE), and photosensitive occipital lobe epilepsy (POLE), are common pediatric epilepsy syndromes with heterogeneous clinical management. We performed a scoping review to synthesize evidence regarding the use, effectiveness, safety, and discontinuation of antiseizure medications (ASMs) in children with SeLFEs.Nine databases were searched from inception to January 2026. Eligible studies included original research reporting ASM-related outcomes in children with SeLFEs. PRISMA-ScR (Preferred Reporting Items of Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses, extension for scoping reviews) guidance was followed.Sixty-two studies met eligibility criteria, including 11 randomized controlled trials (RCTs). Most studies evaluated SeLECTS (6171 participants), whereas substantially fewer investigated SeLEAS (n = 348), COVE (n = 91), or POLE (n = 26). Evidence was highly heterogeneous and consisted predominantly of retrospective observational studies. In SeLECTS, reported 12-month seizure freedom rates after ASM treatment were approximately 72% across studies, although estimates varied considerably. Evidence for SeLEAS, COVE, and POLE was limited and derived mainly from small retrospective cohorts with heterogeneous methodologies and outcome definitions. Failure of first-line ASM therapy occurred in approximately 30% of patients. Adverse events were reported in approximately 22% of treated children and infrequently led to treatment discontinuation. RCTs generally reported similar seizure outcomes across multiple ASMs, although many trials were limited by small sample sizes and open-label designs.Current evidence suggests that children with SeLFEs often achieve seizure control with ASM treatment and that adverse effects are generally manageable. However, the overall certainty of evidence remains limited because of methodological heterogeneity, predominance of retrospective studies, and limited randomized data. Important evidence gaps remain regarding the need for ASM treatment, optimal treatment duration, and timing of medication withdrawal.© 2026 The Author(s). llm_summary: Researchers reviewed 62 studies to understand how well seizure-preventing medications work in children with self-limited epilepsies, which are childhood epilepsy types that tend to resolve on their own. About 72% of children treated with these medications became seizure-free within a year, though results varied widely across studies and roughly 30% of patients did not respond to their first medication tried. The evidence quality remains limited because most studies were small, retrospective observations rather than rigorous controlled trials, leaving important questions unanswered about whether medication is always necessary and when to stop treatment.

title: Sensorimotor impairment and cognitive function across the Alzheimer's disease continuum and major depressive disorder.
abstract: Sensorimotor impairments are associated with cognitive decline, but their cumulative burden across clinical subgroups is not well characterized. To test whether sensorimotor burden is associated with baseline cognition and modifies subgroup-related cognitive differences. We analyzed 511 community-dwelling older adults. Participants were classified as cognitively normal, preclinical Alzheimer's disease (Clinical Dementia Rating score of 0 with amyloid positron-emission tomography positivity), mild cognitive impairment, or major depressive disorder. Cognition was measured with the Preclinical Alzheimer Cognitive Composite. A Sensorimotor Index summed impairments in grip strength, gait speed, reaction time, hearing, vision, and olfaction and was categorized as low (0-1) or elevated (≥ 2). Multivariable linear regression assessed subgroup, index, and subgroup-by-index terms, adjusting for age, sex, race, education, apolipoprotein E ε4 status, and neighborhood deprivation. Without interactions, elevated burden was associated with lower cognitive scores (β =- 0.374; 95% confidence interval, - 0.508 to - 0.240; p < 0.001). In the interaction model, the mild cognitive impairment-by-elevated-index (β =- 0.647; 95% confidence interval, - 0.981 to - 0.313; p < 0.001) and major depressive disorder-by-elevated-index terms (β =- 0.440; 95% confidence interval, - 0.759 to - 0.120; p = 0.007) were significant; the preclinical Alzheimer's disease interaction was not. Dose-response analyses showed progressively lower cognitive scores at higher index levels. Greater sensorimotor burden was associated with lower cognition, with stronger adverse associations in mild cognitive impairment and major depressive disorder. Multidomain sensorimotor assessment may improve characterization of cognitive heterogeneity in older adults.© 2026. The Author(s), under exclusive licence to American Aging Association.

They found that people with multiple sensorimotor impairments had lower cognitive scores, with particularly strong effects in those with mild cognitive impairment or depression. These results suggest that assessing multiple physical and sensory functions together may help doctors better understand why some older adults experience different levels of cognitive decline.

title: Absolute Risk of Progression to Cognitive Impairment Based on Plasma Phosphorylated Tau 217, Age, Sex, and APOE ε4.
abstract: Alzheimer disease (AD) pathology can be detected years before symptom onset, but some individuals who are biomarker positive and cognitively unimpaired (CU) remain asymptomatic.To estimate 5- and 10-year absolute risks of mild cognitive impairment (MCI) and dementia using continuous plasma phosphorylated tau 217 (p-tau217) and p-tau217/amyloid β 42 (Aβ42).This cohort study included participants from the Mayo Clinic Study of Aging (MCSA) and the Alzheimer's Disease Neuroimaging Initiative (ADNI). Participants were CU individuals aged 60 to 90 years with baseline Fujirebio Lumipulse plasma p-tau217 measurements, APOE genotyping, and longitudinal clinical follow-up. The MCSA is a population-based longitudinal cohort of residents in Olmsted County, Minnesota; ADNI is a multicenter observational cohort. MCSA data were ascertained from October 2008 to September 2025; ADNI data from September 2005 to January 2026.Age, sex, APOE ε4, p-tau217, and p-tau217/Aβ42.Transition from CU to MCI and dementia estimated using continuous-time multistate models.In the MCSA cohort (n = 1644), the median (IQR) age was 72 (66-79) years; 804 participants (49%) were female and 840 (51%) were male. In the ADNI cohort (n = 534), the median (IQR) age was 72 (68-77) years; 297 participants (56%) were female and 237 (44%) were male. A p-tau217 of 0.324 pg/mL vs 0.072 pg/mL (90th vs 10th percentile) was associated with 2.66 (95% CI, 2.02-3.51), 3.02 (95% CI, 2.21-4.12), 2.62 (95% CI, 1.99-3.46), and 2.79 (95% CI, 2.04-3.81) greater hazard of clinical progression in MCSA female participants who did not carry the APOE ε4 variant (ε4-), females who did carry the APOE ε4 variant (ε4+), males who were ε4-, and males who were ε4+, respectively. In ADNI, hazards were 2.67 (95% CI, 1.86-3.85), 2.83 (95% CI, 1.89-4.22), 2.08 (95% CI, 1.48-2.92), and 3.99 (95% CI, 2.59-6.13), respectively. In MCSA, higher baseline p-tau217 and older age were associated with greater absolute risk of progression. At age 75 years and assuming sex and APOE are at the MCSA means of 0.511 and 0.268, 5-year absolute risk of MCI increased from 7% (95% CI, 5%-8%) to 17% (95% CI, 13%-20%) for a p-tau217 concentration of 0.072 vs 0.324 pg/mL; 10-year absolute risk of MCI increased from 15% (95% CI, 12%-18%) to 35% (95% CI, 29%-41%; P < .001 for both). At 0.324 pg/mL, 5-year MCI risk increased from 6% (95% CI, 4%-8%) to 37% (95% CI, 32%-43%) for ages 65 to 85 years; 10-year risks were 17% (95% CI, 12%-21%) and 66% (95% CI, 57%-74%; P < .001 for both). Results were similar for p-tau217/Aβ42.This study found that higher plasma p-tau217 and older age were associated with higher 5- and 10-year risk of cognitive impairment. Plasma p-tau217 concentrations, combined with age, sex, and APOE ε4 status, can enable individualized estimation of short-term absolute risk of cognitive impairment in CU individuals, with applications in prognosis and trial enrichment in preclinical AD.

title: Etentamig in Relapsed/Refractory Multiple Myeloma: Pooled Phase 1 Data of an Investigational BCMA Bispecific Antibody.
abstract: Etentamig is an investigational B-cell maturation antigen (BCMA) x CD3 bispecific T-cell engager, composed of a low-affinity CD3 binding domain, potentially reducing cytokine release syndrome (CRS) and infections, a high-avidity bivalent BCMA-binding domain, and retained FcRn binding supporting monthly (Q4W) dosing after a single step-up dose (SUD). We report long-term efficacy and safety from the ongoing, open-label, phase 1 (dose escalation/expansion; NCT03933735) and Arm A of the phase 1b (NCT05650632) studies of etentamig in adult patients with relapsed/refractory multiple myeloma, triple-class exposure, and ≥3 prior lines of therapy (LoT). In phase 1, patients received etentamig 60 mg Q4W or 40 mg Q3W, and in phase 1b, a SUD on Day 1 and 60 mg Q4W on Day 4. Among 146 patients (median age: 68 years; median [range] prior LoT: 4 [3-23]), median follow-up was 13 months (range: 1-48). Objective responses and ≥ very good partial responses occurred in 66% and 54% of patients. Median duration of response and progression-free survival were not reached. Pooled data suggest etentamig has a manageable safety profile, with Grade 3/4 neutropenia and infection occurring in 38% and 23% of patients. In phase 1b Arm A (n=23), overall CRS incidence was 30% (26% Grade 1; 4% Grade 2) with modified dexamethasone premedication and 1 SUD; median onset was 22.3 hours (range: 5.5-29.6) hours, with resolution in 20.7 hours (range: 1.8-131.7). title: A Lighter Approach to Language Access: Virtual Interpreter Utilization in Emergency Medical Services (EMS).
abstract: Limited English Proficiency (LEP) may create communication barriers during prehospital care. Although on-demand interpreter services are often available to emergency medical services (EMS) clinicians, utilization may be limited by device accessibility, workflow barriers, and clinician adoption. Our objective was to evaluate whether implementation of agency-issued lightweight clinician-carried smartphones was associated with increased utilization of virtual interpreter services during prehospital care.We conducted an observational retrospective pre-post cohort study of virtual interpreter service utilization within a large multistate Midwest EMS agency. On June 1, 2025, the agency issued smartphones (Apple iPhone 16, ∼6 ounces) to all clinicians, providing continuous access to virtual audio and video interpreter services (LanguageLine Solutions). Previously, interpreter services were accessed using large Toughbook laptops (∼6.1 pounds). Interpreter utilization was compared between pre-implementation (October 30, 2024, to May 31, 2025) and post-implementation (June 1, 2025, to December 31, 2025) periods. Interpreter requests per 100 encounters were compared using rate ratios (RRs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs).Interpreter requests increased from 104 pre-implementation (0.19 per 100 encounters, 95% CI: 0.15-0.23) to 326 post-implementation (0.57 per 100 encounters, 95% CI: 0.51-0.63; RR= 3.04, 95% CI: 2.44-3.79; p < 0.001). Audio requests increased from 68 calls (0.12 per 100 encounters) to 271 calls (0.47 per 100 encounters; RR = 3.86, 95% CI: 2.96-5.03; p < 0.001). Video requests increased from 36 calls (0.06 per 100 encounters) to 55 calls (0.10 per 100 encounters), although the observed increase did not reach statistical significance (RR= 1.48, 95% CI: 0.97-2.25; p = 0.066). The most commonly requested languages were Spanish (n = 153, 36%), Somali (n = 146, 34%), and Arabic (n = 41, 10%).Implementation of agency-issued lightweight clinician-carried smartphones was associated with a threefold increase in virtual interpreter utilization. This increase was driven primarily by audio interpretation, while the observed increase in video utilization did not reach statistical significance. These findings suggest that improving point-of-care accessibility of interpreter services through lightweight mobile devices may facilitate greater utilization during prehospital encounters with patients with LEP.

title: Higher Doses of Perioperative Dexamethasone are Not Associated with an Increased Risk of Infection Following Total Hip and Knee Arthroplasty.
abstract: Dexamethasone has been used with increased frequency perioperatively during total knee (TKA) and hip arthroplasty (THA) to prevent postoperative nausea and vomiting. Higher doses of dexamethasone have been shown to decrease pain and prevent complications such as pulmonary embolism and acute kidney injury. However, less is known regarding the effect of increasing doses on infectious complications, particularly among patients who have diabetes.Utilizing a national healthcare database, we identified adult patients undergoing primary total joint arthroplasty (TJA) between 2016 and 2023. Patients were stratified with respect to the dexamethasone dose administered on the day of surgery into a no-dose, low-dose (four to five- miligrams[mg]), medium-dose (eight to 12 mg), or high-dose (16 to 32 mg) group. The primary outcome, the 90-day risk of periprosthetic joint infection (PJI), was compared across all dexamethasone dosing levels using mixed-effect logistic regression, with the no-dexamethasone group as the reference, in both diabetic and non-diabetic patients.Of the identified 1,483,703 TJA patients, 618,654 (41.7%) received no dexamethasone, 252,978 (17.1%) received a low dose, 481,551 (32.5%) received a medium dose, and 130,520 (8.8%) received a high dose on the day of surgery. Among non-diabetic patients, high-dose dexamethasone was not associated with an increased risk of PJI following either TKA (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] 0.93, 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.79 to 1.09, P = 0.354) or THA (aOR 0.82, 95% CI 0.68 to 1.00, P = 0.050). Low- and medium-dose dexamethasone were also not associated with an increased risk of PJI after either procedure. These findings held true among diabetic patients.Higher perioperative doses of dexamethasone were not associated with an increased risk of infection even among patients who have diabetes. title: Can Outpatient Total Hip Arthroplasty Be Done at a Complex, Academic, Quaternary Referral Center?
abstract: Primary outpatient (same-day discharge) total hip arthroplasty (THA) has gained popularity, but results from academic medical centers remain limited. Same-day discharge shifts perioperative responsibilities to the surgeon. In contrast, surgeon reimbursements continue to decline. We retrospectively evaluated 90-day rates of emergency room (ER) visits, reoperations, revisions, and postoperative touches associated with outpatient THAs at our complex, academic, quaternary referral center.At our institution, 1,970 outpatient primary THAs were performed between 2019 and 2024 in 1,813 unique patients. The mean age was 61 years, 56% were men, the mean body mass index (BMI) was 30, the mean American Society of Anesthesiologists (ASA) score was 2.2, and the mean Charlson Comorbidity Index (CCI) was 1.2 (range, 1 to 10). Medical comorbidities, ER visits, reoperations, revisions, and postoperative touches within 90 days after THA were collected. Univariate logistic regression analyses were completed.Rates of ER visits, reoperations, and revisions within 90 days of surgery were 8.6, 1.5, and 0.9%, respectively. Hips averaged nine postoperative touches, and total touches increased from 131 in 2019 to greater than 4,800 in 2024. The most common first-time ER visit reason was a medical issue unrelated to surgery (39%), followed by dislocation (14%) and venous thromboembolism (VTE) evaluation (12%; actual VTE incidence 0.3%). The most common reason for reoperation and revision was acute periprosthetic joint infection (PJI; incidence 0.7%). Increasing BMI was associated with risk of reoperations (odds ratio [OR] 1.1; P = 0.02), revisions (OR 1.1; P = 0.03), and PJI (OR 1.1; P = 0.03), but not with ER visits or dislocations. Increasing CCI was associated with risk of first-time ER visits (OR 1.2; P < 0.001) and dislocations (OR 1.3; P = 0.02). Increasing ASA score was associated with risk of ER visits (OR 1.8; P < 0.001).Outpatient THA patients had a high rate of ER visits within 90 days postoperatively, with almost 40% unattributable to surgery. Increasing BMI was associated with increased reoperation, revision, and PJI risk, while increasing CCI and ASA score increased ER visit risk, and increasing CCI increased dislocation risk. Hips averaged nine postoperative touches. As outpatient THA grows, surgeon compensation should be reevaluated given the heightened administrative burden.Copyright © 2026 Elsevier Inc. title: Machine learning for small-molecule antibiotics - discovery to pre-clinical optimization.
abstract: The rapid rise of antimicrobial resistance (AMR) poses a critical global health crisis, with 4.71 million associated deaths and 1.14 million attributable deaths in 2021. By 2050, these tolls are forecasted to rise to 8.22 million associated deaths and 1.91 million attributable deaths annually. Despite this growing burden, the antibacterial pipeline is alarmingly lean, with few candidates exhibiting truly novel mechanisms of action (MOA). This innovation gap is worsened by the lack of economic incentives for large pharmaceutical companies to develop new antibiotics, placing increasing pressure on academic laboratories and small biotechnology companies. Machine learning (ML) has emerged as a promising, albeit unproven, toolset to accelerate and reduce the cost of antibiotic discovery and development.To review a cross-section of ML methods and their applications across the preclinical antibiotic discovery and development pipeline.Google Scholar and PubMed were searched through June 2026, combining terms for machine learning, deep learning, and artificial intelligence with antibiotic discovery and development, virtual screening, generative molecular design, and ADMET prediction. Primary research articles were prioritized, with preprints from arXiv and bioRxiv included where no peer-reviewed version was available. Reference lists of retrieved articles and WHO antibacterial pipeline reports were also screened.ML approaches enable more efficient exploration of vast chemical spaces in silico, facilitating the discovery of structurally novel antibacterial compounds in phenotype- and target-based applications. Both discriminative and generative models have demonstrated success in discovering new scaffolds and in multi-property optimization tasks. In target-based discovery, ML-guided docking strategies have improved scalability relative to more computationally demanding physics-based methods.ML-guided methods can improve the efficiency, scalability, and success rate of antibiotic discovery and development programs. However, the implementation of these models will require high-quality training data and rigorous experimental validation prior to end-to-end integration.Copyright © 2026 The Author(s). title: Distinct patterns of activity in the prelimbic cortex track task-related differences for cocaine and water reinforcers.
abstract: The pursuit of drugs is a fundamental element of substance use. Different tasks assess drug pursuit in the face of effort, punishment, or the absence of the drug, and recent studies have suggested that a shared latent variable may drive behavior across these tasks. The prelimbic cortex (PL) is implicated in these behaviors, but it is unknown if its role is driven by distinct neural ensembles. We recorded PL activity using in vivo endoscopic calcium imaging in 32 male and female Sprague-Dawley rats as they completed cocaine or water self-administration, extinction, progressive ratio, and punished self-administration. We found that behavior across tasks covaried in water, but not cocaine rats. We also found that slow, sustained neural excitations following response for reward were lower in extinction. Furthermore, exploratory analysis suggests that those individual rats that had more responsive neurons also had significantly higher levels of reward pursuit in the extinction task. Notably, this relationship was true across cocaine and water rats, suggesting a general role independent of reward type. Thus, our findings suggest that extinction behavior is tracked by a distinct neural pattern in the PL.Copyright © 2026. Published by Elsevier Ltd.

title: The Genomic Landscape and Treatment Outcomes Associated with CDKN2A/MTAP Loss in Patients with Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer.
abstract: Homozygous deletion of the 9p21 locus, containing CDKN2A/B and MTAP [CDKN2A/MTAP deletion (CMdel)], underlies emerging therapeutic strategies, including PRMT5/MAT2A inhibition. The clinicogenomic context and treatment outcome associations of CMdel in non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) remain incompletely defined.We analyzed Tempus Lens records with paired DNA (xT) and RNA (xR) sequencing. After quality filtering (purity ≥40%), 16,947 patients were included in the primary dataset, and 10,996 were included in the validation dataset and stratified by deletion status [CMdel vs. CM wild-type (CMwt)]. IFN status was defined by IFN-kappa (IFNK) expression [log2(TPM + 1)] using the 25th percentile of CMwt as the threshold. Immune composition was inferred by quanTIseq. First-line regimens were grouped as immune checkpoint inhibitor (ICI) monotherapy, ICI chemotherapy, chemotherapy, or tyrosine kinase inhibitors (TKI). Best response and time to next treatment (TTNT) with risk-set adjustment and 18-month truncation were assessed.CMdel occurred in 11.7% (n = 1,991) and 15% (n = 1,676), respectively, and was enriched in mucinous histology, stage IV disease, and never smokers. CMdel was associated with EGFR, TERT, and SMARCA4 alterations, whereas CMwt was associated with RB1, SETD2, and ARID2. CMdel tumors exhibited lower PD-L1, mutation burden, and immune infiltration. title: Consensus on biomarker utility for ACTH-dependent Cushing syndrome: a Pituitary Society Modified Delphi Panel.
abstract: Biochemical test results are central to clinical decision-making for the diagnosis and management of Cushing syndrome (CS). With emerging research and increasing availability of different tests, updated consensus on the utility of these biomarkers is warranted.To establish an updated consensus on the role of biomarkers in the diagnosis and monitoring of adrenocorticotropic hormone-dependent CS, address novel therapeutic approaches, and identify areas for future research.A modified 2-round Delphi panel was conducted. Consensus was defined as ≥70% agreement/disagreement for Likert-scale statements or ≥70% selection of the same option for single-choice questions.Participants represented a range of international expertise.Forty-one participants took part in the Delphi panel, with no attrition between rounds (one nonclinician was not required to complete the second round). An 8-member Steering Committee guided statement development.Of statements designed to reach consensus, 45% (14/31) and 44% (11/25) statements reached consensus in Rounds 1 and 2, respectively. Notably, most panelists reported the use of late-night salivary cortisol for diagnosis of mild CS and for monitoring following pituitary surgery or medical or radiation therapy. Most panelists responded that block-and-replace therapies can be considered in patients with cyclical or severe CS, and consensus was reached that restoration of circadian rhythm is a treatment goal for patients with CS.Areas of alignment among experts on the diagnosis and monitoring of CS are presented. The findings from this study are intended to support clinicians in their clinical decision-making and highlight priority areas for future research.© The Author(s) 2026. title: Peritoneal Recurrence After Resection of Appendiceal Goblet Cell Adenocarcinoma.
abstract: Goblet cell adenocarcinoma of the appendix has a predilection for peritoneal dissemination, but recurrence patterns and risk factors after curative-intent resection are poorly defined.We retrospectively identified patients undergoing definitive surgery at three Mayo Clinic sites from 1990 through 2024. Pathology was rereviewed using contemporary World Health Organization criteria. The primary end point was first peritoneal recurrence. Associations were estimated using cause-specific Cox regression, with Fine-Gray competing-risk analyses as sensitivity analyses.Among 125 patients, 104 (83%) underwent right hemicolectomy, 15 (12%) appendectomy, and 6 (5%) ileocecectomy; 39 (31%) received adjuvant systemic therapy. During a median follow-up of 3.7 years (interquartile range, 2.1-6.3 years), 22 patients (18%) developed recurrence. Every first recurrence involved the peritoneum; 5 patients also had locoregional recurrence, and 1 had distant recurrence. Median time to recurrence among patients with recurrence within the 10-year analysis window was 3.5 years (interquartile range, 1.3-6.4 years). In the multivariable model, pathologic T4 disease (hazard ratio, 5.11; 95% confidence interval, 1.92-13.6; P=.001) and positive margins (hazard ratio, 5.34; 95% confidence interval, 1.08-26.5; P=.040) were associated with recurrence. In competing-risk analysis, the association with pathologic T4 disease persisted, whereas the margin estimate remained directionally similar but imprecise. Although pT4 disease identified a group at increased risk, recurrence also occurred in patients with pT0-3 disease.Peritoneal involvement characterized every first recurrence after curative-intent resection of nonmetastatic GCA. Pathologic T4 disease was the most consistent risk factor for recurrence, with positive margins providing additional prognostic information. title: Biomarkers in Cardiology: A Critical Appraisal of Historical Successes, Pitfalls, and Emerging Uses.
abstract: In preventive cardiology, low-density lipoprotein cholesterol and blood pressure are validated surrogate endpoints, with multiple randomized trials demonstrating that their reduction improves cardiovascular morbidity and mortality. In contrast, raising high-density lipoprotein cholesterol (HDL-C) with niacin or cholesteryl ester transfer protein inhibitors failed to improve outcomes despite promising observational data and biological plausibility. In the Cardiac Arrhythmia Suppression Trial of class IC antiarrhythmics to suppress premature ventricular complexes, biomarker-targeted therapy increased mortality. Contemporary biomarkers, including lipoprotein(a), coronary artery calcium scoring, and high-sensitivity C-reactive protein, are increasingly used to refine risk and guide therapy. However, despite favorable guideline recommendations, randomized trials showing that biomarker-guided or biomarker-targeted treatment improves hard clinical endpoints are lacking. This review presents historical biomarker reversals in cardiology and critically appraises the evidence supporting emerging biomarkers. Our core argument is that practice recommendations for biomarker-guided therapy should await appropriately designed randomized trials adequately powered for cardiovascular events and mortality.Copyright © 2026 Wolters Kluwer Health, LLC. title: Updated clinical recommendations for cardiovascular risk assessment to facilitate hormone therapy prescribing: incorporating PREVENT risk calculator and the 2026 multisociety lipid guidelines.
abstract: Cardiovascular disease (CVD) remains the leading cause of death among women and is a key consideration when evaluating candidates for menopausal hormone therapy (HT). Over the past two decades, recommendations regarding HT use have evolved substantially and now include the understanding that cardiovascular risk varies according to age, time since menopause onset, and baseline cardiovascular health. Consequently, cardiovascular risk assessment has become an integral component of menopause management. The recent introduction of the Predicting Risk of Cardiovascular Disease Events (PREVENT) calculator and incorporation of PREVENT into the 2026 American College of Cardioloty/Amercian Heart Association multisociety dyslipidemia guideline represent an important shift in CVD prevention. PREVENT includes contemporary cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic risk factors and estimates both 10-year and 30-year cardiovascular risk for adults ages 30-79 years without known CVD. Concurrently, updated lipid management recommendations emphasize individualized risk assessment and consideration of risk-enhancing factors, and in some cases, coronary artery calcium scoring, along with more explicit lipid-lowering targets. This perspective provides a practical framework for integrating PREVENT-derived risk categories into menopause care. We outline cardiovascular risk stratification strategies for women considering HT, discuss the role of coronary artery calcium scoring and female-specific risk enhancers, and align contemporary lipid management recommendations with decisions regarding initiation of HT, including route of administration. By integrating cardiovascular risk assessment and menopause management, clinicians can optimize cardiovascular risk reduction and individualize treatment decisions for symptomatic midlife women.Copyright © 2026 The Author(s). title: Longitudinal Detection of Circulating Tumor DNA in Children with Pleuropulmonary Blastoma: A Report from the International PPB/DICER1 Registry.
abstract: Pleuropulmonary blastoma (PPB) is the most common lung cancer of early childhood. Nearly all PPBs have biallelic DICER1 variants: a loss-of-function allele (often germline) and a second RNase IIIb domain "hotspot" substitution. Except in somatic mosaicism, these hotspots are tumor-specific and ideal liquid biopsy targets.For individuals with PPB enrolled in the International PPB/DICER1 Registry, blood samples were collected at timepoints coordinated with clinical venous access. Tumor sequencing identified each patient's RNase IIIb hotspot, enabling personalized droplet digital PCR assays to detect that variant in circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA).We analyzed 482 samples from 20 type I and 53 type II/III PPB patients. Among 13 pre-operative type II/III patients sampled pretreatment, 11 (85%) had detectable ctDNA, with tumor size moderately correlated with ctDNA burden (Spearman's ρ=0.574, p=0.051). In contrast, among 8 patients sampled after resection but before chemotherapy, none had detectable ctDNA (p<0.001 vs. unresected). After chemotherapy initiation, ctDNA levels spiked within 1-2 days before rapidly declining. During post-event surveillance, ctDNA was detectable a median of 5.3 weeks before clinical progression (21.7 weeks for negative samples; p=0.001). In type I PPB, DICER1 variants were detectable only in patients with somatic mosaicism.In type II/III PPB, ctDNA correlates with tumor size and resection status. The transient rise and fall in ctDNA following initiation of chemotherapy suggests that ctDNA could serve as a real-time in vivo assay of tumor responsiveness, and these findings support further investigation as a pharmacodynamic biomarker for disease response and recurrence detection.

title: Ivabradine Versus Digitalis Glycosides in Heart Failure With Reduced Ejection Fraction: A Comparative Appraisal of Two Additional Medical Therapies.
abstract: Resting heart rate predicts outcome in heart failure (HF) with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF), but lowering it benefits only hemodynamically stable patients. This narrative review compares ivabradine and the digitalis glycosides, the only additional medical therapies in the 2026 ESC guidelines that slow the heart rate, as add-ons to foundational medical therapy (FMT).We searched PubMed and the Cochrane Library through August 2026 and current guidelines, giving greatest weight to large randomized trials and contemporary meta-analyses.Ivabradine reduced cardiovascular death or heart-failure hospitalization (HR 0.82, 95% CI 0.75-0.90) without a mortality benefit; it is restricted to sinus rhythm with LVEF ≤ 35% and heart rate ≥ 70 bpm (Class IIa B1). The digitalis glycosides act in any rhythm, with LVEF ≤ 40% (Class IIa B1), and reduce worsening-heart-failure events (pooled HR 0.75, n = 9,013) without affecting mortality, within narrow, agent-specific therapeutic windows (digoxin 0.5-0.9 ng/mL; digitoxin 8-18 ng/mL). DIGIT-HF (digitoxin) was positive and DECISION (digoxin) neutral; their estimates are similar in direction and magnitude, but differences in drug, population and endpoint preclude calling them concordant. Digoxin withdrawal is associated with deterioration, although contemporary data rest on few events.Ivabradine and the digitalis glycosides are not symmetric alternatives. Ivabradine is a narrow add-on for sinus-rhythm patients who remain tachycardic despite beta-blockade; the glycosides serve both ventricular rate control in atrial fibrillation and prevention of worsening HF irrespective of rhythm. title: Improved Knee Function and Activity Levels After Circumferential Repair Versus Partial Meniscectomy for Horizontal Cleavage Meniscus Tears: A Minimum 2-Year Propensity-Matched Comparative Study.
abstract: To evaluate and compare patient-reported outcome measures between 2 propensity-matched cohorts of patients undergoing circumferential repair and partial meniscectomy for isolated meniscal horizontal cleavage tears (HCTs) and compare return to sport (RTS) characteristics between groups at a minimum 2-year follow-up.A retrospective study identified patients with isolated meniscal HCTs undergoing circumferential repair between 2015 and 2022 at a single academic institution. Patients undergoing circumferential repair were propensity-matched to a partial meniscectomy cohort 1:1 by age, sex, body mass index, knee laterality, and meniscus laterality. Patient-reported outcome measures, including International Knee Documentation Committee (IKDC), Tegner activity scale, and visual analog scale scores, and RTS data were collected at a minimum 2-year follow-up and analyzed. Failures were defined as knee reoperations or significant symptoms that required additional intervention.In total, 32 patients (69% men; 66% right knees; 50% lateral menisci; mean age 31 ± 13 years) underwent circumferential repair for isolated meniscal HCTs. At an average follow-up of 5.0 years (range 2.1-8.7 years), failures occurred in 3 (13%) circumferential repair and 5 (22%) partial meniscectomy patients (P = .700). The circumferential repair cohort showed significantly greater IKDC (82.0 vs 44.7; P < .001) and Tegner scores (6.2 vs 4.7; P = .046) compared with the partial meniscectomy cohort. In total, 27 patients (60%) played sports preoperatively, and RTS was achieved in 16 (84%) circumferential repair and 7 (88%) partial meniscectomy patients (P > .999), with 15 (94%) and 5 (71%) returning at the same or higher level, respectively.Patients who underwent circumferential repair of meniscal HCTs yielded significantly higher knee function (IKDC) and activity levels (Tegner) at an average follow-up of 5.0 years compared with propensity-matched partial meniscectomy controls. Circumferential repair was also associated with more patients achieving reported Patient Acceptable Symptom State thresholds for IKDC compared with partial meniscectomy. The all-cause failure and RTS rates were similar between groups.Level III, retrospective cohort study.© 2026 the Arthroscopy Association of North America.

llm_summary: Researchers compared two surgical approaches for treating a specific type of meniscus tear in the knee: repair versus removal of the damaged tissue. Patients who underwent repair showed significantly better knee function and activity levels after five years of follow-up compared to those who had tissue removed. Both groups had similar rates of treatment failure and successful return to sports, suggesting repair may offer better long-term outcomes without increased risk.

title: Most Chemotherapy Administration Sites Are Rural: Evidence From the Minnesota All-Payer Claims Database and a Framework for State-Level Cancer Care Surveillance.
abstract: Chemotherapy is widely assumed to be concentrated in urban cancer centers, but state-level data on its geographic distribution are limited. We used the Minnesota All-Payer Claims Database (MN APCD) to characterize rural and urban chemotherapy administration sites, assess quality certification rates, and present a replicable methodology for other states.Claims for carboplatin (J9045) and paclitaxel (J9264, J9267) from the 2022 MN APCD were analyzed. Chemotherapy administration sites were identified from billing claims, geolocated, and assigned Rural-Urban Commuting Area (RUCA) codes (urban: 1-3; rural: 4-10). Quality Oncology Practice Initiative (QOPI) certification and Commission on Cancer (CoC) accreditation were matched by facility. National QOPI (N = 217) and CoC (N = 1,093) data were analyzed by RUCA category for comparison.Among 104 sites, 55 (52.9%) were rural, accounting for 10,117 (27.0%) of 37,526 claim lines. No rural site held QOPI certification (0% v 16.3% urban). Rural CoC accreditation was lower (25.5% v 42.9%). Nationally, rural practices comprised 14.7% of QOPI-certified sites and 13.4% of CoC-accredited programs, 15%-20% of the US population living in rural areas.Despite published ASCO workforce data showing that only 7%-11.7% of medical oncologists practice in rural areas, 52.9% of Minnesota chemotherapy administration sites are rural, challenging the assumption that chemotherapy delivery is an urban and suburban phenomenon. Rural sites deliver 27.0% of claim volume, suggesting a broadly distributed but lower-intensity rural oncology infrastructure invisible to workforce-based mapping. This APCD-based framework is scalable and replicable; with approximately 25 states operating or developing mandatory APCDs, it can inform cancer control planning, direct resources to where care is delivered, and help close rural oncology disparities nationwide.

title: Inflammatory Bowel Disease in Pregnancy.
abstract: Inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) presents unique clinical considerations related to fertility, medical therapy, and delivery planning. The strongest predictor of adverse pregnancy outcomes is active disease, making maintenance of remission a central management priority. Prepregnancy counseling for patients with IBD should address reproductive goals, nutritional status, and the potential effect of prior pelvic surgery on fertility. Most established IBD therapies, including aminosalicylates, thiopurines, and biologic agents, can be continued to maintain remission, whereas methotrexate is contraindicated, and Janus kinase inhibitors and sphingosine-1-phosphate receptor modulators are generally avoided. Delivery planning should be individualized, with cesarean delivery generally favored for active perianal Crohn disease or rectovaginal fistula and shared decision making emphasized for patients with an ileal pouch-anal anastomosis. Optimal outcomes depend on coordinated multidisciplinary care that prioritizes disease control, treatment continuation, and individualized reproductive and delivery planning.Copyright © 2026 by the American College of Obstetricians & Gynecologists. llm_summary: This review examines how to safely manage inflammatory bowel disease, a chronic condition affecting the digestive system, during pregnancy and childbirth. The most important factor for healthy pregnancy outcomes is keeping the disease under control, and most common medications can be safely continued except for methotrexate, which must be avoided. Doctors should work with patients before pregnancy to plan individualized care that balances disease management with reproductive goals and delivery decisions.
llm_summary_expert: Inflammatory bowel disease in pregnancy presents distinct clinical management challenges requiring coordinated multidisciplinary care across fertility, medical therapy, and delivery planning. Active IBD disease represents the strongest predictor of adverse pregnancy outcomes, making maintenance of remission the central management priority throughout pregnancy. Prepregnancy counseling should address reproductive goals, nutritional status, and the potential impact of prior pelvic surgery on fertility in patients with IBD. Most established IBD therapies including aminosalicylates, thiopurines, and biologic agents can be continued during pregnancy to maintain remission, while methotrexate is contraindicated and Janus kinase inhibitors and sphingosine-1-phosphate receptor modulators are generally avoided. Delivery planning should be individualized based on disease phenotype, with cesarean delivery generally favored for active perianal Crohn disease or rectovaginal fistula and shared decision making emphasized for patients with ileal pouch-anal anastomosis.

title: Blood Pressure Estimation for Hemodynamic Monitoring Using Reduced Photoplethysmography Features in Intensive Care Units: Prospective Machine Learning Study.
abstract: Continuous, noninvasive blood pressure (BP) monitoring is clinically important for managing hemodynamic instability in the intensive care unit (ICU). However, current ICU practice primarily relies on invasive arterial catheterization. While this is the clinical gold standard for continuous measurement, it carries risks such as infection and thrombosis and is typically limited to select critical care settings.To reduce reliance on invasive arterial lines, we developed an interpretable estimation framework for systolic blood pressure (SBP), mean arterial pressure (MAP), and diastolic blood pressure (DBP) from single-sensor photoplethysmography (PPG).Synchronized PPG and arterial line 10-minute recordings from 100 patients in the ICU were analyzed. Using a hybrid feature selection strategy (RReliefF and intrinsic model-specific rankings), we reduced 201 initial features to an optimized subset of 30 core features. Model development and evaluation were designed to minimize information leakage and overfitting, incorporating nested cross-validation and patient-wise testing to assess generalizability across heterogeneous ICU populations. We developed and validated predictive models using machine learning techniques, specifically XGBoost (XGB), random forest, and support vector regression, with XGB serving as our primary model.Among the evaluated models, the Hybrid Top 30 XGB configuration provided the best balance between estimation performance, model compactness, and computational efficiency. The model achieved mean absolute errors of 8.61 mm Hg (SBP), 3.50 mm Hg (MAP), and 2.62 mm Hg (DBP). For MAP and DBP, mean difference (SD) values of -0.09 (4.54) mm Hg and -1.07 (3.51) mm Hg, respectively, satisfied the Association for the Advancement of Medical Instrumentation numerical criteria, while performance corresponded to Grade A according to the British Hypertension Society grading criteria. Although SBP exhibited greater variability, estimation performance was largely preserved using a physiologically informed subset of 30 features (approximately 15% of the original feature set). Feature importance analysis revealed distinct physiological feature patterns across SBP, MAP, and DBP estimation.Interpretability analysis identified key predictors associated with wave reflection, systolic timing, low-frequency vasomotor activity, and autonomic regulation. By explicitly linking predictive features to underlying cardiovascular physiology, the proposed framework addresses a key limitation of existing black-box cuffless BP models. Ultimately, this study demonstrates that an optimized XGB framework using physiologically informed PPG features can provide accurate and computationally efficient BP estimation in ICU settings and may support the assessment of clinically relevant hemodynamic states using a single-sensor PPG platform. title: Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonist use and overall survival in endometrial cancer: a multicenter propensity score-matched cohort study.
abstract: To evaluate the association between glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonist (GLP-1RA) use and overall survival in women with endometrial cancer.Using the TriNetX network, we identified women aged 18-75 years with endometrial cancer diagnosed between 2018 and 2024 and propensity score matched those with a GLP-1RA record within 12 months before diagnosis to women without prior use, with follow-up anchored to the date of diagnosis. A 2-year landmark analysis compared new GLP-1RA use within 2 years of diagnosis with no use among women alive at 2 years without evidence of advanced disease, and sensitivity analyses included an active comparator, race-stratified analyses and a negative-control outcome. The outcome was 5-year all-cause mortality.In the primary analysis (2646 matched pairs), 5-year survival was 91.6% among GLP-1RA users and 90.2% among non-users (hazard ratio [HR] 0.81; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.65-1.02), and in the 2-year landmark analysis (2275 pairs) it was 96.4% and 96.3% (HR 0.92; 95% CI, 0.63-1.34). Results were similar against dipeptidyl peptidase-4 inhibitors (HR 0.91; 95% CI, 0.45-1.84) and by race (interaction P = 0.46), whereas a comparison with women who never received a GLP-1RA, as in previous studies, yielded an HR of 0.58 (95% CI, 0.48-0.70).Once follow-up was anchored to the date of diagnosis, GLP-1RA use was not associated with significantly lower all-cause mortality in women with endometrial cancer, and these hypothesis-generating findings should temper the extrapolation of survival associations reported in other cancers until prospective trials are completed.Copyright © 2026 Elsevier Inc. title: Neoadjuvant talazoparib, irinotecan, and standard chemotherapy for early breast cancer in the I-SPY2 trial.
abstract: Preclinical evidence suggests synergy between poly-ADP-ribose inhibitors and camptothecin chemotherapy. We tested the talazoparib and irinotecan combination (TI) in the neoadjuvant setting in the I-SPY2 trial in patients with HER2-negative locally advanced breast cancer.I-SPY2 is a phase II platform trial for stage 2/3 early breast cancer at high risk of recurrence. Participants were adaptively randomized to one of several experimental neoadjuvant therapies or control based on receptor subtypes defined by hormone receptor (HR), HER2 status, and MammaPrint risk (MP1, MP2). The primary endpoint was pathological complete response (pCR). Treatments 'graduate' if/when they achieve an 85% Bayesian probability of success in a subtype-specific phase III trial. Only HER2-negative patients were eligible for randomization to the TI arm. All patients received weekly paclitaxel for 12 weeks, followed by doxorubicin/cyclophosphamide and surgery. Participants randomized to the TI arm received daily oral talazoparib and irinotecan infusions every other week. Pathway-specific biomarkers were assessed for response prediction.The combination of talazoparib and irinotecan failed to graduate from the I-SPY2 trial, with a 19% modeled posterior probability of pCR in the TI arm compared with 20% in the control arm among all patients with HER2-negative breast cancer. The most common adverse events were neutropenia and anemia in the TI arm and neuropathy and fatigue in the control arm. pCR rates were highest in patients with germline Breast Cancer Gene 1 or 2 (BRCA1/2) mutations receiving TI (pCR rate 50%) and in those with tumors expressing a DNA repair deficiency signature.TI will not be further explored as a combination given lack of improved efficacy over control (paclitaxel) for neoadjuvant treatment in patients with HER2-negative breast cancer. pCR rates were highest (50%) among patients with germline BRCA1/2 mutations, likely due to the efficacy of talazoparib alone. Further combinations could be explored in patients with HER2-negative breast cancer and a germline BRCA1/2 or PALB2 mutation.Copyright © 2026 The Authors. Published by Elsevier Ltd.. title: Mitral Annular Calcification - Association with Comorbidities and Left Ventricular Mechanics.
abstract: Mitral annular calcification (MAC) is common in the general population, more pronounced in women and patients with left ventricular (LV) pressure overload conditions, which may increase stress on the mitral valve inducing and exacerbating the calcification process. The pathogenesis of MAC is presumed multifactorial but remains poorly understood. Women display a different LV response to pressure overload compared to men, but this association has rather not been thoroughly investigated.The DANCAVAS (Danish Cardiovascular Screening) pilot study included randomly selected individuals from the general population aged 60-75 years to undergo a computed tomography (CT)-based screening program. MAC was graded by mitral valve calcification (MVC) score assessed by CT and compared to echocardiographic data. Among 463 participants, MAC was found in 165 (35.6%) with MVC scores ≤100 AU in 20.7%, 100-400 AU in 8.2% and >400 AU in 6.7%. While MAC was most prevalent in men, women presented with higher MVC scores and severe MAC on echocardiography. Patients with MAC were elderly with cardiovascular risk factors. Concentric LV geometry with smaller LV cavities and higher relative wall thickness were highly associated with MAC (p<0.001). From multivariable analyses, relative wall thickness and the mechanical load on the mitral valve (i.e. StressMV) strongly associated with MAC (SD-adjusted OR 28.8, 95% CI [15.6;53.5] and 2.97 [2.25;3.91], respectively) and MAC severity (10.9 [7.74;15.5] and 2.98 [2.33;3.82], respectively). The predictive performance was high with AUC of 0.78 [0.74;0.82] by including StressMV in the model of age, sex and cardiovascular comorbidity (p<0.001). However, relative wall thickness had distinctive importance (AUC 0.96 [0.94;0.98], p<0.001) regardless of sex.MAC is common in the general population with the highest prevalence among men. LV geometry and the pressure on the mitral valve are crucial factors in the pathogenesis of MAC, and sex-specific differences in LV response to pressure overload may elucidate why more extensive grades of MAC mainly affect women.Copyright © 2026. llm_summary: Researchers examined whether heart structure and pressure on the mitral valve (a heart valve) were linked to calcium buildup in the mitral annulus (the ring of tissue surrounding the valve) in 463 middle-aged and older adults. They found that thicker heart walls and increased mechanical stress on the valve were strongly associated with this calcium buildup, which was more severe in women despite being more common in men. These findings suggest that how the heart responds to pressure overload may explain sex differences in this condition, though this is an observational study and does not prove cause and effect.
llm_summary_expert: The DANCAVAS pilot study examined 463 randomly selected individuals aged 60-75 years from the general population using computed tomography to grade mitral annular calcification (MAC) by mitral valve calcification score and compare findings to echocardiographic data. MAC was present in 165 participants (35.6%), with higher mitral valve calcification scores observed in women despite greater prevalence in men, and concentric left ventricular geometry with increased relative wall thickness strongly associated with MAC presence (p<0.001). In multivariable analyses, relative wall thickness and mechanical load on the mitral valve (StressMV) were independently associated with MAC and MAC severity, with relative wall thickness demonstrating distinctive predictive importance across both sexes (area under the curve 0.96). The addition of StressMV to a model including age, sex, and cardiovascular comorbidity improved predictive performance to an area under the curve of 0.78 for MAC detection. These findings suggest that left ventricular geometry and pressure on the mitral valve are crucial factors in MAC pathogenesis, with sex-specific differences in left ventricular response to pressure.

title: Types of self-expandable metal stents for palliative drainage of unresectable extrahepatic malignant biliary obstruction: a network meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials.
abstract: The optimal self-expandable metal stent (SEMS) for endoscopic drainage of unresectable extrahepatic malignant biliary obstruction (MBO) with endoscopic retrograde cholangiopancreatography (ERCP) remains unclear due to limited randomized controlled trial (RCT) evidence. Prior meta-analyses have relied on observational data, introducing heterogeneity and bias. To overcome these limitations, an RCT-only network meta-analysis was performed to evaluate the efficacy and safety of SEMS types.A literature search was conducted to identify RCTs assessing fully covered SEMS (FCSEMS), partially covered SEMS (PCSEMS), and/or uncovered SEMS (UCSEMS) for ERCP drainage of unresectable extrahepatic MBO. Study outcomes included recurrent biliary obstruction (RBO), specific causes of RBO, overall survival, and adverse events. A frequentist network meta-analysis was performed to estimate hazard ratios (HRs) and incidence rate ratios (IRRs) with their 95%CIs and overall P-scores.10 RCTs (1659 patients) were included. There were no significant differences in time to RBO, incidence of any RBO, or overall survival between stent types. UCSEMS had the lowest rates of stent migration, tumor overgrowth, and sludge occlusion, whereas FCSEMS most effectively prevented tumor ingrowth. Adverse event rates were similar across groups; however, FCSEMS, but not PCSEMS, had significantly higher rates of acute cholecystitis than UCSEMS in patients with an intact gallbladder.There were no differences in RBO, overall survival, or adverse events excluding acute cholecystitis between SEMS types, although each type has its advantages and disadvantages. FCSEMS was associated with a higher risk of acute cholecystitis, emphasizing the need for careful patient selection, particularly regarding gallbladder status.Thieme. All rights reserved.

title: Contextualizing web-based decision support for endocrine therapy for breast cancer risk reduction: Usability and context insights in a cluster randomized trial.
abstract: Despite the benefit of endocrine therapy (ET) for breast cancer risk reduction among high-risk women, uptake remains low. In the MiCHOICE trial, we evaluated the effectiveness of a patient decision support tool, RealRisks, compared to standard educational materials in improving informed choice among women with high-risk breast lesions. We found no significant difference in informed choice, but about half initiated ET. To better understand these outcomes, we conducted a qualitative study to explore factors influencing the effectiveness of this tool. We conducted interviews among patients and clinicians assigned to the intervention arm. Interviews were analyzed using the Technology Acceptance Model (TAM). Among 15 enrolled clinicians, 87% were female and 73% were breast surgeons or oncologists. Among 23 enrolled patients, median age was 49.7 years and 70% completed RealRisks. Patients and clinicians found RealRisks' multimodal presentation of risk to be useful, priming patients for the clinic visit and facilitating more productive conversations regarding ET. However, ease of use was limited by technological barriers and navigation challenges. Patients indicated that RealRisks reinforced clinic conversations rather than changing decisions. Despite positive patient and clinician attitudes toward RealRisks, targeted refinements to the decision aid are needed to translate perceived usefulness into measurable improvements in informed choice. The effectiveness of decision aids may depend not only on their content, but on timing and clinical context. Further studies should evaluate these tools among high-risk women identified in screening mammography or primary care, where impact may be greater.

title: Diagnostic Performance of Biochemical Parameters to Diagnose Endogenous Hyperinsulinemic Hypoglycaemia.
abstract: The gold standard for diagnosing endogenous hyperinsulinemic hypoglycaemia (EHH) is the fasting test. The respective diagnostic value of insulin, C-peptide, proinsulin and beta-hydroxybutyrate levels in relation to glucose levels at the end of the fasting test remains ill-defined. We, therefore, aimed to explore the relevance of these parameters based on a literature review and individual data provided by different authors.Extensive literature research was conducted in the databases Embase and Medline to identify case reports and original studies that report data on the fasting test e.g. fasting duration, blood glucose and insulin levels at the end of the fast, as well as C-peptide, proinsulin and beta-hydroxybutyrate levels, where available. Histology after surgery was defined as the diagnostic gold standard for patients with positive fasting tests.Data on fasting tests of 522 individual patients and 36 individual controls were identified. Sensitivity and specificity of the fasting test were 75.7% [95%CI 71.8-79.2] and 94.4% [95%CI 81.9-98.5], respectively, in our cohort. Whereas blood glucose, insulin and C-peptide are measured and reported in most cases, proinsulin and beta-hydroxybutyrate were reported in only 51% and 50%, respectively. In relation to blood glucose levels, C-peptide concentrations reached higher diagnostic accuracy (AUC 0.97) than insulin (AUC 0.93). Meanwhile, proinsulin and beta-hydroxybutyrate had an even higher diagnostic accuracy (both AUC = 0.99).In our dataset, combined glucose and C-peptide showed a strong discriminatory performance for EHH. However, proinsulin and beta-hydroxybutyrate show the highest diagnostic accuracy for diagnosing EHH yet are not measured on a regular basis.© The Author(s) 2026. title: Ventricular Morphology and Atrioventricular Valve Regurgitation in Adults Post-Fontan: Associations With Exercise Hemodynamics.
abstract: Right ventricular (RV) dominance and atrioventricular valve regurgitation (AVVR) are associated with adverse outcomes post-Fontan palliation, but their underlying hemodynamic correlates, particularly during exercise, remain incompletely characterized.In this cross-sectional cohort, exercise hemodynamics by ventricular morphology and AVVR severity were assessed invasively (supine exercise catheterization) in 108 individuals and semi-invasively (semisupine exercise with echocardiography and peripheral venous pressure) in 108.Age of the invasive cohort was 32.1 (25.6-37.2) years; 41 had RV dominance, 19 had moderate or severe AVVR, and 16 had both. Resting and peak mean pulmonary artery pressure and pulmonary artery wedge pressure were similar across ventricular morphologies and AVVR severity. However, RV dominance was associated with lower systemic (systemic blood flow, 67% [22-93] versus 86% [63-105] predicted; P=0.006) and pulmonary (pulmonary blood flow, 57% [33-75] versus 72% [61-89] predicted; P<0.001) cardiac output responses to exercise and steeper Δpulmonary artery pressure/Δpulmonary blood flow, (4.3 [2.6-10.6] versus 3.0 [1.7-4.8] mm Hg/L per minute; P=0.004). Patients with moderate or severe AVVR showed a similar pattern, with lower systemic blood flow (64% [19-92] versus 77% [57-101], P=0.10) and pulmonary blood flow (57% [36-74] versus 70% [55-88] predicted, P=0.03) responses. Findings were replicated in the semi-invasive cohort, where RV dominance and moderate or severe AVVR were associated with lower peak systemic blood flow and higher Δperipheral venous pressure/Δ systemic blood flow, despite similar peak peripheral venous pressure.Resting and exertional pulmonary artery wedge pressure, pulmonary artery pressure, and peripheral venous pressure are unrelated to ventricular morphology and AVVR severity. Conversely, impaired flow augmentation and steeper pressure-flow relationships during exercise were associated with RV dominance and moderate or severe AVVR, emphasizing the role of dynamic provocation to unmask occult cardiovascular reserve limitations.

title: Infective endocarditis after heart transplantation: clinical characteristics and outcomes.
abstract: Recipients of heart transplantation (HT) require prolonged immunosuppressive therapy and frequent healthcare interventions, increasing infection risk. However, the epidemiology of infective endocarditis (IE) after HT is limited.To describe the prevalence, clinical characteristics and outcomes of IE among HT recipients seen at our institution.We retrospectively identified adults with possible or definite IE after HT at Mayo Clinic from 2010 through 2024 using the 2023 Duke-International Society of Cardiovascular Infectious Diseases criteria.This brief report presents three (0.2%) cases of possible/definite IE among 1674 HT recipients who underwent transplantation at our institution between 2010 and 2024, with an additional patient referred with IE after HT elsewhere. One case developed two months post-HT with a Candida albicans sternal wound infection, one resulted from previously unrecognised pre-HT Q fever, and two were late cases associated with bloodstream infections. The median interval from HT to IE diagnosis was 17.5 months. The tricuspid valve was involved in three patients with pre-existing post-transplant valvulopathy. One patient underwent valve replacement, while two received minimally invasive repairs. No deaths or IE relapse occurred at one-year follow-up.IE in HT recipients is exceedingly rare. Tricuspid valve involvement and need for surgical intervention may be underrecognized.

title: The hippocampus as a latent diffusion engine for memory, perception and cognitive dysfunction.
abstract: The hippocampus is a central cognitive hub whose dysfunction contributes to most neurodegenerative dementias. Despite extensive knowledge of its anatomy, physiology and circuitry, a unifying account that links hippocampal dynamics to cognition and clinical syndromes remains lacking. Drawing on systems neuroscience and recent advances in generative artificial intelligence, we conceptualize the hippocampus as a latent diffusion engine that compresses sensory, interoceptive and cognitive inputs into low-dimensional representations and regenerates percepts, episodic memories and imagined scenes for cortical integration. Travelling waves of cortico-hippocampal oscillations, aligned with large-scale functional gradients, schedule and structure this generative process and organize distributed neural activity into coherent, semantically grounded constructs. We formalize this proposal as stochastic latent oscillatory diffusion (SLOD), a biologically grounded framework that maps hippocampal-cortical computations onto specific anatomical substrates and dynamical processes. While we do not suggest that the hippocampus implements diffusion algorithms per se, we show that its computations can be decomposed into homologous operations including compression, stochastic exploration, conditioning and reconstruction, whose formal structure closely parallels that of latent diffusion models. Finally, we demonstrate how major neurodegenerative dementias, including the Alzheimer's disease spectrum, dementia with Lewy bodies and frontotemporal dementia, can be understood as selective breakdowns of distinct components of this generative architecture.© The Author(s) 2026. title: From Priority Questions to Registry-Nested Trials: An AJRR-C Road Map for Advancing Arthroplasty Research.
abstract: The American Joint Replacement Research-Collaborative (AJRR-C) is a National Institutes of Health-funded P30 Core Center for Clinical Research and seeks to accelerate practice-changing arthroplasty research by leveraging the American Joint Replacement Registry (AJRR) and shared multicenter research infrastructure. The AJRR-C convened 2 complementary meetings to establish a scalable coordinated pathway from the identification of high-priority clinical questions to the initiation of prospective studies.In July 2025, leaders from The Hip Society, The Knee Society, the American Association of Hip and Knee Surgeons, the AJRR, the Orthopaedic Research and Education Foundation, and the broader research community identified and prioritized clinical research questions regarding infection, perioperative management, new technologies, surgical techniques, implants, and quality. In April 2026, orthopaedic surgeons, methodologists, and artificial intelligence experts reconvened to evaluate contemporary approaches for addressing these priorities.A central theme of the meetings was the importance of utilizing a fit-for-purpose approach in which study design is tailored to the clinical question, available data, and potential sources of bias. Clinical questions with clear equipoise and feasible interventions may warrant randomization, whereas questions involving rare outcomes, rapidly evolving technologies, surgeon preferences, or long-term surveillance may be better addressed with observational studies. Participants emphasized the need for a robust, sustainable network for arthroplasty clinical trials that provides the shared infrastructure necessary for coordinated site engagement, standardized data definitions, reliable longitudinal follow-up, and AJRR linkage across multicenter trials. Two new AJRR-nested randomized trials arose from the priority-topics meeting, and their development demonstrates the potential of the AJRR-C consensus model to translate research priorities into practice-changing evidence generation.The AJRR-C established a coordinated pathway from the prioritization of research to the implementation of multicenter studies to address high-priority arthroplasty research questions. title: Improving Documentation Quality in Oncology: Impact of a Standardized Oncology-Specific Note Template With an Embedded Structured Data Capture Form.
abstract: Oncology provider notes are often lengthy, inconsistent, and incomplete, limiting clinical utility and contributing to cognitive burden. Standardized templates may improve note quality while enabling downstream real-world data use. This study evaluates the impact of a standardized, oncology-specific electronic health record (EHR) note template on documentation completeness in outpatient oncology clinics.In March 2019, a template with an embedded structured data capture form was implemented to facilitate point-of-care capture of key disease- and treatment-related data elements. Data elements aligned with ASCO's Quality Oncology Practice Initiative and Minimal Common Oncology Data Elements standards. Notes were evaluated for the presence of eight predefined quality metrics (QMs) and compared based on template usage, provider template adoption patterns (regular users v nonusers), and time period.We reviewed 2,366 encounter notes written by 41 providers between 2018 and 2022; 917 (38.8%) used the template. Female sex, fewer years since graduation, and disease-specific clinic settings were associated with higher odds of adoption. Template use was associated with significantly greater documentation completeness across nearly all QMs. Overall completeness improved from 62.3% to 89.9% (P < .001, Cohen d = 1.14). Cancer stage documentation increased from 62.4% to 97.8%, treatment phase from 26.2% to 92.4%, treatment intent from 40.8% to 94.8%, and performance status from 62.3% to 90.1% (all P < .001). Within-provider analyses confirmed sustained improvements for regular users; nonusers showed minimal change.A standardized oncology-specific note template with embedded structured data capture significantly improved documentation completeness of clinically meaningful QMs in outpatient oncology clinics. Gains persisted over time and across providers, underscoring the potential of template-based documentation to enhance communication, reduce variability, and improve data quality.

title: Automating the Pediatric Index of Mortality 3 in the Electronic Health Record: Automated Risk Scoring Using Structured Clinical Documentation.
abstract: Background The Pediatric Index of Mortality 3 (PIM3) is a validated severity-of-illness score widely used for risk adjustment, benchmarking, quality improvement initiatives, and research in pediatric intensive care units (PICUs). Its use in electronic workflows is limited by required variables that rely on clinical judgement and are traditionally abstracted manually from narrative documentation. Objectives To design, implement, and evaluate an automated PIM3 calculation within the electronic health record (EHR) using structured clinical documentation to capture non-discrete variables, and to assess clinician adoption, documentation accuracy, and concordance with manual abstraction. Methods A structured documentation template with standardized response options was developed to capture non-discrete PIM3 variables, including ventilation status, elective admission status, procedural recovery, and diagnosis category. These clinician-entered data were mapped to discrete structured data elements and combined with physiologic and laboratory inputs for automated score calculation. Documentation completion and accuracy were evaluated over a 12-month period. Automated scores were validated against manually abstracted gold standard PIM3 scores in a convenience sample of 20 targeted encounters. Results Among 923 PICU encounters, clinician compliance with structured PIM3 documentation was 95% (n=877). Of the completed entries, 84% (n=773) contained no documentation errors. Identified errors were primarily related to binary clinical judgements rather than diagnostic clarification. Of the 20 encounter validation sample, automated PIM3 scores and associated probabilities of death demonstrated near-complete concordance with manually calculated gold standard values, with no clinically meaningful discrepancies. Conclusion Automated PIM3 calculation using structured clinical documentation within the EHR is feasible and reliable for supporting standardized data capture and timely availability of risk-adjustment information. This approach reduces reliance on manual abstraction and provides a scalable informatics framework for quality improvement, benchmarking, and research in pediatric critical care.Thieme. title: The Completeness of Surgery Index (CoSI) in Chronic Rhinosinusitis with Nasal Polyps: A Multi-Institutional Study.
abstract: The Completion of Surgery Index (CoSI) is a CT-based scoring system designed to identify patients with chronic rhinosinusitis with nasal polyps (CRSwNP) who have had previously incomplete endoscopic sinus surgery (ESS). Single-institution studies have shown that a CoSI <70, reflecting incomplete prior surgery, is associated with greater improvement in sino-nasal outcome test (SNOT-22) and asthma control following high-quality revision surgery.To validate CoSI in a large multi-institutional CRSwNP cohort.We retrospectively analyzed CRSwNP patients who underwent revision ESS across eight tertiary care centers from 2022 to 2024. Demographic, clinical, and treatment-related data were collected, including preoperative CoSI scores, timing of treatment, and pre- and postoperative SNOT-22 scores.160 subjects undergoing revision ESS for CRSwNP were included. Patients with incomplete prior surgery (CoSI <70) experienced significantly greater postoperative improvement in SNOT-22 scores (6-24 months) than patients with CoSI ≥70 (35.2 ± 17.8 vs 18.7 ± 18.6 points; p<0.001). This association remained significant after adjustment for demographic factors, aspirin-exacerbated respiratory disease status, asthma, number of prior ESS, biologic use, and baseline SNOT-22 score. Nonlinear and threshold analyses were consistent with a clinically relevant transition near the CoSI 70 threshold.Preoperative CoSI is an independent predictor of symptomatic improvement after revision ESS in CRSwNP. A CoSI <70 identifies patients who are most likely to benefit from complete revision surgery. title: Isolated Tibial and Both Component Revision Total Knee Arthroplasty for Loosening Have Similar 10-Year Outcomes.
abstract: Isolated tibial revisions are relatively uncommon, and data comparing them to both component revision total knee arthroplasty (TKA) is limited. The purpose of this study was to review implant survivorship, radiographic, and clinical outcomes after isolated tibial revision and compare to a matched cohort of both component revision TKAs.We identified 112 cases of isolated tibial revision TKAs at a single tertiary care academic center from 2000 to 2022. All were performed for tibial component aseptic loosening. Metaphyseal fixation was utilized in 53%. There were 74 cases that were propensity-score-matched 1:1 to 74 both-component revision TKAs based on surgical indication, age, sex, surgical year, and American Society of Anesthesiologists Physical Status (ASA) Classification. The patient's mean age was 66 years, 63% were women, and their mean body mass index was 35. The mean follow-up was seven years (range, 2 to 20).After isolated tibial revision, the 10-year survivorship free from re-revision of the tibial component for aseptic loosening, re-revision for instability, and any re-revision was 84, 96, and 82%, respectively. The most common indications for re-revision were infection (n = 6), aseptic loosening of both the femur and tibia (n = 2), aseptic loosening of the tibial component only (n = 2), and instability (n = 2). There were two of the four tibial components re-revised that had metaphyseal fixation. The 10-year survivorship free from any reoperation was 75%. In the matched cohort analysis, there were no differences in 10-year survivorship free from re-revision of the tibial component for aseptic loosening (P = 0.31), any re-revision (P = 0.32), or any reoperation (P = 0.32). The mean Knee Society Score improved from 52 to 65 at the most recent follow-up (P = 0.71).Isolated tibial revision for aseptic loosening demonstrated modest 10-year survivorship from any re-revision of 82%. title: Abdominal reirradiation: practice principles from Reirradiation Collaborative Group (ReCOG).
abstract: Abdominal reirradiation (reRT) is an increasingly common treatment consideration as people live longer due to advances in cancer care. How we deliver courses of reRT still remains individualised and limited prospective data exists to support practice. This Reirradiation Collaborative Group (ReCOG) effort describes principles of practice and insights into clinical approaches for abdominal reRT.Six cases demonstrate challenges inherent to abdominal reRT scenarios, including urgent palliation, partial high dose overlap with prior treatment, and when reRT may not be offered. Cases and relevant literature were discussed by an expert panel to offer a structured approach to treatment decision-making and provide guidance for clinical practice.The cases demonstrate scenarios in which abdominal reRT can be an effective treatment and the uncertainties that may arise, requiring individualized treatment. The safety of proposed reRT should be balanced against the probability of side effects from therapy versus sequelae from uncontrolled tumour. This risk-to-benefit ratio can vary considerably depending on the intention of treatment and goals of care which impact decision making.This case-based overview offers practical suggestions from an expert panel on how best to approach challenging cases, while we await a more standardised framework for abdominal reRT.Copyright © 2026 The Author(s). title: High Natural Variation of BvCR4 Homologs in Sea Beet Contrasts with the Narrow Genetic Base of Sugar Beet: Implications for Cercospora Leaf Spot Resistance.
abstract: Cercospora leaf spot (CLS) is a destructive disease of sugar beet (Beta vulgaris subsp. vulgaris L.) for which resistance conferred by the gene BvCR4 has been introgressed from sea beet (Beta vulgaris subsp. maritima). BvCR4-mediated resistance has been broadly deployed to manage CLS globally in sugar beet; however, continuous implementation exerts strong selection pressure, increasing the risk of disease outbreaks owing to resistance-breaking Cercospora beticola populations. This study aimed to identify BvCR4 variants in public B. vulgaris spp. germplasm to assess their genetic and structural diversity. PCR screening of 589 public B. vulgaris spp. germplasms detected BvCR4 homologs in 32 accessions with diverse responses to CLS, including historically relevant sugar beet lines represented in breeding programs and Mediterranean sea beet populations of diverse genetic backgrounds. Analysis of the genomic sequences revealed higher diversity in sea beet compared with sugar beet. Additionally, population genetic analysis indicated that BvCR4 homologs in sugar beet likely originated from sea beet populations in Italy and Greece. We identified historical cultivated materials carrying full proteins encoded by BvCR4 alleles and delineated geographic regions where sea beet populations harbor BvCR4 homologs that may be useful in breeding programs. Structural variation was largely circumscribed within leucine-rich repeat domains, although CLS resistance phenotyping was not associated with specific polymorphisms, suggesting BvCR4-mediated resistance may rely on interactions with other coreceptors. This study provides resources for sugar beet improvement by enabling the identification of BvCR4 homologs in diverse germplasm and disclosing materials with potentially novel resistance.
