title: A cross-sectional survey investigating norms and opinions concerning unvaccinated and vaccinated individuals (INOCU-VAX).
abstract: Vaccine hesitancy remains a major public health concern, yet limited attention has been given to how individuals judge vaccine refusal versus acceptance. Clarifying how people judge the vaccination decisions of others may help identify the social norms that shape vaccination attitudes. We conducted a cross-sectional survey of 2,115 adult patients within a large integrated US healthcare system from January 29 to February 19, 2025. Respondents rated their agreement with two statements regarding adult and parental vaccine refusal using a 5-point Likert scale. Responses were categorized as disagree/strongly disagree, neutral and agree/strongly agree for analysis. Additional measures included agreement with additional vaccine-related attitude items and demographic characteristics. Most respondents agreed or strongly agreed that people who refuse recommended vaccines for themselves or their children are making a bad decision, while very few agreed or strongly agreed that accepting recommended vaccines is a bad decision. Refusal-disapproving respondents were more likely to endorse vaccine benefits, support physician encouragement of vaccination, and report receiving recommended vaccines. They were also more likely to be older and report higher educational attainment, income, and liberal political views. Most respondents (even those who were refusal-approving) agreed that vaccines are beneficial. Although respondents differed markedly in how they judged vaccine refusal, most viewed vaccine acceptance positively. Normative disagreement appears to center on refusal rather than vaccination itself. title: Immunosuppressive monocytes promote infection in patients with alcohol-associated hepatitis.
abstract: Broad immune cell dysfunction known as immune paralysis is a hallmark of severe alcohol-associated hepatitis (AH). This process may drive susceptibility to infection and contribute to high short-term mortality in these patients. However, the mechanisms of immune paralysis are incompletely understood. The aim of this study was to elucidate the role of myeloid cells in immune dysfunction in severe AH to identify potential biomarkers of infection risk and therapeutic targets.We analyzed the peripheral immune compartment of AH patients, heavy drinkers, and healthy controls and discovered that AH patients at risk for infection had an expanded peripheral monocyte population that was CXCR5+CCR4+ (C-X-C chemokine receptor type 5, C-C chemokine receptor type 4) and had lower activity of pro-inflammatory pathways (eg, Tumor Necrosis Factor alpha, TNF-α, and Interleukin-1 beta, IL-1β) compared with controls. The frequency of circulating CXCR5+CCR4+ monocytes in AH patients negatively correlated with 12-month transplant-free survival. Ex vivo CXCR5+ AH monocytes had reduced phagocytic activity, and they suppressed T-cell proliferation compared with CXCR5- and healthy control monocytes. CXCR5+ AH monocytes expressed PD-L1 (Programmed Death Ligand 1), which is a costimulatory molecule known to inhibit T-cell activation, and TMEM176B (Tolerance-Related and Induced, TORID-1), which is an intracellular cation channel that regulates calcium flux. Inhibition of TORID-1 promoted human monocyte phagocytosis and IL-1β release.CXCR5+CCR4+ monocytes arise in patients with severe AH and have impaired phagocytosis, reduced pro-inflammatory cytokine production, and suppress T-cell proliferation. These cells may promote susceptibility to bacterial infection and predict outcomes in severe AH. title: Mortality due to sepsis is increasing among patients with cirrhosis compared with other chronic diseases: US trends, 1999-2024.
abstract: Sepsis is a major contributor to death across chronic diseases, but population-level trends in sepsis-associated mortality among decedents with cirrhosis relative to other chronic conditions remain incompletely characterized. We evaluated US national trends in sepsis-associated mortality among decedents with cirrhosis, congestive heart failure (CHF), and chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD).We analyzed the CDC WONDER Multiple Cause-of-Death database (1999-2024) to identify decedents with cirrhosis, CHF, or COPD, and sepsis as a contributing cause of death. Age-adjusted sepsis-related mortality rates per 100,000 US population were calculated, and Joinpoint regression estimated average annual percent change (AAPC). Prespecified analyses evaluated trends by age, sex, race, liver disease etiology, and infection source.Results:Sepsis-related mortality increased most rapidly in decedents with cirrhosis, with an AAPC more than 4-fold higher than CHF [AAPC 3.29% (95% CI 2.96-3.54) vs. 0.78% (95% CI 0.34-1.21)], while COPD showed no significant increase [AAPC -0.12% (95% CI -0.62 to 0.23)]. Among decedents with cirrhosis, mortality increased across demographics, particularly among American Indian/Alaska Native individuals, White individuals, females, and adults aged ≥65 years. Source-specific increases in cirrhosis were greatest for genitourinary infections, followed by pneumonia and intra-abdominal infections. By cirrhosis etiology, the steepest increases occurred in MASLD [AAPC 11.36% (95% CI 9.46-13.30)], followed by alcohol-associated liver disease [AAPC 5.04% (95% CI 4.45-5.61)].At the population level, average age-adjusted sepsis-related mortality increased substantially faster in decedents with cirrhosis than in CHF and COPD, with the greatest increases observed in decedents with MASLD and alcohol-associated liver disease. title: Longitudinal changes in a blood-based prognostic liver secretome signature and long-term hepatocellular carcinoma risk in cirrhosis.
abstract: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) risk in patients with cirrhosis can be predicted by cross-sectional assessment of biomarkers and/or clinical scores, including the Prognostic Liver Secretome signature (PLSec)-based PAaM score. However, HCC risk may change over time, potentially limiting the accuracy of cross-sectional risk prediction. We aimed to evaluate whether longitudinal changes in HCC risk biomarkers/scores improve upon one-time risk assessment.In this nested case-control study within the multi-center prospective National Cancer Institute HCC Early Detection Strategy (HEDS) cohort of patients with cirrhosis, we evaluated longitudinal changes in PLSec over 1 or 2 years. Paired baseline and follow-up serum samples were available for 31 cases and 93 controls for 1-year changes, and for 25 cases and 75 controls for 2-year changes. Cross-sectional PLSec scores were higher in cases than in controls at baseline, Year 1, and Year 2 (p<0.05). title: Gammaherpesvirus infection of myeloid cells reveals divergent outcomes regulated by host and viral factors.
abstract: The gammaherpesviruses establish a lifelong infection, with the cellular outcome of infection intimately regulated by cell type. Myeloid cells are an early infection target characterized by diverse outcomes. To investigate this, we use murine gammaherpesvirus 68 to demonstrate that macrophages are readily infectable, resulting in three divergent infection outcomes dictated by viral and host factors. Infection in vivo and in a cell culture model results in a high frequency of viable cells characterized by restricted viral transcription and unexpected transcription of the ORF75 locus, with rare cells initiating lytic replication. Restricted infection can be fully converted to productive lytic replication by pre-treatment with the host cytokine interleukin 4 (IL-4). Finally, infection with a high viral dose also results in productive infection, but it triggers increased cell death. These studies demonstrate stepwise regulation of virus infection and identify virus and host factors that dictate divergent outcomes in a single cell type.© 2026 The Author(s).

llm_summary: Researchers investigated how macrophages—immune cells that fight infection—respond when infected with gammaherpesvirus, a virus that causes lifelong infections in humans and animals. They found that macrophages can be infected in three different ways: most cells survive with limited viral activity, some cells develop full viral replication, and high viral doses trigger cell death, with a host immune signal called IL-4 able to switch cells from survival to productive infection. These results show that both viral and host factors work together to determine whether infected cells survive, produce more virus, or die.
llm_summary_expert: Researchers used murine gammaherpesvirus 68 to investigate how macrophages, a primary myeloid cell target, respond to gammaherpesvirus infection in both in vivo and cell culture models. Macrophage infection resulted in three distinct outcomes: a high-frequency state of viable cells with restricted viral transcription and unexpected ORF75 locus transcription, rare cells undergoing lytic replication, and productive infection triggered by either IL-4 pretreatment or high viral dose inoculation. Pretreatment with the host cytokine interleukin 4 converted restricted infection to productive lytic replication, demonstrating that host factors can fundamentally alter viral replication patterns. High viral dose infection produced lytic replication but concurrently increased cell death, indicating a dose-dependent relationship between viral burden and cytopathic effects. These findings demonstrate stepwise regulation of gammaherpesvirus infection in macrophages and identify both viral and host factors that dictate divergent infection outcomes within a single cell type.

title: Mediating and moderating effects of individual resilience between meaning in life and family resilience among Chinese family caregivers of cancer patients.
abstract: To investigate the mediating and moderating roles of individual resilience in the relationship between meaning in life (MIL) and family resilience among Chinese family caregivers of cancer patients (FCCPs).A descriptively cross-sectional study was conducted with Chinese FCCPs (n = 272) at a tertiary hospital in Anhui Province. Survey instruments included the Chinese version of Family Resilience Assessment Scale (FRAS), the Chinese version of Meaning in Life Questionnaire(MLQ) and the Chinese version of the Individual Resilience Scale - 14 (RS-14). The PROCESS macro using SPSS examined the mediating and moderating roles of individual resilience in the relationship between MIL and family resilience.The mean scores (M ± SD) of the FRAS, MLQ, RS-14 were 149.59 ± 13.57, 44.01 ± 8.52, and 72.40 ± 10.69, respectively. The MIL and individual resilience were each positively correlated with family resilience (r = 0.471-0.572, Ps < 0.01). Individual resilience played a partial mediating role in the relationship between MIL and family resilience, indirect effect of MIL on family resilience through individual resilience (β = 0.34, 95% CI = 0.22 ~ 0.50, P < 0.001). title: The 2026 American Heart Association/American Stroke Association Guideline Updates to Management of Patients with Acute Ischemic Stroke: A Guide for Radiologists.
abstract: The 2026 guideline for early management of acute ischemic stroke retains many foundational recommendations while introducing clinically meaningful updates spanning imaging, broader inpatient management, and reperfusion strategies including IV thrombolysis and endovascular thrombectomy. llm_summary: The 2026 American Heart Association guideline updates recommendations for treating acute ischemic stroke, which occurs when blood flow to the brain is blocked. The new guidelines maintain core treatment strategies while adding expanded guidance for medium-sized blood vessel blockages and including pediatric stroke recommendations that were largely missing from previous versions. These updates are intended to improve imaging workflows and clinical decision-making for radiologists managing acute stroke patients.
llm_summary_expert: The 2026 American Heart Association/American Stroke Association guideline update addresses the early management of acute ischemic stroke with recommendations spanning imaging protocols, inpatient management strategies, and reperfusion therapies including intravenous thrombolysis and endovascular thrombectomy. The guideline retains foundational recommendations from prior iterations while introducing clinically meaningful updates that impact radiologic workflows and clinical decision-making. Notable additions include expanded guidance for medium vessel occlusions, which represent an important subset of acute ischemic stroke cases previously lacking detailed recommendations. title: Aligning the Electronic Health Record With Age-Friendly Care in Hospitals: Qualitative Multisite Study.
abstract: The geriatric 4Ms framework conceptualizes 4 evidence-based elements (ie, Mobility, Mentation, Medication, and what Matters) that are important to high-quality care for older adults. Improving on these measures is central to the Age-Friendly Health Systems initiative. Electronic health records (EHRs) are critical to modern health systems including being able to review patient information and act on geriatric health concerns.This study aimed to examine how clinicians use a commercial EHR to access 4Ms-relevant information during inpatient and emergency care of older adults to inform the design of scalable, age-friendly 4Ms EHR tools.We interviewed clinicians and clinical staff (n=20), including physicians, advanced practice providers, nurses, pharmacists, and physical therapists from 5 large academic health systems across the United States regarding their experiences using the EHR during inpatient and emergency care for older adults. All included health systems used the same EHR and had geriatric quality programs in place. Participants completed virtual interviews that included narrated walkthroughs of their local EHR builds in response to 3 brief clinical vignettes focused on falls, home care needs, and delirium. Interviews were screen-recorded with audio and transcribed for coding and thematic analysis.Major themes spanned the 4Ms and consisted of (1) difficulty finding information about the 4Ms, (2) poor 4Ms data quality, (3) sparse EHR data sharing, (4) variable intrafacility practices, and (5) homegrown 4Ms EHR tools. Interviewees shared some examples of tools that had been implemented in their practice settings that increased access to 4Ms data, including documentation search workarounds, trackboards, and alerts.Among a sample of clinicians and clinical staff representing large academic medical centers, 4Ms data in the EHR were characterized by multilevel barriers related to access and accuracy. Alternatively, interviewees demonstrated innovative EHR-embedded tools to improve accessibility of some 4Ms-relevant data. title: Reproductive Outcomes in a Longitudinal Hazardous Medication Surveillance Program Among Healthcare Workers.
abstract: We evaluated a Hazardous Medication Surveillance Program (HMSP) with analysis of reproductive outcomes.The HMSP included a biennial questionnaire and a complete blood count. Invited healthcare personnel (HCP) were anticipated to handle hazardous medications ≥2 times/week, >26 weeks/year. Two consecutive surveillance cycles were compared using chi-square or Fisher exact testing. Reproductive outcomes were stratified by exposure time.Cycles 1 and 2 included 2625 and 2057 participants (mean age of 31 vs 34; 81.4% female). Among females aged 18-44, adverse reproductive outcomes were 9.5% and 10.5% with miscarriage reported in 4.4% of HCP in cycle 2. Outcomes increased with exposure (p≥0.009).An exposure-outcome gradient supports exposure and age stratification in HMSPs. These findings highlight the need for safety programs and effective exposure-control strategies to reduce occupational risk among HCP handling hazardous medications.Copyright © 2026 American College of Occupational and Environmental Medicine.

title: Allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplantation after CD19-directed CAR T-cell therapy in children and adults with B-cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia: a GoCART coalition study on behalf of the PDWP, ALWP, and CTIWP of the EBMT.
abstract: Hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (HSCT) can rescue B-cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia (B-ALL) recurring after CD19-directed chimeric antigen receptor T cells (CAR19 T cells). However, in patients at high risk of relapse, the indication for and timing of consolidative HSCT are controversial. We retrieved data on 112 patients who received an HSCT at a median of 6.1 months after CAR19 T-cell infusion. Indication for subsequent HSCT were: (I) Rescue in 72 (64%) patients for disease recurrence; (II) Pre-emptive in 21 (19%) for loss of B-cell aplasia; (III) Consolidative in 19 patients (17%). The 2-year post-transplant Leukemia-Free Survival (LFS) was 54% and the 2-year cumulative incidence of relapse was 32%. Children had better LFS than adults (63% vs 38%). Older age was associated with inferior LFS (HR per 10-year increase 1.30; p= 0.01) and patients receiving a rescue HSCT had a significantly lower 2-year LFS (41%), compared to pre-emptive (74%) and consolidative HSCT (78%), respectively (p=0.002). Haploidentical donor was also associated with inferior LFS (HR: 2.21 95%CI: 1.15-4.25, p=0.02). This "real-world" study corroborates the need to identify patients at higher risk of relapse and optimization of strategies to improve outcome in patients with R/R B-ALL receiving CD19-directed CAR T cells.

title: Incidence, Risk Factors and Natural History of Atrial Arrhythmias in Patients With Systemic Right Ventricle.
abstract: The incidence and risk factors for atrial arrhythmia (AA; atrial fibrillation and atrial flutter) in adults with systemic right ventricle (sRV), specifically congenitally corrected transposition of the great arteries and dextro-transposition of the great arteries palliated with atrial switch procedures, are not well understood. This study aims to better define these risks.Adults with sRV presenting to Mayo Clinic between 2000 and 2022 were identified. Their clinical characteristics, electrocardiographic, and echocardiographic parameters at the time of first presentation were recorded. The incidence of sustained AA (>30 seconds) during follow-up was documented. Cox regression analysis was used to identify associations of incident atrial fibrillation/atrial flutter and mortality during follow-up.Among 447 patients with sRV (median age, 33.1 [24.6-42.8], 55.9% male, 247 cm3-TGA; 200 dextro-transposition of the great arteries postatrial switch), AA was present at first visit in 113 (25.3%). Out of the remaining 334 patients, new-onset AA occurred in 125 (37.4%) patients during a median follow-up of 11.1 years (interquartile range, 3.6-19.3). Isolated atrial fibrillation was observed in 89 (37.4%), isolated atrial flutter in 76 (31.9%), and both atrial fibrillation and atrial flutter in 73 (30.7%) patients. In multivariable analysis, the risk factors for incident AA included age (hazard ratio, 1.04 [1.03-1.06]; P<0.001), d-TGA (hazard ratio, 1.96 [1.00-3.85]; P=0.05), and QRS duration (hazard ratio, 1.01 [1.00-1.02]; P=0.02). AA was associated with hospitalization for heart failure in 19% of patients. Among those treated with anti-arrhythmic drugs and ablation, recurrence occurred in over 50% of patients. AA was not an independent predictor of mortality.AA occurred in more than half of this cohort with sRV, with risk increasing significantly after the third decade of life. Advancing age, dextro-transposition of the great arteries, and prolonged QRS duration were associated with increased risk of AA. Close monitoring for AA and early interventions are warranted in all adults with sRV.

title: Intracranial aneurysm risk and cerebrovascular outcomes in thoracic versus abdominal aortic aneurysms: a national analysis of 114,805 hospitalizations.
abstract: Aneurysmal disease is increasingly recognized as a systemic vasculopathy, yet large-scale comparisons between thoracic (TAA) and abdominal aortic aneurysms (AAA) regarding intracranial aneurysm (ICa) burden and cerebrovascular outcomes remain limited. This study leverages a nationally representative database to compare the frequency of coded coexisting ICa, cerebrovascular events, and in-hospital outcomes between TAA and AAA, and to identify factors associated with coexisting ICa.A retrospective cohort study using the National Inpatient Sample (2000-2020) identified adult hospitalizations with TAA or AAA that included an aortic aneurysm repair; dissections and thoracoabdominal or unspecified-site aneurysms were excluded. Propensity score matching (1:1, nearest-neighbor, caliper 0.2 SD) adjusted for demographic and clinical differences, with covariate balance assessed by standardized mean differences. Primary outcomes included administratively coded coexisting ICa and cerebrovascular events (ischemic stroke, hemorrhagic stroke, coded subarachnoid hemorrhage [SAH]). Secondary outcomes included mortality, length of stay, charges, and discharge disposition. Multivariable logistic regression and exploratory random forest machine learning examined factors associated with coded ICa. Counts are unweighted NIS discharge records.Among 114,805 hospitalizations (2.3% TAA, 97.7% AAA), coded coexisting ICa was present in 168 (0.15%); its frequency was higher in TAA than in AAA before matching (1.0% vs. 0.1%, p < 0.001) but not after matching (1.0% vs. 0.7%; OR 1.45, 95% CI 0.79-2.65; p = 0.23). The propensity-matched analysis (n = 5,330) demonstrated higher rates of ischemic stroke (5.5% vs. 3.9%, p = 0.007), hemorrhagic stroke (0.5% vs. ≤0.4%, p = 0.007), and coded SAH (0.8% vs. ≤0.4%, p = 0.003) in TAA; E-values indicated that these hemorrhagic associations were robust to residual confounding, whereas ischemic stroke and mortality differences were sensitive to residual imbalance in atrial fibrillation and repair modality. In multivariable analysis, TAA was independently associated with coded coexisting ICa (aOR 1.17, 95% CI 1.07-1.27). Female sex showed the strongest association (aOR 2.56), followed by smoking, hypertension, and dyslipidemia. TAA had higher mortality (4.9% vs. 3.0%), longer stays (9.83 vs. 6.21 days), greater non-home discharge (53.7% vs. 28.3%), and higher charges (all p < 0.001). Among all hospitalizations with an unruptured aortic or intracranial aneurysm diagnosis, the TAA share increased from approximately 11% to 35% between 2003 and 2020. Machine learning identified age as the most influential variable, with key interactions involving age × female sex and age × vascular comorbidities.TAA is associated with higher coded cerebrovascular event rates, worse in-hospital outcomes, and greater healthcare utilization than AAA. Because ICa in administrative data are identified through clinical recognition rather than systematic screening, these data should not be construed to mean that ICa are more prevalent among patients with TAA, although cerebrovascular events appear more frequent and more morbid in this population. Prospective imaging-based studies are needed before targeted intracranial screening can be recommended, particularly for younger women with TAA and vascular comorbidities.© 2026. title: Feasibility and Adherence of a Multicomponent Digital Health Monitoring Platform in Ambulatory Heart Failure: Multicenter Observational Study.
abstract: Digital health platforms combining wearable biosensors with smartphone apps offer scalable approaches to heart failure (HF) management, yet sustained patient engagement and initial technology adoption, particularly among older adults, remain uncertain.We conducted a prospective, multicenter observational study to explore the feasibility and adherence of using a digital health monitoring platform for 8 weeks in a population of ambulatory patients with HF.In this prospective multicenter observational study, patients with New York Heart Association (NYHA) class I to III HF were prescreened across 6 institutions in the United States and Singapore. Participants wore an Everion multisensor armband and an Apple Watch continuously and completed daily electrocardiograms (ECGs), daily symptom questionnaires, weekly voice recordings, and biweekly KCCQ-12 (Kansas City Cardiomyopathy Questionnaire-12) assessments. Prespecified end points included recruitment yield, device wear-time, task-specific compliance, dropout rate, and adverse events.Of 3386 prescreened individuals, 520 (15.4%) were clinically eligible; 66 consented (1.9% of prescreened; 12.7% of eligible), with technology-related concerns driving most declinations. Among 65 enrolled patients (mean age 56.5, SD 12.3 years; n=53, 81.5% male), 52 (80%) completed 8 weeks. Mean daily wear-time was 11.7 (SD 5.7) hours, significantly exceeding the 8-hour benchmark (P<.001). Task completion rates were 76.6% (2788/3640, daily ECG), 68.5% (2493/3640, daily symptoms), 86.5% (450/520, weekly voice), and 88.1% (229/260, biweekly KCCQ-12). Adherence did not differ significantly by age group (P=.81). No serious device-related adverse events occurred.Enrolled patients with HF, including older adults, sustained robust engagement with a multicomponent digital platform over 8 weeks. However, technology-related concerns prevented most eligible patients from enrolling, identifying adoption, not adherence, as the primary barrier to scalable remote monitoring.ClinicalTrials.gov NCT04191356; https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT04191356.©Christopher J McLeod, Charles Bruce, Kuldeep Singh Rajput, Joseph S Ross, Sy Jackie Lou Velarde, Felis Dwiyasa, Chen Hao, Yan He, Stephanie Zawada, Maulik Majmudar. title: CARD9 Deficiency in an Intractable Orbital Fungal Infection: A Case Report.
abstract: Invasive sino-orbital fungal infections in putatively immunocompetent individuals are rare and can present diagnostic and therapeutic challenges. Herein, we report a 48-year-old man with an 11-year history of treatment-refractory right orbital inflammation characterized by recurrent pain, proptosis, and diplopia. Orbital biopsy demonstrated granulomatous inflammation with septate fungal hyphae, and culture grew Aspergillus flavus complex. Disease persisted despite multiple antifungal regimens and surgical debulking, prompting immunologic evaluation. Whole-genome sequencing identified a homozygous pathogenic splice-site variant (c.1434 + 1G>C) in CARD9, a key adaptor in antifungal immune signaling. Following multiple systemic and local antifungal therapies, posaconazole and investigational fosmanogepix have produced radiographic improvement with stable visual acuity. To our knowledge, this is the first reported case of isolated sino-orbital aspergillosis associated with inherited CARD9 deficiency, expanding its recognized phenotypic spectrum. Refractory fungal orbitopathy without conventional immunocompromising risk factors should prompt consideration of inherited immunodeficiency, which may inform long-term treatment and surveillance.Copyright © 2026 The American Society of Ophthalmic Plastic and Reconstructive Surgery, Inc.

abstract: To describe a novel technique involving endoscopic transurethral buccal mucosa graft urethroplasty and report early outcomes.A retrospective review was performed of patients undergoing endoscopic buccal urethroplasty for bulbar urethral strictures requiring completely endoscopic graft deployment. Patients underwent cystoscopy at 4 months, followed by annual uroflowmetry and International Prostate Symptom Score (IPSS) assessment. Success was defined as the ability to accommodate a 17 French cystoscope at 4 months and freedom from reintervention. For those lost to follow-up, recurrent obstructive symptoms or need for additional urethral intervention was considered treatment failure.Forty-nine men were included in this study. Mean stricture length was 6.5 cm, and mean operative time was 94.6 minutes. Success rates were 95.5% at 4 months and 85.1 % at 1 year. title: Efficacy of [177Lu]Lu-PSMA-617 With and Without Androgen Receptor Pathway Inhibitors for mAPM-R Prostate Cancer: Secondary Analysis of VISION.
abstract: The potential clinical benefit and impact on tolerability of combining androgen receptor pathway inhibitors (ARPIs) with [177Lu]Lu-PSMA-617 remain uncertain and were not evaluated in the primary analysis of VISION (NCT03511664). In this secondary analysis, we assessed efficacy and safety of [177Lu]Lu-PSMA-617 with and without concomitant ARPIs in previously treated patients (≥1 ARPI and 1 or 2 taxanes) with metastatic androgen pathway modulator-resistant prostate cancer (formerly metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer). Methods: Prostate-specific antigen (PSA) response, duration of PSA response, PSA progression-free survival (PSA-PFS), radiographic progression-free survival, overall survival (OS), and adverse events were explored in this post hoc analysis. For OS, a time-adjusted multivariate analysis was performed to control for biases. Results: Among patients randomized to [177Lu]Lu-PSMA-617, 289 versus 262 in the full analysis set and 283 versus 246 patients in the safety analysis set received treatment with and without concomitant ARPIs, respectively. Among patients treated with versus without ARPIs, 49.7% versus 42.2% had a PSA response (≥50% reduction in PSA level) (odds ratio, 1.41; 95% CI, 0.93-2.13; nominal 2-sided P = 0.103), with a median response duration of 9.4 mo versus 8.8 mo, respectively. The median PSA-PFS was 8.6 mo versus 7.3 mo (hazard ratio, 0.87; 95% CI, 0.70-1.09; P = 0.120 [nominal 1-sided stratified log-rank test]). title: Tenecteplase vs Alteplase in Basilar Artery Occlusion Treated with Endovascular Thrombectomy: A Propensity Score-Matched Analysis of 90- and 180-Day Outcomes.
abstract: The effectiveness of tenecteplase vs alteplase as bridging thrombolysis in basilar artery occlusion undergoing thrombectomy is uncertain. This study evaluates both drugs in adult patients with basilar artery occlusion undergoing endovascular thrombectomy.We performed a retrospective cohort study using the TriNetX Research Network (113 health care organizations). Adults (18 years or older) with basilar artery occlusion stroke treated with IV thrombolysis plus endovascular thrombectomy between 2016 and 2025 were identified using International Classification of Diseases, Tenth Revision, Clinical Modification, International Classification of Diseases, Tenth Revision, Procedure Coding System, and normalized drug vocabulary codes. Documented NIHSS coding was required. Propensity score matching (1:1 nearest-neighbor greedy, without replacement, caliper 0.10 SD of the logit) was adjusted for demographics, comorbidities, stroke severity categories, presenting neurologic symptoms, etiology proxies, relevant procedures, and antithrombotic medications. Outcomes at 90 and 180 days included major bleeding, intracranial hemorrhage, all-cause mortality, functional dependency (code-based proxy), emergency department visits for critical illness, and rehabilitation needs (code-based use). A prespecified sensitivity analysis was restricted to NIHSS ≥10. Bonferroni correction was performed to adjust for multiple testing.Among 553 patients (tenecteplase 193; alteplase 360), matching produced 167 pairs for 90-day and 168 pairs for 180-day analyses with adequate covariate balance (postmatch standardized mean differences ≤0.10 at 90 days and ≤0.13 at 180 days). At 90 days (matched), rehabilitation needs were nominally higher with tenecteplase (59.88% vs 46.11%; hazard ratio, 1.48; 95% CI, 1.10-2.00; raw P = .007) but did not survive Bonferroni correction (adjusted P = .08). There were no significant differences in major bleeding (hazard ratio, 0.91; P = .73), intracranial hemorrhage (hazard ratio, 0.98; P = .95), mortality (hazard ratio, 0.96; P = .83), functional dependency (hazard ratio, 1.05; P = .81), or critical illness emergency department visits (hazard ratio, 1.10; P = .46). At 180 days (matched), findings were similar (rehabilitation: hazard ratio, 1.48; raw P = .007, adjusted P = .08; all other outcomes were nonsignificant). In the prespecified NIHSS ≥10 subgroup (110 matched pairs), no outcome differed between tenecteplase and alteplase at either time point (rehabilitation 90-day: hazard ratio, 1.06; P = .74).Tenecteplase and alteplase demonstrated comparable safety, mortality, and functional outcomes through 180 days in those with basilar artery occlusion treated with bridging thrombolysis and endovascular thrombectomy. A nominally higher rehabilitation utilization signal with tenecteplase did not survive multiple-testing correction and was not preserved in the NIHSS ≥10 subgroup, suggesting survivor bias, temporal confounding, and coding-based ascertainment rather than a true therapeutic difference.© 2027 by American Journal of Neuroradiology.

title: DNA methylation signatures from tissue and cell-free DNA in alpha-1 antitrypsin deficiency mirror clinical pathologies providing a potential non-invasive tool to monitor liver disease progression.
abstract: Alpha-1 antitrypsin deficiency (AATD) is a serpinopathy in which mutations in the SERPINA1 gene cause misfolding of alpha-1 antitrypsin (Z-AAT), leading to hepatic protein accumulation, proteotoxic stress, inflammation, fibrosis, and an increased risk of hepatocellular carcinoma. Despite a uniform genetic mutation in most affected individuals, liver disease severity varies, reflecting contributions from environmental exposures and epigenetic heterogeneity (e.g. DNA methylation). As RNA-interference therapy has emerged as a promising treatment, understanding how epigenetic variation relates to the clinical and histopathologic features of AATD may provide insight into disease heterogeneity, progression, and therapeutic response. We analyzed a longitudinal cohort of ZZ-genotype AATD patients with paired liver biopsies, plasma cell-free DNA (cfDNA), and clinical data collected at baseline and 3-y follow-up. Genome-wide DNA methylation profiling of liver tissue identified 15 CpG clusters associated with liver disease severity, immune pathways, and clinical measures including METAVIR fibrosis score and γ-glutamyltransferase. Parallel methylation profiling of matched plasma-derived cfDNA identified eight analogous CpG clusters enriched for similar biological pathways and associated with clinical parameters. Integration of tissue and cfDNA datasets revealed fifty-one shared CpGs representing disease-associated methylation signatures, including loci such as ZFP57 that tracks with portal inflammation. We also identified a DNA methylation signature associated with fibrosis progression based on changes in METAVIR score. These findings demonstrate that liver- and cfDNA-derived DNA methylation signatures robustly stratify AATD patients by relevant measures of liver injury and fibrosis, supporting their potential as non-invasive biomarkers for diagnosis, prognosis, and monitoring responses to emerging therapies.

title: Prevalence and prognosis of gait dysfunction in patients operated on for cervical spondylotic myelopathy: a Spine CORe™ analysis of QOD data.
abstract: Among patients undergoing surgery for cervical spondylotic myelopathy (CSM), the prevalence of gait disturbance and the likelihood of gait improvement remain unclear. The aim of this study was to determine the prevalence and prognosis of gait disturbance in CSM and identify factors associated with gait improvement postoperatively.This was a retrospective analysis of the CSM cohort of the prospectively collected 14-site Spine CORe™ Study Group Quality Outcomes Database (QOD) registry. Outcomes of interest included postoperative ambulatory function at 24 months defined by lower extremity score on the modified Japanese Orthopaedic Association scale and predictors of improved ambulation. The p values for descriptive statistics were obtained using paired and unpaired t-tests and chi-square tests as appropriate. For multivariable analysis, a logistic regression model was fit for improvement in gait in the subset of patients with baseline gait impairment.Of the 1141 patients meeting prespecified inclusion criteria, 1135 had baseline gait data; of these, 877 (77.3%) had baseline gait dysfunction and 258 (22.7%) did not. At baseline, patients with gait dysfunction were older (61.5 ± 11.6 vs 57.2 ± 11.7 years, p < 0.001), had higher BMI (30.4 ± 6.6 vs 29.3 ± 6.0 kg/m2, p = 0.008), were less likely to have private insurance (46.0% vs 67.4%, p < 0.001), and had more comorbidities. Preoperatively, patients with gait dysfunction had worse neck disability (Neck Disability Index [NDI], 41.0 ± 20.8 vs 30.2 ± 18.4, p < 0.001) and quality of life (EQ-VAS, 56.2 ± 21.4 vs 70.0 ± 18.9, p < 0.001; and EQ-5D, 0.5 ± 0.2 vs 0.7 ± 0.2, p < 0.001). Patients with impaired ambulation at baseline were less satisfied with surgery at 24 months (North American Spine Society satisfaction questionnaire [NASS] score 1, 51.4% vs 60.9%, p = 0.004). Among 596 patients with gait dysfunction who received follow-up postoperatively at 24 months, 304 (51.0%) showed improvement and 292 (49.0%) did not. Patients who improved also demonstrated greater improvement in visual analog scale (VAS) neck pain (-3.3 ± 3.2 vs -2.1 ± 3.9, p < 0.001) and arm pain (-3.2 ± 3.9 vs -2.1 ± 3.9, p < 0.001) scores, as well as better NDI (16.5 ± 17.4 vs 26.8 ± 20.9, p < 0.001), EQ-VAS (74.1 ± 20.0 vs 60.2 ± 23.2, p < 0.001), EQ-5D (0.8 ± 0.2 vs 0.6 ± 0.2, p < 0.001), and NASS (score 1, 74.0% vs 53.8%, p < 0.001) scores. Multivariable analyses revealed that lower BMI (OR 1.01, 95% CI 1.00-1.02, p = 0.01) and lower American Society of Anesthesiologists (ASA) class (for ASA class I or II, OR 1.7, 95% CI 1.04-2.80, p = 0.04) were associated with gait improvement.In this cohort, 77.3% of patients who underwent surgery for CSM demonstrated gait dysfunction preoperatively. Of these patients, 51% had gait improvement after cervical spine surgery. Lower BMI and ASA class were associated with improved gait postoperatively. Patients who improved reported superior quality of life, satisfaction with surgery, and decreased pain and disability.

title: Biomarker testing in tumours of the digestive system.
abstract: Precision oncology has profoundly transformed the management of digestive malignancies, making predictive biomarker testing an integral component of routine pathology practice. Beyond identifying actionable molecular alterations, pathologists now face the challenge of selecting appropriate testing strategies, preserving limited tissue, ensuring analytical quality and integrating increasingly complex biomarker data into multidisciplinary therapeutic decision-making. This review provides a practical overview of clinically actionable biomarker testing across digestive cancers, focusing on current testing strategies, methodological challenges and tumour-specific applications. We discuss the complementary roles of immunohistochemistry, in situ hybridisation and molecular techniques, together with practical aspects of tissue stewardship, pre-analytical optimisation, tumour heterogeneity and biomarker re-testing. Particular emphasis is placed on integrating predictive biomarkers into routine diagnostic workflows while maintaining analytical robustness and clinical relevance. Current biomarker requirements are reviewed across the major digestive tumour types, including upper gastrointestinal, colorectal, small bowel, hepatocellular, biliary and pancreatic cancer, as well as gastrointestinal stromal tumours, highlighting both organ-specific biomarkers and emerging tumour-agnostic approaches. The review also addresses contemporary frameworks for clinical actionability, multidisciplinary interpretation of molecular findings and future developments, including comprehensive genomic profiling, liquid biopsy, digital pathology and artificial intelligence. By integrating methodological principles with tumour-specific applications, this review highlights the central role of the pathologist in delivering high-quality precision oncology and provides practical guidance for implementing predictive biomarker testing in routine clinical practice.© 2026. title: A Decade of Music Therapy Integration Within an Academic Palliative Care Program: Lessons Learned and Future Directions.
abstract: Background and ObjectiveMusic therapy (MT) is increasingly recognized as a nonpharmacologic approach to address the physical, emotional, relational, spiritual, and existential needs of patients with serious illness. Less is known about how MT services are developed, integrated into clinical workflows, and sustained within academic palliative care programs. We describe the development and integration of MT within an academic palliative care program over a decade and identify lessons for implementation, sustainability, and future growth.MethodsThis interdisciplinary program review examines the evolution of MT services within palliative care from 2016 to 2026, including early collaborations, pilot initiatives, interdisciplinary integration, electronic ordering and documentation processes, staff perspectives, service adaptations, and emerging research efforts.ResultsAfter a 2016 palliative medicine pilot, MT became an established part of our program. Music therapists have completed 14,031 patient visits across the palliative care program (9,801 visits since 2016) and the Inpatient Palliative Care Service (4,230 visits since 2021). In a staff survey (n = 51), respondents most often referred patients for psychosocial support, pain and symptom management, and coping, and nearly all rated MT as very or extremely effective in improving quality of life. Program growth included electronic ordering and documentation refinements, virtual visits and outpatient groups introduced during the COVID-19 pandemic, and individualized offerings such as veteran recognition ceremonies and heartbeat legacy projects.ConclusionsSuccessful integration of MT depended on sustained interdisciplinary collaboration, clinician education, adaptable service delivery, clearly defined referral and documentation processes, and institutional support. Prospective, multisite evaluation of clinical, caregiver, workforce, and health-system outcomes is needed, along with continued attention to equitable access, staffing, and sustainable funding.

title: Integrating Technologies for Synthetic, Systems, and Spatial Approaches in Cancer Research.
abstract: Emerging tools for spatial analysis, systems biology, and synthetic biology offer opportunities to observe, dissect, and perturb cancer mechanisms, to design strategies for the prevention of oncogenesis, and to identify therapies that lead to durable tumor control. Here, we summarize perspectives from the virtual Innovation Lab on "Synthetic and Systems Approaches to Interrogate Spatiotemporal Processes in Cancer" (S3) hosted by the National Institutes of Health (NIH), which assembled interdisciplinary experts to discuss cancer spatial organization and dynamic cellular interactions and how they can be addressed by leveraging novel synthetic and systems biology approaches. These discussions focused especially on cancer initiation, which results from a failure of systems control. llm_summary: An interdisciplinary group of cancer researchers convened to discuss how new tools in synthetic biology, systems biology, and spatial analysis could be combined to better understand cancer development and find new treatments. The team focused particularly on cancer initiation, which occurs when normal cellular control systems fail, and identified key insights for integrating these three approaches to advance cancer research. This collaborative vision aims to help researchers observe, manipulate, and ultimately prevent or control cancer by understanding how cancer cells interact and organize within tissues.
llm_summary_expert: An interdisciplinary Innovation Lab convened by the National Institutes of Health assembled experts to discuss integrated approaches combining synthetic biology, systems biology, and spatial analysis for cancer research. The workshop focused on understanding cancer spatial organization and dynamic cellular interactions, with particular emphasis on cancer initiation as a failure of systems control. Participants discussed how emerging tools for spatial analysis and synthetic perturbation can be leveraged to observe, dissect, and perturb cancer mechanisms at multiple biological scales. The collaborative effort aimed to identify strategies for preventing oncogenesis and discovering therapies capable of achieving durable tumor control through mechanistic understanding. The assembled experts synthesized key insights from these discussions into a comprehensive vision for integrating synthetic, systems, and spatial approaches to advance cancer research across the scientific community.

title: Moral distress in teams providing extracorporeal membrane oxygenation and mechanical circulatory support: A qualitative study.
abstract: BackgroundMoral distress occurs when clinicians perceive constraints in carrying out the ethically appropriate action. While extensively studied among nurses, less is known about the interprofessional experience of moral distress, particularly in extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO) and mechanical circulatory support (MCS) care settings.Research question/aim/objectivesTo describe moral distress among interprofessional CVICU clinicians caring for patients receiving ECMO and/or MCS, identify perceived barriers and facilitators to addressing morally distressing situations, and explore desired support strategies.Research designThis qualitative descriptive study used interprofessional focus groups and inductive content analysis.Participants and research contextThirty-two professionals from a cardiovascular intensive care unit (CVICU) at a large academic medical center participated in 10 focus groups with two to six individuals per group.Ethical considerationsThe study was approved by the study-site Institutional Review Board, and participants provided informed consent before participation.Findings/resultsThree major themes were identified: (1) Purpose and emotional impact of providing care; (2) Relational dynamics of care; and (3) Organizational responsiveness to the frontline realities of ECMO/MCS care. Accounts of responsibility for patient care without a corresponding voice in decisions most clearly illustrate constrained moral agency. Meaningful work, grief, and coping provided a related context that situates the complexity of the moral distress experience for those working in this practice setting.ConclusionsThe findings suggest that support should help clinicians raise and act on ethical concerns and address other sources of distress (e.g., emotional strain, exhaustion, and professional grief). Notably, moral distress in the CVICU is shaped by the emotional impact of ECMO/MCS care, relational dynamics within and around the care team, and organizational responsiveness to frontline realities. Tailored strategies that strengthen communication, ethics and palliative engagement, team support, leadership awareness, and resource alignment are needed to optimize patient and family care and promote staff well-being.

llm_summary: Researchers interviewed thirty-two healthcare professionals from a cardiovascular intensive care unit to understand the moral distress they experience when caring for patients on advanced life support machines like ECMO and mechanical circulatory support devices. The study found that clinicians felt most distressed when they held responsibility for patient care but lacked a meaningful voice in medical decisions, compounded by emotional strain and grief from the work. The findings suggest that healthcare organizations should improve communication, strengthen team support, and involve ethics specialists to help clinicians address these concerns and better support staff well-being.
llm_summary_expert: Researchers conducted a qualitative descriptive study using interprofessional focus groups with thirty-two cardiovascular intensive care unit clinicians to examine moral distress among teams providing extracorporeal membrane oxygenation and mechanical circulatory support. Inductive content analysis identified three major themes: the purpose and emotional impact of providing care, relational dynamics of care, and organizational responsiveness to frontline realities. Participants described moral distress characterized by responsibility for patient care without corresponding voice in clinical decisions, reflecting constrained moral agency. The findings indicate that moral distress in this setting is shaped by emotional strain, grief, team relational dynamics, and organizational factors rather than clinical factors alone. The authors conclude that tailored support strategies addressing communication, ethics engagement, team support, and leadership awareness are needed, though the qualitative design limits generalizability beyond the study site.

title: Delirium prevalence and practices across intensive care units in Singapore: a point prevalence survey.
abstract: Delirium is characterised by a disturbance in attention and awareness, alongside an acute change in cognition that develops over a short period and fluctuates in severity. It is associated with critical illness. This study aimed to determine the point prevalence of delirium in Singapore's intensive care units (ICUs) and assess the adherence of local delirium management practices and evidence-based international guidelines.A point prevalence survey was conducted on World Delirium Awareness Day, 13 March 2024. Local ICU leads completed questionnaires, and data on delirium prevalence and management practices were collected and compared with international guidelines.Responses were received from 12 adult and two paediatric ICU leads, representing 66% of adult and 100% of paediatric ICUs in Singapore's public health institutions. Of 143 ICU patients, 92 (81.4%) were assessed for delirium, with 32 (34.8%) screening positive. Adult ICUs generally adhered to PADIS recommendations, including limiting benzodiazepine use, routinely assessing for delirium, and implementing protocols for pain management and sedation. However, holistic non-pharmacological care was lacking. Paediatric ICUs showed strong adherence to PANDEM guidelines, although deficiencies remained in delirium assessment and noise reduction practices. The most frequently reported barriers to improving management strategies were manpower shortages, time constraints and educational gaps.Overall, local practices aligned well with international guidelines, but gaps remained in non-pharmacological interventions, resources, time and education. Addressing these gaps through quality improvement initiatives may enhance delirium management in ICUs.Copyright © 2026 Singapore Medical Journal.

title: Indocyanine Green Assists in Identification of Solid Tumor Pulmonary Metastases.
abstract: The presence of pulmonary metastases reduces overall survival in patients with certain solid tumors; therefore, surgical clearance is crucial to cure for some types. This multi-institutional prospective study sought to determine the utility and diagnostic accuracy of indocyanine green (ICG) for delineating pulmonary metastases in diverse pediatric, adolescent, and young adult solid cancers.Thirteen member institutions of the Pediatric Surgical Oncology Research Collaborative administered preoperative ICG to patients undergoing pulmonary metastasectomy for primary or recurrent solid tumor malignancy (2019-2023). Surgeons reported their perspective on ICG utility for pulmonary metastasectomy following each operation. The diagnostic accuracy of ICG fluorescence to identify a pathologically confirmed tumor-containing specimen was determined.Of 829 specimens resected during 134 pulmonary metastasectomies (30.6% hepatic, 47.0% osteosarcoma, 17.2% non-osteosarcoma-type sarcomas ["other sarcomas"], 5.2% other non-hepatic and non-sarcoma tumor types ["other tumor types"]). Surgeons reported ICG as helpful in 77.6% of procedures. In 11.9% of cases, ICG identified viable metastases not visualized on preoperative imaging. Adjusted diagnostic accuracy and sensitivity (95% confidence interval [CI]) for metastases from all tumor types was 80.7% (77.9%-83.3%) and 82.5% (78.9%-85.8%), respectively. By primary tumor histology, adjusted accuracy and sensitivity (95% CI) were 83.2% (74.4%-89.9%), 46.7% (28.3%-65.7%) for metastases from other sarcomas, 80.6% (75.3%-85.2%), 95.6% (91.8%-98.0%) for hepatic tumors, 80.6% (76.6%-84.2%), 77.1% (71.4%-82.2%) for osteosarcoma, and 72.7% (49.8%-89.3%), 60.0% (26.2%-87.8%) for other tumor types.During pulmonary metastasectomy, adjusted diagnostic accuracy of ICG was 80.7%, and, importantly, 11.9% of metastasectomies contained viable tumors identified by ICG but not by preoperative imaging.© 2026 Wiley Periodicals LLC.

title: Comparison of Rule-Based Natural Language Processing and Diagnosis Code Approaches to Detecting Bleeding in the Electronic Health Record: Algorithm Validation Within a Retrospective Cohort Study.
abstract: Anticoagulant use is prevalent and increasing. High-quality anticoagulation management balances individual thrombotic and bleeding risks to optimize care. An automated algorithm to accurately extract major bleeding events from the electronic health record (EHR) of a large health care system would be extremely useful for tracking outcomes of anticoagulated patients.The study aims to assess the accuracy of a natural language processing (NLP) approach, compared with and in conjunction with a diagnosis code (Dx Code)-based strategy, for detecting major bleeding from the EHR.Patients with at least 1 prescription for apixaban, dabigatran, edoxaban, rivaroxaban, or warfarin between January 1, 2019, and December 31, 2023, were analyzed for major bleeding events. Major bleeding was defined similarly to the International Society on Thrombosis and Haemostasis definition. For the NLP algorithm, clinical notes and radiology reports were screened for mentions of bleeding. MedTagger, an open-source, rule-based NLP tool, was then used on the notes. The NLP results were transformed into a feature set, which was used to create a support vector machine model. Three NLP models were created for central nervous system bleeding, critical site bleeding, and bleeding with a hemoglobin drop or transfusions (other major bleeding). Training and test datasets were created using an active learning approach. The model was trained using 80% of the dataset, while the remaining 20% was used for testing. After model finalization, an independent random sample was used to validate the model. Dx Codes were also used to detect major bleeding, similar to previously published approaches. Five unique algorithms were compared: (1) NLP, (2) Dx Code in the primary position, (3) Dx Code in any position, (4) NLP∩Dx Code in any position, and (5) NLP∪Dx Code in any position. All 5 algorithms were compared with manual chart review.The final analysis identified 111,338 patients prescribed outpatient anticoagulation during the study. Manual adjudication was performed for 1189 of the 111,338 (1%) patients. Most of the 5 approaches performed well on the test data, with F1-scores ranging from 0.545 to 0.959, except for Dx Code-Primary, with an F1-score of 0.353 for critical site bleeding. The F1-scores for the validation data ranged from 0.509 to 0.679. The NLP∩Dx Code in any position approach yielded excellent precision of 0.864 (95% CI 0.667-0.953) but only 0.559 (95% CI 0.395-0.711) sensitivity. The NLP∪Dx Code in any position approach yielded good sensitivity of 0.824 (95% CI 0.665-0.917) but only 0.368 (95% CI 0.269-0.481) precision.Electronic tools can screen the EHRs to identify major bleeding outcomes in large patient cohorts within a multisite health care network with high precision but only moderate sensitivity. llm_summary: Researchers compared two automated methods for detecting major bleeding events in electronic health records of patients taking blood thinners: one using artificial intelligence to read clinical notes and another using diagnosis codes. The combination of both methods achieved high accuracy in confirming true bleeding cases but missed some actual bleeding events, suggesting that automated tools can reliably screen large patient groups but may need improvement to catch all cases.
llm_summary_expert: Researchers evaluated five automated algorithms for detecting major bleeding events in electronic health records of 111,338 anticoagulated patients, comparing natural language processing (NLP) approaches with diagnosis code-based strategies against manual chart review as the reference standard. The NLP algorithm used rule-based text extraction from clinical notes and radiology reports combined with a support vector machine model trained on 80% of manually adjudicated data and validated on an independent sample. The combined NLP and diagnosis code approach in any position achieved excellent precision of 0.864 but only moderate sensitivity of 0.559, while the union of both methods yielded higher sensitivity of 0.824 at the cost of lower precision of 0.368. Individual algorithm performance varied substantially, with F1-scores on validation data ranging from 0.509 to 0.679, indicating that most approaches performed adequately but with meaningful trade-offs between sensitivity and precision. Electronic screening tools can identify major bleeding outcomes in large patient cohorts with high precision but only moderate sensitivity, requiring additional development to enhance detection of true bleeding events while maintaining specificity.

title: Advances in the understanding and treatment of pyoderma gangrenosum.
abstract: Pyoderma gangrenosum (PG) is a rare, neutrophilic inflammatory skin disease characterized by sterile pustules that evolve to painful, progressive inflammatory ulcers. Limited awareness among nondermatologists, subjective interpretation of current diagnostic frameworks, and absence of specific diagnostic biomarkers render PG diagnosis challenging, causing delays, increased healthcare resource utilization, and even limb amputations. Effective treatment options remain limited. Wound care management and pain relief strategies are crucial to accelerate healing. Recent technological developments and imaging modalities are poised to lead improvements in the diagnosis, treatment, and monitoring of patients. In this article, we discuss management and future directions of care for patients with PG.Copyright © 2026 The Author(s). Published by Elsevier Inc. All rights reserved.

Current treatment options are limited, though wound care and pain management are important for helping patients heal. New imaging technologies and diagnostic tools may improve how doctors identify and treat this condition in the future.

title: Patient-perceived relevance of the EuraHS-QoL and HerQLes questionnaires: a cross-sectional analysis and sex-based comparison.
abstract: The EuraHS (European Registry for Abdominal Wall Hernias) and HerQLes (Hernia-Related Quality of Life Survey) are validated patient-reported outcome measures developed by expert consensus without direct patient input. This study assessed patient-perceived relevance of questionnaire items and whether relevance differed by sex.A prospective, cross-sectional survey of adult patients presenting for hernia repair was conducted. Participants completed the EuraHS and HerQLes questionnaires, and the relevance of each item was rated on a 0-10 scale (0 = least relevant, 10 = most relevant). Relevancy ratings and sex-based differences in scores were assessed.A total of 137 patients (61 female, 76 male) were included. Median age was 64 (IQR 51.5-70) and BMI was 30.1 kg/m² (IQR 26.3-36.1). Females had higher rates of depression (39.3% vs. 11.8%, p < 0.001) and anxiety (34.4% vs. 13.2%, p = 0.003). There were no differences in hernia recurrence or ostomy prevalence. Across nine EuraHS items, there was no difference in overall median relevance ratings between men and women [7.61 (IQR = 4.72-9.83) vs. 7.78 (IQR 5-10), p = 0.45]. Women rated "shape of the abdomen" as more relevant than men [10 (IQR = 8-10) vs. 8.50 (IQR = 4-10), p = 0.002). Across twelve HerQLes items, overall relevance ratings did not differ between men and women [7.13 (IQR = 3.96-9.42) vs. 7.33 (IQR 4.42-9.83), p = 0.63].Women rated cosmetic outcomes as more relevant on EuraHS; no sex-based differences were observed for HerQLes. Anxiety and depression were significantly more prevalent among women. Further investigation into sex-specific hernia-related patient-reported outcomes is warranted.© 2026. The Author(s).

title: MOG-IgG in the cerebrospinal fluid: a narrative review.
abstract: Myelin oligodendrocyte glycoprotein (MOG) antibody-associated disease (MOGAD) is a recently described inflammatory demyelinating disorder of the central nervous system (CNS) associated with antibodies against MOG (MOG-Abs). MOG-Abs are mostly synthesized in the peripheral compartment, but recent studies reported paired/isolated MOG-Abs cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) positivity, suggesting the possible occurrence of intrathecal synthesis. Nonetheless, this is of unclear diagnostic and prognostic significance, with concerns on the specificity and overall clinical relevance of isolated CSF MOG-Abs positivity. Consequently, current diagnostic criteria emphasize MOG-Abs seropositivity, while requiring additional clinical/radiological supportive features to diagnose MOGAD in patients with isolated CSF positivity. The aim of this narrative review is to clarify the diagnostic and prognostic significance of MOG-Abs CSF positivity.© 2026. Springer-Verlag GmbH Germany, part of Springer Nature.

llm_summary: This narrative review examines when antibodies against myelin oligodendrocyte glycoprotein (MOG), a protein in the brain's protective coating, appear in cerebrospinal fluid and what this means for diagnosing MOG-associated disease, an inflammatory brain disorder. Researchers found that while MOG antibodies can be detected in cerebrospinal fluid, suggesting local production in the nervous system, the clinical significance and reliability of this finding remain unclear. Current diagnostic guidelines therefore prioritize blood tests for MOG antibodies and require additional clinical evidence before confirming the disease in patients with antibodies only in cerebrospinal fluid.

While MOG antibodies are predominantly synthesized peripherally, recent studies have identified paired or isolated MOG antibodies in CSF, suggesting possible intrathecal synthesis of these autoantibodies. title: The first-in-class SFK 'OFF' inhibitor NXP900 suppresses YAP signaling and demonstrates tumor growth suppression in cholangiocarcinoma.
abstract: Cholangiocarcinoma (CCA) is an aggressive malignancy with limited targeted therapeutic options and few validated strategies for molecular patient stratification. Src family kinases (SFKs) and YAP signaling contribute to CCA progression, but prior approaches to therapeutically target this axis have shown limited efficacy. Here, we evaluate the preclinical therapeutic potential of NXP900, a first-in-class SFK 'OFF' inhibitor, in CCA.The antitumor activity of NXP900 was assessed across CCA cell lines, syngeneic murine models, and patient-derived xenografts (PDXs). Mechanistic studies examined the impact of SFK 'OFF' inhibition on YAP signaling. Integrated transcriptomic and proteomic analyses were used to identify molecular features associated with response and resistance.NXP900 demonstrated decreased tumor cell viability in CCA cell lines and significant tumor growth suppression in PDX models. SFK 'OFF' inhibition suppressed YAP signaling through dual mechanisms involving inhibition of YAP Y357 phosphorylation and activation of Hippo pathway signaling. NXP900 enhanced the efficacy of gemcitabine and cisplatin, supporting its potential use in combination regimens. Multiomic analyses identified enrichment of sensitivity to NXP900 in IDH-mutant CCA models, defining a clinically actionable molecular subset. In addition, resistance to SFK 'OFF' inhibition was associated with activation of an IL13RA2-AKT signaling axis, which was pharmacologically targetable, providing a rational framework for combination strategies.These findings establish SFK 'OFF' inhibition with NXP900 as a promising therapeutic strategy in CCA and support biomarker-guided clinical evaluation, including in molecularly defined patient subsets and in combination with standard chemotherapy.

title: Placement of triangular fusion implant superjacent to S2-alar-iliac screws during multilevel spine fusion and the incidence of sacroiliac joint pain: 24-month results of a randomized trial.
abstract: Pelvic fixation during multilevel spinal fusion to the sacrum improves fusion rates at the lumbosacral junction, reduces mechanical failures, and maintains alignment correction. Preliminary data suggest it might reduce the incidence of postoperative sacroiliac joint (SIJ) pain, reported to occur in up to 30% of patients. The aim of this study was to determine the clinical benefit of simultaneous placement of a triangular fusion implant superjacent to S2-alar-iliac (S2AI) screws during multilevel spinal fusion and assess clinical outcomes over 24 months.A prospective randomized trial was conducted (May 2020-October 2022) internationally across 29 centers. Participants (n = 222) were enrolled and randomized to placement of a single S2AI screw plus a triangular titanium implant (TTI) across the SIJ versus a single S2AI screw alone. Randomization was stratified based on the planned upper instrumented vertebra and presence of SIJ pain at baseline. The primary clinical endpoints were 1) the proportion of patients without SIJ pain at baseline who develop SIJ pain within 24 months, and 2) the postoperative change in SIJ pain in patients with preoperative SIJ pain.Preoperatively, 35 of 222 patients (15.8%) had confirmed SIJ pain. Overall, a mean of 8 (3.4 SD) levels were fused during the procedure. At the 24-month follow-up, new-onset SIJ pain was less common in the S2AI+TTI group compared with the S2AI alone group (1.1% [1/93] vs 8.5% [8/94], p = 0.018). In patients who experienced SIJ pain at baseline, pain at the posterosuperior iliac spine improved by a mean of 4.5 points in the S2AI+TTI group and 3.7 points in the S2AI alone group (p = 0.0834). The proportion of patients undergoing pelvic revision surgery was similar across groups (8/109 [7.3%] in the S2AI+TTI group vs 8/113 [7.1%] in the S2AI alone group).SIJ pain is common in patients with adult spinal deformity. Concurrent placement of a triangular fusion implant superjacent to an S2AI screw was associated with lower incidence of new-onset SIJ pain following multilevel spinal fusion with pelvic fixation.

title: Systematic Review Supporting the American Society of Hematology Practice Guidelines on the Management of Myelofibrosis.
abstract: Myelofibrosis (MF) is a Philadelphia-negative clonal disorder of hematopoietic stem cells associated with substantial clinical practice variation. The American Society of Hematology (ASH) convened a guideline panel that prioritized ten clinical questions to inform evidence-based recommendations. We performed a comprehensive systematic review of MEDLINE, EMBASE, Cochrane databases, and Scopus through January 2025 to identify studies that addressed the ten clinical questions. Meta-analyses were performed where feasible. Two reviewers independently selected and appraised studies. Certainty of evidence was assessed using GRADE. Of 3,007 records screened, 43 unique studies met inclusion criteria for the ten questions. Extended molecular testing identified high-risk mutations (ASXL1, EZH2, SRSF2, IDH1/2) that were significantly associated with decreased overall survival (hazard ratios ranging 1.5-4.5). JAK inhibitors improved spleen and symptom responses in symptomatic lower-risk MF and in patients with anemia, with momelotinib improving transfusion independence. However, survival effects were not clearly demonstrated and hematologic toxicity remained common. Evidence for treating asymptomatic high-risk patients with JAK inhibitors was particularly limited. Early allogeneic hematopoietic cell transplantation was associated with higher early mortality but improved long-term survival compared with delayed transplantation. Pretransplant JAK inhibitor exposure did not significantly affect mortality, GVHD, or graft failure. Evidence for interferon, aspirin, and iron chelation was limited and largely indirect. The certainty of evidence was very low or low across nearly all outcomes.Copyright © 2026 American Society of Hematology.

title: FLT3 Mutations in Myelodysplastic Syndromes and Chronic Myelomonocytic Leukemia: A Multi-Center Analysis.
abstract: FLT3 mutations are established high-risk drivers in acute myeloid leukemia (AML), but their role in myelodysplastic syndromes (MDS) and chronic myelomonocytic leukemia (CMML) remains poorly defined. We assembled 115 patients with FLT3-mutant MDS (n=63) or CMML (n=52) across six academic institutions and compared clinicogenomic features and outcomes with FLT3-wildtype controls using propensity score matching and multivariable modeling. FLT3-mutant MDS and CMML displayed a proliferative phenotype, with higher white blood cell counts, increased frequency of CMML-2, and significantly higher rates of AML transformation. FLT3-mutant MDS was enriched for signaling co-mutations, such as NRAS, PTPN11, and CBL, whereas FLT3-mutant CMML showed frequent co-mutation with ASXL1 and SRSF2. FLT3 mutations were independently associated with inferior survival in both entities. After matching, FLT3-mutant MDS had worse median overall survival (OS: 19.9 vs 44.2 months, p=0.046) and leukemia-free survival (LFS: 13.8 vs 37.1 months, p=0.023). In CMML, median OS was 30.4 vs 67.2 months (p=0.017) and LFS 17.2 vs 65.6 months (p=0.014). FLT3-TKD was associated with more favorable outcomes than FLT3-ITD. FLT3-targeted therapy was associated with longer survival in unadjusted comparisons (median OS 14.3 vs 45.9 months in MDS; 20.6 vs 35.0 months in CMML), although this association was attenuated and no longer statistically significant after accounting for immortal time bias introduced from variable treatment initiation timing (adjusted time-dependent HR 0.66, MDS; 0.64, CMML). These findings support early identification of FLT3-mutant MDS and CMML and highlight the need for prospective studies evaluating early therapeutic intervention in this high-risk molecular subset.Copyright © 2026 American Society of Hematology.

title: Multimodal AI for Rhinoplasty Consultation and Simulation: A Blinded Expert Evaluation.
abstract: Multimodal AI can generate rhinoplasty advice and postoperative simulations, but patient-specific validity is uncertain. We assessed expert ratings of clinical content, image quality, coherence, and consultation utility.GPT-5.5 generated rhinoplasty consultations and simulated postoperative images from preoperative photographs using a standardized patient-voiced prompt.Preoperative photographs from 20 rhinoplasty patients were retrospectively evaluated.Four blinded fellowship-trained facial plastic surgeons rated each output using 12 five-point items, two utility items, and one surgical-plan agreement item. Mixed models included crossed random effects for case and evaluator. Institutional review board approval was obtained.Language clarity scored highest (4.05/5); procedure appropriateness (2.90), avoidance of inappropriate procedures (2.59), and plan-to-simulation fidelity (2.33) scored lowest. The primary comparison between image and text domains was not significant (- 0.39; 95% CI: - 0.99 to 0.21; p = 0.18). Consultation usefulness received unqualified endorsement in 5.0% of assessments and qualified endorsement in 78.8%; full agreement with the plan occurred in 7.6%.Despite clear language and visually plausible simulations, patient-specific clinical validity was inconsistent, supporting supervised adjunctive use only.Thieme. title: Biomimetic-Inspired Limited Basement Membrane Proteolysis Modulates Mesenchymal Stem Cell Transmigration while Preserving Endothelial Quiescence on Xenogeneic Extracellular Matrix Scaffolds.
abstract: The success of tissue-derived acellular extracellular matrix (ECM) scaffolds for blood contacting applications depends on preserving basement membrane (BM) integrity to promote quiescent reendothelialization, while simultaneously facilitating progenitor cell infiltration to repopulate underlying stromal compartments. However, achieving this balance remains a central challenge in vascular tissue engineering. This study aimed to determine whether biomimetic-inspired limited proteolysis using proteinase K (PK) can modulate BM structure to enhance mesenchymal stem cell (MSC) transmigration (i.e., stromal repopulation), while maintaining scaffold integrity and BM-mediated endothelial cell (EC) quiescence. Antigen-removed bovine pericardium (AR-BP) ECM scaffolds were treated with increasing PK concentrations (0-20 µg/mL) and characterized using histology, immunofluorescence for bovine BM components (i.e., laminin and collagen IV (Col IV)), and biomechanical testing. Human MSC transmigration was assessed through DAPI staining, quantitative migration analysis, and migratory mechanism probed using RNA sequencing. Human aortic endothelial cells (HAECs) were seeded to evaluate EC polarization, adherens junction organization, new BM synthesis (i.e., human laminin and Col IV), nitric oxide production, and inflammatory response. abstract: Thymic epithelial tumors (TETs) are rare malignancies. Since they occur infrequently, most physicians encounter only a small number of patients, resulting in limited experience with their diagnosis and management and a scarcity of large-scale studies. title: Artificial Intelligence in Thoracic Pathology and Biomarker Assessment: An IASLC Pathology Committee Review.
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is starting to transform pathology by enhancing diagnostic accuracy, prognostication, and therapeutic prediction through advanced computational analysis of histopathological images. This review explores key AI methodologies and their applications in lung cancer diagnostics. Supervised learning dominates current clinical AI tools, relying on annotated whole-slide images (WSIs) for tasks like tumor subtyping, quantitation of tissue-based parameters, prediction of driver alterations (e.g. EGFR and KRAS mutations, ALK rearrangement), and assessment of tumor microenvironment (TME) features. Meanwhile, weakly supervised and self-supervised learning (SSL) methods, such as multiple instance learning (MIL) and contrastive learning, reduce dependency on labor-intensive annotations and uncover novel prognostic morphologic patterns. AI demonstrates strong performance in predicting therapeutic responses, including immune checkpoint inhibitor efficacy and pathologic response to neoadjuvant therapy, while emerging techniques like spatial transcriptomics and multiplex immunofluorescence further leverage AI to decode complex spatial biology and generate novel biomarkers. Despite much progress, major challenges persist in validation, reliability, interpretability, regulatory approval, ethics and data privacy standards, cost and reimbursement, equity, and integration into clinical workflows. Adoption requires scalable digital pathology infrastructure, interdisciplinary collaboration, and suitable reimbursement frameworks. Regulatory efforts aim to address ethical and safety concerns, but global harmonization remains incomplete. We also consider the professional consequences of adoption, including cognitive deskilling, workforce displacement, and the conditions under which pathologist oversight remains meaningful rather than nominal, and argue that liability should follow the reality of control. As AI evolves, particularly with foundation models and large language models (LLMs), thoracic pathology stands to benefit from substantially extended diagnostic and predictive capabilities, pending resolution of implementation barriers.Copyright © 2026. title: Proliferative Glomerulonephritis with "Monoclonal" Immunoglobulin Deposits: Time for Revising the Name and a New Classification.
abstract: Proliferative glomerulonephritis with "monoclonal" immunoglobulin deposits (PGNMID) is a glomerular-limited disease characterized by glomerulonephritis with non-organized monotypic immunoglobulin deposits. Most cases are derived from IgG3, while the remainder are derived from IgG1, IgG2, IgA, IgM, or immunoglobulin light chain (LC) only. Despite the known low rates of detection of monoclonal gammopathy (MG) and B-cell clonal proliferative disorders in PGNMID (especially PGNMID-IgG3), it has traditionally been considered a monoclonal gammopathy of renal significance (MGRS) lesion. However, the association with MG has been recently challenged by demonstration that clone detection rate is rare in PGNMID-IgG3 despite ultrasensitive sequencing techniques and that the glomerular deposits in clone-negative cases, while monotypic, are in fact polyclonal. In contrast, most cases of PGNMID-LC and elderly PGNMID-IgG1 are associated with MG. Based on recent advances, we propose changing the official name of the disease from "proliferative glomerulonephritis with monoclonal immunoglobulin deposits" to "proliferative glomerulonephritis with monotypic immunoglobulin deposits", and classifying the disease into MGRS PGNMID and non-MGRS PGNMID. Kidney biopsy reporting of PGNMID should include the immunoglobulin class (and subclass for PGNMID-IgG) given the notable differences in hematologic characteristics among these immunofluorescence morphologic variants. The new terminology and classification of PGNMID should improve communication between pathologists, nephrologists, and hematologists and help stratify patients for precision therapy.Copyright © 2026.
