title: Transcarotid Artery Revascularization in Patients with Asymptomatic Carotid Artery Stenosis Demonstrates Excellent Outcomes: A Decade Review of Three Stroke Centers.
abstract: Transcarotid artery revascularization (TCAR) represents an alternative to carotid endarterectomy (CEA) for high-grade carotid artery stenosis treatment. We compared perioperative safety, long-term neurologic and cardiovascular outcomes, and durability after TCAR and CEA across three stroke centers.Retrospective cohort study.We analyzed CEA and TCAR procedures for asymptomatic carotid artery stenosis from January 2017 through February 2026 across three institutions. One-to-one nearest-neighbor propensity score matching was performed without replacement. Thirty-day outcomes were compared using the exact McNemar test. Long-term outcomes were evaluated using Cox regression with robust variance estimates. Fine-Gray regression was used to treat death as a competing event for nonfatal outcomes.The final cohort included 889 procedures, 750 CEAs and 139 TCARs. Matching yielded 136 balanced pairs. No ipsilateral stroke, transient ischemic attack (TIA), myocardial infarction (MI), or death occurred within 30 days after TCAR, and no 30-day outcome differed significantly between matched groups. In adjusted analyses of the full cohort, TCAR was associated with mortality (adjusted hazard ratio [aHR], 1.57; 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.07-2.31), stroke or death (aHR, 1.64; 95% CI, 1.13-2.36), and the composite of TIA, stroke, MI, or death (aHR, 1.57; 95% CI, 1.11-2.24). After matching, these associations did not reach statistical significance. Median follow-up in the matched cohort was 4.0 years. Long-term neurologic outcomes also did not differ significantly. Restenosis did not differ significantly (subdistribution HR, 1.43; 95% CI, 0.62-3.30; P = 0.399), and one reintervention occurred in each matched group.Among selected asymptomatic patients, TCAR had low perioperative event rates. After matching, no significant differences from CEA were detected in long-term neurologic outcomes, mortality, composite outcomes, restenosis, or reintervention, while late MI remained higher after TCAR. These findings support TCAR as an attractive revascularization option when CEA is less suitable.Copyright © 2026 Society for Vascular Surgery. Published by Elsevier Inc. All rights reserved.

llm_summary: Researchers compared two surgical methods for treating narrowed carotid arteries in the neck: a newer technique called transcarotid artery revascularization and the traditional surgery called carotid endarterectomy, following 889 procedures over nearly a decade. Both procedures had similarly low rates of stroke, heart attack, and death in the short term and over several years of follow-up. The findings suggest the newer technique is a reasonable alternative when traditional surgery is not suitable, though this was an observational study rather than a controlled trial.

title: The Mayo Obesity Staging Index (MOSI): A Novel Staging Framework for Metabolic Surgery.
abstract: Despite marked heterogeneity in terms of metabolic burden and end organ involvement among patients with obesity, no widely adopted framework exists to capture this complexity. We developed and evaluated the Mayo Obesity Staging Index (MOSI) as a pragmatic preoperative framework for obesity severity stratification in bariatric surgery candidates.Retrospective single-center cohort study of 3,192 adults who underwent primary SG, RYGB, or BPD-DS/SADI-S between 2008 and 2023. MOSI was constructed using 3 domains: BMI class (M), metabolic organ disease burden (O), and systemic impairment (Si). The primary endpoint, optimal clinical response (OCR), was total weight loss (TWL) ≥ 20% at 12 months. The independent association of MOSI stage with outcome was evaluated after adjustment for procedure, age, and sex. Discriminative performance was compared with BMI-only and EOSS-proxy reference models using DeLong's test.MOSI classified 3,192 stageable patients as Stage I (6.0%), Stage II (48.3%), Stage III (40.6%), or Stage IV (5.1%). Among 2,939 patients with 12-month follow-up, OCR declined monotonically across stages: 91.6%, 87.4%, 80.3%, and 58.5% for Stages I-IV respectively (ordinal trend, adjusted OR per stage 0.79; 95% CI 0.68-0.92; p = 0.003). In the fully adjusted model, higher MOSI stage was independently associated with lower odds of OCR (Stage III vs. I: OR 0.44, 95% CI 0.24-0.77; Stage IV vs. I: OR 0.47, 95% CI 0.24-0.88).MOSI provides a clinically interpretable staging framework that separates bariatric surgery candidates into distinct severity groups with meaningfully different weight-loss and disease outcomes and may serve as a foundation for severity-adjusted treatment comparisons across evolving therapeutic modalities.© 2026. The study of nearly 3,200 patients found that those in higher severity stages were significantly less likely to achieve substantial weight loss after surgery, with success rates dropping from 92% in the mildest stage to 59% in the most severe stage. This staging framework may help doctors better predict surgery outcomes and compare different treatment approaches for patients with varying obesity severity.

title: MOSAIC: A global study of the clinical, humanistic and economic burden of geographic atrophy in patients and caregivers.
abstract: The purpose of the study was to explore the impact of visual impairment from geographic atrophy (GA) on patients and caregivers, focusing on clinical, humanistic and economic burdens.MOSAIC was a noninterventional, cross-sectional study comprising a two-stage method to assess burden of disease on patients aged ≥60 years with GA secondary to age-related macular degeneration and unpaid caregivers across the United Kingdom, Australia, Canada, France and Germany. Patients completed the 25-item National Eye Institute Visual Function Questionnaire (NEI VFQ-25); caregivers completed the Zarit Burden Interview (ZBI) and the Caregiver Indirect and Informal Care Cost Assessment Questionnaire (CIIQ). Both groups completed novel items developed for this study.GA negatively affected patient mobility and independence, especially related to driving (mean NEI VFQ-25 driving subscale score: 23.1/100), with substantial effects on distance and near activities. Caregiving was considered a burden by 58% of caregivers, with greater burden for those caring for a parent than a partner (mean ZBI scores: 35.5 vs. 20.1, respectively). Financial concerns affected 44% of patients and 39% of caregivers. More than a quarter of caregivers altered their living arrangements. A moderate correlation was found between NEI VFQ-25 near activities subscale score and self-reported frequency of need for assistance (r = 0.52, p < 0.0001) and between self-reported reading ability and NEI VFQ-25 mental health subscale score (r = -0.53, p < 0.0001).The MOSAIC study confirms profound impacts of GA on patients' and caregivers' daily activities, independence and mental health. The findings emphasise the need for treatment options and support strategies to alleviate challenges faced by patients with GA.© 2026 The Author(s). llm_summary: Researchers examined how geographic atrophy, a serious eye condition causing vision loss in older adults, affects patients and their unpaid caregivers across five countries. The study found that the condition severely limited patients' ability to drive and perform daily activities, with over half of caregivers reporting significant emotional burden and financial strain. These findings highlight the substantial impact on quality of life and underscore the need for better treatment options and support services.
llm_summary_expert: MOSAIC was a noninterventional, cross-sectional study conducted across five countries that assessed the clinical, humanistic, and economic burden of geographic atrophy in patients aged ≥60 years and their unpaid caregivers using validated questionnaires including the NEI VFQ-25, Zarit Burden Interview, and novel study-specific items. Patients demonstrated substantial functional impairment, with a mean driving subscale score of 23.1/100 on the NEI VFQ-25 and significant limitations in distance and near activities, while 58% of caregivers reported caregiving as burdensome with higher burden observed in those caring for parents (mean ZBI score 35.5) compared to partners (mean ZBI score 20.1). Financial concerns were reported by 44% of patients and 39% of caregivers, and more than 25% of caregivers altered their living arrangements. Moderate correlations were observed between near activities subscale scores and self-reported need for assistance (r = 0.52) and between reading ability and mental health subscale scores (r = -0.53).

title: Developing and prioritizing standardized quality measures for pharmacist-led care of inflammatory bowel disease with a modified Delphi process.
abstract: Pharmacist management of care for patients with inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) encompasses therapy education and optimization, monitoring, adherence support, and immunosuppression safety processes and thereby holds substantial promise for improving patient outcomes. However, the absence of a structured set of quality measures often results in fragmented efforts among clinic-based pharmacists, specialty pharmacy pharmacists, and managed care pharmacists. To address this shortcoming, we used an established modified Delphi process to develop and prioritize pharmacist-driven quality measures for the care of patients with IBD.This multisite project was conducted at Mayo Clinic in Minnesota, Arizona, and Florida from October 30, 2023, through February 6, 2024. Stakeholders included IBD physicians, clinic-based pharmacists in medication management services, specialty pharmacy pharmacists, managed care pharmacists, and pharmacy leadership. An environmental scan identified existing quality measures, and a subsequent 3-round modified Delphi process was used to rate the quality measures for importance, feasibility, and validity before final ranking and consensus review.Thirty-one potential quality measures were identified. We prioritized 10 quality measures that emphasized adherence, safety screening, and timeliness of treatment initiation. These consensus-derived quality measures provided a foundation for systemwide performance tracking and quality improvement in pharmacist-led IBD care.Prioritized quality measures were successfully identified to create a consistent, systemwide quality framework for pharmacist-led IBD care. Implementation of shared documentation standards and electronic health record-embedded tools are critical next steps to streamline efforts and monitor their effects on the quality of care for patients with IBD.© American Society of Health-System Pharmacists 2026. An environmental scan identified existing quality measures, which were then evaluated across three Delphi rounds for importance, feasibility, and validity before final ranking and consensus review. Implementation of shared documentation standards and electronic health record-embedded tools were identified as critical next steps to enable consistent monitoring and assessment of these quality measures' effects on patient care.

title: Effects of Dietary Supplements on Resolution Biology.
abstract: Dietary supplements are consumed by up to 50-75% of the US population with omega-3 polyunsaturated fatty acids (PUFAs) being one of the most consumed. These supplements can exert diverse and potential biologically beneficial effects on the resolution of inflammation. Despite the widely available literature in clinical chronic disease settings, the influence of dietary supplements on the resolution phase of inflammation has only recently been recognized. Resolution of inflammation is a biologically active, tightly regulated process partially mediated by endogenously synthesized specialized pro-resolving mediators (SPMs) that aid in restoration of cellular and tissue homeostasis without immune suppression. Among dietary supplements, omega-3 PUFAs, notably the 20-carbon eicosapentaenoic acid (EPA) and 22-carbon docosahexaenoic acid (DHA), serve as the principal substrates for SPM biosynthesis. However, the conversion of dietary omega-3 fatty acids into bioactive mediators is constrained by several factors, including enzymatic bottlenecks, metabolic disease, genetic variability, sex differences, and competing lipid pathways. Emerging evidence, much of which is from preclinical models, suggests that both omega-3 supplementation and direct SPM administration can enhance resolution capacity across multiple organ systems, including the gastrointestinal tract, cardiovascular system, musculoskeletal tissues, nervous system, respiratory system, and reproductive system. This chapter reviews the mechanistic basis by which dietary supplements influence effective resolution biology, which includes efferocytosis, macrophage reprogramming, and epithelial repair systems. The chapter also evaluates current clinical evidence and outlines possible future directions for precision nutrition strategies targeting endogenous resolution pathways.© 2026. title: Novel cardiovascular metabolic risk factor mechanisms and therapeutic opportunities.
abstract: Metabolic disorders such as obesity, type 2 diabetes, and dyslipidaemia are major drivers of cardiovascular risk and have reached epidemic levels in Western populations. Recent advances in clinical research have uncovered unexpected and often beneficial effects of pharmacological classes of metabolic drugs on cardiovascular outcomes, revealing complex interactions between metabolism and cardiac pathology. Despite their clinical efficacy, the molecular and cellular mechanisms through which many of these agents act remain only partially understood. This gap in knowledge underscores the urgent need for fundamental research that not only dissects the biology of metabolic disorders and cardiovascular disease but also reveals the mechanistic basis of existing and emerging therapies, thereby enabling rational therapeutic development. This scientific statement, developed by researchers from the European Society of Cardiology (ESC) Council on Basic Cardiovascular Science and several ESC Working Groups, provides a state-of-the-art overview of the emerging molecular and cellular pathways linking metabolic abnormalities with vascular and cardiac disease. By illuminating these critical connections and unresolved questions, this article aims to catalyse innovation in the prevention and management of cardiovascular disease in the context of metabolic dysfunction and to suggest new directions for future research.© The Author(s) 2026. The study found that while these medications work clinically, scientists still don't fully understand the biological mechanisms behind their benefits. The authors call for more fundamental research to uncover how metabolism and heart disease connect, which could lead to better prevention and treatment strategies.

title: Senescence markers diverge in space, timing, and phenotypic relevance during skin aging in mice.
abstract: The cell theory of aging posits that senescent cells accumulate with age, altering their environment and causing functional organ decline. The dynamics of their accumulation during normal aging and the extent to which it contributes to age-associated damage and disease remain unclear. Using the Study of Longitudinal Aging in Mice, which tracks two strains in both sexes, we identified skin health as a strong predictor of frailty. Quantification of three canonical senescence-associated markers (p16, p21, and γH2AX) in the skin of 320 animals showed variable effects of age on marker abundance: p16 increased with age, whereas p21 and γH2AX showed little or nonuniform changes. Associations between marker burden and age-related phenotypes were highly heterogeneous and varied by marker, sex, and strain. These findings underscore a complex, context-dependent relationship between senescence-associated markers and aging phenotypes, challenging the view that senescent cell accumulation uniformly drives organ decline.

llm_summary: Researchers examined whether senescent cells, which are aging cells that stop dividing and accumulate over time, drive skin aging and frailty by studying 320 mice across two strains and both sexes. They measured three markers of cellular aging in skin and found that only one marker increased consistently with age, while the others showed little change, and the relationship between these markers and aging symptoms varied significantly by sex and strain. These results suggest that senescent cell accumulation does not uniformly cause aging damage in a simple, straightforward way.
llm_summary_expert: Researchers examined senescence markers in skin samples from 320 mice across two strains and both sexes as part of the Study of Longitudinal Aging in Mice, a longitudinal study tracking age-related changes. Three canonical senescence-associated markers—p16, p21, and γH2AX—were quantified in skin tissue to assess their accumulation patterns with age and association with frailty phenotypes. p16 abundance increased with age, whereas p21 and γH2AX showed little or nonuniform age-related changes across the cohort. Associations between individual marker burden and age-related phenotypes were highly heterogeneous, varying substantially by marker type, sex, and mouse strain. These findings indicate a complex, context-dependent relationship between senescence-associated markers and aging phenotypes that does not support a uniform model of senescent cell accumulation driving organ decline.

title: Innovations in intradialytic hypotension management: pathophysiology, precision monitoring, and emerging therapeutic strategies.
abstract: Intradialytic hypotension (IDH) is one of the most frequent and consequential complications of maintenance hemodialysis, affecting up to 40% of treatments depending on the definition used. IDH is independently associated with myocardial stunning, cerebral hypoperfusion, loss of residual kidney function, vascular access failure, and increased mortality. Despite extensive investigation, heterogeneity in diagnostic criteria, incomplete mechanistic understanding, and reliance on intermittent blood pressure measurements continue to limit prevention and management. We performed a narrative review of clinical trials, observational studies, systematic reviews, and guideline statements addressing intradialytic hypotension in adult hemodialysis populations. Evidence was synthesized across pathophysiologic mechanisms, monitoring strategies, and therapeutic approaches, including conventional and digital health interventions. IDH arises from an interplay of ultrafiltration-plasma refill mismatch, impaired vascular responses, reduced cardiac reserve, osmotic and thermal shifts, and medication effects. Epidemiologic estimates vary due to inconsistent definitions, although a nadir systolic blood pressure below 90 mmHg shows the strongest and consistent association with mortality. Traditional intermittent cuff-based blood pressure monitoring underestimates the burden and severity of IDH. Advanced monitoring approaches, including continuous noninvasive blood pressure measurement, volume assessment tools, and integrated dialysis machine feedback systems, enable improved detection of subclinical and evolving hypotension. Recent machine learning and artificial intelligence models leveraging clinical and real-time intradialytic data demonstrate strong performance for IDH prediction and support individualized ultrafiltration and dry weight optimization. Overall, IDH remains a multifactorial and under-recognized driver of morbidity in hemodialysis patients, and integration of precision monitoring with AI-enabled analytics may improve hemodynamic stability and clinical outcomes.

title: Sotatercept Improves Right Heart Mechanics Despite Reduced Myocardial Contractility in Pulmonary Arterial Hypertension: A Prospective Exercise Hemodynamic Study.
abstract: The right ventricular (RV) response to pressure overload is a crucial determinant of outcomes in pulmonary arterial (PA) hypertension. Sotatercept improves clinical outcomes, but its effects on the right ventricle have been inconsistent. We evaluated the effects of sotatercept on load-independent measures of RV contractility, RV-PA coupling, and right heart deformation at rest and exertion in patients with PA hypertension.In this prospective trial among participants with PA hypertension recruited between July 2024 and May 2025, we performed simultaneous echocardiography and invasive pressure measurements during rest and exercise to evaluate changes in RV contractility (end-systolic elastance [Ees]), afterload (PA elastance [Ea]), RV-PA coupling (ratio of arterial Ea to Ees), and right heart deformation, including RV and right atrial strain, before and after 24 weeks of sotatercept using mixed models.Among 30 participants (n=21; 70% female; mean age, 49.3 years [SD 13.5]), sotatercept decreased PA Ea. These changes were associated with reduced RV contractility, PA pulsatility index, and the maximal rate of RV pressure increase over time (dP/dtmax; P<0.001 for all). The decrease in Ees was associated with a decrease in PA Ea (r=+0.70 [95% CI, +0.44 to +0.85]; P<0.0001) with preserved RV-PA coupling (mean difference, +0.08 [95% CI, -0.11 to +0.26]; P=0.42). Although systolic indices measured at the base of the right ventricle (tricuspid annular plane systolic excursion and systolic velocity of the lateral tricuspid annulus) decreased after sotatercept use, there was an increase in RV free wall-dependent systolic indices, including resting and exercise RV free wall strain (mean difference, +6.2% [95% CI, +4.5 to +7.8]; P<0.0001) and fractional area change (P=0.0001). Beyond the right ventricle, there was also improved right atrial filling and contractile performance across rest and exercise (P<0.0001 for all).Sotatercept decreases RV contractility in proportion to reduced afterload, while preserving the RV-PA coupling relationship. Despite decreased RV contractility, global measures of right heart performance, such as RV free wall strain and RA strain, improve, alongside redistribution of RV deformation from annular motion to free wall shortening. These data suggest that sotatercept causes an energetically favorable reduction in resting RV contractility to match the lower afterload, which does not appear physiologically detrimental when considering the concurrent improvement in RV free wall contractile mechanics and exertional right heart reserve.URL: https://www.clinicaltrials.gov; Unique identifier: NCT06409026.

title: Impact of cytoreductive therapy in myeloproliferative neoplasm-associated splanchnic vein thrombosis.
abstract: Patients with myeloproliferative neoplasms (MPN) are at risk of splanchnic vein thrombosis (SVT). Previous studies have failed to demonstrate a benefit of hydroxyurea therapy in preventing recurrent thrombosis after SVT, but they are limited by small sample sizes and inability to account for starting, stopping, or switching of cytoreductive therapies. To better assess the impact of cytoreductive therapy on thrombosis recurrence, we performed a retrospective cohort study of patients with MPN-SVT from the international GASTRO-MPN consortium, treating cytoreductive therapy as a time-dependent covariate. We identified 757 patients, of whom 43% were treated with cytoreductive therapy. During a median follow-up of 7.4 years, 256 patients (34%) had thrombosis recurrence; 145 (19%) had SVT extension/recurrence/transjugular intrahepatic portosystemic shunt thrombosis, and 138 (18%) had a thrombosis recurrence outside the splanchnic bed (74% were venous). In addition, 262 patients (35%) experienced clinically relevant bleeding and 170 (22%) died. After adjusting for age, sex, previous thrombosis, timing of MPN diagnosis relative to SVT, anticoagulation initiation within 30 days of SVT diagnosis, MPN type, JAK2 status, other cancers and cirrhosis, cytoreductive therapy was associated with a decreased risk of recurrent thrombosis (hazard ratio [HR], 0.67; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.50-0.89; P = .01). This was driven by a lower risk of SVT extension/recurrence (HR, 0.62; 95% CI, 0.42-0.90; P = .01) but not by extra-splanchnic thrombosis recurrence (HR, 0.97; 95% CI, 0.72-1.30; P = .82). In a subgroup of patients without erythrocytosis/thrombocytosis at initial SVT (n = 275), cytoreductive therapy was associated with an HR of 0.65 (95% CI, 0.40-1.07; P = .09) for recurrent thrombosis. title: Diagnostic accuracy of fat pad sampling and bone marrow biopsy for AL amyloidosis: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
abstract: In this systematic review, we aimed to assess the diagnostic test accuracy of abdominal fat pad sampling and bone marrow biopsy for immunoglobulin light-chain amyloidosis using organ biopsy as the reference standard. We searched the literature using PubMed, Embase, and Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials (CENTRAL) databases from inception to March 2024. We used Quality Assessment of Diagnostic Accuracy Studies-2 to assess the risk of bias and the Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development, and Evaluation approach to assess the certainty of evidence. After deduplication, 29 237 records were screened and 31 studies were included. Among the studies, 25 (n = 4649) reported on fat pad sampling, with a pooled sensitivity of 0.77 (95% confidence interval, 0.72-0.81), whereas 20 (n = 2771) reported on bone marrow biopsy, with a pooled sensitivity of 0.55 (0.46-0.63). All studies enrolled patients with confirmed disease; specificity was not reported in the included studies. Fat pad aspiration (15 studies, n = 1590) and surgical or punch biopsy (4 studies, n = 222) had similar sensitivities of 0.80 (0.76-0.83) and 0.77 (0.61-0.88), respectively. In a single study (n = 612), performing both tests together yielded a sensitivity of 0.89. Certainty of evidence was judged to be moderate for fat pad sampling and low for bone marrow biopsy.© 2026 American Society of Hematology. Published by Elsevier Inc. title: Outcomes after 7/8 and <7/8 mismatched unrelated donor PBSC transplantation with PTCy: results from the ACCESS trial.
abstract: The ACCESS trial is a prospective, multicenter phase 2 trial evaluating peripheral blood stem cell (PBSC) transplantation using 4/8 to 7/8 HLA-mismatched unrelated donors (MMUD) with posttransplant cyclophosphamide (PTCy), tacrolimus, and mycophenolate. Adults undergoing first hematopoietic cell transplantation (HCT) with myeloablative conditioning or reduced-intensity conditioning (RIC)/nonmyeloablative conditioning (NMA) were enrolled. This expanded analysis includes all enrolled adult PBSC HCT recipients, including the protocol-specified RIC/NMA cohort expansion, to improve precision of outcome estimates and provide descriptive analyses by HLA-match level. Among 268 adults, 183 received 7/8 and 85 received <7/8 MMUD grafts; 82.4% of the <7/8 cohort received 6/8 MMUD grafts. Median follow-up among survivors was 11.9 months. At 1 year, overall survival was 78.6% (95% confidence interval [CI], 71.9-83.9) in the 7/8 cohort and 85.6% (95% CI, 76.0-91.5) in the <7/8 cohort. One-year relapse, nonrelapse mortality, and graft-versus-host disease (GVHD)-free relapse-free survival were 17.1%, 13.7%, and 51.1% vs 22.8%, 8.4%, and 54.6%, in the 7/8 and <7/8 cohorts, respectively. The cumulative incidence of grade II to IV and grade III to IV acute GVHD by day 100 was 36.6% and 7.7% in the 7/8 cohort vs 28.3% and 5.9% in the <7/8 cohort. Moderate-to-severe chronic GVHD at 1 year was 11.3% vs 7.7% in the 7/8 and <7/8 cohorts, respectively. Among adult ACCESS trial participants treated on a uniform young-donor PBSC/PTCy platform, short-term outcomes with predominantly 6/8 MMUD transplantation were encouraging. Because donor match level was not prospectively assigned and between-group comparisons were exploratory, these findings are descriptive and should not be interpreted as establishing equivalence with 7/8 MMUD transplantation. title: Evaluation of modern hematology-oncology home call: optimizing patient care, physician well-being, and trainee education.
abstract: Traditional home call, managing after-hours pager communications, remains a common component of hematology-oncology fellowship and modern practice. Little is known about these patient-related interactions and implications. The aim of this project was to characterize after-hours pager volumes and evaluate perceived impacts on care, physician well-being, and trainee education. We performed a mixed-methods study at a tertiary academic center, analyzing after-hours pager activity from 2020 to 2024 across hematology consult pagers (HCP), hematology outpatient pagers (HOP), and medical oncology pagers (MOP). A survey of hematology-oncology fellows evaluated perceptions and attitudes toward the home-call experience using free-text responses and a 5-point Likert scale. After-hours pager burden was substantial and sustained. The MOP received >3000 pages annually, with medians of 5 to 6 per weekday and 15 to 15.5 per weekend day. The HOP volume nearly doubled over the study period (960-1721 annually), with median pager volumes of 1 to 3 per weekday and 2 to 7 per weekend day. The HCP volume ranged from 594 to 768 pages annually. Survey response rate was 58% (19/33). Only 16% of fellows endorsed educational value from patient calls on MOP or HOP, and ≤5% agreed that call tasks required physician-level expertise. Respondents reported that the pager resulted in fatigue, anxiety, and social disruptions. Free-text responses revealed themes of low educational value, high nonurgent call volume, and system inefficiencies. Contemporary home call had substantial pager burdens with limited actionability, adverse effects on well-being, and low educational value. Systems engineering, including triage processes and augmented patient education, could help optimize patient care, physician well-being, and trainee education.© 2026 American Society of Hematology. title: Kidney Disease: Improving Global Outcomes (KDIGO) Summit on Genetics in Kidney Health: A United States Perspective.
abstract: Genetic testing and genomics are now essential components of precision kidney care, with the potential to inform diagnosis, management, family planning, and transplant decisions. Expansion of genetic testing is increasingly feasible with continuing improvements in diagnostic yield and variant interpretation as well as declining costs. The Kidney Disease: Improving Global Outcomes (KDIGO) Genetics in Kidney Health Summit convened experts in nephrology, genetics, genetic counseling, and related disciplines, together with patients and caregivers, to identify strategies for incorporating genetic testing more fully into kidney care in the United States. Patients and caregivers described genetic testing as a possible means of obtaining clarity about the cause of disease, even when treatment options are limited, and of informing reproductive decisions and cascade testing in at-risk relatives. Reflecting these perspectives, summit participants discussed a shift from criteria-based selection toward a more inclusive testing strategy, reframing the question "who should be tested?" to "who should not be tested?" To avoid exclusion of patients who could benefit from genetic testing, testing strategies should be broad and inclusive, potentially approaching universal testing within key clinical contexts, such as early-onset disease, atypical clinical features, family history of CKD, CKD of unexplained cause, or the presence of extrarenal manifestations. To address the current shortage of experts in nephrogenetics and genetic counselors, collaboration of major American nephrology and genetics organizations is needed to enhance kidney genetics training for both trainees and practicing clinicians. Centers of excellence, which at minimum should include a nephrologist with demonstrated expertise in genetic kidney diseases, at least one genetic counselor, and access to accredited laboratories and bioinformatics, can provide guidance to community nephrologists through telemedicine, virtual case discussions, and shared protocols.Copyright © 2026 by the American Society of Nephrology.

title: Changes in senescence biomarkers, frailty, and physical function during the first year after kidney transplantation.
abstract: Pre-transplant senescence biomarkers are associated with frailty in patients undergoing kidney transplantation (KT). We examined the relationship between changes in senescence biomarkers, frailty, and physical function during the first year post-KT. Plasma concentrations of senescence biomarkers, frailty (Physical Frailty Phenotype), and physical function (Short Physical Performance Battery) were simultaneously measured. Relaxed least absolute shrinkage and selection operator methods were used to select variables for multivariable models. Among 188 participants, mean age was 53 ± 13 years, 62% were male, 34% had diabetes, and 30% underwent deceased donor KT. During the first year after KT, age ≥ 60 was associated with smaller reductions in GDF-15 and IL-8, whereas Black race was associated with greater reduction in RAGE. Alemtuzumab was associated with smaller reduction in IL-7 compared to other induction agents, whereas deceased donor KT was associated with greater reduction in PAI-1. On multivariable analysis, more improvement in frailty was significantly associated with reduction in uPAR concentrations (β - 0.23, 95% CI - 0.38 to - 0.08, p = 0.003). Changes in biomarker concentrations were not independently associated with changes in physical function. Whether interventions affecting the abundance or behavior of senescent cells may counter frailty in KT recipients warrants further exploration.© 2026. The Author(s).

llm_summary: Researchers examined whether markers of cellular aging changed during the first year after kidney transplant and whether these changes related to improvements in frailty and physical strength. They found that patients whose levels of a protein called uPAR decreased more showed greater improvement in frailty, suggesting a possible link between reducing cellular aging and recovering physical function. However, changes in other aging markers were not independently connected to improvements in physical strength, indicating the relationship between cellular aging and recovery after transplant is complex.
llm_summary_expert: Researchers examined changes in senescence biomarkers, frailty, and physical function during the first year after kidney transplantation in 188 participants with mean age 53 years, of whom 62% were male, 34% had diabetes, and 30% received deceased donor kidneys. Plasma senescence biomarkers were measured simultaneously with frailty assessment using the Physical Frailty Phenotype and physical function using the Short Physical Performance Battery, with variable selection performed using relaxed least absolute shrinkage and selection operator methods. On multivariable analysis, greater improvement in frailty was significantly associated with reduction in uPAI concentrations (β −0.23, 95% CI −0.38 to −0.08, p = 0.003). Changes in senescence biomarker concentrations were not independently associated with changes in physical function, and demographic and transplant characteristics including age ≥60, Black race, induction agent type, and donor type showed differential associations with biomarker reductions. The authors note that whether interventions targeting senescent cells may counter frailty in kidney transplant recipients requires further investigation.

title: Hallmarks of Oncological Radicality in Perihilar Cholangiocarcinoma: International Investigation of Margin Clearance and Resection Extent.
abstract: To define a clinically relevant threshold for pR0 and determine the oncological relevance of individual margins.No uniform definition of pR0 exists for perihilar cholangiocarcinoma (pCCA), and it is uncertain which patients benefit the most from wider margin clearances.This retrospective international cohort study included patients undergoing curative-intent major hepatectomy for pCCA in 23 expert centers across North America and Europe (2004-2024). Overall survival (OS), and initial recurrence patterns were compared across proximal, distal, and radial (RM) margins with clearance categorized as 0 mm, submillimeter (>0-<1 mm), or ≥1 mm.Among 1475 included patients, the 5-year OS decreased from 46.6% for ≥1 mm clearance to 36.6% for submillimeter clearance and 26.3% for 0 mm clearance. Both submillimeter and 0 mm clearance were associated with worse OS (adjusted hazard ratio [HR], 1.24 [95% CI, 1.03-1.50] and 1.58 [95% CI, 1.36-1.84]). Only progressively narrower RM clearance from submillimeter to 0 mm conferred an increased risk of local recurrence (subdistribution HR, 1.70 [95% CI, 1.11-2.61] and 2.37 [95% CI, 1.58-3.56]). Nodal metastasis influenced RM submillimeter-OS association (Pinteraction=0.02), and RM 0 mm remained adverse regardless of nodal status (Pinteraction=0.28).Margin clearance at ≥1 mm appears to define pR0. Survival worsened from submillimeter to 0 mm radial margin clearance, with tumor biology refining this distinction. Narrowing clearance was associated with local recurrence but had limited relevance to nonlocal recurrence. Operative strategy should balance greater clearance against tumor biology and risks of extending resection.Copyright © 2026 Wolters Kluwer Health, LLC. All rights reserved.

llm_summary: Researchers examined 1,475 patients who underwent surgery for a type of bile duct cancer to determine how much healthy tissue margin around the tumor is needed for the best outcomes. They found that patients with at least 1 millimeter of clear margin had significantly better five-year survival rates (47%) compared to those with no clear margin (26%), suggesting that wider margins improve survival. The study indicates that surgeons should aim for at least 1 millimeter of healthy tissue around the tumor, though the decision must also consider individual tumor characteristics and surgical risks.
llm_summary_expert: An international retrospective cohort study examined 1,475 patients undergoing curative-intent major hepatectomy for perihilar cholangiocarcinoma across 23 expert centers in North America and Europe from 2004 to 2024, comparing overall survival and recurrence patterns across surgical margins categorized by clearance distance (0 mm, submillimeter, or ≥1 mm). Five-year overall survival decreased progressively from 46.6% with ≥1 mm margin clearance to 36.6% with submillimeter clearance and 26.3% with 0 mm clearance, with both narrower categories associated with worse survival (adjusted hazard ratios of 1.24 and 1.58, respectively). Only progressively narrower radial margin clearance from submillimeter to 0 mm conferred increased risk of local recurrence, while margin clearance had limited relevance to nonlocal recurrence patterns. The study defines margin clearance at ≥1 mm as pR0 and identifies radial margin status as the most oncologically relevant margin, with nodal metastasis.

title: Nutritional Scores and Survival Outcomes in Cortisol-Secreting Adrenocortical Carcinoma.
abstract: Laboratory-based indices such as the Prognostic Nutritional Index (PNI) and Controlling Nutritional Status (CONUT) score have been associated with outcomes in malignancies, but their significance in cortisol-secreting adrenocortical carcinoma (ACC) is unknown.To characterize PNI and CONUT in patients with cortisol-secreting ACC and investigate their associations with hypercortisolism severity, disease stage, and survival outcomes.Retrospective international study including patients with Cushing syndrome secondary to ACC (CS-ACC). Baseline PNI and CONUT scores were calculated at ACC diagnosis. Primary outcomes were overall survival (OS) and progression-free survival (PFS).Ninety-one patients were included (74.7% women); 46.2% ENSAT stage IV. Median urinary free cortisol (UFC) was 5.8-fold above the upper limit of normal. 20.6% of patients had PNI <40 and 29.4% CONUT ≥5. Higher UFC levels were associated with lower PNI values (P = 0.020) and metastatic disease with lower PNI and higher CONUT scores. In univariable analysis, PNI <40 was associated with shorter OS (14 vs 47 months; P = 0.002) and PFS (13 vs 25 months; P = 0.007). Similarly, CONUT ≥5 was associated with shorter OS (14 vs 68 months; P = 0.002) and PFS (17 vs 32 months; P = 0.040). Neither index remained independently associated with survival after adjustment.Abnormal PNI and CONUT values were common in CS-ACC and were associated with hypercortisolism severity, advanced disease, and adverse survival outcomes in unadjusted analyses. However, these indices may reflect the combined systemic effects of cortisol excess and tumor burden rather than nutritional impairment alone. Prospective studies incorporating independent nutritional and body-composition assessments are needed.© The Author(s) 2026. title: Bayesian assessment of stool-based colorectal cancer screening tests demonstrates differential likelihood of meeting CMS coverage criteria.
abstract: To evaluate the probability that next-generation multitarget stool DNA (ng-mt-sDNA) and multitarget stool RNA (mt-sRNA) colorectal cancer (CRC) screening tests meet Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services (CMS) performance-based coverage criteria using a Bayesian framework that accounts for statistical uncertainty.Observed test performance data were extracted from publicly available US Food and Drug Administration reports. Bayesian beta-binomial models with non-informative uniform priors estimated posterior probabilities of meeting two CMS performance pathways: CRC sensitivity ≥90% with specificity ≥87%, or sensitivity ≥79% with specificity ≥90%. Analyses included overall intended-use and Medicare-eligible (age ≥65 years) populations and three specificity definitions (primary: CMS-adopted category 6.2).In the intended-use population, ng mt-sDNA demonstrated a 94% posterior probability of achieving CRC sensitivity ≥90% and >99% probability of achieving specificity ≥87%, yielding a 94% probability of satisfying the first CMS pathway. For mt-sRNA, the corresponding probabilities were 54% for sensitivity and <1%-81% for specificity, yielding <1%-44% probability of satisfying the first pathway. Under the second pathway, ng mt-sDNA demonstrated >99% probability of meeting the specificity threshold, compared with <1% for mt-sRNA. In Medicare-eligible participants, the probability of achieving sensitivity ≥90% was 72% for ng mt-sDNA and 5% for mt-sRNA, although the latter estimate was based on only three CRC cases.Bayesian assessment provides a complementary measure of certainty around coverage-relevant performance thresholds. Ng mt-sDNA demonstrated higher probabilities of meeting CMS criteria than mt-sRNA across separate pivotal trials, although differences in study populations and limited Medicare subgroup data warrant cautious interpretation.

abstract: In patients with metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) or metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH), severe fibrosis is associated with poorer clinical outcomes; however, the prognostic significance of moderate fibrosis is not well established. Moreover, the relationship between disease severity-assessed by liver stiffness measurements (LSM) categories or biopsy-confirmed fibrosis stages-and cardiovascular (CV) outcomes, remains limited. This study estimated the risk of CV and liver outcomes in patients with MASLD stratified by magnetic resonance elastography-determined LSM category (normal [< 3.1 kPa], moderate [3.1-4.4 kPa], severe [> 4.4 kPa]) and in patients with MASH stratified by biopsy-confirmed fibrosis stages (F0-F4).This longitudinal cohort study used Mayo Clinic Enterprise electronic health records (01/01/2005-03/31/2024) to compare the risk of major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) and major adverse liver outcomes (MALO) in patients with MASLD (n = 3092) or MASH (n = 4458) stratified by baseline disease severity.Patients with MASLD and moderate LSM were at higher risk (hazard ratio; 95% CI) of all MALO and nonfatal ischemic stroke (1.94; 1.15-3.27; P < 0.05), CV-related death (2.84; 1.52-5.29; P < 0.01), and 3-point MACE, a composite of ischemic stroke, myocardial infarction, and CV-related death (1.43; 1.10-1.86; P < 0.01), compared with patients with normal LSM. Compared with patients with MASH and F0-F1, patients with F2 were at higher risk for cirrhosis (1.40; 1.00-1.96; P < 0.05) and cirrhosis-related complications (1.37; 1.03-1.82; P < 0.05) and patients with F3 were at higher risk for cirrhosis (2.54; 1.86-3.47; P < 0.01), cirrhosis-related complications (1.70; 1.28-2.26; P < 0.01), hepatocellular carcinoma (4.56; 1.84-11.32; P < 0.01) and liver transplantation (5.52; 1.42-21.37; P < 0.05). Patients in the most severe disease cohorts (i.e., severe LSM or F4) experienced elevated risk of nearly all MACE and MALO outcomes.Patients with MASLD and moderate LSM or MASH and F2-F3 at baseline had an elevated risk for clinical outcomes compared with patients with normal LSM or mild-to-no fibrosis, respectively.© 2026. title: Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy: A Review.
abstract: Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy is defined as left ventricular hypertrophy of greater than 15 mm in any part of the left ventricular wall in the absence of valvular disease, uncontrolled hypertension, or other chronic conditions causing severe left ventricular hypertrophy such as uncontrolled hypertension or cardiac amyloidosis. Most people with hypertrophic cardiomyopathy have a normal lifespan; however, hypertrophic cardiomyopathy is associated with a 0.8% annual incidence of sudden cardiac death.Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy affects an estimated 0.2% of people worldwide (including more than 600 000 people in the US) and is typically diagnosed with echocardiography. Approximately 35% to 40% of patients report effort-related dyspnea, chest pain or pressure, or lightheadedness. Approximately 30% to 40% of people with hypertrophic cardiomyopathy have a pathogenic gene variant that encodes for cardiac sarcomere proteins (predominantly myosin binding protein C, myosin heavy chain, and troponin). Other patients with hypertrophic cardiomyopathy may have a polygenic predisposition and/or nongenetic risk factors. The sarcomeric gene variants cause hypercontractility and delayed relaxation of the cardiac sarcomere, which characterizes the underlying pathophysiologic problem in people with hypertrophic cardiomyopathy. Approximately 60% to 70% of patients have obstructive hypertrophic cardiomyopathy, characterized by dynamic left ventricular outflow tract obstruction due to basal septal hypertrophy. The remainder do not have outflow tract obstruction and, therefore, have nonobstructive hypertrophic cardiomyopathy. Patients with hypertrophic cardiomyopathy should participate in regular low- to moderate-intensity physical activity (such as brisk walking, jogging) as part of a healthy lifestyle. Medical therapies such as β-blockers (eg, metoprolol, bisoprolol, nadolol) and nondihydropyridine-class calcium channel blockers (eg, verapamil or diltiazem) are first-line medical therapy for patients with symptoms due to hypertrophic cardiomyopathy. If first-line therapies do not relieve symptoms, alternative treatments include disopyramide, which improves symptoms in approximately 60% of patients, cardiac myosin inhibitors (mavacamten or aficamten), which improve symptoms in approximately 70% to 80% of patients, or procedures to thin the septal wall of the left ventricle, including percutaneous alcohol septal ablation, which improves symptoms in approximately 75% to 80% of patients, or surgical septal myectomy, which improves symptoms in approximately 90% to 95% of patients. Guidelines recommend that first-degree relatives of patients with hypertrophic cardiomyopathy undergo screening for hypertrophic cardiomyopathy with genetic testing or echocardiography.Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy is caused by a monogenetic pathogenic variant in approximately 30% to 40% of patients and can cause effort-related dyspnea, chest pain or pressure, or lightheadedness. Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy is associated with an incidence of sudden cardiac death of 0.8% per year. First-line therapies for symptomatic hypertrophic cardiomyopathy are β-blockers (eg, metoprolol, bisoprolol, nadolol) or nondihydropyridine calcium channel blockers (eg, verapamil, diltiazem).

title: Efficacy and bystander effects of EGFR-targeting 40H3 antibody-drug conjugates in glioblastoma PDX models.
abstract: Epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR) is amplified and overexpressed in approximately half of glioblastomas (GBMs) and is a promising target for antibody-drug conjugate (ADC) therapy in this disease. In this study, five different payloads were screened for cytotoxicity across five GBM patient-derived xenograft (PDX) lines, and two compounds, PBD dimer SG-3199 and monomethyl auristatin E (MMAE), were used to construct EGFR-targeted ADCs built on the 40H3 antibody backbone: 40H3-tesirine (40H3-TS) and 40H3-MMAE, respectively. Both 40H3-TS and 40H3-MMAE showed robust cytotoxicity, lysosomal internalization, and activation of payload-associated signaling pathways in EGFRvIII-amplified GBM PDX cells. Because SG-3199 and MMAE are cell-permeable drugs, significant bystander effects were observed in non-EGFR-expressing cells tested by (a) co-culture with EGFRvIII-overexpressing cells and (b) culture with conditioned media collected from ADC-treated EGFRvIII-amplified or -overexpressing cells. 40H3-TS and 40H3-MMAE reduced tumor burden and significantly prolonged survival in orthotopic GBM6 and GBM39 PDX models; however, 40H3-TS was limited by a narrow therapeutic window. In summary, although further optimization is required, EGFR-targeted ADCs have potential as an effective therapy for patients with GBM.

title: Predicting Time to Total Knee Arthroplasty: The Effects of Minimum Joint Space Width and Hip-Knee-Ankle Angle in 34,105 Knees.
abstract: The timing of progression to total knee arthroplasty (TKA) in patients who have knee osteoarthritis remains difficult to predict, yet accurate prediction is crucial for patient management. The purpose of this study was to evaluate the effect of minimum joint space width (mJSW) and hip knee ankle angle (HKAA) on time to arthroplasty in the osteoarthritic population.We identified patients who have standard weight-bearing antero-posterior knee radiographs at our institution who underwent primary TKA from 2000 to 2025. We used validated deep learning algorithms to measure HKAA and mJSW in both knees. In total, 34,105 knees from 18,255 patients were included, of which 67% progressed to TKA (median 4.2 years). Using baseline mJSW and HKAA (absolute deviation from neutral alignment), we fit Cox proportional hazards models with time to TKA as our primary outcome, correcting for patient-level effects and effects from age (mean 65 years), sex (58% women), and body mass index (BMI) (mean 32). We performed sensitivity analyses by restricting the cohort to patients who had greater than two mm mJSW or to patients who had greater than one year between imaging and TKA.In the univariate model, each one mm lower baseline mJSW was associated with a 30% increase in the risk of undergoing TKA (hazard ratio (HR): 1.3, P < 0.001). In the multivariable model, the mJSW effect was attenuated, but remained significant (HR: 1.2, P < 0.001), and each 1° increase in baseline absolute HKAA from neutral resulted in a 10% increase in TKA risk (HR: 1.1, P < 0.001). Demographic traits had no meaningful impact on time-to-TKA, and all mJSW and HKAA effects were consistent across sensitivity analyses.In a cohort of 34,105 knees, joint space narrowing and HKAA deviation were the strongest independent radiographic predictors of time to TKA, with weaker effects from sex and BMI and no association with age. Early radiographic phenotyping using mJSW and HKAA may improve surgical referral timing and expectation management for patients.Copyright © 2026 Elsevier Inc. All rights reserved.

llm_summary: Researchers examined whether two measurements visible on knee X-rays—joint space width and alignment angle—could predict how soon patients with knee arthritis would need replacement surgery, studying 34,105 knees over 25 years. They found that narrower joint spaces and misaligned knees were the strongest predictors of needing surgery sooner, with each millimeter of space loss increasing risk by about 20 percent. These radiographic measurements may help doctors better time surgical referrals and set realistic expectations for patients with arthritis.

title: A Comparative Usability Study of Three AI Interpretation Tools in Simulated ICU Family Meetings.
abstract: Background Effective communication in the ICU is essential, yet timely access to professional interpreters remains challenging for patients with non-English language preference. Language discordance in high-acuity settings has been associated with miscommunication, delays in care, and adverse outcomes. Speech-based artificial intelligence (AI) interpretation tools have emerged as potential adjuncts to bridge communication gaps, but comparative usability data in high-stakes clinical settings remain limited. Objective To evaluate and compare clinician-reported usability of three speech-based AI interpretation tools during physician-led simulated ICU family meetings. Methods We conducted a comparative study involving 21 ICU physicians. Each participant completed three simulated ICU family meetings representing high-stakes scenarios including ECMO discussion, tracheotomy planning, and transition to comfort care. Participants were assigned to one non-English language (Spanish, Chinese, or Arabic) and used three speech-based interpretation tools (AI-TransLATE, ChatGPT, and Gemini) in counterbalanced order. After each encounter, clinicians completed the System Usability Scale (SUS) and structured Likert-scale assessments of satisfaction, perceived communication effectiveness, effort, and acceptability. Results AI-TransLATE achieved a median SUS of 70.0 (IQR 64.4-75.6) and ChatGPT 72.5 (IQR 70.0- 75.0), both meeting the acceptable threshold (≥70). Gemini received 40.0 (IQR 25.0-57.5), falling below the acceptable range. Gemini differed significantly from both AI-TransLATE and ChatGPT, while AI-TransLATE and ChatGPT did not differ significantly. Satisfaction, perceived communication effectiveness, and willingness to use in clinical practice were also significantly higher for AI-TransLATE and ChatGPT compared with Gemini. Conclusion In simulated ICU family meetings, select speech-based AI interpretation tools demonstrated acceptable clinician-reported usability, supporting further investigation of their potential as complementary interpretation tools when professional interpreter access is limited. Future work should prioritize validation and evaluation of patient understanding in real-world settings , to support safe and scalable implementation.Thieme. All rights reserved.

llm_summary: Researchers tested three artificial intelligence interpretation tools designed to help doctors communicate with patients who don't speak English during intensive care unit family meetings. Two of the tools, AI-TransLATE and ChatGPT, performed acceptably according to doctors' ratings, while the third tool, Gemini, performed poorly in comparison. The findings suggest these AI tools may help bridge communication gaps when professional interpreters are unavailable, though testing with actual patients in real clinical settings is still needed.

AI-TransLATE achieved a median System Usability Scale score of 70.0 and ChatGPT 72.5, both meeting the acceptable threshold of 70, while Gemini scored 40.0 and fell below acceptable range, with AI-TransLATE and ChatGPT showing significantly higher satisfaction and perceived communication effectiveness than Gemini. title: Clinical reasoning research priorities for advancing diagnostic safety: researcher and patient perspectives.
abstract: This study used both researcher and patient perspectives to identify high-priority research questions related to clinical reasoning.This study integrates findings from two previously published research prioritization exercises aimed at advancing the science of diagnostic safety, focusing on questions relevant to clinical reasoning. In Study 1 (April 2019), 97 researchers submitted 177 unique research questions that could be useful "to reduce patient harm in the diagnosis process". In Study 2 (November 2019), 41 patients/caregivers/advocates submitted 84 unique research questions on the same topic. In an in-person meeting, a subset of these participants identified 81 of these questions as high-priority (51 from Study 1; 30 from Study 2). For the current study, five investigators identified questions that focused on clinical reasoning, first independently and then by consensus. They then categorized the clinical reasoning questions into inductively identified themes.Twenty-nine of the 81 high-priority research questions addressed clinical reasoning and were categorized into 5 themes: understanding clinical reasoning and cognition (12 questions), decision support/technology (6 questions), team-based decision making (5 questions), how to learn from cases/scenarios (3 questions), and patient engagement (3 questions). Questions addressed a range of basic/foundational science and clinical applications, and involved individuals, teams, and/or systems.Identification of high-priority clinical reasoning research questions can help medical educators, clinicians, researchers, and funders catalyze research and discovery of interventions to improve clinical reasoning and ultimately improve patient outcomes.© 2026 Walter de Gruyter GmbH, Berlin/Boston.

llm_summary_expert: Researchers conducted two prioritization exercises to identify high-priority clinical reasoning research questions from both expert and patient perspectives, with 97 researchers submitting 177 questions in Study 1 and 41 patients/caregivers/advocates submitting 84 questions in Study 2. Five investigators independently reviewed and then reached consensus on which questions focused specifically on clinical reasoning, ultimately identifying 29 of 81 high-priority questions that addressed clinical reasoning. The 29 clinical reasoning questions were categorized into five themes: understanding clinical reasoning and cognition (12 questions), decision support/technology (6 questions), team-based decision making (5 questions), learning from cases/scenarios (3 questions), and patient engagement (3 questions). These high-priority research questions can guide medical educators, clinicians, researchers, and funders in directing resources toward interventions aimed at improving clinical reasoning and patient outcomes.

title: Risk outcome assessment with novel long-T ITC complex and high sensitivity troponin I and T in patients with suspected acute coronary syndromes: MERITnI substudy.
abstract: Understanding whether the novel long-T ITC complex might assist in interpreting clinical prognostic utility compared to established cardiac biomarkers is needed. We determined long term major adverse cardiac events (MACE) and all-cause mortality (ACM) predicated on novel long-T ITC complex and high sensitivity cardiac troponin I (hs-cTnI) and T (hs-cTnT) assays in the emergency department (ED).cTn assays were measured on the Mindray CL-1200i platform at presentation in consecutive patients enrolled in 'Mindray hs-cTnI Assay Analytical and Clinical Evaluation for the Diagnosis and RIsk Assessment of Myocardial InfarctIon' (MERITnI) (NCT05853042) trial with suspected ischemia. Sex specific 99th percentiles upper reference limits (URLs) were: hs-cTnI female 14 ng/L, male 15 ng/L; hs-cTnT female 10 ng/L, male 19 ng/L; long-T ITC complex 0.9 ng/L, same for female and male.Of 1,070 patients, 59.4 % were male, 43.4 % White, 45.5 % Black, and 39.5 % ≥65 years. Independent of biomarkers, a continuum of risk over 1 year showed MACE increased to 16.1 % and ACM to 16.5 %. Long-T ITC complex did not show a continuum change, increasing only 0.1 % (HR: 1.001 (1.0-1.001) per ng/L. However, hs-cTnI increased 1.8 % (HR: 1.018 [1.009-1.027] for each ng/L (p<0.0001) and hs-cTnT increased 0.3 % per ng/L (HR: 1.003 [1.001-1.006]) (p=0.0028). Between subjects ≤URLs and >URLs, MACE and ACM all biomarkers showed significant (p<0.0001) differences over 1 year. For MACE in those >URL long-T ITC complex increased 11.2-25.2 %, hs-cTnI 18.0-35.0 % and hs-cTnT 8.9-24.2 %. For ACM in those >URL long-T ITC complex increased 4.5-23.3 %, hs-cTnI 5.0-26.2 %, and hs-cTnT 3.6-24.1 %.Novel long-T ITC complex did not provide new prognostic value to either hs-cTnI or hs-cTnT. llm_summary: Researchers examined whether a novel heart damage marker called long-T ITC complex could help predict which emergency department patients with suspected heart attacks would experience serious cardiac events or death within one year. High sensitivity troponin I and T, established blood tests for heart damage, showed strong predictive value with risk increasing as levels rose, but the novel long-T ITC complex did not provide additional prognostic information beyond these existing tests. Patients with elevated troponin levels had substantially higher rates of major cardiac events and death at one year compared to those with normal levels.
llm_summary_expert: The MERITnI substudy evaluated whether a novel long-T ITC complex biomarker could improve risk stratification compared to high-sensitivity cardiac troponin I (hs-cTnI) and T (hs-cTnT) in 1,070 emergency department patients with suspected acute coronary syndromes, measuring these biomarkers at presentation and following patients for one year to assess major adverse cardiac events (MACE) and all-cause mortality (ACM). While all three biomarkers showed significant differences in MACE and ACM rates between patients with concentrations above versus below sex-specific upper reference limits (p<0.0001), the long-T ITC complex demonstrated minimal prognostic utility with a hazard ratio of 1.001 per ng/L compared to hs-cTnI at 1.018 per ng/L and hs-cTnT at 1.003 per ng/L. Over one year, MACE increased to 16.1% and ACM to 16.5% across the study population, with patients exceeding upper reference limits showing.

title: Association between body mass index and perimenopause symptom burden: a cross-sectional global study using the Flo App.
abstract: To evaluate the association between body mass index (BMI) and overall perimenopause symptom burden, measured by the total Menopause Rating Scale (MRS) score, and domain-specific psychological, somatic, and urogenital symptoms.This cross-sectional study was conducted through the Flo app between December 2024 and May 2025 and included 1,988 women in perimenopause aged 35 years or older. BMI was categorized into six groups from underweight to obesity class III. Total and domain-specific MRS scores were compared using ANOVA and pairwise comparisons. Multiple linear regression identified predictors of symptom burden.In multivariable regression models adjusting for age, race and ethnicity, income, education, smoking, physical activity, alcohol use, and comorbididities (anxiety, depression, and diabetes), obesity classes I-III were independently associated with higher total (B=1.21-1.42, all P<0.05) and somatic (B=0.76-0.92, all P<0.001) MRS scores relative to normal weight, whereas no BMI category was independently associated with psychological or urogenital scores. Comorbid anxiety and depression emerged as the strongest independent predictors of symptom burden across all domains, followed by insufficient income, lower educational attainment, and active smoking, whereas more frequent physical activity was associated with lower symptom burden.Higher BMI was independently associated with greater perimenopause symptom burden, particularly in the somatic domain, underscoring the multifactorial nature of symptom burden during the menopause transition.Copyright © 2026 The Author(s). title: 124I-Evuzamitide Positron Emission Tomography/Computed Tomography for Diagnosing Cardiac Amyloidosis: The REVEAL Nonrandomized Clinical Trial.
abstract: Diagnosing cardiac amyloidosis remains challenging because current imaging approaches are limited to transthyretin amyloidosis. A noninvasive test capable of directly imaging cardiac amyloidosis from various amyloid types and in multiple organs could address an important unmet diagnostic need.To evaluate the sensitivity and specificity of 124I-evuzamitide positron emission tomography (PET)/computed tomography (CT) for diagnosing cardiac amyloidosis.Prospective, multicenter (18 US centers), single-group study evaluating the efficacy of 124I-evuzamitide to diagnose cardiac amyloidosis. This study was conducted from January 14, 2025, to March 12, 2026, including a 60-day follow-up period. Three physicians with cardiac PET/CT experience independently reviewed PET/CT images for visual cardiac 124I-evuzamitide uptake while blinded to clinical data. Three expert clinical amyloidosis physicians, blinded to PET/CT data, independently adjudicated the diagnosis based on the standard-of-care diagnostic algorithm. A total of 195 adults suspected of having cardiac amyloidosis were enrolled when they presented for diagnostic evaluation at participating institutions, excluding patients with an established diagnosis of cardiac or systemic amyloidosis.PET/CT scans were obtained 3 to 5 hours after intravenous administration of 1 mCi of 124I-evuzamitide. title: Gene Silencer Therapy in Transthyretin Amyloid Cardiomyopathy: A Meta-Analysis of Outcomes Trials.
abstract: Gene-silencing therapies reduce hepatic transthyretin (TTR) production and have been evaluated in phase 3 trials in TTR amyloid cardiomyopathy (ATTR-CM). However, differences in trial design and background therapies have limited assessment of the overall treatment effect and its consistency according to baseline TTR stabilizer use.To assess the effect of TTR gene-silencing therapies in patients with ATTR-CM.PubMed was searched through June 15, 2026, for randomized, placebo-controlled, phase 3 outcome trials of gene-silencing therapies in ATTR-CM.Two reviewers independently extracted data, following the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) guideline. Fixed-effects meta-analysis estimated rate ratios (RRs) or hazard ratios (HRs) with 95% CIs.The prespecified primary outcome was the composite of all-cause mortality and recurrent cardiovascular events. Secondary outcomes included all-cause mortality, cardiovascular death, time to first primary outcome, functional capacity (6-minute walk distance), and health status (Kansas City Cardiomyopathy Questionnaire-Overall Summary Score).A total of 2 studies (HELIOS-B and CARDIO-TTRansform) met the inclusion criteria and included 2086 patients with ATTR-CM. The studies included 1902 men with a median age of 77 years (range for HELIOS-B, 45-85 years; for CARDIO-TTRansform, 41-91 years). Gene-silencing therapy reduced the primary end point by 19% (RR, 0.81; 95% CI, 0.69-0.94; P = .006), with no heterogeneity between trials (P for heterogeneity = .27). Gene-silencing therapy also reduced the risk of all-cause death (HR, 0.74; 95% CI, 0.61-0.91) and time to first all-cause death or cardiovascular events (HR, 0.77; 95% CI, 0.67-0.89) compared with placebo. Gene silencers preserved 6-minute walk distance (placebo-corrected difference, +22.2 m; 95% CI, 14.3-30.0) and Kansas City Cardiomyopathy Questionnaire-Overall Summary Score (+4.5; 95% CI, 2.7-6.2), with no evidence of between-trial heterogeneity. Treatment effects on primary end points differed according to baseline stabilizer use, with significant benefits observed among patients not receiving background stabilizer therapy (RR, 0.69; 95% CI, 0.57-0.85) and no significant incremental benefit observed for those receiving concomitant stabilizer at baseline (RR, 0.97; 95% CI, 0.77-1.23; P for heterogeneity = .03). Similar heterogeneity was observed for functional capacity and health status.The findings from this meta-analysis support TTR gene silencing for ATTR-CM. The attenuated benefit observed for patients receiving concomitant TTR stabilizer therapy may reflect residual differences in case mix, disease duration, or magnitude of TTR suppression or a true ceiling on additional benefit of gene silencing in the setting of background TTR stabilization.PROSPERO registration: CRD420261421656. title: Time to Flip the Script: Advanced Therapy Is Appropriate for Most Patients with Recently Diagnosed IBD.
abstract: Guidelines recommend initiating advanced therapy in patients with moderate-to-severe inflammatory bowel disease (IBD). Although early use of advanced therapy may be beneficial in slowing or halting disease progression, there is limited clinical trial and real-world evidence defining appropriateness of starting advanced therapy within 1 year of diagnosis. To address this gap, 11 IBD specialists defined 144 hypothetical scenarios representative of patients seen in clinical practice and rated them as inappropriate, uncertain, or appropriate for advanced therapy initiation using the RAND Appropriateness Method. We considered key variables likely to drive treatment decisions in this first year, including endoscopic disease severity, degree of symptoms, prior mesalamine in ulcerative colitis (UC), disease extent in Crohn's disease (CD), prior systemic corticosteroids, and age. Scenarios were rated independently, then re-rated via an anonymous survey after discussion at an in-person meeting. Overall, our expert panel identified few clinical scenarios in which it would be inappropriate to initiate advanced therapy within 1 year of IBD diagnosis. For patients with UC, panelists rated it appropriate to start advanced therapy in those with Mayo 3 disease and inappropriate in nearly all patients with Mayo 1 disease and no prior use of mesalamine. For patients with CD, panelists rated advanced therapy appropriate for all patients with deep ulcers, and nearly all with shallow ulcers or erosions who are symptomatic. Scenarios rated uncertain included asymptomatic patients with UC Mayo 2 not previously treated with mesalamine, as well as all asymptomatic patients with CD erosions. Our findings support a role for early advanced therapy in most patients within 1 year of IBD diagnosis and underscore the importance of individualizing treatment decisions in IBD.Copyright © 2026 by The American College of Gastroenterology.

The expert panel identified few scenarios in which advanced therapy initiation would be inappropriate, rating it appropriate for patients with ulcerative colitis Mayo 3 disease and inappropriate in nearly all patients with Mayo 1 disease without prior mesalamine exposure. title: Surgical approach impacts patient-reported symptoms following arthroplasty for femoral neck fractures.
abstract: We aimed to compare outcomes between patients with displaced femoral neck fractures (FNFs) managed with total hip arthroplasty (THA) or hemiarthroplasty (HA) via an anterolateral/lateral compared with posterior approach.We used data from the Hip fracture Evaluation with Alternatives of Total hip arthroplasty versus Hemiarthroplasty (HEALTH) trial, which randomized 1,441 patients aged 50 years and older with displaced femoral neck fractures to receive THA or HA. We calculated each patient's propensity to undergo arthroplasty via posterior approach, and matched each patient to one control (anterolateral/lateral approach) based on age (SD 5 years), BMI (SD 3 points), and propensity score (using a caliper of 0.2 SDs). We used chi-squared and Fisher's exact tests to compare dichotomous outcomes between matched groups, and repeated measures analysis of variance (ANOVA) to examine differences in patient-reported outcomes at baseline and one year postoperatively. We used logistic regression to identify independent predictors of reoperation for instability in the posterior group.A total of 1,306 patients met the inclusion criteria; 876 (67.1%) received arthroplasty via an anterolateral/lateral approach, and 430 (32.9%) through posterior approach. Following propensity score matching, we retained 790 patients, 395 in each group, with no differences in patient, fracture, or implant characteristics. The rate of treatment for dislocation was higher in the posterior approach group. Repeated measures ANOVA revealed significantly better Western Ontario and McMaster Universities osteoarthritis index (WOMAC) pain, stiffness, function, and total scores in the posterior group. We identified THA (vs HA, odds ratio (OR) 2.05, 95% CI 1.05 to 4.01) and being a primary wheelchair ambulator or bedridden (OR 3.27, 95% CI 1.29 to 8.29) as independent predictors of reoperation for instability in the posterior group.Our analyses suggest that patients with displaced FNFs who undergo arthroplasty via the posterior approach may report better symptoms and functional outcomes at one year compared with an anterolateral/lateral approach, despite increased risk of reoperation for instability. llm_summary: Researchers compared two surgical approaches for treating hip fractures in older adults using artificial hip joints, examining whether patients had better outcomes with a posterior (back) approach versus an anterolateral/lateral (front or side) approach. Patients who received surgery through the posterior approach reported less pain and better function one year after surgery, though they had a higher rate of hip dislocation requiring additional treatment. The findings suggest the posterior approach may offer symptom benefits despite increased instability risks, though further research is needed to confirm these results.
llm_summary_expert: Researchers examined 1,306 patients aged 50 years and older with displaced femoral neck fractures from the HEALTH trial who underwent total hip arthroplasty or hemiarthroplasty, comparing outcomes between posterior and anterolateral/lateral surgical approaches using propensity score matching to create balanced groups of 395 patients each. The posterior approach group experienced a higher rate of treatment for dislocation but demonstrated significantly better Western Ontario and McMaster Universities osteoarthritis index pain, stiffness, function, and total scores at one year postoperatively compared with the anterolateral/lateral approach group. Independent predictors of reoperation for instability in the posterior group included total hip arthroplasty versus hemiarthroplasty (odds ratio 2.05, 95% confidence interval 1.05 to 4.01) and being a primary wheelchair ambulator or bedridden (odds ratio 3.27, 95% confidence interval 1.29 to 8.29). Although patients undergoing posterior approach arthroplasty reported superior functional outcomes at one year, this observational analysis cannot establish causation and the increased.

title: Outcomes of Semiconstrained and Nonconstrained Implants in Patients Undergoing Cervical Disk Arthroplasty.
abstract: Cervical disk arthroplasty (CDA) implants differ in their degree of constraint, potentially influencing postoperative outcomes. The objective of this study was to compare perioperative and long-term outcomes between patients receiving semiconstrained and nonconstrained CDA implants.A retrospective multicenter cohort study was conducted on 129 patients who underwent one-level CDA between 2017 and 2024 at 4 participating clinical sites. Patients were categorized by implant type: semiconstrained (Prestige; Medtronic) or nonconstrained (Mobi-C; Highridge Medical). The primary outcomes were index-level reoperation rates, device removal rates, and all-cause hospital readmission rates at 30 days, 90 days, and 1 year. Secondary outcomes included operative time, hospital length of stay, estimated blood loss, and patient-reported outcomes, assessed using Patient-Reported Outcomes Measurement Information System domains at baseline, 3 months, and 1 year postoperatively. Continuous variables were compared using Student's t-test and categorical variables using χ2 tests.Baseline demographics were comparable between groups. Semiconstrained implants were associated with lower rates of index-level reoperation at 90 days (0.0% vs 8.3%, P = .020) and 1 year (1.1% vs 11.1%, P = .021), all of which were device removals. Semiconstrained implants also showed lower 90-day (1.1% vs 11.1%, P = .021) and one-year (3.4% vs 16.7%, P = .018) readmission rates compared with nonconstrained implants. At 1 year, semiconstrained implants demonstrated greater improvement in fatigue (4.2 vs -2.2, P = .017) and social role participation (10.1 vs 2.8, P = .044), whereas other Patient-Reported Outcomes Measurement Information System domains were not significantly different.Semiconstrained implants were associated with significantly lower 90-day and one-year index-level reoperation and hospital readmission rates compared with nonconstrained implants, with all reoperations attributable to device removal. These findings suggest that implant design plays an important role in clinical outcomes after CDA.Copyright © Congress of Neurological Surgeons 2026. All rights reserved.

title: Urinary Metabolomic Signatures in Chronic Pancreatitis: A Discovery Phase Investigation of the PROCEED Study.
abstract: Chronic pancreatitis (CP) is an inflammatory disease lacking diagnostic or prognostic biomarkers. Metabolomics has been previously reported by our research group to detect differences in urinary metabolites within a small group of subjects with pancreatitis. We screened urine samples collected from subjects with CP for metabolites that may serve as biomarkers. Here we perform a discovery, pilot study using an advanced platform to investigate urinary metabolite signatures in CP.Urine samples from control (n = 40) and definitive CP (n = 40) PROCEED subjects were analyzed by ALEX-CIS GC-TOF Mass Spectrometry. Each urine sample was analyzed across 328 metabolites:139 named and identified; 189 un-identified. Metabolite levels were normalized to sample median metabolite abundances for further analyses.Direct comparison of urinary metabolite abundances identified 21 metabolites that were differentially expressed in CP versus control groups with 6 metabolites reduced and 15 enriched in urine samples. All 21 showed good discriminatory performance (AUC range; 0.77 - 0.83) with top classifiers (AUC > 0.8) including phenoxyacetic acid, mannose, glycerol-3-galactoside (G3G), xylulose, and ribonic acid (RA). Correlation and hierarchical clustering analysis identified two distinct metabolite clusters. Univariate and subgroup analyses further show several metabolites are also associated with CP-related clinical factors, such as diabetes and exocrine pancreatic dysfunction (EPD), supporting a urinary metabolic signature reflective of both disease status and relevant metabolic comorbid conditions.These data support urinary metabolomic profiling as a promising noninvasive tool for pancreatic disease detection and characterization, providing justification for more comprehensive investigation.Copyright © 2026 The Author(s).
